News.title: At least hapless Starmer kept his distance from foul-mouthed internet clowns unlike cringe-inducing Burnham
News.content:
Bad influence







Next

ANDY Burnham has been mocked by critics as “Keir Starmer with better TikTok videos”.

Turns out that’s an insult to Sir Keir.



At least Burnham’s hapless predecessor had the sense to keep his distance from foul-mouthed internet clowns.

Not our cringe-inducing Prime Minister.



He rolled out the red carpet for a potty-mouthed creator — spurned by his predecessor — who proceeded to film a deeply offensive clip right outside the famous black door.

Burnham even gave him the honour of being his warm-up act at a No10 reception for 60 fame-hungry influencers.

He wasn’t the only embarrassment, either. Another guest was allowed to prance through the corridors recreating Hugh Grant’s cheesy Love Actually dance before tossing the PM softball questions on a cosy podcast.

In just four months in office, Burnham has blown £800,000 of taxpayers’ cash courting these internet Z-listers in a desperate bid to “get down with the kids”.

Instead of looking cool, he has trashed the dignity of his office, ducked proper scrutiny from real journalists and turned himself into a laughing stock.

Sickening docs

LABOUR ministers often lecture us that those with the broadest shoulders should bear a heavier burden during hard times.



Try telling that to their union buddies in the British Medical Association.

A doctors strike leader who earns £138,000 a year is demanding more pay and a shorter working week for all consultants.

It takes brass neck to threaten NHS walkouts while pocketing three times the average salary ­— especially when hospital bosses are warning of the worst ever winter beds crisis.

Millions of families surviving on far less will struggle to find an ounce of sympathy.

But is it too much to ask the BMA to find some compassion for patients in the run-up to Christmas?



With A&E departments already breaking records ahead of the flu season, holding the country to ransom for inflation-busting pay rises is completely out of touch.

BMA leaders should end their militant posturing, accept the economic reality… and put patients before their own pockets.

Cold comfort

HARD-WORKING families face a fresh winter squeeze as energy bills are set to soar by £443 in the New Year.

Ed Miliband promises to slash the cost of heating our homes by £300 — yet so far they have rocketed by double that amount instead.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yesterday’s hammer-blow hike will leave millions shivering through the current big freeze.



Forget the £100 handout that won’t touch the sides. Ministers must show some backbone and axe costly green levies now.

News.title: Andy Burnham’s desperate digital debasement of No10 in bid to be liked has a major flaw… and it’s not ‘serving c**t’
News.content:
Next

TIKTOK, TikTok, drrrrrinnnggg! There goes the idiot alarm . . . again.

It’s like Groundhog Day for Andy Burnham, forever woken by the sound of Britain howling a collective “WTF?!”.





And lo, our great leader has done yet another stupid thing involving what we politely describe as “influencers”.

In a desperate bid to be liked, Our Andy has offered up his storied office as a backdrop for content creators to camp it up and wiggle their bums, or recite songs about “bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets” at No10.

Of course, our vainglorious PM just shrugged off all the initial criticism ’cos he’s doing things a bit differently, mate.

And then, oops, it blows up in his face.

No10 would like us to know that despite it having hit the “like” button on Max Balegde’s now infamous “pussywagon” ditty, this content was, in fact, “clearly unacceptable”.

Oh dear.

That daft clip has now been deleted by its creator, who describes himself on Insta as “presenter, podcaster, idiot”.

But hours later another of his charming messages emerged, from inside No10’s White Room, in which he declared: “They hate when you serve c*** at 10 Downing Street x.”





Whatever that nonsense may mean. And it won’t be long before another clanger comes along.

As we revealed yesterday, No10 is now so in thrall to influencers that it hosted a special event for 60 of them earlier this month, complete with a so-called Glambot camera to capture all their self-promoting inanity.

Our industrious PM has also found the time in his diary to do no less than 30 “interviews” with influencers in the last four months.

Of course, when I say interviews, I mean field a few underarm bowls such as, “Are Oasis the greatest British band?” (LADbible, October) or, “Would you agree that the NHS is pretty slay?” (TikTokker Maddy Lucy Dann).

No chance he’ll face anyone who might not think he’s doing a “really good job“, as Live, Laugh, Luke podcaster Luke Hamnett gushed to his 1.2million TikTok followers this week.

It goes without saying that all this attention-seeking is distinctly unserious for a leader who surely must have far better things to do as Russia plots to build a nuclear arsenal in space. But no, Burnham is far too obsessed with becoming a Heineken PM — reaching the parts of Britain other politicians can’t reach.

He figures that if you want to connect with the politically jaded and, perhaps most importantly, Gen Z — all of whom will soon be allowed to vote, thanks to Labour introducing this for 16-year-olds — you need to barge into their scrolling.

And to be fair, he has a point here — they ain’t watching Kuenssberg, bruv.



Yet there is an inherent problem with our Prime Minister’s chosen path of digital debasement — beyond the glaringly obvious fact that if you piss about with pranksters, you’ll end up getting pranked.

Because, while the vast majority of influencers he entertains have large audiences — Balegde’s is 3.6million strong — it remains to be seen if they have any real political influence.

They are mostly echo-chamber chancers successfully playing the algorithms by constantly churning out the same flavour of content over and over again.

Guests like eager Andy are simply curious cameos in non-stop shows about themselves.

Their followers don’t want to be dragged out of their comfort zones and made to think about things that might actually decide the next election — like immigration or, God forbid, Brexit.

But they will give you a “like” and maybe a “share” as they spin through TikTok hunting for the perfect meme to send to their WhatsApp group.

You can almost feel the glee emanating from the PM’s growing social media team as the likes tick up.

“The message is really hitting home, Boss — we’ve got 10,000 likes.”

Yet the majority of those likers will have forgotten every single word you said before their phone battery dies, if they even heard it at all in the first place.

An Ipsos poll last month revealed that, despite four months of social media saturation under Burnham’s premiership, a third of Gen Z said they had no idea how they felt about him — and 28 per cent that they weren’t happy with him.



So, perhaps his best bet for appealing to the youth vote he so desperately craves is not to simply clog up their feeds with smarmy platitudes, but instead to roll up his sleeves and do things that will make their lives better.

Take action on crippling university loans, bring down inflation so young people might stand a chance of buying a house, and put a few more quid in their pockets so they can get their round in down the pub.

Do all that and they might actually pay attention.

Until then, stop showing off to fawning influencers and do your damn job.

Joy of wedlock for Mr Huang

Jensen Huang Is a lucky bugger – he quits AI giant Nvidia after reportedly shagging staff and a suspected Chinese spy, then rides back into the top job with the full backing of the board.

Shares in the company duly shoot up, netting Huang a few gazillion dollars along the way.

And all this with the backing of President Trump, who celebrated the adulterer as a “great patriot and national treasure” (as he too saw his estimated 370,000 Nvidia shares increase in value).

Trebles all round!

Yet while no grown-ups seem to have a problem with letting Huang take back control of the $4trillion mothership, his return hasn’t been a cakewalk.



No sooner had his re-coronation been announced than the internet was awash with piss-taking memes.

My favourite is a video of his long-suffering wife fitting a padlock to the belt of his yo-yoing trousers.

All created by AI, of course, using the very Nvidia chips Jensen has built his fortune on.

Hands solo to rescue

The old “no sex please, we’re British” mantra is alive and well, according to a major new survey that claims we’re having half as much nookie as we did in the Nineties.

But wait, what’s this?

The very same report, conducted by some actual sexperts, claims that we are having some sex – just with ourselves.

This is all down to the rise of online porn which, ahem, friends tell me you can now get for free, any time you like, on your mobile phone.

So what this report is actually saying is that Britain has become a nation of . . . w*****s.

I often give Gordon Ramsay a bit of stick, mainly because I know he secretly loves a bit of rough and tumble (and he can be a complete prat).



But fair play to him for landing the Top Gear job.

The second I heard it seemed so obvious – he’s forever driving about town in his impressive collection of penis extensions.

Perhaps that’s why he got the gig.

With the BBC slashing costs left right and centre, they agreed to give him the job if he supplied the motors.

Oopsie Daisy Rupesy

Restore Britain, the excitable little party run by former Reformer Rupert Lowe, is being promoted online by an army of ’bots, a cyber- firm has deduced.

Lowe is having none of that and insists his followers on TikTok and X – where his pal, “Utopian anarchist” Elon Musk, actively promotes him for shits and giggles – are real.

And what of those replying to Lowe’s comments?

His proclamations are typically met with a torrent of abuse, as opponents slam what they regard as his party’s “far right” agenda.

Are they also real, Rupert?



I do like a bit of RooB40

Poor old Wazza, getting bollocked by the boring woke brigade for singing Rat In Mi Kitchen, with a Jamaican twang, on the so-far humdrum I’m A Celeb.

Of course, this egregious offence has been branded as “cultural appropriation” because Wayne Rooney is a white fella and the song was written and sung by a black dude (from famously mixed-race reggae band UB40).

Well, be careful what you wish for, wokies, because I’m not sure you’ve thought this through.

If you heard me singing Pass The Dutchie in my Derbyshire accent you’d beg me to pack that accent in, and culturally appropriate to my heart’s content.

AI boffins now tell us the omnipotent tech could help us live to the age of 1,429.

I’ll take that, if it means I’ll get 1,362 years of blissful retirement – and a state pension to keep that going.

But the news has no doubt sent shivers down the King’s spine.

You get a card signed by the monarch at age 100, then 105 and each year after that.



So that’s a lot of ink Charles is gonna need for that “bloody” pen of his.

Cheap & Woeful

After Sunday’s woeful performance by Bruno Fernandes and his Man United team-mates I can no longer scoff at City’s potential relegation.

This time next year we could both be slugging it out in the Championship.

At least getting a ticket might be a bit easier, as I doubt the clueless tourists pushing up prices at Old Trafford will find second-tier footie on a rainy Tuesday night quite as glamorous.

News.title: Wild moment special forces capture ruthless cartel leader during raid on home after huge shootout erupted on streets
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment special forces detain a notorious cartel kingpin during a wild raid where savage gunfire erupted on the streets.

Newly released footage shows the moment troops burst into the holding house of Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores after years of evading capture.



Known as “El Chapo Isidro” the ruthless drug lord was marched out in handcuffs during the dramatic operation last Friday.

Bodycam footage shows armed forces storming the luxurious Sinaloa property in Guasave city via the garage.



Guided by torch-lit weapons, cops entered an upstairs room, revealing the FBI Most Wanted kingpin slumped over in handcuffs.

His capture brought an end to a bloody reign responsible for years of tragedy in Mexico and the United States.

When soldiers arrived in armed trucks around 4pm they were welcomed by a barrage of gunfire.

Mexican military helicopters opened fire with footage showing a hail of bullets raining from the chopper as they flew low over the location.



As the raid unfolded, residents recorded footage of flaming cars and gunfight in the streets.

The violent clashes sent fans fleeing from a nearby baseball game in terror.

Separate footage shows baseball fans at the Kuroda Park stadium scrambling from the stands as gunfire cracks through the air.



Shouts of “get down!” and “duck” can be heard in the terrifying clip as people frantically clambered over barriers.

Seven suspects were killed in the operation as well as four members of the Mexican army who were en route as reinforcements.

Eight alleged drug cartel members were detained for their involvement in violence.

Intelligence from Donald Trump’s administration helped authorities capture him, the Mexican government said in a report early Saturday.

Meza-Flores is accused of possession, distribution, and importation of large quantities of heroin, meth, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the US, the FBI said.



In recent years, his influence had grown amid a conflict between two other major factions of the cartel — the Guzmán and Zambada families.

Their members, the sons of drug lords Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán and Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, have been waging a war against each other for nearly two years.

The crime boss was previously indicted for drug trafficking violations and possession of a firearm in 2019, and in 2012 for drug trafficking charges.

Authorities hope his arrest will put a dent in the drug trade and curb bloodshed in the gang-ravaged region.

News.title: Spanish army mobilises to tiny Canary Island after record number of small boat migrants doubles population in ‘invasion’
News.content:
Next

THE SPANISH army has mobilised to the Canary Islands after a record number of migrants arrived on small boats amidst an immigration crisis.

More than 2,000 men, women and children reached the tiny island of El Hierro yesterday, prompting the Spanish Government’s response.



Amongst those making the journey were a pregnant woman and a two-month-old baby.

Regional president Fernando Clavijo has branded the growing crisis “anything but under control” on a “sadly historic” day.



The surge has sparked growing fears that the situation in El Hierro – home to roughly 11,500 residents – could spiral into a full-blown Ceuta-style crisis.

An estimated 100,000 to 120,000 people swam or walked into Ceuta from Morocco at the end of July in a mass border breach which transformed the lives of residents in Spain’s North African enclave.

In response, an aircraft carrying personnel and equipment is expected to depart early tomorrow from the Torrejon de Ardoz airbase in Madrid.

The plane will head to an air base in Gando on the eastern coast of Gran Canaria before members of the Military Emergencies Unit are transferred to the tiny island.



Another military unit will also be dispatched as the island struggles to cope with the thousands of migrants who arrived earlier this month.

The military reinforcements will be tasked mainly with alleviating pressure on El Hierro’s already-strained health services which are designed for its 12,000-strong population.

An influx earlier this week saw thousands of men, women and children packed into eleven cayucos coming from Senegal and Gambia.

The Tuesday crossings mark the highest number in a single day since records began in Spain, emergency services operating in the port of La Restinga confirmed.

The arrivals included nearly 200 women and over 100 children, including a baby of only two months.



The newborn was one of 127 children and 203 women on the boats that arrived yesterday, carrying migrants from eight countries including Gambia, Senegal, Mauritania and Mali.

The Atlantic crossing between Africa and the Canaries is one of the most dangerous, with new figures showing one in five migrants die en route.

A field hospital had to be opened last week to ease the problems that were being caused.



The Canary Islands’ president has previously criticised the government for not doing enough to help alleviate the situation.

He also requested an urgent meeting with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to call for an “extraordinary” EU response.

The Canary Islands’ president said of the drama: “It is unsustainable, and it is certainly anything but under control.”

Now, with the military intervention, there are hopes that there may be an ease of the overcrowding currently taking place.

At least 800 of the new arrivals were being ferried to Tenerife today and others will be flown to mainland Spain.



A four-star hotel in Torrox near Malaga is one of the places that has been used to temporarily accommodate them.

So far in November, there have been only five days when a migrant boat didn’t reach the Canary Islands.

Clavijo said: “The surge in November has led us to declare a migration emergency, mobilise over 20 million euros, and bolster search-and-rescue resources, healthcare services, and the transfer of minors.

“We will continue working with the regional government. I want to send a message to the people of the Canary Islands: the situation is under control because, this time, we were prepared.

“During the 2020 crisis, even with fewer arrivals, the islands’ systems collapsed. Since then, we have established new resources to ensure an effective and reliable response.”



Vox leader Santiago Abascal described what was happening in the Canary Islands as an “invasion” during a fiery speech in Tenerife last week.

The other immigration flashpoint has been Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta, where thousands of undocumented migrants swam or walked onto EU soil at the end of July.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It recently emerged Spanish police had concluded between 100,000 and 125,000 undocumented migrants entered Ceuta at the end of July, far more than the original 72,500 estimate.

Most returned in subsequent days but around 12,000 people are thought to have remained.

News.title: Foul-mouthed TikToker who used C-word inside No10 was embraced by Burnham AFTER he failed vetting when Starmer was PM
News.content:
CLOWNING STREET Foul-mouthed TikToker who used C-word inside No10 was embraced by Burnham AFTER he failed vetting when Starmer was PM







Next

ANDY Burnham has been accused of embracing a controversial TikTok star who had previously been rejected as too crude by Sir Keir Starmer.

The PM was yesterday forced to condemn footage of Max Balegde miming the words “bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets” outside the No10 front door.

Source: @max_balegde/TikTok



A separate video shows the influencer posing in the grand state rooms with a caption that used the c-bomb.

Both were disowned by Downing Street following a Commons onslaught by Kemi Badenoch who branded the clips “grotesque”.



But The Sun can reveal that Balegde was previously ruled out as a partner creator by Sir Keir Starmer’s government because he was deemed too risky.

A well-placed source said the prolific influencer was suggested as someone who could collaborate with No10 but then axed because his content was seen as inappropriate.

They pointed to Sir Keir’s engagement with influencers being largely focused on specific policy issues, such as working with Love Island star Georgia Harrison to highlight violence against women and girls.

Yet under Mr Burnham, Balegde was picked to host a reception at No10 on November 9 for dozens of social media stars.

The PM yesterday declined to apologise after being accused of debasing his office, while No10 left the door open to another visit by the TikToker.

Mr Burnham hit back at Mrs Badenoch in the Commons, saying: “She sneers at TikTokers. She sneers at influencers.”



He insisted he would not apologise for engaging with people young Brits turn to for information, while acknowledging the video was unacceptable.

The revelations raise serious questions over Mr Burnham’s judgement and how a man with a history of controversial videos sailed through the selection process.

Whitehall guidance for working with contracted influencers recommends checking up to five pages of internet search results and a year’s worth of social media posts to identify potentially problematic content.

It remains unclear what vetting was carried out by Mr Burnham’s team or whether they were aware of the previous decision to reject Balegde.

Balegde was forced to apologise on Tuesday after posting footage of himself miming along to a viral song featuring the lyrics “bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets” outside the famous black door.



Bomboclaat is a Jamaican profanity referring to a menstrual cloth while pussy is a slang term for female genitals.

The Sun yesterday also uncovered footage of Balegde striking a saucy pose between two Union Jacks inside Downing Street.

He captioned the clip: “They hate when you serve c*** at 10 Downing Street x.”

It is the very same spot where Rishi Sunak welcomed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in February 2023 on his first visit to Britain since Putin launched his full-scale invasion.

Influencers were even handed taxpayer-funded phones to film inside No10 before being sent the footage.



In his video diary of the evening, Balegde revealed there was “wine on tap” but that he had been “shouted at for having a glass of wine downstairs”.

Despite the backlash, the TikToker could still be welcomed back.

Balegde claims Mr Burnham invited him for tea.

Asked yesterday whether the influencer would be invited back, the PM’s official spokesman said: “I’m not going to get ahead of future events.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Pressed on the tea invitation, he again said he would not get ahead of “future receptions”.

News.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade POSTPONED due to weather for 1st time in 100yr history as Nor’easter barrels towards NYC
News.content:
Next

THE Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to an incoming storm.

It is the first time the event has been called off because of weather in its 100-year history.



In a statement shared by NBC 4 New York, a spokesperson for Macy’s said: “The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration.

“Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28.



“Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8.30 am on Saturday.”

They added, “Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

The historic postponement comes after days of mounting fears that the parade’s iconic balloons could be grounded.

City officials had even considered bringing forward Thursday’s start time in a bid to beat the worst of the storm.

Under city safety regulations, the giant helium balloons cannot fly when sustained winds reach 23 mph or gusts hit 34 mph.

The looming nor’easter is also threatening to spark holiday travel chaos for millions of Americans.



New York Governor Kathy Hochul warned on Wednesday that New York City, Long Island and the lower Hudson Valley could be battered by heavy rain, coastal flooding and wind gusts of up to 60 mph.

“The worst of it is expected late tomorrow afternoon,” Hochul wrote on X.

“A good time to stay inside, watch some football and sleep off that big meal!”

The governor said state emergency teams were ready to respond and urged New Yorkers to monitor their local forecasts and exercise caution if traveling over the holiday.



New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani also warned that the powerful winds could bring down trees and power lines, leaving residents facing potential Thanksgiving power outages.

He urged New Yorkers to secure outdoor furniture and holiday decorations and charge their phones ahead of the storm.



Those living in basement apartments or flood-prone areas were also advised to move to higher floors before the heavy rain hits.

“As we gather for Thanksgiving, let’s look out for one another,” Mamdani wrote on X.

The parade has only been canceled three times since its debut in 1924, between 1942 and 1944, when rubber and helium were needed for the World War II effort.

Organizers have been working for the last five years to make the 2026 parade the best ever.

A record 100 inflatables had been lined up for the festivities, including many new additions.



More than 11,000 volunteers and performers were also expected to take part, including around 5,000 costumed participants, among them 1,000 clowns.

Country music sensation Megan Moroney and Grammy-nominated singer Teddy Swims had been tapped to headline performances outside Macy’s flagship store in Herald Square.

Queen Latifah, Keke Palmer, Natasha Bedingfield, JoJo and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots were also among the names scheduled to perform.

British singer Raye was due to open the festivities alongside her two sisters.

Today show favorites Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker were set to return as hosts of NBC’s parade coverage.



It remains unclear whether the same star-studded lineup will be available for Saturday’s rescheduled event.

New balloon designs featuring Bluey, Hello Kitty, Mickey Mouse and Snoopy were set to soar above the streets of Manhattan.

Macy’s had also unveiled a Harry Potter-themed float inspired by HBO’s upcoming television adaptation.

The beloved Blue Hippo balloon was also set to make its grand return after a 95-year absence.

The 30-foot-long inflatable was painstakingly recreated using old photographs and footage after the original disappeared in 1931.



Its comeback was set to include a touching tribute to Fiona, the famous Cincinnati Zoo hippo who died on November 19 at the age of nine after swallowing a knit hat.

Balloon handlers were due to wear purple patches featuring Fiona’s face inside a heart alongside the words “Celebrating Fiona.”

Macy’s also made a donation to the zoo in her memory.

News.title: Body found in search for missing Kelsey Hunter after four-days as boyfriend, 21, appears in court charged with murder
News.content:
Next

A BODY has been found during the search for missing Kelsey Hunter.

The 20-year-old was reported missing from Castle Douglas, Kirkcudbrightshire, on Saturday night, sparking a major police search.



Specialist cops made the tragic discovery at 7:15pm tonight (Wednesday, November 25) after days of tireless efforts to find her.

Cops say Kelsey’s “completely heartbroken” family have been made aware and said a post mortem examination will take place in due course.



Forensic teams spent most of Wednesday focused on a ravine area close to Kelsey’s home in Springholm, Kirkcudbrightshire, before it was announced that her body had been found tonight.

Kelsey’s boyfriend Daniel McKnight, 21, has appeared in court charged with murder.

He made no plea to the charge during a hearing at Dumfries Sheriff Court on Tuesday, where he also faced charges of attempting to pervert the course of justice and an alleged bail offence.

McKnight was remanded in custody after appearing in the dock.

Detective Chief Inspector Stephen McGrath, of Police Scotland’s Major Investigation Team, said: “Our thoughts are with Kelsey’s family at this extremely difficult time.

“They are completely heartbroken and continue to be supported by specialist officers.



“A team of officers are continuing to work around the clock to get them answers.

“This is clearly a significant development and extensive work remains ongoing.

“We are building up a picture of Kelsey’s movements in the days and weeks prior to her being reported missing, and I would like to thank everyone for their help so far.”

Kelsey last seen in Cotton Street area of Castle Douglas around 5pm on Saturday, 21 November, 2026.

Searches were continuing to find her body even after her boyfriend had appeared in court.



Detectives and forensics officers switched their focus to the search zone near Kelsey’s house.

A nearby field was also cordoned off and around five forensic officers were seen entering the new site, which is being guarded by a police officer around the clock.

Detective Chief Inspector McGrath pleaded for information.



He said: “I would again appeal to any of her friends, who may have information and have not yet spoken to officers, to come forward.”

“There will continue to be a police presence in the area while our enquiries continue.

“Anyone with any concerns, or any information, can approach these officers.

“Door-to-door enquiries are still being carried out and I would urge anyone who has any information, including CCTV or dashcam footage, to get in touch with us.”

Cops said uniformed and plain-clothed officers from the local division, as well as detectives from the Major Investigation Team, will remain in the area over the coming days as our enquiries continue.



Local Area Commander Emma Dodds said: “We understand how concerning this will be for the local community, but we have a significant amount of resources dedicated to this investigation.

“There will be a lot of police activity in the area over the coming days as our enquiries continue.

“Anyone with any concerns, or information, can approach these officers – we are here to help.”

We told how drones and a mountain rescue team have been mobilised in the hunt for Kelsey, who was reported last seen at around 5pm on Saturday in Castle Douglas – six miles from her home in nearby Springholm.

Forensics teams surrounded the area around the property and Police Scotland’s dog branch were also involved.



The police’s air support unit had earlier been drafted in to fly a drone along the route from the back of Kelsey’s home to the woods, which were sealed off on Monday.

A specialist rope access team was also called to the sleepy Scots village.

Locals expressed their sadness at the tragedy.

One said: “It is so tragic that the young lassie is dead.

“She would always be walking about with her dog.

“I really hope they find her and get her back to her family.”

Anyone with any information is asked to contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 2269 of 22 November.

News.title: I’m A Celebrity LIVE: Mariella Frostrup breaks down in tears live on air after Ant and Dec news
News.content:
Ade on how he met his wife

Ade revealed that he met his wife, who he now has two children with, at the National Television Awards.





He said: “I went and I was in a bad mood, because I was trying to buy my first house and I got turned down on a mortgage, so I roll up to the NTAs and I’m like ‘I’m just gonna get drunk’.”





However, he went to the VIP room and “got absolutely hammered on champagne” and later went to the after party.





Despite there likely being a lift, he decided to take the stairs. “I just fell down the stairs, landed at the bottom of the stairs, it was quite painful, so I’m down there and everyone at this after party is like people from Eastenders, all the soaps, Corrie, and then I saw Linda, she was sitting on her own by a table and as I pushed, she just like smiled this massive smile and I was like- there’s something special about this woman, so I pushed over to her and we just started chatting.”





AJ exclaimed: “All from a smile!”





He responded: “She just had this lovely aura, a really special aura.”





The pair didn’t swap numbers that night but he later found her on Facebook. He explained that they spoke for months back and forth before he asked her out on a date.





Speaking about their first date, which saw her help him move into his new house, he said: “We sat on the floor in an empty house because I had no furniture and just chatted for 4 hours straight.”





He added: “It's nice because you don’t always think you’ll find someone that’s for you, that’s going to be your forever person, and I waited a long time.”

News.title: Ade Adepitan faced judgement over 17-year age gap with celebrity wife
News.content:
Ade Adepitan faced judgement over 17-year age gap with celebrity wife

I'm A Celebrity star and Paralympic medallist Ade Adepitan and his wife Linda Harrison have been together for more than 16 years, but their 17-year age gap caused some initial reservations for the TV presenter

View 3 Images Ade Adepitan and Linda Harrison have been together for over 16 years (Image: Dave Benett, Dave Benett/Getty Images for National Geographic & Disney+)

I'm A Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here! contestant Ade Adepitan has lived a remarkable life, conquering challenges to become a Paralympic medallist and one of Britain's most familiar faces on television. Yet behind the scenes, the 53-year-old has also discovered love with his wife, Scottish singer-songwriter Linda Harrison, who is 17 years his junior.

‌



‌



The duo have been an item for over 16 years, having first encountered each other at the National Television Awards in January 2010. Linda was just 19 at the time, while Ade was already a well-known television figure and ex-Paralympic competitor.

‌



Their initial encounter was rather unconventional, with Ade noticing Linda seated alone after her mates had momentarily vanished. Speaking to The Guardian, he said he clocked her beaming grin and felt instantly attracted to her.

‌



Linda recalled Ade making his way over and remarking on her stripy tights, before they engaged in effortless chat. Ade snapped a photo of them both and requested her email so he could forward it.

What transpired was a series of exchanges that would ultimately result in matrimony. Of course, Linda quipped that she chose to do some digging of her own after he disclosed he'd discovered clips of her performing online.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"If he's going to stalk me, I'm going to stalk him," she recalled. She looked him up online and uncovered the remarkable feats he'd already achieved, including securing bronze at the 2004 Paralympic Games and scaling a volcano on his hands and knees for five hours when his wheelchair couldn't go any further.

Linda subsequently confessed she was astounded by what she found. She said: "I just went: 'That's my person.'"

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

At that point, Linda was studying music while chasing her dream as a vocalist performing under the stage name Elle Exxe. Their first real date happened in Guildford, where she was at university, though Ade turned up an hour behind schedule.

‌



The couple rapidly realised they relished each other's presence, with Linda even perching on Ade's lap as they tumbled down a hillside heading back towards the car park.

The 17-year age gap

Despite the immediate spark, their romance wasn't without its challenges. Ade has openly acknowledged that their 17-year age difference initially left him uncertain, especially given Linda was still in her teens when they first crossed paths.

‌



He also found himself out of his comfort zone when he turned up at one of her performances, with Linda's musical preferences and edgy look being completely alien to his own world. He even dubbed her 'Indie Lindie' after experiencing her music scene.

Yet it was the gap in their ages that proved most troubling for him. He confessed: "It definitely threw me at first."

‌



He revealed that he was mindful of the different life stages they occupied and wished to allow Linda time to mature before contemplating marriage. He added: "I felt I had to wait until Linda was in her mid-20s," explaining that if they remained together and content, marriage would follow naturally.

Their romance also endured a temporary split when professional obligations and differing priorities risked driving them apart. Ade was regularly absent, travelling extensively on the wheelchair tennis circuit, while Linda was focused on finishing her degree.

‌



Nevertheless, an invitation to accompany him on a Portuguese holiday marked a pivotal moment. Linda was initially hesitant, but the couple enjoyed themselves to such an extent that she confessed she didn't want to resume normal life.

She ultimately relocated to London, though they maintained separate residences for approximately five years before cohabiting shortly ahead of their wedding.

‌



View 3 Images Ade Adepitan's wife is 17 years his junior (Image: Jeff Spicer, Getty Images for Great Show Productions Ltd.)

Confronting prejudice surrounding their partnership

The couple have also discussed openly the assumptions and discrimination they have faced, with Ade disclosing that their age gap, his disability and their contrasting backgrounds have all shaped how certain people view their relationship. He explained: "Disability, race, age, all of that. People judge all the time."

‌



Linda has been especially vocal about some of the responses she has encountered, remembering how people would essentially praise her for being in a relationship with a disabled man. She characterised the mindset as peculiar and said it was one of the reasons the couple chose to launch a YouTube channel, hoping to challenge the presumptions people made about them.

"They seem to need a motive for us to be together, other than love," she said. Ade, meanwhile, has described their relationship as a partnership founded on understanding each other's strengths and weaknesses, supporting one another and enabling both of their careers to thrive.

‌



View 3 Images Ade Adepitan is currently on I'm A Celeb (Image: Molly Darlington, Getty Images)

Fairytale wedding and family life

Ade's prediction that he would one day marry Linda ultimately came true in August 2018, when they wed at the iconic St Paul's Cathedral. The wedding followed a romantic proposal beside Lake Como in Italy, although the moment itself came with a humorous exchange between the pair.

‌



Recalling the proposal to HELLO!, Ade revealed that Linda insisted he needed to get down on one knee, despite his disability making the movement difficult. He eventually got down on both knees instead, before asking her to marry him.

Their wedding was covered exclusively by HELLO!, with Ade later describing it as an occasion that exceeded even his expectations.

Article continues below

"Everyone says it's the best day of your life but it was probably better than that," he said. The pair have since started a family, with their first child, son Bolla, arriving in January 2021.

Their family expanded further in March 2025 with the arrival of daughter Zayla. Ade has previously discussed the delights of being a father, remarking that their son tends to mimic everything his parents say, requiring them to be mindful of conversations held in his presence.

News.title: Body found in search for missing woman Kelsey Hunter, 20, after man arrested
News.content:
Body found in search for missing woman Kelsey Hunter, 20, after man arrested

Police said a body was found in the search for 20-year-old Kelsey Hunter, who was reported missing in Springholm, Dumfries and Galloway, on Saturday afternoon

View 3 Images Kelsey Hunter, 20, was reported missing over the weekend (Image: Facebook)

A body has been found in the search for a missing woman tonight.

‌



‌



Kelsey Hunter, 20, who went missing in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland over the weekend. The discovery was made in a wooded area in the village of Springholm, where an intensive search has been taking place over the last few days.

‌



Cops say Kelsey’s “completely heartbroken” family have been made aware and said a post mortem examination will take place in due course.

‌



Ms Hunter was last seen in the nearby town of Castle Douglas at around 5pm on Saturday. The discovery comes a day after 21-year-old Daniel McKnight appeared in private at Dumfries Sheriff Court charged with murder and attempting to defeat the ends of justice. He did not submit a plea, and is due to appear again within eight days.

View 3 Images Detectives had searched areas near Kelsey's home in Springholm, in Dumfries and Galloway (Image: Daily Record)

Detective Chief Inspector Stephen McGrath, of Police Scotland’s Major Investigation Team, said: “Our thoughts are with Kelsey’s family at this extremely difficult time. They are completely heartbroken and continue to be supported by specialist officers.

‌



"A team of officers are continuing to work around the clock to get them answers. This is clearly a significant development and extensive work remains ongoing.

"We are building up a picture of Kelsey’s movements in the days and weeks prior to her being reported missing, and I would like to thank everyone for their help so far."

‌



View 3 Images Kelsey's family is said to be 'completely heartbroken' (Image: Facebook)

Searches were continuing to find the young woman's body even after McKnight had appeared in court. Detectives and forensics officers switched their focus to the search zone near Kelsey’s house.

‌



A nearby field was also cordoned off and around five forensic officers were seen entering the new site, which is being guarded by a police officer around the clock.

Detective Chief Inspector McGrath had pleaded for information. He said: “I would again appeal to any of her friends, who may have information and have not yet spoken to officers, to come forward.”

‌



“There will continue to be a police presence in the area while our enquiries continue. Anyone with any concerns, or any information, can approach these officers.

“Door-to-door enquiries are still being carried out and I would urge anyone who has any information, including CCTV or dashcam footage, to get in touch with us.”
