News.title: Russia could launch a nuclear-armed weapon into space by the end of the year
News.content:
Russia could launch a nuclear-armed weapon into space by the end of the year

European leaders fear Vladimir Putin could launch a nuclear-armed weapon into Earth's orbit within 60 days - as NATO vowed to defend 'every inch' of its territory from outer space threats

View 3 Images Russian president Vladimir Putin could be about to deploy a nuclear-armed satellite (file photo) (Image: AP)

Vladimir Putin could launch a nuclear-armed weapon into space by the end of the year, intelligence bosses fear.

‌



‌



German chancellor Friedrich Merz warned today that Russia is targeting "outer space" as part of its campaign of escalation, after reports earlier this week suggested a nuclear-capable satellite could be launched within 60 days.

‌



He is the latest to comment on the alarming claims after NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte vowed to "defend" allies from space weapons.

‌



In comments aimed "far left and far right" lawmakers sympathetic to the Kremlin, Merz told the Bundestag: "Russia knows exactly what it wants, and Russia wants more than Ukraine.

View 3 Images German chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that Russia is 'even escalating tensions in outer space' (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

RAF warplanes being moved into protective shelters over fears of kamikaze drone attacks READ MORE :

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



"Anyone who fails to grasp this either does not understand the world as it is, or is pursuing an entirely different agenda - one that stands in opposition to the freedom, openness, and liberal values of our own country.

"Russia is escalating tensions in the Baltic region, in Poland, in the Black Sea, and even in outer space. It is escalating on a massive scale - including here within our own borders, even at the cost of human lives. "That is the situation, ladies and gentlemen. And that is why we, as Europeans, must and will - set clear boundaries for Russia."

‌



NATO chief Mr Rutte told a press conference yesterday: "I can assure you, we will always make sure that we defend every inch of NATO territory, and that includes making sure that we are safe when it comes to space."

View 3 Images A launch by Russia's space agency in Kazakhstan earlier this year (Image: Russian Space Agency Roscosmos/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The concerns centre around the Sputnik-S satellite, which is now believed to be ready to launch after being under development by engineers around Moscow for several years.

Equipped with a nuclear weapon, the craft would give Moscow the ability to detonate a warhead in low-Earth orbit - generating an electromagnetic pulse capable of crippling vital Western satellite networks such as SpaceX’s Starlink, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications.

‌



It would also mark a direct breach of the 1967 UN Outer Space Treaty, which bans nations from placing nuclear weapons or other weapons of mass destruction in orbit.

An investigation by broadcasters WDR and NDR and German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung found an intelligence assessment from early November that said the satellite could be launched "within 60 days."

Article continues below

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the claims on Monday, telling reporters: "No, we haven't seen the report. But there are so many 'alleged' and 'possible' claims in it, attributed to who knows whom, that it's certainly hardly worth taking them seriously."

News.title: CCTV footage shows moment father and daughter wheeled murder victim's body to canal
News.content:
CCTV footage shows moment father and daughter wheeled murder victim's body to canal

Security footage shows the moment ‘evil’ murderer John Anslow and his daughter Hayley-Marie Ferguson pushed his victim in a wheelchair before dumping her lifeless body in a canal

Father and daughter push corpse in wheelchair to dump body in canal

CCTV footage has captured the chilling moment an ‘evil monster’ pushed a mother-of-one he murdered in his wheelchair before dumping her body in a canal.

‌



‌



‌



The footage, from the early hours of September 29, shows John Anslow, 65, walking unaided alongside his daughter Hayley-Marie Ferguson pushing his victim’s body in the wheelchair along the darkened streets towards the well-to the Walsall Canal.

‌



They are both seen walking freely despite each purporting to be severely disabled. Police bodycam footage also shows officers going through Ferguson's wheelie bin where she had disposed of Ms Bailey's clothes.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 4 Images John Anslow duped his victim into helping wheel him home before he murdered her (Image: West Midlands Police /Press Association)

Anslow recruited his ‘daddy’s girl’ daughter, 42, to help him clean the murder scene. She arrived to meet him with paving slabs from her garden for their plot to weigh down the victim's body and dump it in a canal.

‌



Anslow described as "evil" and a "monster" in court by Bailey’s relatives was found guilty of murder in September after jurors heard how he met Ms Bailey by chance in Great Bridge, West Midlands, and asked the 36-year-old to push his wheelchair to his home, where he broke her jaw and inflicted injuries to her private parts before killing her.

‌



Today, he was sentenced to life with a minimum term of 26 years at Worcester Crown Court. The twice-convicted rapist was likely to die in jail, Judge Simon Drew Kc said.

View 4 Images The father and daughter pair wheeled Chereiss Bailey’s lifeless body to a canal (Image: West Midlands Police /Press Association)

‌



Mother-of-five Ferguson, 42, who attended a Peaky Blinders-themed event after helping her father dispose of evidence, was jailed for six years for assisting an offender and preventing a lawful burial.

‌



The judge told Ferguson, who helped dispose of bloodstained clothing and bedding: “You played an active and crucial part in a carefully planned and executed enterprise.”

Judge Drew also criticised Ferguson for taking a photograph of the victim’s body inside her father’s house “presumably as some form of trophy” and taking another picture of it in the wheelchair as “another ghoulish record of your actions”.

‌



View 4 Images CCTV footage showed the walk in the early hours to dispose of the body (Image: West Midlands Police)

In a statement issued after the sentencing, the family of the victim said: “We have waited a long time for this day, carrying a pain that no family should ever have to carry.

‌



“Throughout everything, we have stood together for Chereiss. On the days one of us has struggled, the rest of us have held them up and that is how we have made it this far.

“We would like to thank everyone who has supported our family and kept Chereiss in their thoughts. Every message, kind word and act of support has meant more than people probably realise.”

‌



View 4 Images Police found Ms Bailey's clothes in Ferguson's bin (Image: West Midlands Police)

‌



The family added of their loved one: “Chereiss was a much-loved daughter, sister, mother, auntie, granddaughter and friend, but those words alone could never explain what she meant to us.

“Most heartbreaking of all, her little boy has been robbed of growing up with his mum beside him. We will make sure he grows up knowing exactly who she was, how much she adored him and how fiercely she was loved.”

News.title: Nigel Farage accused of 'misreading mood of nation' as he launches defend Brexit campaign
News.content:
Nigel Farage accused of 'misreading mood of nation' as he launches defend Brexit campaign

In an echo of the 2016 Brexit referendum wars, the underfire Reform boss and his old ex-Leave.EU ally Arron Banks said they were setting up pressure group 'Keep Britain Out'

View 2 Images Nigel Farage with his old Leave.EU ally Arron Banks (Image: ANDY RAIN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Nigel Farage has been accused of misreading the mood of the nation as he launched a campaign to defend Brexit and fight Andy Burnham's bid for closer EU ties.

‌



‌



In an echo of the 2016 Brexit wars, the under-fire Reform boss and his old Leave.EU ally Arron Banks said they were setting up pressure group 'Keep Britain Out'.

‌



The Eurosceptics launched their fight for attention after Lord Michael Gove - a veteran of the official Vote Leave camp - recently joined the rival "Stay Out" campaign.

‌



Brexit bankroller Mr Banks, who loaned around £8million to the unofficial Leave campaign during the EU referendum, told a press conference today he would leave Lord Gove's campaign "with the dripping wet Tories".

But chief executive of pro-EU campaign group Best for Britain, Naomi Smith, told The Mirror: “Voters will find it frustrating that Nigel Farage has said that they are afraid of change and that ‘the status quo’ will help his campaign.

“People are crying out for help, not just with the cost of living crisis, but to end the restrictions on their travel plans, their retirement plans, or their family businesses caused by being outside the EU.

‌



Andy Burnham vows Brexit deal will bring down the cost of weekly shop READ MORE :

View 2 Images 'Keep Britain Out is an insurance vehicle,' says Reform boss Nigel Farage (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

“He’s once again misread the mood of the nation, is increasingly out of touch, and this campaign is likely to help his opponents.”

‌



Supporters of the new outfit 'Keep Britain Out' will be asked to sign a 10-point pledge sheet, suggesting the campaign will only support would-be MPs who back their stance.

It includes a commitment to reverse any steps to move closer to the bloc, including axing the PM's Brexit reset deal to slash red tape for businesses and drive down costs for families.

‌



During press conference in Westminster, Mr Farage appeared on stage with his old pal and Brexit bankroller Mr Banks while strategist Andy Wigmore was working behind the scenes.

Mr Banks once branded the trio behind the 2016 Leave.EU camp the “Bad Boys Of Brexit”.

‌



During the event, Mr Farage, who continues to face a parliamentary probe over a £5million gift from a crypto billionaire, said: “Well, here we go again.”

He added: “The big difference here is we now own the status quo. Prior to 2016 the establishment owned the status quo and quite naturally people fear change.”

‌



And he described the new campaign as an insurance vehicle. He said: “I won’t say I look forward to this campaign, I hope we never have to fight it. Arron [Banks] is an insurance mogul and he’s set this up - Keep Britain Out is an insurance vehicle.

“It’s an insurance vehicle that will be needed if Labour or Labour and the Liberal Democrats form a majority after the next general election."

Article continues below

Mr Banks also told reporters the Prime Minister had “started the firing gun on a second referendum”. He then claimed: “We see a Brexit [general] election, probably in May and at the heart of that is going to be the promise of a second referendum.”

News.title: Brits long to return to the 90s – the top 20 things the nation wants to bring back
News.content:
Brits long to return to the 90s – the top 20 things the nation wants to bring back

Research reveals top 20 things people would revive from the 1990s, including Woolworths, handwritten letters and Top of the Pops

View 2 Images Shoppers miss Woolworths (Image: PA)

Brits are yearning for a return to the 1990s, with Woolworths, life before social media, and catching up with friends without smartphones among the things they'd most like to see make a comeback.

‌



‌



A survey of 2,000 adults has revealed the top 20 things people would resurrect from the decade if given the chance, including handwritten letters, Top of the Pops as well as being able to head out without being reachable.

‌



Classic Saturday morning television is longed for by 20%, while 19% hanker after the days of dropping off a film and waiting patiently for their holiday photographs to be developed.

‌



The same proportion would welcome back video rental shops, while 18% miss lifting the landline receiver for a proper natter with friends.

The nostalgic research was commissioned by Renault, which worked with Louise Redknapp to celebrate the return of one of its own 90s icons, the Twingo.

View 2 Images 90s pop icon Louise Redknapp celebrates the launch of the all-new Renault Twingo (Image: PinPep)

‌



Louise Redknapp said: "There was something really special about the 90s. Life felt a bit simpler, you weren't constantly looking at your phone and there were so many brilliant things that instantly take you back to that time.

"For me, music is obviously a huge part of those memories, but it's funny how something as simple as a song, an outfit or even a car can transport you straight back to a particular moment.

‌



"I love that so many things from the decade are having another moment now. There's clearly a real appetite for the fun, personality and character we associate with the 90s."

‌



It seems nostalgia for the decade runs far deeper than Game Boys and Britpop. More than one in five (22%) admit they miss the 90s "a lot", while another 38% miss the decade "a little."

Life before social media is particularly fondly remembered, with 21% saying it's what they long for most, while 13% yearn for the days before smartphones. And 12% are still pining for the decade's music.

‌



Almost half (46%) reckon the high street was superior back then, while 44% believe face-to-face conversations were better and 38% think people had longer attention spans.

Even cars get the nostalgia treatment, with 13% believing vehicles and their designs were better in the 90s.

‌



The OnePoll.com study revealed that 62% believe the 1990s was a greater time to be alive than today, with 41% going even further by declaring it the best decade to have lived through.

Adam Wood, managing director of Renault, said: "The 90s was a decade packed with personality, from the music people listened to, the clothes they wore and the cars they drove.

‌



"It's fascinating to see how many people still have such affection for that period, and particularly how much they have nostalgic memories for everyday life back then.

"The Twingo brings that spirit back and blends it with the best of modern cars; it's full of character and fun, is compact yet packed with big car technology and available for a scarcely believable price.

Article continues below

"Whether you are driving it or looking at it, it's going to spread some '90s-inspired joy on roads in the coming months."

TOP 20 THINGS BRITS WANT TO BRING BACK FROM THE 90s:

News.title: 'I want to support my best mate, but she’s in the wrong'
News.content:
Dear Coleen,

My best friend had an affair with her friend’s partner and the you-know-what has now hit the fan and everyone knows. She’s in a real state and has no idea how things will play out.

My question is: how do I support her? On the one hand, I can’t help judging what she did – I think she’s in the wrong and she’s hurt people. However, she’s also hurting and she’s been my best friend since we were 13.

I literally don’t know what to say to her, other than I’m here if she wants to get things off her chest, but if she’s looking to me to say what she did was OK, then I can’t do it.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



She doesn’t have children with her own partner, but her friend and the guy she was having an affair with have a two-year-old daughter.

View 2 Images Coleen says: "She’s going to have to accept that some people will lose trust in her." (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

I’m angry with her for doing this. She’s the kind of person who thrives on male attention, even though her partner is lovely and absolutely adored her. Her friend is also a good person and she’s crushed by what’s happened. How should I deal with this?

Coleen says,

I think you should say that you can’t make her feel better about what’s happened, but you’ll listen and support her. If she pushes you to condone what she did, then I think it’s fine to say you’re not OK with it, but you’re there for her as a friend.

‌



I guess other people might ostracise you for sticking up for her but, you know, we all do things we’re not proud of and we all make mistakes, and sometimes people get hurt. That’s life sometimes.

But she’s going to have to accept that some people will lose trust in her (and him, of course). An affair is exciting when you’re getting away with it but, the risk is, you have to take the consequences if you get found out. Part of those consequences are causing heartache and mayhem in everyone’s lives. It’s horrible to bear the responsibility for that.

I think you are a good friend for wanting to support her and what you have to remember is that it takes two to tango. This isn’t all on her.

She will learn a big lesson from this – relationships aren’t a game and you can’t play fast and loose with people’s feelings and their lives. I hope she’ll also realise that there must have been serious issues in their relationships for them to end up in an affair.

‌



Coleen’s words of wisdom

Gratitude is simply the habit of appreciating what you have instead of focusing on what you don’t have. It encourages positivity and it reminds you of the people and things that make your life good.

News.title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
News.content:
Kelvin Blake, 62, who has worked for the firm for 25 years, and whose partner has been there 29 years, said he was feeling "down, depressed", and because of his age, feared he would not find a job elsewhere.

"We didn't want it, but it's come so now we've just got to face it and see what the future holds.

"My income's gone," he added. "Obviously, we'll be working until we're told to leave."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Poundland was "part of the fabric of high streets and communities up and down the country".

He said the news of it going into administration just weeks before Christmas would be "deeply concerning for workers and their families".

He added: "While it is worrying, going into administration does give other potential buyers the opportunity to engage and we will work hard with all the relevant parties to ensure the best possible outcome."

Alix Partners, which has been appointed as administrator, said they would look at all options for the business, "including sales of the business and its assets, either in whole or part".

"We appreciate this is a deeply concerning time for all involved - customers, suppliers and, in particular, Poundland colleagues," they said.

Gordon Brothers has been criticised over how it handled a potential sale of Poundland, with accusations the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off the chain's 600 shops and stock piecemeal after running it into the ground.

Gordon Brothers, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied such claims.

On the funding question, Gordon Brothers said it had loaned the firm Â£85m over a year to help save it from insolvency.

But insiders critical of the US firm have said it stands to make its loans back and more from the insolvency process.

Previously, Gordon Brothers netted millions from liquidating the stock of fashion retailer LK Bennett, and in insolvency fees.

Labour MP Liam Byrne told the BBC the House of Commons' Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee will recall Gordon Brothers before Parliament - two weeks after Gordon Brothers representatives last appeared at the committee to answer questions about Poundland, and where MPs said they were "deeply concerned" about the business.

Byrne said: "I am really worried that a 'greed is good' approach to business by its owners has forced [Poundland] into an administration."

He added the committee wants to know "how much money they're ripping out and crucially, how do we make sure, as a country, that we don't have this kind of scenario unfold again".

News.title: Wife drugged and raped by husband asked police if she was to blame, mass sexual offence trial hears
News.content:
Warning: This article contains distressing content

A woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he's done this?", a court heard.

The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's right to anonymity, has admitted a litany of offences against her - including rape, administering a substance with intent and inviting 13 other men to join the abuse.

Nine of those men have pleaded not guilty to sexual offences against her and are standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court.

Giving evidence in court for the first time, the woman also said claims she had been "pretending to be asleep" during the abuse were a "load of rubbish".

The victim, in her 60s, was formally interviewed by Greater Manchester Police on 7 November last year, around two weeks after officers had arrived at her family home to arrest her husband.

In the interview, played to the jury, she told Det Con Anouska Barker: "I had no knowledge of what you told me had happened and I still can't believe it's true, and I think you have made a mistake."

News.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
News.content:
Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s, and its five members became global hearththrobs.

Their indelible hooks and airbrushed music videos found a natural home on the newly-launched MTV, giving their career a huge boost in the US.

They became so popular in the States that the press labeled them the leaders of a "Second British Invasion" of the charts - alongside groups like Spandau Ballet, Human League and Eurythmics.

During a hiatus in 1984, Andy and John Taylor enlisted Robert Palmer for their successful but short-lived side project the Power Station.

The following year, the guitarist decided to quit Duran Duran, after a miserable experience performing at Live Aid.

"We'd reached rock bottom and we had absolutely nothing to say to each other," he wrote in his autobiography, Wild Boy.

"We drove to the venue through streets packed with excited rock fans, but inside the bus the atmosphere was as if we were on a way to a funeral."

He went on to play on Robert Palmer's Addicted To Love, and released a solo album, Thunder, in 1987.

After a period writing and producing albums for other artists, he rejoined Duran Duran in 2000, lasting for just one album (2004's Astronaut) before parting ways again.

In 2022, when the band were inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Taylor was notably absent from the ceremony, despite public plans for a reunion.

When the group took the stage, singer Simon Le Bon read a letter from the guitarist, in which he revealed his diagnosis with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

Nonetheless, he contributed to the following year's Halloween-themed album Danse Macabre, marking his final collaboration with the band.

News.title: Gordon Ramsay to host Top Gear as show revived after Flintoff crash
News.content:
TV chef Gordon Ramsay is to lead the new presenting line-up on BBC motoring show Top Gear, which is being revived four years after it was last on air.

Ramsay will take the driving seat alongside as yet unnamed co-presenters when the show starts filming next year. It will return to screens in 2028.

The long-running programme has been off air since 2022, when co-host Andrew Flintoff suffered serious facial and rib injuries after his open-topped three-wheeled car overturned at the show's test-track.

In a statement announcing his new role, Ramsay said he wants to bring "a fresh energy and ambition" to the show's formula of being "surprising, entertaining and [with] just the right amount of chaos".

News.title: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
News.content:
Former England footballer Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended sentence after admitting dangerously driving his Lamborghini while inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon on a motorway.

The 31-year-old, from Berkshire, who later crashed into a metal gate during rush hour, gave no reaction as he was handed a 12-month jail term, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court.

Sterling had pleaded guilty to dangerous driving of a Lamborghini Urus and possessing nitrous oxide on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road on 28 May.

The judge said Sterling's use of the Class C drug had became a "maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period" in his career.

Sterling, who left the court without making any comment, was ordered to complete 100 hours unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He was arrested after crashing near the M3 in Hampshire.

News.title: Energy bills to rise by 26% from January after gas prices surge
News.content:
Energy bills will soar by 26% for millions of households in January after a surge in gas prices sparked by the Iran war.

A typical bill will increase by about Â£37 a month in the first three months of the new year, although the price will depend on how much energy a household uses, so it could be closer to Â£60 extra a month in winter.

A household using a typical amount of energy in England, Scotland and Wales and paying by direct debit, would see their annual bill rise from Â£1,723 to Â£2,166 if the increase was sustained for a year, said regulator Ofgem.

The government will pay millions of households Â£100 from 4 January to help cover winter costs on top of an existing VAT cut on electricity.

News.title: Hundreds complain about I'm A Celebrity after Mariella Frostrup called AJ Odudu 'aggressive'
News.content:
Frostrup replied that she thought being labelled "aggressive" was "a woman thing more than anything else".

"I think women who speak their mind and are forthright, that's 'aggressive', whereas a man who speaks his mind and is forthright is a 'strong man'," she said, but added that "I totally get that there's more" when race is involved.

Odudu responded: "I do definitely see your point and agree with it, but those words stick as well. Those words can stick for us. The moment passes for you and it doesn't pass for me."

"But hopefully it has?" Frostrup asked.

Odudu replied: "Well, I wasn't being aggressive, so it shouldn't have been there."

Signs of friction resurfaced when Frostrup told Odudu that "you don't take an apology well".

Odudu replied that "of course" she had accepted her apology, before Frostrup accepted that "it's really important to me to understand why it's triggering".

Odudu added: "It's good you asked, but it's a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women."

"Good to know," Frostrup concluded.

An ITV statement said: "The production monitors everyone in camp 24/7 and if at any time we feel someone has overstepped the line by using inappropriate language or displaying unacceptable behaviour, we would take steps to intervene and speak to everyone involved.

"The duty of care for our contestants is of the utmost importance to us. We take the welfare of the celebrities very seriously and have measures in place to ensure they are supported at every stage of the process: before, during and after filming."

News.title: Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show
News.content:
Donald Trump's investment portfolios have bought or sold shares in chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times this year, a review of the US president's financial disclosures shows.

Trump's most recent public declarations of his investment trading show that between January and September the portfolios purchased between $5.2m and $17m (Â£4m and Â£13m) in Nvidia stock - and sold between $4.4m and $12m. His portfolios held between $12.5m and $58m of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025.

Financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics report a low and high range of transaction values, so a more precise analysis of how much Nvidia stock was traded is not possible.

The period of recent turmoil at Nvidia and volatility in its share price is not covered by the disclosures. In the last two weeks, co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned and then Trump played a significant part in his reinstatement.

The White House has said that Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties and neither he nor his family "has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold".

News.title: MP calls for action after her likeness used for AI porn deepfakes
News.content:
A member of parliament whose name and image were used in AI content on porn sites said the issue could make women less likely to want to enter public life.

Mims Davies, the shadow Welsh Secretary, said she received an email in her parliamentary inbox which said "her likeness was found on forums in abusive and pornographic content".

The Conservative frontbencher said people making money from deepfakes was "grotesque", urging people to report it if it happens to them so that "culprits can be held to account".

"It's completely unacceptable, it's a violation and an outrage," she told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast.

Deepfakes are videos, pictures or audio clips made with artificial intelligence to look real.

It is illegal, external to share or threaten to share intimate photos or videos of someone without their consent, including through deepfake images.

Davies said she had waived her right to anonymity to call for more resources to find and prosecute culprits.

Ofcom, the communications regulator, said "significant action is being taken to tackle intimate image abuse" but added there was "more to do".

Davies, MP for East Grinstead and Uckfield in East Sussex, said: "There are things you expect to be dealing with these days in public life and frankly this is not it.

"This could be any woman. This could be anyone in politics, in business, or down in your high street.

"We need to be able to protect ourselves from deepfakes."

She added: "This is going to have an effect on our daily lives, on our lifestyles. We need an answer to this.

"There's a problem, a new frontier which we need to battle."

She previously told the BBC she was spiked on a night out in 2019.

News.title: EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme
News.content:
The UK could be included in the EU's proposed scheme to protect car manufacturing in Europe without Britain having to impose import taxes on Chinese electric cars, under draft plans.

The proposal has been drawn up by Ireland, which currently holds the EU's rotating presidency, and will be discussed by EU governments.

It comes after previous suggestions the EU would demand the UK align its tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles as a condition of joining the scheme.

Senior figures in the British government have been talking increasingly positively about the potential to join on terms London would be willing to sign up to, and are cautiously optimistic about this latest move.

The "Made in Europe" scheme, known formally as the Industrial Accelerator Act, aims to protect EU manufacturing with restrictions on goods from outside countries, with a particular focus on both China and the car industry.

The idea is potentially dangerous to the UK, as being outside the EU would mean being exposed to restrictions principally intended for others.

Germany and France had previously agreed a joint position under which UK involvement would have been conditional on matching EU import restrictions and tariffs on imports of Chinese electric cars and hybrids.

Alignment in this area with the EU would increase the price of increasingly popular Chinese cars in the UK, as well as raising the prospect of a potential Chinese retaliation with its own tariffs imposed on British-made cars.

News.title: Badenoch challenges Burnham over university fees for EU students
News.content:
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has challenged Andy Burnham over whether EU students in the UK could pay lower university tuition fees as part of his deal with the bloc.

The prime minister insisted the issue of tuition fees was "a separate deal", with discussions on this continuing.

Asked whether he could rule out EU students paying the same fees as British students, Burnham said this was "the European negotiating position" and "won't be put on the table".

At a UK-EU summit last Friday, the two sides agreed a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth travel scheme.

A joint statement said they would also work towards a "supplementing" agreement on tuition fees for EU students in the UK and British students in the EU, with negotiations concluding within six months.

EU sources had earlier suggested the bloc might hold up applying the wider deal until it was agreed that EU students who wanted to study in the UK would pay the same fees as British students.

But the UK has insisted the wider deal will come into force regardless of whether the two sides can reach an agreement on tuition fees.

News.title: Boy, 3, died after choking in nursery, inquest hears
News.content:
A three-year-old boy died after choking at a Greater Manchester nursery earlier this month, an inquest heard.

Thiago Wall died on 5 November after becoming critically ill at Cosy Toes Nursery, in Middleton, on 2 November.

An inquest at Rochdale Coroner's Court heard on Wednesday that Thiago had choked on a bowl of food and died three days later at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital. A CT scan later confirmed the toddler had suffered a brain injury.

The nursery - and three other nurseries owned by Cosy Toes LTD - remain closed.

The inquest heard the toddler had a hypoxic brain injury, which can be a result of decreased oxygen supply to the brain.

An investigation by Greater Manchester Police continues.

News.title: UK Town of Culture bid withdrawn in Strabane after it causes 'great division'
News.content:
A competition that is supposed to celebrate local towns has been rejected by a council after it caused "great division" over its UK title.

The mainly-nationalist town of Strabane in County Tyrone was shortlisted as one of 15 possible locations for the inaugural UK Town of Culture 2028, with the chance to win Â£3m.

However, the local council voted not to go ahead with the bid on Wednesday with one councillor claiming it "has the potential to be a disaster for Strabane - for community relations".

The motion, which was put forward by independent councillors, was backed by the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) and Sinn FÃ©in.

The council has to date spent around Â£40,000 on the bid.

A report prepared for councillors said that money had come from a Â£60,000 Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) grant, and would need to be repaid if the bid did not make it to the final submission stage.

The competition is run by the DCMS.

Independent Paul Gallagher, who had previously expressed concerns about the town's entry in the competition, said it had "caused great division in Strabane town".

He said there was widespread concerns about the competition's UK title.

"If it was to go forward it would create a major distrust in this council among the residents of Strabane," said Gallagher.

Strabane, he said, would become "a very uncomfortable place" if the bid was progressed, adding there was the potential for protests in the town.

News.title: Two men charged with trying to steal cufflinks and clock from royal home
News.content:
Two men charged with trespassing at the Prince and Princess of Wales's country home are accused of trying to steal cufflinks and a clock.

Police were called to Anmer Hall, on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, shortly before 18:00 GMT on Monday after reports of suspicious activity.

Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, both of no fixed address, have been charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site.

Both appeared at Norwich Magistrates' Court earlier and have been remanded in custody until a hearing on Monday. Prosecutors said a third suspect remained at large.

The men, who appeared in court in black sweatshirts, are accused of stealing six pairs of cufflinks and a clock.

Both spoke through an Albanian interpreter, but did not enter pleas.

The court heard one of the pairs of cufflinks were described as "the Duke of Edinburgh cufflinks".

News.title: Body found in search for missing 20-year-old woman
News.content:
A body has been found in the search for a missing 20-year-old woman in Dumfries and Galloway.

Formal identification has not yet taken place but the family of Kelsey Hunter has been informed. She was last seen in Castle Douglas at 17:00 on Saturday and a major search has been taking place in her nearby home village of Springholm.

Daniel McKnight, 21, appeared on Tuesday on petition in Dumfries Sheriff Court charged with murder and two other charges, including defeating the ends of justice.

He made no plea and was remanded in custody.

Police say the body was recovered at about 19:15 from a wooded area in Springholm.

A post mortem examination will take place.

Det Ch Insp Stephen McGrath, of Police Scotland's Major Investigation Team, said officers are supporting her "heartbroken" family as extensive inquiries continue.

He said: "A team of officers are continuing to work around the clock to get them answers.

"This is clearly a significant development and extensive work remains ongoing.

"We are building up a picture of Kelsey's movements in the days and weeks prior to her being reported missing, and I would like to thank everyone for their help so far."

He asked any of her friends who have not yet spoke to officers to contact police, external.

News.title: No 10 does not rule out inviting back influencer at centre of video row
News.content:
The spokesman was responding to a comment the influencer filmed after he had left the event on 9 November and posted in a YouTube video before the public criticism.

In it, Max Balegde said of the event the PM hosted, "well guys that was a huge success, Andy's invited me round for tea".

The PM's spokesman was unable to confirm whether that invite was legitimate or whether a further meeting would go ahead.

Downing Street also could not say whether Balegde had ever been paid taxpayer money to collaborate with the government on social media posts.

No influencers were paid to attend the Downing Street reception, the PM's spokesman added, but influencers have in the past been paid when working with other government departments.

About 60 content creators were invited to the Downing Street reception on 9 November, with videos from the event, including of Burnham DJing, subsequently emerging online.

In one video, Max Balegde, whose real name is Max Trobe, mouths the words "bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets", using audio from a meme that is trending online.

At Prime Minister's Questions, Badenoch said the words used were "so offensive that I will not repeat them in this House".

"Disgusting and pejorative comments about women's private parts, obscene language that referred to white women as cheap meat.

"This is grotesque. Labour MPs constantly tell us about their commitment to fighting violence against women and girls. Those MPs were silent yesterday, I won't be."

Burnham said the Tory leader was "right to call out that, because it was not acceptable" but he would "not apologise" for engaging with young people.

"She sneers at TikTokers, she sneers at influencers," he added, accusing Badenoch of "having nothing positive to say to the country" and of "constantly talking it down".

The two leaders continued the argument throughout their weekly Commons clash, with Burnham saying "it's true I have spoken to influencers, and then I have to come to this House, with the opposite of influencers".

Badenoch said the PM preferred to "take questions to people dancing around Downing Street", a reference to a video of another content creator dancing through Number 10 and down the stairs in an attempt to recreate a scene from the film Love, Actually.

This prompted Burnham to make a jibe about "lockdown parties" in Downing Street during the Covid pandemic.

Responding to the row about his now-deleted TikTok video in an Instagram post on Tuesday, Balegde said: "My content is always meant to be silly, fun, and light-hearted.

"If anybody was offended by that video, I sincerely apologise."

But he said "nobody was offended for weeks until revolting right-wing people tried to put this disgusting narrative on it".

"And if anybody then looks at the video and is offended, I get that. So hence why I took it down because I think that is disgusting."

News.title: Sporting v Man United LIVE: United winner disallowed by VAR in bonkers Champions League clash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first win as Manchester United manager against Sporting as his side saw a late winner disallowed by VAR in a bonkers Champions league clash in Lisbon.

Referee Szymon Marciniak was in the thick of the action throughout and in the 84th minute ruled that Patrick Dorgu had fouled Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, who let a corner from Bruno Fernandes slip through his fingers.

United had only just conceded a late equaliser themselves when goalkeeper Senne Lammens fumbled a high cross and allowed Sporting striker Luis Suarez to hook in his second of the night.

A freak Fernandes goal had looked to have given United a lucky win as the captain, playing against his former team, saw his long-range shot take a wicked deflection off a divot in the pitch to beat the stranded goalkeeper.

It was a second goal for Fernandes in the space of three minutes as he levelled from the penalty spot, after Lisandro Martinez was brought down in the box.

United had trailed after a chaotic first half where they conceded two penalties in the space of three minutes, with Lammens saving the first from Suarez before conceding another 75 seconds later, with Suarez scoring at the second attempt.

Pochettino’s side were also aggrieved when Amad Diallo saw an equaliser disallowed for a foul in the build up, with Youri Tielemans instead penalised. Tielemans was booked, and was then sent off in stoppage time for picking up his second yellow card.

News.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Taylor, the former Duran Duran guitarist, has died aged 65 "following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", the group has announced.

Taylor’s death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran’s website.

The musician rose to fame as a member of the award-winning 1980s rock group, renowned for tracks such as Hungry Like the Wolf and Rio.

In a statement, the band said: “Andy was there at the very beginning of our story.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.

“His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.

“It was great to make music with him again when the original five reunited in the early 2000s, and that time together, both on stage and in the studio, meant a tremendous amount to all of us. When we were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, Andy was too unwell to join us, but his words that night reminded everyone of his strength and the bond we shared.

“Andy faced his illness with remarkable courage, honesty and grace.

“Our thoughts are with his wife Tracey, his children Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew, and grandson Albie. They all loved him deeply and we ask that their privacy be respected at this very difficult time.”

open image in gallery Andy Taylor, left, was inducted in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022 ( AP Photo/Lo Sai-hung )

On the night he was inducted in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote.

“You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one’s own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

He is survived by his wife of more than 40 years Tracey Wilson, who praised him as “the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather”.

She said: “To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather.

open image in gallery Andy Taylor performing on stage at the Brit Awards in 2004 ( Yui Mok/Press Association )

“He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first.

“Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home.

Andy faced the last few years with so much courage and determination. He never gave up, fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life.

“The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful.

“Andy knew just how deeply he was loved, and we take great comfort in that. We will miss him every single day."

Lead singer Simon Le Bon said: “There’s a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart. It’ll never close up; I won’t let it. I will miss him & love him for all my days.”

The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the UK and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

News.title: Pacifica Pier collapses as massive waves wreak havoc in California
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Part of a pier in the Northern California city of Pacifica has collapsed as powerful waves batter the West Coast.

Video captured the moment a massive wave tore down a portion of the pier and slammed it into the ocean.

The pier, which is L-shaped and 1,140 feet (350 meters) long, had been closed by officials in the summer after cracks were found in the structure.

Officials warned that more beachfront homes in the area are at risk of flooding.

open image in gallery The Pacifica Pier on Wednesday before part of it collapsed into the sea ( AP Photo/Noah Berger )

Beachfront homes in Pacifica, which sits south of San Francisco, began flooding this week as king tides arrived in the area. King tides are the highest tides of the year.

North of San Francisco, officials in Marin County issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront properties in Stinson Beach.

They said large waves expected through the afternoon could send water and debris into roads and homes.

open image in gallery A wave crashes over a breakwater as high surf and tides impact Pacifica, Calif., on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026 ( AP Photo/Noah Berger )

The National Weather Service issued a coastal flood warning for the Pacific Coast and bay shorelines along San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay through 4 p.m. Wednesday.

It also issued a high surf warning in the Bay Area for Wednesday, when breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet (6 to 9 meters), about two to three stories high, could overpower swimmers and sweep people into the ocean.

open image in gallery A car in floodwaters on Nov. 25, 2026 in Pacifica, California ( Getty Images )

“Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal area,” the weather service said.

King tides occur when the gravitational pull of the moon and sun aligns to raise water levels.

Their effects this year are being amplified by the ongoing super El Niño, which has warmed the ocean and led to an increased volume of seawater.

open image in gallery November’s King Tides in the Bay Area are being amplified by El Niño conditions ( Getty )

High tides have already flooded several communities this week along California's coast.

In the Bay Area, some homes and streets flooded in the coastal Marin County cities of Mill Valley, Larkspur, Sausalito and Corte Madera.

Farther north, in Humboldt County near the Oregon border, the sheriff's office ordered evacuations in a small coastal community where most of the buildings flooded.

News.title: NBC turns to rerun after Macy’s postpones Thanksgiving Day parade for first time
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade has been postponed as a nor’easter barrels toward New York City.

The historic decision was made to cancel the 100-year Turkey Day tradition hours after crews filled the iconic balloons with helium in preparation for Thursday morning.

A source at NBC confirmed the postponement to The Independent and said that the network will, instead, air last year’s parade in all time zones tomorrow morning.

The parade has been rescheduled for Saturday morning, with festivities kicking off at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. The decision was made for the safety of the performers and spectators, The Independent was told.

open image in gallery Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade has been postponed for the first time in its 100-year history as a nor’easter barrels toward New York City ( AFP via Getty Images )

New York City is expected to be hit with rain, which can turn heavy at times, on Thursday. One to two inches of rain is possible, according to the National Weather Service.

The wind is also supposed to pick up to between 28 and 34 mph, causing a headache for parade operators if the show were to go on as scheduled.

“Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year,” Macy’s said in a statement shared by NBC News. “We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

The first Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was held in 1924, but back then it was called the Macy’s Christmas Parade. There were Macy’s employees dressed in costumes, a jazz band and even tigers. For the grand finale, Santa climbed the marquee of Macy’s flagship store on West 34th Street to unveil the store’s holiday window display.

The parade stretches 2.5 miles through the heart of Manhattan, starting near Central Park and ending at Macy’s Herald Square location.

open image in gallery The decision was made for the safety of the performers and spectators, The Independent was told ( Getty Images )

This year’s parade will mark the 100th year of the celebration. It was only canceled three times from 1942 to 1944 due to World War II, but has never been postponed due to weather — until now.

The New York Post, which was the first to report the postponement.

The beloved parade balloons have only once been grounded because of inclement weather in 1971, but the show continued with floats and other festivities.

Strong winds are taken seriously by parade operators following the infamous 1997 incident when the Cat in the Hat balloon crashed into a lamppost, critically injuring a spectator. Restrictions were subsequently put in place that grounded parade balloons when sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts reach 34 mph.

There have also been several instances when Macy’s lowered the height of its balloons because of the weather. In 2006, parade inflatables were flown lower to the ground because of an all-day downpour. The balloons were lowered again in 2019 due to gusty winds.

open image in gallery The parade has been rescheduled for Saturday morning, with festivities kicking off at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time ( AFP via Getty Images )

Macy’s plans to kick off its 100th parade with a record 100 inflatables depicting everyone’s favorite characters like the famed Snoopy balloon.

"Snoopy has always been my personal favorite," Jen Neal, the executive vice president of live events and specials at NBC and Peacock, said in a promotional article. "I grew up watching the Parade with my family, so there’s something about seeing Snoopy that immediately takes me back.

Crews will begin deflating this year’s balloons at 7 p.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday and then re-inflate them Friday to have them ready for the new parade day, according to WABC.

Ryan Parker contributed to this report.

News.title: Why was Man United’s late winner against Sporting disallowed?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Manchester United saw a late goal disallowed against Sporting after Patrick Dorgu was ruled to have fouled goalkeeper Kaique Pereira after he had punched the ball into his own net.

In an incident-packed Champions League clash, Mauricio Pochettino looked to have secured his first win as United manager when Pereira failed to hold onto a Bruno Fernandes corner.

But Szymon Marciniak, who was in the thick of the action throughout, was sent to the pitchside monitor by VAR and ruled that Dorgu had fouled Pereira when challenging for the cross.

Dorgu, Lisandro Martinez and Leny Yoro were all in close proximity as Pereira attempted to punch the cross, with the referee ruling that Dorgu had jumped into the goalkeeper.

Earlier this month, United saw a very similar goal stand when Senne Lammens challenged Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Dorgu scored to earn a 4-4 draw in the Premier League.

Marciniak, who officiated the 2022 World Cup final and is one of Europe’s top referees, had earlier disallowed a United equaliser when he blew up before Amad Diallo scored.

Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio in the build-up, but VAR could not check the decision because Marciniak had already stopped play before Diallo scored.

Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad.

Tielemans was also booked by Marciniak, and the midfielder was sent off in stoppage time for picking up his second yellow card of a crazy game.

It came after Pochettino saw his new defence concede two penalties in the space of three minutes in a shambolic first-half spell.

The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg.

If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left.

But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box.

Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row.

It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season.

Fernandes also scored a bizarre goal as his long-range shot took a fortuitous bobble off the Estádio José Alvalade pitch.

Moments after the United captain levelled against Sporting from the penalty spot, Fernandes saw his low strike beat goalkeeper Pereira after what appeared to be a deflection.

But the assist went to a divot in the pitch, as the low left-footed shot from Fernandes struck the turf and diverted away from the stranded goalkeeper Pereira to find the net.

The uneven pitch almost acted as a ramp as the ball suddenly jumped up and flew over Pereira, who was left with no chance.

It was perhaps the lucky break new United manager Pochettino needed after a chaotic first half where several decisions went against his team.

United conceded two penalties in the space of three minutes and had an equaliser from Diallo controversially disallowed by the referee Szymon Marciniak.

It also came after Leny Yoro was ruled to have been wrongly sent off in the eighth minute of United’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday in Pochettino’s first match.

United’s fortunes began to turn after half-time in Lisbon when Lisandro Martinez was fouled and Fernandes stepped up form the spot to equalise.

United captain Fernandes, who played 137 times for Sporting in three seasons in Lisbon, then tried his luck from distance but was rewarded with the deflection.

But goalkeeper Lammens then fumbled a high cross and allowed Sporting striker Luis Suarez to hook in his second of the night as a crazy game finished 2-2.

News.title: Every effort needed to save Northern Ireland Poundland jobs – Economy Minister
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Every effort must be made to project the jobs of Poundland staff in Northern Ireland, the Economy Minister has said, as they face the possibility of becoming unemployed before Christmas.

The discount retailer has fallen into administration after failing to secure a takeover deal, putting about 11,000 jobs in total at risk, including those of staff in 28 stores in Northern Ireland.

The chain, which runs roughly 600 stores, has held urgent talks over the past month to seek a buyer but has entered insolvency after failing to strike a deal before a key deadline late on Wednesday.

Economy Minister Dr Caoimhe Archibald said her department will “monitor the situation closely” and ensure support is available for workers in Northern Ireland should they be affected.

open image in gallery Economy Minister Caoimhe Archibald said every effort must be made to project the jobs of Poundland staff in Northern Ireland (Liam McBurney/PA) ( PA Archive )

“The news that Poundland has entered administration will understandably cause huge concern for the workers impacted and their families,” she said.

“The immediate priority must be protecting as many jobs and stores as possible, and I would encourage all parties involved in the administration process to work towards that objective.

“Where employees are impacted, it is vital that they are treated fairly and with respect, and that the proper redundancy processes are followed, with workers receiving everything to which they are entitled.”

AlixPartners confirmed that experts from the corporate finance firm have been hired as administrators for Poundland.

The retailer will continue to trade from its stores as the administrators seek a sale of the retailer and its assets, such as stores.

Retail NI chief executive Glyn Roberts said the closures will impact Northern Ireland beyond the stores themselves.

Mr Roberts said: “With the likely closure of all 28 Poundland stores across Northern Ireland now a sad reality, our immediate concern must be for the staff and their families who face the prospect of losing their jobs so close to Christmas.

“The impact will extend far beyond the loss of these stores. The reduction in footfall from these closures will also have serious consequences for surrounding traders and businesses on our local high streets, an impact that must not be overlooked.

“This is undoubtedly another significant blow to our high streets at a time when local businesses are already facing considerable challenges.”

open image in gallery Retail NI chief executive Glyn Roberts said the closures will impact Northern Ireland beyond the stores themselves (Liam McBurney/PA) ( PA Archive )

Gordon Brothers bought the business for £1 early last year before overseeing a major overhaul, which included shutting more than 100 shops, including 11 in Northern Ireland.

Poundland’s ownership had received a number of offers, including from Irish real estate firm Martin Property Group, investment firm Xyra Holdings and German investment firm Zachert Private Equity, but failed to secure a deal.

Administrators said the sale talks failed to “identify a viable solvent solution” for Poundland as a whole.

It is likely the group will be broken up, with retailers such as Tesco and B&M already having expressed interest in buying parts of the company, including stores.

A spokeswoman for the administrators said: “We appreciate this is a deeply concerning time for all involved: customers, suppliers and, in particular, Poundland colleagues.

“Our priority now is to work with all stakeholders, including representatives from Government and Usdaw, as we identify the best possible route forward.”

News.title: Mick Harford: ‘My prostate cancer diagnosis was a shock. As a footballer, I’d felt bulletproof’
News.content:
However, an MRI scan and a PSMA PET scan at UCLH, where I had been referred, showed only a little bit of growth on my prostate, and I was told I would be fine. But, while I was symptomless at the time, within around eight months I was getting up three or four times in the night to go to the toilet, and then feeling the urge to go back again only two minutes later. I instinctively knew something was wrong.

Upon my return to UCLH in December, I was told my PSA was now “very high”, at around 48 ng/mL – far more elevated than the 4.5 ng/mL considered healthy for my age group. Advanced prostate cancer was then confirmed with a biopsy. The first person I told was my son, William, in a phone call from the car at the hospital. It was horrible – it was not just me who would suffer, but my family too. I also needed to tell Luton Town, who were amazing and gave me as much time off work as I needed from my role as assistant manager.

Facing the opponent

My brilliant oncology team immediately had a plan for me. They got me on a course of hormone therapy medications called Enzalutamide and Zoladex, in preparation for me to begin radiation treatment from mid-August. I had 49 sessions over the space of about eight weeks, and it was daunting each time I travelled into London on the train from my home in Harpenden to go underground to the hospital’s Radiotherapy Department.

But I got through it, even with a bit of collateral damage. While my ongoing symptoms are not a pleasant conversation, it’s an important one, because it has affected my life in so many ways. My sleep is disrupted because I still need to get up multiple times during the night to go to the toilet so I can avoid an accident in bed. I also have to wear a nappy every day in case of leakage, and need to be careful when I’m out to ensure I’m close to a toilet.

I’m still on a hormone therapy called Triptorelin to block my testosterone, which feeds the cancer, and takes the form of an injection every six months. As a result, I’m going through the “male menopause”, which is not very nice and can cause tiredness, sleep issues and brain fog. It has given me lots of sympathy for women of my generation.

However, as I approach six years since my diagnosis, I’ve tried to stay proactive as much as possible. The discipline and drive instilled in me as a footballer have come in handy. To be a successful player, you need to stick to a routine. In the same way that I worked hard to ensure my teammates and coaches respected me on the pitch, so I’ve adhered to what all the doctors have advised – including trying to be diligent in terms of lifestyle.

News.title: Underperforming Manchester City are an accident waiting to happen
News.content:
Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

Maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

News.title: Arsenal get the best and worst of Gyokeres on frustrating night for Arteta
News.content:
Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

News.title: Emery unhappy with ‘unfair’ referee but Aston Villa are toothless
News.content:
Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Anthropic falls below stock market listing price
News.content:
Anthropic’s shares dropped below their initial public offering price for the first time, sealing a dramatic reversal of fortunes for the AI giant following its blockbuster stock market debut last week.

The Claude chatbot maker saw its shares fall more than 8pc from their $83 offer price to stand at around $76 as investors appeared to grow sceptical of its valuation.

The slide on the Nasdaq exchange was set to wipe over $200bn from the company’s market value.

Anthropic raised more than $81bn in the biggest IPO on record, with its valuation surging to $2tn as the shares peaked at around $115.

But the company bucked Monday’s huge rally following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia with the shares slipping from Friday’s close.

Wall Street resumed its slide on Tuesday as underlying fears over the AI trade appear to have outweighed the impact of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as chief executive.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 was down as much as 3pc, with the benchmark S&P 500 around 1.2 pc lower.

In London, the FTSE 100 closed slightly lower, down 0.1pc, unable to sustain gains made in global markets on Monday.

The ability of AI companies to generate sufficient returns on their massive investment has proved more important than Nvidia’s boardroom drama, according to Goldman Sachs analysts.

Sharon Bell told Bloomberg: “The AI trade really depends on whether companies can make a return on the capex they spend.

“If the answer is yes, then the tech sector should do well over time and if the answer is no, it won’t do so well.”

Ms Bell argued that the management changes at Nvidia would not “make a huge difference either way”.

Glenn Yin at online trading platform ACCM told the Reuters Global Markets Forum: “By the end of ​the day, these businesses need to make enough money to justify investors’ expectations.

“‌My point is: Jensen’s return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion.”

Major chipmakers saw their stocks sink on Tuesday as general AI-related optimism faded.

Nvidia, the world’s largest chipmaker, saw its stock fall more than 7pc, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index, which tracks the major US manufacturers of chips, fell 8pc.

Microchip maker AMD’s share price was down as much as 10pc, while shares in Broadcom were down around 3pc.

The dollar eased back from its highest level in almost two years after Jensen ​Huang’s return to Nvidia revived the AI rally and fuelled expectations of more interest rate rises.

The President’s intervention, however, is a “slippery slope”, according to a top Republican senator.

Dave McCormick, the former boss of hedge fund Bridgewater, told Bloomberg: “I am worried about the precedent of the executive branch getting involved in real ownership deals with companies but also in board governance and making these decisions.

“This is a precedent that I don’t think we want to replicate or reinforce.”

Mr McCormick will be one of the politicians grilling the Nvidia boss next week when he testifies before the Senate Banking Committee.

Todd Blanche, the US Attorney General, has labelled Nvidia “a good corporate citizen” despite questions over whether Jensen Huang’s alleged affair could have threatened national security.

Mr Blanche added that if Nvidia was the target of a criminal investigation, “that wouldn’t be the message”.

News.title: Meningitis outbreak triggers epidemic alert in Gaza
News.content:
Cases of meningitis have risen dramatically in Gaza and have triggered an epidemic alert, the territory’s health ministry has said.

At least 272 cases were recorded across the enclave in October, more than eight times the usual monthly rate of 30 to 50 cases, Dr Nidal Ghoneim, a senior health ministry official, told a press conference on Tuesday.

Children under one year old account for 71 per cent of cases, with newborns alone accounting for 13 per cent, World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said in a separate briefing.

Dr Ghoneim added that 15 Palestinians had died of meningitis since the start of the year, and that the spread of the disease through the strip threatened the lives of thousands of people, mostly children.

It is thought that most cases are being driven by enterovirus – the leading cause of viral meningitis – which is shed through faeces and can spread rapidly between people in unsanitary environments.

All six wastewater treatment plants in Gaza are currently out of operation, meaning an estimated 150,000 cubic metres of untreated sewage flows into the environment every day, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

News.title: Trapped Ebola health workers rescued after three days of fighting in Congo
News.content:
Ebola health workers have been rescued after being trapped by fighting for more than three days, in clashes further hampering efforts to curb the virus in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, head of the World Health Organization, said staff had been evacuated from a hospital in Akwe, Ituri province, “under very challenging circumstances”.

The health chief had earlier pleaded for peace, and warned staff had “been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward of the facility for over 24 hours”.

Staff were caught in a crossfire between the Congolese army, and the People’s Revolutionary Convention (CRP) group led by former International Criminal Court (ICC) convict, Thomas Lubanga, French RFI radio reported.

Local media reported heavy clashes between the army and the CRP in Ituri in recent days. At least 10 people were killed and a stream of refugees fled to the provincial capital, Bunia.

As security worsened, the WHO said it had relocated health teams from Mongbwalu.

News.title: Welsh slogger blasts England to crushing win over Australia
News.content:
It will take more than a few lusty blows to become the cricketing Don in these parts, but an extraordinary display of six-hitting from Aneurin Donald, ably supported by Phil Salt, helped England and Wales to a stunning eight-wicket victory over Australia.

Donald and Salt, the Welsh-born opening pair, put on 151 to help chase down Australia’s 184 with 41 balls to spare. David Gower famously flew a pre-war Tiger Moth between the floodlights, about 200 feet above the ground, on England’s only previous visit to this ground in 1991. It was a good thing he was doing no such thing tonight, with balls flying everywhere off Donald’s blade. He hit nine sixes, one shy of Salt’s England T20 record, in his 85 from 32 balls, before being caught on the fence with the game as good as won.

Donald, who turns 30 next month, has taken the slow road to the big stage. As a teenager, he smashed 234 off 136 balls for Glamorgan against Derbyshire in the County Championship at Colwyn Bay, but at 21 left for Hampshire. Two serious ACL injuries derailed his career, and he moved to Derbyshire in 2023, where he has turned into a formidable T20 opener.

“I am pretty decent at slogging and not too good at batting, so I will keep swinging as hard as I can,” he reflected afterwards. “Luckily there might be a career in it now, not a few years ago.”

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes talks up Sporting return as Man Utd prepare to face his former team
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes talks up Sporting return as Man Utd prepare to face his former team

Bruno Fernandes left Sporting Lisbon to join Manchester United but has talked up a return to the Portuguese capital, underlining how happy he was

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes has spoken candidly about a move back to Portugal

Bruno Fernandes has opened the door to a Sporting Lisbon return as the Manchester United talisman admitted: "I was happy here and I’d like to be again."

‌



‌



The Portguese star spent two and a half years playing for Sporting before his performances prompted the Red Devils to spend £67million to sign him in January 2020. He's gone on to become the most successful signing of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era.

‌



He recently shelved contract talks and has been heavily linked with a move away in the past. A return to his homeland and the city where he once played is clearly something that appeals.

‌



Whilst on Sporting's books Fernandes scored 64 times in 137 appearances and was named the best player in Portugal in back-to-back seasons. The 32-year-old also insists there were aspects that exceeded football that made him happy in Lisbon.

Fernandes said on the prospect of returning: “The time I spent here makes me think I’d like to come back. There are many things beyond football. If that possibility arises one day, why not? I was happy here and I’d like to be again.”

The playmaker quickly became the main man at Old Trafford after arriving, inspiring them to third and second place finishes in successive seasons. He was just named the PFA Player of the Year and has, for so long, been a rare bright light despite the team's struggles.
