Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes’ private thoughts on Michael Carrick sacking after chat with ex-Man Utd teammate
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes’ private thoughts on Michael Carrick sacking after chat with ex-Man Utd teammate

Bruno Fernandes spoke his mind behind closed doors when Manchester United replaced Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes made his feelings clear over the international break. (Image: Sportsphoto/Allstar, Getty Images)

Rasmus Hojlund has claimed that Bruno Fernandes was left heartbroken by Michael Carrick's dismissal.

The Napoli striker, who departed Old Trafford for the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium during the summer in a transfer valued at £44m, caught up with the Manchester United captain throughout the November international break, when Portugal welcomed Denmark for the penultimate match of the UEFA Nations League group stage phase.

While they were on duty for their national sides, the Reds dismissed Carrick. The next day, mere hours before Hojlund and Fernandes faced each other at the Braga Municipal Stadium, United revealed the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds captain praised the arrival of the Argentine after domestic football resumed, characterising him as someone who delivers 'very good energy' to the squad, while also being 'very strong' and 'strict'.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

During an interview with The Independent, the former United striker disclosed what Fernandes had privately expressed about the managerial change before making public comments.

Hojlund said: "In the international break, when I spoke with Bruno and Diogo, they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going, but also looking forward to some change.

"I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu, his Denmark teammate] and I just wish the guys all the best and I am sure they will turn it around this season."

View 2 Images Rasmus Hojlund said, "There's only one club in Manchester," after scoring against City on Tuesday night. (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

United have managed just a solitary Premier League victory, stretching back to August when they overcame Ipswich Town, and find themselves embroiled in what is shaping up to be a desperate fight against the drop.

Despite an absolutely dreadful start to the campaign, Hojlund has backed his former side to embrace the challenge of turning their fortunes around. The Dane, who netted only 26 goals in 95 appearances across two seasons at Old Trafford, said: "United is a massive club and you can't take anything away from that.

"There are so many people following the club around the world and you can't really escape from it, it is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad, so it is all about trying to be in that middle and now I think I tried both the highs and the lows there. The pressure is part of the club. It comes with playing for Man United."

Hojlund, who was back in Manchester this week for Napoli's 2-2 draw to Enzo Maresca's side in the Champions League, grew up as a United supporter and continues to follow their results closely.

"I am watching all the games I can," added the 23-year-old. "Especially from the red side of Manchester. It is unfortunate [that United are struggling]."

United currently sit second from bottom in the Premier League, yet Hojlund insists they possess far too much quality to suffer relegation. He said: "It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top.

"The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth were in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.

"They have got a lot of quality. I have seen the guys training day by day and I know the players really well and they have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals, so I am sure they will turn it around. Hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio."

Sports.title: Blame Beyonce, NFL, AJ and Spurs - why Saudi-backed Newcastle need even more cash
Sports.content:
News that PIF, Newcastle United's majority shareholders, are looking to sell up to 25 per cent of the club through the issuing of new shares will naturally ring alarm bells with the club's supporters.

After all, from the moment the Saudi Public Investment Fund completed its takeover of the club, alongside the Reuben family and Amanda Staveley, their long-term commitment to the Newcastle United project has been questioned - certainly from the outside.

That has been accentuated this year with Newcastle's results on the pitch regressing and prompting accusations of the Newcastle project stagnating, as well as PIF's decision to pull the plug on funding for the LIV Golf tour.

Indeed, just this month, Chronicle Live reported on comments made by Professor Simon Chadwick, an expert in Afro-Eurasian sport, questioned their long term ambitions for the Magpies.

‌



"Newcastle United fans don't like me, because I posted this before and they've told me - I fail to see what coherence and investment in Newcastle United has with wider Saudi Arabian sporting strategy.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

"What is clear and what we've all got to learn from what has happened over the last year, two years, is if the Saudi Arabians think, well, you know, we're not making any money out of this, it's too disruptive, it's impacting upon perceptions of us, they will withdraw."

But PIF governor, and Newcastle United chairman, Yasir Al-Rumayyan's presence at the annual Matfen Hall summit provided some reassurance that they remain fully invested in the project. PIF chief Jacobo Solis has been a consistent presence around the club since - both in La Manga in the summer and at the training ground last month - and that was backed up by Al-Rumayyan's appearance at St James' Park.

‌



And it is St James' Park, or more namely, the decision over whether to remain there or move to a new stadium, where this decision for PIF to sell shares in the club centres on, rather than their interest dwindling, clarifies Chronicle Live.

Instead, a reduction in their holding of the club isn't an admission that the club is for sale or they have lost ambition, rather a statement of ambition as they look towards fresh investment to accelerate that key stadium decision.

Sources close to the club say that a minority investor is being sought to help fund some of their major infrastructure projects. Chronicle Live understands that the club are attempting to create liquidity to invest and the issuing of new shares is deemed one way of funding it, although that is just one potential option.

View 3 Images Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Chairman of Newcastle United, at a game (Image: Getty)

‌



The decision to sell up to 25 per cent of the club through the issuing of shares will not see any money paid to PIF, who currently own around 84 per cent of the club. The money would be injected straight into the club and in exchange for providing that cash, any new investor would receive a stake in the club.

It is no secret PIF have been looking for investors to help finance the stadium project and it has never been the expectation they would entirely finance the redevelopment of St James' Park or build a state of the art new stadium at Leazes Park, which would cost more than £1.3billion.

Fresh investment would help finance that project which would allow the club to make a tangible step in reducing the commercial revenue gap between themselves and the 'big six'.

It was earlier this year that football finance expert Kieran Maguire told Chronicle Live that the only way Newcastle can realistically bridge that gap is by building a new stadium that increases their commercial revenue streams.

‌



After Sandro Tonali swapped Newcastle for Tottenham in July, Maguire said: "Blame Beyonce and Coldplay," Maguire joked. "Blame NFL, Anthony Joshua. That's the reason why (Spurs can spend over £200million already this summer despite narrowly avoiding relegation last season).

"Newcastle United, are £100million behind Arsenal, they're £100million behind Manchester United, they're £70million behind Spurs, they're £60million behind Liverpool, when it comes to ticket sales.

"So, St James' Park, again, as an away fan, everybody loves a trip to Newcastle. It's in the centre of town, everybody's so friendly, it's a proper footballing city. All of these positives don't turn into cash for the club.

View 3 Images Newcastle are considering building a new stadium adjacent to St James' Park (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"Spurs are very good at what they do. And what they are very good at doing is being an entertainment complex. That's how I'd describe them. Whereas Newcastle United is a football club.

"Tottenham made, on average, £83 per fan per seat and that compares to Newcastle at £49 according to the 2024/25 figures. Spurs also have 30 non-football events a year at full capacity.

"As a result of that, their commercial income has gone through the roof. They made £277million from commercial income. That compares to £123million Newcastle netted. So there's £140 million [gap]. You've got £70million more in matchday income. You put those two together, and that's £200million."

‌



"As a result of that, their commercial income has gone through the roof. They made £277million from commercial income. That compares to £123million Newcastle netted. So there's £140 million [gap]. You've got £70million more in matchday income. You put those two together, and that's £200million."

And now that PIF's desire to sell those shares is in the public domain and JP Morgan have been appointed as advisors and the process to find that investment is under way, it suggests progress on the stadium decision will be accelerated. And that is the key conclusion to draw from this decision, which should put a pin in any doubts over the owners' long term commitment to the club.

Sports.title: Wesley Fofana accidentally exposed the rotten culture problem at Chelsea - they must sack him
Sports.content:
Wesley Fofana accidentally exposed the rotten culture problem at Chelsea - they must sack him

OPINION: Chelsea must be ruthless and sack Wesley Fofana - because his mentality is poison for a young, fragile dressing room

View 3 Images Wesley Fofana epitomises everything that's wrong with Chelsea in 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

There's no shame whatsoever in hating your job and staying put strictly for the money. In fact, it's practically the load-bearing wall of the British economy.

‌



‌



Every weekday morning, millions of us drag ourselves onto damp commuter trains, stare blankly at spreadsheets, nod thoughtfully on Teams calls, and quietly pray for Friday afternoon.

‌



Premier League football, however, is supposed to be different. When you're living out a fantasy the majority of us would kill for, giving a toss isn't optional. And even if you are a stone-cold mercenary, could you at least have the decency to, you know, pretend not to be?

‌



Enter Wesley Fofana, who seems to be trying his darnedest to become Chelsea's most regrettable transfer blunder of all time - which, given the depth of competition at Stamford Bridge, is really saying something.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Raheem Sterling avoids jail after crashing his Lamborghini while inhaling laughing gas READ MORE :

Alejandro Garnacho takes Aston Villa action with Chelsea transfer now in the balance READ MORE :

In an interview that must have had the club's communications department reaching for the gin before noon, the 25-year-old defender confessed that during Enzo Maresca's reign - having already endured cruciate ligament and meniscus nightmares, followed by two consecutive hamstring strains - he genuinely decided to pack it all in. "That's it, I'm retiring, I'm done playing," he recalled thinking. "I was serious."

‌



Fair enough. Elite sport is brutal, and watching your own legs repeatedly betray you would break even the toughest of characters. So Fofana summoned his agents for a crisis meeting. And here, dear reader, is where the tragedy veers sharply into farce.

Rather than rallying their client with stirring speeches about glory, silverware, or the proud traditions of Stamford Bridge, Fofana's representatives reached straight for the calculator.

‌



"They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that," Fofana recounted cheerfully. "'It's simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there's a lot of money to be made. Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you're injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.'"

View 3 Images Fofana's interview took place unbeknownst to Chelsea (Image: Zack Nani / Youtube)

‌



You have to admire the sheer, brass-necked clarity of it. Come in every day. Keep smiling. Cash the cheques. It's the corporate philosophy of 'quiet quitting,' except instead of nicking highlighter pens from the stationery cupboard, the Frenchman is pocketing £220,000 every single week... until 2029.

Indeed, Fofana's deal is a magnificent archaeological relic from the wild, giddy summer of 2022, just before BlueCo's spreadsheet-wielding overlords pivoted to heavily incentivised, performance-related contracts. He's the last dinosaur stomping happily around a freshly landscaped theme park, munching on the most expensive foliage while everyone else has to earn their supper.

‌



The problem isn't that he wants his money. The problem is that he has just announced, in glorious high definition, that he is emotionally clocked out - and he seems to find the whole thing rather amusing.

Consider, for example, another gem from the same chat, in which Fofana laughed off a missed penalty against Liverpool last month, and declared that he "couldn't care less" about it. Stop and savour that for a second. Missing a decisive spot-kick against one of Chelsea's most bitterly loathed rivals, and the response is a shrug and a giggle. It's one thing to be privately disillusioned with your body and your profession - it's quite another to broadcast to a paying fanbase that you are essentially rinsing the club while treating its biggest fixtures like a kickabout in the park.

‌



And that is why Fofana has become something much more troubling than an unfortunate, injury-ravaged signing. He has become the rotten core at the centre of Chelsea's great, gleaming, scatter-brained malaise.

View 3 Images Chelsea must be ruthless when it comes to 'poisonous' players like Fofana (Image: Eddie Keogh/Getty Images)

‌



Cast your mind back to 2023, when Frank Lampard returned for his brief, haunted spell as interim manager and looked like a man who had just wandered into an abandoned fair ground. Lampard warned, as politely as his blood pressure allowed, that the atmosphere at Chelsea was broken - that standards had evaporated, that too many players simply weren't pulling their weight or caring enough about whether the club actually won anything. Three years on, those words read less like a failed caretaker's sour grapes and more like a medical diagnosis.

Watch Chelsea today and you see a team that is perpetually on the verge of a nervous breakdown: flimsy, inconsistent, allergic to resilience, and liable to fold like a cheap deckchair at the first hint of adversity. Then compare it to the concrete-and-barbed-wire Chelsea of the Roman Abramovich and Jose Mourinho years. Can you imagine John Terry, Didier Drogba, or Lampard himself giggling about a miss against Liverpool? Can you imagine what Terry would have done if a team-mate had breezed into the dressing room announcing he was only there because his agent told him to keep picking up his pay packet? There would have been a small, localised weather event in the boot room.

‌



Those teams were built on lions - men who treated second place like a personal bereavement, let alone fourth, sixth, or 10th. You cannot build that kind of ruthless, suffocating winning culture when one of your highest-paid senior figures is openly treating the club like a very generous pension fund.

At this point, whether you think Fofana is a Rolls-Royce defender trapped in a porcelain body or a walking defensive liability is entirely beside the point. His mentality is contagious, and in a young, fragile dressing room desperate for leadership, it's pure poison.

‌



Chelsea need to stop being polite and start being ruthless. If nobody will take him off their hands, buy out his contract, hand him his golden parachute, and wish him a long, smiling retirement somewhere far away from west London.

Cutting Wesley Fofana loose won't magically cure everything that ails this club overnight. But you cannot rebuild a fortress while someone is sitting in the middle of the courtyard laughing at the cracks in the walls.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres sends clear message to Mikel Arteta over Arsenal future
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres has insisted he is fully committed to Arsenal - and warned they will take their goal frustrations out on someone.

Incredibly, Arsenal have won eight games by a one goal margin this season which has helped them go six points clear at the top of the Premier League. But it seems that the familiar 1-0 to the Arsenal scoreline is no longer enough because they have been pegged back in their last two games and been wasteful with their finishing.

Arsenal had a staggering 30 shots against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League but only four were on target and they were held to a draw by the Bundesliga leaders.

Gyokeres says that sooner rather than later there will be a goal rush - and it could be against Manchester City on Sunday. They were also pegged back after going in front in their previous game at Newcastle.

‌



Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

The Gunners striker said: “Yeah, in one way it is a bit frustrating after a game when we don’t win, of course. But, overall, I think the way we attacked - and the amount of chances we have created - it is just a matter of time until there are going to be a lot of goals.

“We always go into games wanting to win. I think, overall, we have done really well this season. Obviously, we have drawn two games that we could have won, with the amount of chances that we had in both games.

“But Sunday is another game and we are going to prepare for that one, and we are going to go for it.

‌



“I have been feeling good in the last couple of games. Obviously, we should have probably won against Dortmund with the amount of chances. But overall, I think we played really well and that was good, at least.”

Gyokeres has started just one Premier League game this season but there was a reminder of his quality with his wonder strike against Borussia Dortmund. Despite limited opportunities, the Arsenal striker insists he is not thinking about January or the club being linked to other forwards and the impact that could have on him.

Instead, Gyokeres insisted he is happy and will seize his chance when it comes.

View 2 Images Gyokeres was on the scoresheet against Borussia Dortmund

‌



"For me, I always focus on the games,” he said. “I want to do well when I get a chance to play. That is my main goal. I really enjoy being here and playing here. That’s always my aim.

“When I get to play, I just try to do my best and that is going to be the case going forward as well. I prepare myself and I am ready.”

Gyokeres says Arsenal are determined to win back-to-back titles with Mikel Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the Premier League.

That would show how strong they are but they have been struggling to put games to bed after throwing away leads in their last two games against Dortmund and Newcastle.

‌



Gyokeres added: “Of course, we always want to win titles and we know how tough it is in the Premier League with the games and the teams.

“It is always going to be tough. But we have an amazing squad, amazing players, so that’s the aim. We push each other every day to achieve that and we are definitely going to go for it.”

Sports.title: John Motson added to EAFC 27 game through AI as tribute to legendary commentator
Sports.content:
John Motson added to EAFC 27 game through AI as tribute to legendary commentator

Football commentary legend John Motson, who was the voice of FIFA games for three decades, will return to the franchise through the use of AI and old voice recordings

View 2 Images John Motson's voice will return to the EAFC franchise (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

John Motson, the iconic football commentator who died in 2023, will return to the EAFC 27 video game franchise through the assistance of AI and previous voice recordings, it has emerged.

‌



‌



EA Sports, the game's developer, have confirmed that the move to bring back Motson, who passed away at the age of 77, as a "digital tribute" has been worked on with the blessing of Motson's family.

‌



Motson is widely viewed as one of the greatest commentators of all time, having worked for the BBC for over 50 years. As well as covering 10 World Cups, 10 European Championships and 29 FA Cup finals, Motson was also the voice of the FIFA franchise - which was rebranded to EAFC in 2023 - for 30 years.

‌



Motson's son, Fred, has expressed gratitude on behalf of he and his family for the work done to bring Motson's iconic voice to a new generation of fans.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

“My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,” he said in a statement.

‌



“His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.”

View 2 Images The iconic Motson passed away in 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



EA Sports added: “We’re honoured to bring back the iconic voice of John Motson, the legendary English football commentator and unmistakable voice of a decade of EA SPORTS™ football titles from 1996-2006.

“Motson became the voice of football, covering more than 2,500 matches and 20 international tournaments during his 50 years with the BBC. His exceptional broadcasting career was recognised with a BAFTA Special Award at the British Academy Television Awards in 2018.

Article continues below

“With the blessing and partnership of Motson’s family, EA SPORTS FC™ have worked with extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game’s greatest voices, inspiring a whole new generation of football fans.”

Sports.title: Newcastle owners PIF 'start process to sell part of club' as £5billion plan hatched
Sports.content:
Newcastle owners PIF 'start process to sell part of club' as £5billion plan hatched

Newcastle United's majority owners have started the process of selling part of the club via newly issued shares

View 2 Images Newcastle United's majority owners are looking for investment (Image: Getty)

Newcastle United's majority owner, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, is looking to sell up to 25 per cent of the club. PIF is working with JPMorgan to sell newly issued shares to attract outside investment.

‌



‌



The sovereign wealth fund currently holds an 85 per cent majority stake in the Magpies. The other 15 per cent is owned by the Reuben Family.

‌



Rather than cashing out, this new plan to dilute the PIF's holding and issue new shares directly injects capital into the club and could be earmarked to fund major infrastructure projects. Rumours suggest this may involve a new stadium or upgrades to the training ground.

‌



PIF manages roughly $900billion (£688bn) in assets and according to reports, the internal view if a minority financial partner can be found is that Newcastle could eventually be worth a whopping £5billion.

Bruno Guimaraes opens up on Arsenal frustration after being booed on Newcastle return READ MORE :

How Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle tried to convince Bruno Guimaraes to snub Arsenal READ MORE :

The fund's involvement with Newcastle began in 2021 when PIF completed a £305m takeover, ending Mike Ashley's 14-year tenure as owner.

View 2 Images Yasir Al-Rumayyan is the PIF governor and chairman of Newcastle (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The initial ownership split was among three, with PIF holding 80 per cent, PCP Capital Partners, led by British financier Amanda Staveley and her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, holding 10 per cent and RB Sports and Media, the Reuben brothers, holding 10 per cent.

‌



Hundreds of millions of pounds were injected into the club by PIF and the Reuben family, but Staveley and PCP Capital's stake was slowly diluted as they did not match these injections.

Eventually, in 2024, Staveley and Ghodoussi stepped down from the board and sold their remaining six per cent stake to PIF and RB Sports.

‌



This valued the club at £1bn, with The Athletic reporting on the hopeful £5bn valuation in years to come.

Speaking this month regarding some big future projects at St James' Park, including the prospect of a new stadium, Newcastle CEO David Hopkinson said: "Whatever we do here, it's a generational decision which will define the next era of the club. It's going to be expensive.

‌



"When I arrived, we were in the concept. We're advancing significantly into more clearly defined options and the how-to-do-this stage. It's a project of global significance.

Article continues below

"We've spent a lot of time with bankers from New York recently thinking through how we might do this and what options we can consider.

"I can assure you we're working on this every day and I hope we will have something concrete to share with you soon."

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho takes Aston Villa action with Chelsea transfer now in the balance
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho takes Aston Villa action with Chelsea transfer now in the balance

Alejandro Garnacho was expected to complete a permanent move to Aston Villa after signing on a conditional loan from Chelsea in the summer - but that now feels less certain

View Image Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa future is now in doubt (Image: David Ramos/UEFA)

Alejandro Garnacho has removed all references to Aston Villa from his Instagram account after being omitted from their Champions League match with Galatasaray.

‌



Garnacho, 22, was absent on Tuesday night as Villa went down 1-0 in Istanbul with Unai Emery choosing to name just 11 substitutes rather than 12, including two back-up goalkeepers. The decision comes at a time where Garnacho's long-term future looks increasingly uncertain despite only moving to Villa Park from Chelsea in the summer on a loan deal which was designed to then become permanent.

‌



The Argentina international has yet to start a game for Villa, making seven appearances from the bench this season.

‌



Asked about his absence, Emery fuelled what seems to be becoming a difficult situation for all parties by saying: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

On Wednesday it emerged that Garnacho had removed references to Aston Villa from his Instagram account, with a post of his FA Cup triumph with Manchester United pinned.

‌



Though the deal agreed for Garnacho included a permanent option triggered by appearances, plus a four-year contract already agreed by both parties, Emery's comments and Garnacho's response will only fuel talk doubts over the winger making Villa Park his new long-term home.

If that does prove to be the case then another summer of uncertainty may lie ahead for Garnacho, who only joined from United back in September 2025.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The Blues parted with £40million to sign the exciting young attacker, who had made a big impression at Old Trafford after breaking into the first-team before things turned sour. Garnacho scored just once in the Premier League for Chelsea, whose moves for Morgan Rogers and Geovany Quenda nudged the former United man down the pecking order.

‌



Though any prospective return to Stamford Bridge remains some way off at this point, particularly given there is no clause allowing Garnacho to be recalled in January, he has now failed to even be included in Aston Villa's squad altogether for five of their last six Premier League games.

If Garnacho is unable to force his way back into Emery's plans and the parameters for the permanent deal agreed last summer are not reached then it is likely the winger will spend the season out in the cold before getting a chance to kickstart his career in 2027.

Sports.title: Dubois vs Parker announced for WBO heavyweight title clash
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois will defend the WBO heavyweight world championship against Joseph Parker on January 30 at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.

Dubois and Parker were due to box in 2025 for the IBF title, only for Dubois to fall ill and withdraw just three days before the fight.

Parker knocked out short-notice replacement Martin Bakole and then lost a WBO Interim title bout to Fabio Wardley.

In August he announced that he could continue his career after a suspension was lifted following a failed drug test in October 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO heavyweight rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley. Video credit: Courtesy of DAZN

Dubois lost the IBF strap to Oleksandr Usyk last year but stormed back to form when he twice halted Wardley, winning and retaining the full WBO world championship.

He will now be back in action early in the new year against Parker, who's also recorded standout wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang in recent years.

A former holder of the belt, the New Zealander lost the WBO championship to Anthony Joshua back in 2018 at the Principality Stadium when he became the first professional opponent to go the distance with Joshua.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player WBO heavyweight world champion Daniel Dubois says he is eyeing a future clash against Tyson Fury next year, admitting the fight would be 'ground-breaking'

Frank Warren said: "This heavyweight showdown will deliver a blockbuster beginning to 2027.

"It's a fight everyone wanted to see, and I'm thrilled we can now make it happen. Daniel is entering his prime and when he is on his game it is hard to picture anybody beating him.

"But Joseph has long promised to become world champion again, and now he gets his chance."

Sports.title: Newbury's Coral Gold Cup: Jamie Lynch's horse-by-horse guide
Sports.content:
Jamie Lynch assesses the confirmations and reveals his top tip for one of the most prestigious handicaps of the season this Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

The Coral Gold Cup at Newbury at 3pm is one of the biggest and best handicap chases of the entire season, although conditions will be a break from the norm - the reason the race is a little lighter at the top end this time, with only one rated above 150.

But there is the usual stack of classy second-season chasers with high trajectories and higher aspirations, meaning that - as always - it's going to take a lot of winning. Let's look at all those entered for this high-prestige prize, just one part of a stellar Saturday on Sky Sports Racing.

Watch every race of the Coral Gold Cup meeting from Newbury live on Sky Sports Racing on Friday 27th and Saturday 28th November.

Three Card Brag

Trainer: Gordon Elliott

He ran the race of his life when beating all bar Panic Attack in last year's renewal, conceding weight all round, the same again here, but he hasn't reproduced that level since, though one race was the Grand National and the latest smacked of a prep run, off a break and ridden by a 7lb conditional jockey.

The last top-weight winner was the daddy, Denman, whose mark was 20lb higher, if you don't mind.

King Alexander

Trainer: Willie Mullins

Has had the privilege of residing at two of the finest horseracing hotels in history, trained firstly by Nicky Henderson and then Willie Mullins, for whom he won the Galway Plate in July against the odds, as the outsider of the stable's four.

That has left him with what's probably too high a mark now, so says the Kerry National in which he finished an unthreatening sixth.

Regent's Stroll

Trainer: Paul Nicholls

A nephew of the legendary Denman, who had a mark of 161 when he made a successful reappearance in this race in his second season over fences, Regent's Stroll is not quite on the same trajectory but ended his novice campaign on a high at the Festivals. He was third at Cheltenham to Meetmebythesea and Gold Dancer in the Jack Richards and second to the latter in the Mildmay.

Image: Regent's Stroll represents Paul Nicholls

We haven't seen all he's got, including for stamina, and the stable can still get one primed and readied for this, highlighted by Kandoo Kid in 2024. Big chance.

Downmexicoway

Trainer: Henry de Bromhead

He was third in the Kerry National last time where his status as favourite spoke of his developing talent, having caught the eye in the Plates at both Cheltenham and Galway. Being a second-season chaser from the Henry de Bromhead yard is reason enough to put him on a shortlist, and then there are the added bonuses of his untapped stamina and suitability to non-November ground.

Wendigo

Trainer: Jamie Snowden

The classic profile for this race, as a second-season chaser with a touch of class and an eye on the biggest staying prizes: the most memorable winners of the Hennessy, now the Coral Gold Cup, have all had a look of Wendigo. He was rated 147 following his third to Kitzbuhel in the Kauto Star almost a year ago, and he's still rated that now, perhaps generously so.

Image: Wendigo is the current favourite for Saturday's feature

The signs from his reappearance were loud and clear that he's an improved model, to give 10lb to Potters Charm and a heavy beating to Doyen Quest at Carlisle, all without the need to play his ace card, the stamina card. If you tasked AI with creating a Coral Gold Cup winner, the technical drawings would be of Wendigo.

Masaccio

Trainer: Alan King

This horse missed the whole of last season, not that anybody could have told from his finding, grinding comeback win - at odds of 33/1 - in a 16-runner handicap hurdle at Newbury, like he'd never been away.

As a novice chaser, he was second to The Jukebox Man in the Grade Two John Francome in 2024, as well as third to Jagwar in the Plate at the Cheltenham Festival. That form makes a mark of 147 well within reach, though the 'bounce' factor is obviously high with him.

Panic Attack

Trainer: Dan Skelton

The heroine of last year, but she was coming in hot then, unlike now, absent since April. Also, she's 6lb higher now, or effectively 9lb considering that Tristan Durrell claimed 3lb back then.

Image: Tristan Durrell won last year's Coral Gold Cup aboard Panic Attack

History tells us how hard a repeat is - Arkle being the only one to ever do it in back-to-back years.

Miami Magic

Trainer: Stuart Edmunds

Stuart Edmunds' charge was classy but clumsy as a novice chaser, exemplified by the Mildmay at Aintree, where he went off 7/2 and looked a threat when he came down at the fourth-last. Only Masaccio prevented the perfect prep in a hurdle at Newbury, and Miami Magic has got the game to win a race like this.

He's unbothered by drying ground, but there are 21 fences and almost as many rivals in his way, an unforgiving environment for a sketchy jumper.

Holloway Queen

Trainer: Nicky Henderson

A magical metamorphosis through last season, which started with a PU and a UR and ended in two 'wow' wins, culminating with the National Hunt Chase.

A 10lb hit requires her to pick up where she left off and then some, and the unseasonable autumn has impeded her traditional stable more than most, raising some doubt as to whether she'll be razor sharp first time out.

The Jukebox Kid

Trainer: Willie Mullins

The small print reads differently to Regent's Stroll and Wendigo but the formula fabric is still the same, as a second-season chaser from a leading yard. His reappearance over hurdles was a means to an end, not much in the way of bite even so, after a summer wind op, and this track is very different to right-handed Ascot where he's looked most at home as a chaser.

Myretown

Trainers: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore

This contender fell when favourite for this 12 months ago, the omen for a season which was essentially a write-off. But, with the reset button pressed over the summer, he was back looking more the Myretown of old in dismissing a trio of inferior rivals at Kelso, a confidence-restoring exercise, as well as a greater connecting point back to his showstopper in the 2025 Ultima. That was the reason he topped the market last year off the same mark as now.

Road To Home

Trainer: Willie Mullins

Got better as a novice and showed he can cut it in big-field handicaps with his placings in the Kim Muir and the bet365 Gold Cup, beaten a neck in one and a neck and a short-head in the other. Won a mere maiden chase on his return at Galway but was as big as 9/2 that day, on account of the trip (an inadequate 2m 2f), putting him ahead of schedule for his primary target, at a track that plugs into his properties.

Amirite

Trainer: Chris Gordon

In his time with Henry de Bromhead, he was 0/6 with his British raids, including pulling up in the latest Grand National at 100/1, and his first start for Chris Gordon amounted to little, albeit over hurdles and without the usual tongue tie.

Havaila

Trainer: Jamie and Josh Moore

Seems a lot older than seven, largely because he's high mileage (began with Sir Michael Stoute), which made his spring surge all the more remarkable, not returning until January but improving 25lb and bringing up the hat-trick in the bet365 Gold Cup. As a late bloomer with a come-from-behind style, his ceiling isn't so discernible as many in here.

The Doyen Chief

Trainer: Nick Scholfield

The chief sufferer in the chaotic start when 14/1 for this last year (trained by Alan King), which was more of a window of opportunity for him than this renewal, having lost a bit of lustre in the meantime, for all that his first start for Nick Scholfield when runner-up at Market Rasen suggested that most of his ability was intact.

Booster Bob

Trainer: Olly Murphy

Two for two in handicap chases at Newbury, the first all down to Sean Bowen (having traded at 880/1 in-running) and the second coming on his reappearance on this very day last year, in the 2m 6f event. The rest of the campaign was a bit of a washout but who knows what he can do at this sort of trip, back fresh and back at Newbury? He's something of a mystery box.

One Big Bang

Trainer: James Owen

Thrived in big fields as a hurdler, and his first experience of such a scenario as a chaser prompted a fine third in the National Hunt Chase, after which he was excusably overwhelmed in the Irish National. Another to use the staying hurdle here earlier in the month as a stepping stone to this, and his component parts qualify him as a lively longshot, in the same way his dam's half-brother Madison Du Berlais was when he won this at 25/1 in 2008.

Kap Vert

Trainer: Philip Hobbs and Johnson White

Some going and some stamina to win the Scottish National as a novice, on ground that was officially heavy. But he's not one dimensional, nor maxed out, based on an encouraging return at Aintree, and he's only a six-year-old. A field, or a jumping test, such as this holds no fears for him.

Mr Hope Street

Trainer: Dan Skelton

His success in a high-value handicap at Aintree on National day is the one and only time he's tackled 3m+ over fences, no coincidence in that, nor the fact he has saved his second go for this, after a screw-tightening reappearance over 2m 4f at Stratford. This perceptible plan, and the man orchestrating it (Dan Skelton), are big selling points.

Image: Mr Hope Street represents Team Skelton

Here Comes Georgie

Trainer: Dan Skelton

This contender started with a bang for Skelton at Cheltenham and perhaps had a hangover from that when underwhelming at Aintree a fortnight later. He's in a similar boat but not the same mould as Panic Attack from last year.

JAMIE LYNCH'S VERDICT

The likes of Wendigo and Regent's Stroll speak for themselves, both a profiler's dream for this race, but, for that very reason, the market is giving nothing away for either. The ill-fated Gold Dancer beat both in the Mildmay, and his form is tied in with DOWNMEXICOWAY, who has got in some valuable practice for big-field handicaps while continually hinting at better to come.

Sports.title: London Broncos confirmed as Super League's 15th team for 2027 season
Sports.content:
London Broncos have been confirmed as Super League's 15th team for the 2027 season.

Earlier this month, Super League announced its 14 clubs had voted in favour of a motion to expand to 15 teams for the 2027 season.

Clubs were then invited to apply, with London Broncos - who had made no secret of their desire to be in the top flight - one of those to do so having completed the treble in 2026 during a brilliant season for them in the Championship.

"We are delighted to welcome London Broncos back to Super League for 2027," said chair of Super League Peter Hutton.

"This is an exciting moment for the club and its supporters, and an opportunity to build a lasting presence for our competition in the capital.

"They clearly impressed in the Championship last year, not only winning the League Leaders' Shield but the Grand Final and 1895 Cup in a memorable treble.

"In Grant Wechsel and Darren Lockyer, they have ambitious owners who are intent on making a success of our great sport in London and the surrounding areas.

"On behalf of all Super League clubs, I would like to put on record my thanks to both Grant and Darren for the collaboration they have shown over the last 10 days to enable the RFL to come to this recommendation.

"Expansion is about more than adding another club. We want a compelling, competitive Super League that reaches new audiences while continuing to serve the supporters who are at the heart of our sport.

"With more exciting announcements expected shortly around investment, broadcast deals and new commercial partners for Super League, we look forward to working with the Broncos as they prepare for 2027, and to seeing their supporters enjoy the elite competition in London once again."

After London went back down to the Championship in 2024, they were taken over by an ownership group including NRL and Brisbane Broncos legend Darren Lockyer.

Image: Earlier this month, Super League clubs voted in favour of the motion to expand

Super League clubs approve salary cap amendments

Also this month, clubs voted in favour of two amendments to the league's salary cap regulations that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries.

The first allows teams to claim salary cap dispensation if a player is injured for over eight cap-relevant matches, allowing clubs to sign a replacement player for the period.

It also forbids teams from claiming further salary cap dispensation should a player who was already exempt from salary cap implications becomes re-injured later in the season, unless he missed a further eight matches which affect the salary cap.

The second allows teams to feature a young player aged 23 and under - who has not previously played in any salary capped games - in two matches without triggering an increase in a club's salary cap spending, with that figure increasing to 50 per cent should they play between three and five matches.

Should the player feature in more than five matches, the full amount of their salary will be applied to the cap.

Sports.title: 'Triumph over trauma' - new women's boxing promotion begins
Sports.content:
Fight Back Promotions will have its inaugural event on Saturday at London's Ladbroke Hall; Fight Back Promotions is a women's boxing venture that supports a charitable programme which works with women who have been affected by domestic abuse and gender-based violence

Fight Back Promotions, a new venture to support women affected by domestic violence, begins: 'It's triumph over trauma'

A new boxing promotion, created to support women who have experienced domestic abuse and gender-based violence, will have its inaugural event on Saturday at Ladbroke Hall in London.

Fight Back Promotions was founded by Lesley Sackey, a former GB boxer, Shelly Sweeney, a champion and coach herself, and Poppy Mason-Watts, who has a background in social impact story-telling.

Sackey told Sky Sports: "Fight Back Promotions is an all-female boxing platform. It started from a CIC [a Community Interest Company or social enterprise] called Fight Forward.

"Fight Back Promotions was born as an answer and response to giving a space for all women to be able to step into the ring with not only safety but community, encouragement and a way to promote themselves and go on their own journey.

"It's about using boxing as a vehicle to support women who'd experienced domestic abuse."

Twenty-five per cent of the promotion's profits will go back to Fight Forward's charitable work.

"Women's sport is having a moment and there's still so much more to do," Sackey said. "It really seems like there's opportunity and potential to be a global platform.

"Women put on excellent fights, I don't think we need to prove that any more, and they can sell tickets as well.

"A percentage of whatever we make will always go back feeding into the not-for-profit Fight Forward to support other women in tough, challenging spaces."

Image: A quarter of the promotion's profits will go back to Fight Forward’s charitable work

Sackey formed the concept for Fight Forward, which uses boxing training to support its participants, after leaving an abusive relationship.

"The ring is just a destination, it's really about the journey, it's about the process, it's about the discipline of having to show up for yourself which for so many women in these situations, they've not had the choice or even the opportunity to do something for themselves," she explained.

"It's about discipline, it's about showing up, it's about being connected to your body, it's about being present, resilient. These are all the tools that we teach the women who participate in the sessions. Not all of them are contact. It's not just about contact, it's about community, being around other women who get it.

"Just to put on gloves and see another woman in an empowered position, the ripple effect is huge and it reaches so many women just by seeing that.

"It's triumph over trauma. You don't have to remain in this survivor state."

Sports.title: Williams handed penalties after minor breach of cost cap
Sports.content:
Williams have been given financial and aerodynamic testing penalties after committing a minor overspend breach of Formula 1's cost cap for the 2025 season.

The FIA announced Williams had accepted an Accepted Breach Agreement after being found to have "unintentionally committed" a minor overspend and procedural breach of the sport's spending rules for last year.

Williams overspent by £627,000 - 0.48 per cent over the 2025 cost cap - and in addition to a financial penalty, will receive a 1.5 per cent reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing time over the next 12 months. The 2025 spending cap was $135m (£102m) plus inflation.

An FIA statement read: "The Cost Cap Administration recognised that WGPE [Williams Grand Prix Engineering Limited] has acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process, provided additional information and evidence in a timely manner when so requested and that there is no evidence that WGPE has sought or obtained any advantage [sporting or otherwise] as a result of the identified breaches."

Explaining the nature of the breach, Williams, who finished fifth in last year's Constructors' Championship but are ninth with two races of this year to go, said in a statement: "The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. We believed these costs fell outside of the cap." A minor breach is defined as an overspend of less than five per cent of the cost cap.

"Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap.

Image: Williams will have less wind tunnel time over the next 12 months

"The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process.

"Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future. We have always been and will continue to be strong supporters of the cost cap, which naturally requires accurate policing to be effective."

Alpine were found to have committed a procedural breach, related to inaccuracies in their full year reporting documentation.

The FIA noted that they had also "acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process and has sought to provide additional information and evidence when requested in a timely manner and that there is no accusation or evidence that Alpine has sought or obtained any undue advantage". Alpine's spending was below the cost cap limit.

Alpine will pay a financial penalty to the FIA after also entering into an accepted breach agreement for the procedural breach.

All nine other teams, which included 2026 newcomers Cadillac, were found to be in compliance for 2025, along with all five power unit manufacturers for their respective spending cap.
