Sports.title: Jude Bellingham can win Ballon d’Or but Harry Kane and superstar duo are better than him right now
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham can win Ballon d’Or but Harry Kane and superstar duo are better than him right now

Jude Bellingham will contend for Ballon d'Or glory throughout the next decade, but three players rank above him as of today.

That's the view of talkSPORT pundit Darren Bent, who revealed his star-studded top ten list in world football after another moment of magic by the England superstar.

5 Bellingham stole the show for Real Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday night with another superb goal Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Bellingham came off the bench to score and assist for Real Madrid as they fought from a goal down to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday.

The goal, his 17th in the Champions League, was outstanding - two well-controlled flicks and a shot from the outside of his boot into the corner.

He has tallied seven goals and five assists in 18 matches this season so far, weeks after finishing 11th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

A 23-year-old, he is line for countless years of success on the biggest stage, and talkSPORT Drive host Andy Goldstein is confident that he can be crowned the best player in the world during his career.

"I just think he's going to win the Ballon d'Or, without a shadow of a doubt," he claimed. "In the next five years, maybe even three."

Ex-England striker Bent replied: "For the next decade, maybe a bit longer, whenever there's a Ballon d'Or list, I expect Jude to be in the mix. This year, he finished 11th in the Ballon d'Or, he is better than that.

"But then I think, for years to come, I expect him every single season to be in the top five, because that's how good he is."

Who are the top ten players in the world?

Like his co-host Goldstein, Bent is among millions of fans across the globe who considers Bellingham to be one of the very best around.

However, when listing his top ten during Wednesday evening's show, he named three players who have more quality to their game.

10. Declan Rice - England and Arsenal

Now in his fourth season at Arsenal, Rice has established himself as a key starter at club level and for England.

5 Bent believes that Bellingham can win a Ballon d'Or at some point but, for now, three players are better than him Credit: Getty

The midfielder was instrumental in the Gunners' Premier League title win in 25/26 before reaching the World Cup semi-finals at his fourth major international tournament.

9. Raphinha - Brazil and Barcelona

Barcelona signed Raphinha from Leeds United in 2022 and, this season, he is top of the LaLiga scoring charts on 15.

That is two more than rival Kylian Mbappe, with his total outlay across all competitions sitting at a whopping 19 with a month left to go in 2026.

8. Vitinha - Portugal and Paris Saint-Germain

It has been five years since Vitinha played on loan at Wolves from Porto, and now he is one of the best midfielders on the globe.

He won his second Champions League title with PSG during the summer and has 49 Portugal caps at age 26, starting all five of their matches at the World Cup.

7. Erling Haaland - Norway and Manchester City

Haaland continues to thrive at City having hit 14 goals in 16 this season, even though cracks are starting to appear at the club.

5 Haaland is the Premier League top scorer on nine goals this season, but Bent has him below Bellingham in his list Credit: Getty

Now 26 with 379 goals at club and country level during his career, not many players who can say they are as clinical as him in front of goal.

6. Michael Olise - France and Bayern Munich

Former Crystal Palace wizard Olise remains one of the most skilful and talented wide players as he pulls the strings for France and Bayern.

He managed to hit 22 goals and 31 assists for the latter last season, and is already on 12 and seven this time round.

5. Rodri - Spain and Barcelona

It takes a lot for players to return to their best form after an ACL injury - Rodri is a prime example of that.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner captained Spain to the 2026 World Cup and was awarded the Golden Ball for being player of the tournament.

4. Jude Bellingham - England and Real Madrid

As Goldstein and Bent mentioned earlier, Bellingham certainly has the ability to be win the title of world's best playing in the coming years.

The ex-Birmingham City starlet played every match for England at the World Cup, where he scored seven goals and assisted one other.

3. Harry Kane - England and Bayern Munich

This year's Ballon d'Or winner Kane is just one of five English players to collect the gong, and his triumph came as little surprise.

5 Kane scores goals for fun with England and Bayern, which puts him just one spot above Bellingham in Bent's list Credit: Getty

With a staggering 61 goals in 51 appearances for Bayern last season and another six in the summer, he will go down as an all-time great.

2. Lamine Yamal - Spain and Barcelona

Barcelona appear to have found their second coming of Lionel Messi in Yamal who, at 19-years-old, already ranks as one of the best players.

He was quiet during the World Cup but still lifted the coveted trophy, and has 26 goals and assists with Barca just months into the season.

1. Kylian Mbappe - France and Real Madrid

For Bent, it's superstar Mbappe who he considers to be the best in the world at this moment in time.

France and Madrid have one of the best finishers on their hands as he has 19 goals in 18 outings for this campaign thus far.

Sports.title: £35m Liverpool star suffers worrying injury as stretcher called onto pitch
Sports.content:
Liverpool have been dealt a huge blow with Victor Munoz going off with what appears to be a knee injury.

The Spain winger sustained the knock during the Reds' Champions League clash at Club Brugge on Wednesday night while committing a foul.



3 Munoz went off after making this challenge late in the first half Credit: Getty

A rapid counter-attack saw Munoz receive the ball in Liverpool's half on the right before he charged at the heart of the Club Brugge midfield and defence.

After breezing past multiple opponents, Munoz was unable to pull the trigger as Club Brugge defender Jorne Spileers made a clearance on the cover.

Munoz stretched for the ball and caught Spileers, resulting in a free-kick for the home side.



However, play was delayed for four minutes with Munoz coming off worse from the challenge, the 23-year-old receiving treatment from Liverpool medics on his right knee.

Replays appeared to show both Munoz and Spileers' knees collide with the Belgian not suffering to the same extent as Munoz.



A stretcher was brought onto the pitch, although Munoz was able to leave on foot when he came off. Rio Ngumoha was brought on as his replacement.

Liverpool are currently 1-0 up against the Belgian side with Alexander Isak finishing from close range after some sloppy play by their hosts.



Club Brugge saw goalkeeper Yann Sommer's loose pass was intercepted by Bradley Barcola.

Barcola moved the ball quickly onto Dominik Szoboszlai down the left channel with the Hungarian then finding Isak with a low cross and the striker finished first time from six yards out.

Liverpool have struggled to build on the lead since the goal on 13 minutes with Club Brugge responding well to their early setback.

3 Munoz declined the chance to be taken off on a stretcher Credit: AFP



3 Liverpool took the lead through a trademark close-range Isak strike Credit: Getty

The home side's best chance saw Szoboszlai clear a header off the line following a corner from the right-hand side.

Club Brugge started the evening level on points with Liverpool with nine and only behind them on goals scored.

Victor Munoz's Liverpool career

A win will see Liverpool take a big step towards ensuring they will reach the play-off round at the very least with three league phase matches to spare.



But they will be sweating on the fitness of Munoz, who has settled in well at Anfield having joined in a £35million deal from Osasuna in the summer.

Munoz, who snubbed a move to Newcastle to join Liverpool, has scored three goals including during the Reds' 4-0 thumping of Manchester United last weekend.

He's part of a stacked attack as he competes with the likes of Barcola, Ngumoha and Cody Gakpo for a start out on either wing.

Liverpool's next outing sees them face rivals Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan reveals how Chelsea signed Alejandro Garnacho for £40m after Zoom interview
Sports.content:
Chelsea director Behdad Eghbali decided to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Manchester United after interviewing him on Zoom.

That's according to Simon Jordan, who has doubts over the Argentine's future at top-level football amid his disastrous loan spell with Aston Villa.



4 Garnacho signed for Chelsea a little over a year ago, but is already facing an exit and struggles on loan Credit: Getty

Garnacho completed a £40million move to Chelsea in August 2025 and scored eight goals across all competitions in his first season.

However, only one of those came in the Premier League and talkSPORT reported that he was already up for sale this summer.

A season-long loan deal, which includes a conditional obligation to buy clause, was agreed with Villa ahead of the current campaign.



Garnacho has played only 95 minutes of football though, and had not been named in their last three squads.

This includes the 1-0 Champions League loss at Galatasaray on Tuesday night, after which Unai Emery hinted he was not a 'best option' to play.



Once a prospect at United, Garnacho is facing another underwhelming season on the pitch as his career staggers.

Jordan called the winger 'a little runt' before his move to Chelsea as he took issue with his attitude at Old Trafford.



And he has now revealed that Chelsea thought they had seen enough to sanction a purchase after an online video call with the player.

Jordan on Chelsea Zoom call with Garnacho

"I was very surprised he took him," he said of Villa boss Emery on White and Jordan. I think this player is a waste of time.

"I watched him at Chelsea last year, and I said to Eghbali, 'Why did you pay... didn't he show you what he was at Manchester United?'

4 Eghbali (right) had a Zoom call with Garnacho before completing the £40m deal to sign him for Chelsea from United Credit: Getty



4 Jordan, who has been critical of Garnacho for his attitude and performances, could not believe what he heard from Eghbali Credit: talkSPORT

"He was like, 'Yes, I know, but it was only £40million, and we interviewed him on Zoom'. I thought, 'What?'"

Garnacho has removed anything related to both Villa and Chelsea on his Instagram account after being omitted from yet another match.

In fact, Emery opted to choose only 11 substitutes instead of 12 against Galatasaray, and two of those were goalkeepers.



The decision casts major doubt over how much more game time he will get at Villa, and Jordan is uncertain over his long-term future as he said: "Aston Villa are constrained by certain obligations upon them financially.

"And so, I would suggest there was some degree of subsidy and circumstance that enabled them to get a player that might be worth a punt if you can get something out of him, and (it's) not that much of a problem if you can't."

Jordan added: "He looks like a little boy, he had a lot to say for himself at Manchester United, and his captain (Bruno Fernandes) came out in one of his rare voyages into saying something that vaguely looked like a captain's sort of statement.

4 Jordan is has questioned Garnacho's longevity at the top of football given his ongoing Villa exile Credit: Getty



"And it was wrong what he said at the time, which was, 'The fans need to support Garnacho because he's unhappy about the fact he doesn't get the credit that he should be getting'.

"I think if you remember, he didn't celebrate a goal because he was not happy with the fact that the fans had been on his back for his sub-standard performances.

"I think he's a product of a certain circumstance in football where these players have got clear ability and talent, they're overhyped, they believe themselves.

"They spend more time in the tattoo parlour than they do on the training ground, and out comes a performance that leads you to a situation where they're on an enormous amount of money for doing very little, and it's all about the potential that they might have had once upon a time when they showed it very early in their career.



"And here we are now on the third club, where he's working his way down in terms of stature of club. I know that Villa are performing better on the field than Man United but, in the stature of the club, United are the big fish.

"Chelsea are a slightly smaller fish but, not withstanding that, a big fish, and Villa are the smallest of the three clubs in terms of the recent achievements. And so, with that in mind, where's he going?"

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres is not top draw – he’d be good for Premier League relegation battlers
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres is not top draw – he’d be good for Premier League relegation battlers

Viktor Gyokeres is not the man to fire Arsenal to Champions League glory - his level is Nottingham Forest.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Jason Cundy, who has cast doubt over the £63.7million man after he endured a mixed night despite scoring in the Gunners' 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.



5 Viktor Gyokeres scored a screamer in the Champions League, but still left feeling somewhat disappointed Credit: Getty

Having largely played back-up to Kai Havertz this term, Gyokeres started in the Champions League clash and made his mark almost immediately.

He scored arguably his best goal yet for Arsenal, firing in a stunning 28-yard strike to break the deadlock at Emirates Stadium in the 10th minute.

However, the 28-year-old's luck turned thereafter, as it soon became a night of missed chances for the Gunners, and him especially.



After Max Beier equalised for Dortmund, Gyokeres missed a golden opportunity to put his side back in front when he managed to head wide from six yards out with the goal at his mercy.

With Arsenal ultimately having to settle for a point, the Swede has faced criticism for not being clinical enough, while it once again sparked conversations over his ability to lead the line on a regular basis.



Despite netting 20 goals in all competitions last season, Gyokeres has failed to convince as Arsenal's first-choice striker.

This term he has played second fiddle to Havertz, starting just seven of his 16 appearances - one of which has come in the Premier League - and scoring three goals, leading him to be tipped for a January exit.



And talkSPORT host Cundy has now claimed Gyokeres' level is closer to a struggling Premier League side - with Nottingham Forest his example.

'He's not top draw'

Reacting to Gyokeres' display on the Sports Bar, Cundy said: “He's not top draw.

“He's probably a striker for like, Forest. I mean, I'm looking at Liam Delap, I don't know if there's too much to choose between the pair.

5 Fans saw the best and worse of Gyokeres against Borussia Dortmund Credit: Getty



5 Delap boasts three more Premier League goals than Gyokeres this term, but has been a regular starter Credit: Getty

“Honestly, I like Delap, he’s a Premier League player. Yeah, I'm going to go Forest.”

Despite Gyokeres arriving for an initial £55m in 2025 after a prolific two years with Sporting Lisbon, Cundy likened him to Forest's £50m man Delap - who has three Premier League goals this term.

And while the Arsenal man fired in 14 league goals en route to league glory last term, Cundy named Brentford talisman Igor Thiago and Aston Villa's Nicolas Jackson as strikers he would rather have.



Cundy continued: “Thiago's a different type of player, completely different. I'd rather have Thiago up top than Gyokeres.

“Nicolas Jackson? 100 per cent.”

Gyokeres' game questioned

Gyokeres' all-round game as a striker was also called into question, with Cundy insisting he must finish his chances and hold the ball up better.

5 Gyokeres helped end Arsenal's 22-wait for Premier League glory in his first season, scoring 14 league goals Credit: Getty

The Sports Bar host went on: “Come on, it's a well-struck shot, right? That can happen. That doesn't make him world class."



He added: “The point I'm making is, strikers can score [great goals]. He's set it up, beautifully struck, well done.

“But then you see the body of work that he's got. He's not [world class]."

Naming Havertz as Arsenal's best option up front, Cundy said: “Havertz is going to start up top.

“Arsenal can win the Champions League. Chelsea won the Champions League with Havertz.



He added: “Gyokeres is not going to be the difference maker. There are players out there that can be a difference maker better than Gyokeres, and I will have that argument with anyone.”

5 Cundy insists there is more to a striker's game than scoring screamers Credit: Getty

Rounding off, Cundy then said: “It's a great goal, but that's not what you've signed him for. He's got to score one of those once a season. He isn’t scoring that again, it's a brilliant strike.

“He's not been signed to score bangers from the edge of the box. He's been signed to run in behind, hold up play, bring players in, and do tap-ins on the edge of the six-yard box.



“He missed the easiest chance - the header.”

Sports.title: Conor Coady in surprise contention for EFL job just weeks after retiring
Sports.content:
Conor Coady in surprise contention for EFL job just weeks after retiring

Conor Coady is a leading contender for the Blackpool job, talkSPORT understands.

Blackpool sacked Ian Evatt as their head coach last Thursday after a run of just three wins from 13.

2 Coady could be set to land his first managerial job in senior football as he eyes the Blackpool vacancy Credit: Getty

The Seasiders drew 1-1 with Leicester City on Tuesday night in League One, in which they sit 20th and above the drop on goal difference.

Steve Thompson took charge of the side, but Coady could arrive as the permanent successor to Evatt.

Who is in contention for the Blackpool job?

This comes just weeks after he announced his retirement from football at the age of 33.

Coady, who won ten caps with England, is currently a coach with the U21s alongside Lee Carsley.

The ex-centre-back made 503 appearances at club level, appearing for clubs such as Liverpool and Wolves.

Coady spent the majority of his career at the latter, and last played for Charlton Athletic on loan from Wrexham.

Former Blackpool midfielder Charlie Adam is also understood to be interested in the job.

Adam made 98 appearances for the club, 35 of which came in their one Premier League season.

The ex-Scotland international was a loans manager at Burnley before he became head coach of Fleetwood Town.

After his exit in December 2024, he joined David Moyes at Everton as their new set piece coach.

2 Adam is also interested in taking on the Blackpool job, 15 years after he left as a player Credit: Getty

Matt Bloomfield has been one of the leading candidates for the job at Blackpool after leaving Oxford United in June.

Richie Wellens, a former midfielder at the club who is currently in charge at Leyton Orient, is also a contender.

Other names include Damien Duff, Darren Ferguson, Paul Heckingbottom and Ryan Mason, as well as Gary Rowett.

Blackpool face one of last season's League One play-off hopefuls in Stevenage on Saturday.

Promotion contenders Luton Town follow on December 1 before their FA Cup second round tie away to National League South side Salisbury.

Sports.title: Arsenal told to aim higher than Dominic Calvert-Lewin and urged to sign £100m-rated forward instead
Sports.content:
Arsenal told to aim higher than Dominic Calvert-Lewin and urged to sign £100m-rated forward instead

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has impressed for Leeds United, but Arsenal should aim to sign forwards like Eli Junior Kroupi instead.

That's the view of talkSPORT pundit Joel Beya as the Gunners possibly eye a new attacking option during the January transfer window.



4 Theo Walcott told talkSPORT that he thinks Calvert-Lewin would fit in at Arsenal, but Beya offered some alternative names Credit: Getty

Kai Havertz has been the main striker for Arsenal this season, though his tally of four goals is just one more than bit-part option Viktor Gyokeres.

This lack of firepower has raised concerns for club legend Theo Walcott, who told talkSPORT that there is a 'position up for grabs' in their attack.

Walcott also claimed that Calvert-Lewin is the no. 9 profile that Arsenal are looking for, with the former Everton and Sheffield United frontman scoring six goals in 13 appearances this season.



However, a move now looks unlikely as talkSPORT understands that he is in advanced talks over signing a new deal at Leeds.

Who should Arsenal sign at striker?

When responding to Walcott's Calvert-Lewin suggestion on talkSPORT Breakfast, Beya said: "I like Calvert-Lewin as a back-up striker, maybe. No disrespect, he's obviously still doing a good job at Leeds.



Beya then named Kroupi as the type of player that Arsenal should look to sign if they want Premier League and Champions League success.

"I think we should be looking at the Kroupi's of this world, we should be looking at people that are going to take us forward."



Kroupi is yet to score for Bournemouth this season as he was sidelined for weeks with a foot injury.

However, as talkSPORT reported in our Transfer Notebook, the 20-year-old has been given a £100million price tag for any suitors looking to sign him in January.

Bournemouth do not intend to sell the French international, who also has interest from Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain.

4 Kroupi has had a slow start to this season and could cost £100m, but Beya believes he is a player Arsenal should have their sights on Credit: Getty



Beya later revealed that he devised a list of options for Arsenal, starting with a former summer target.

"We've still got (Julian) Alvarez, he's not scoring as much as people think he's scoring, by the way."

Atletico Madrid held talks with Arsenal over a deal for Alvarez, but he is said to have told the former that he didn't want to join.

The former Manchester City star has scored only two goals this season after a summer saga in which he asked to be sold.



"Endrick as well, I think he's an option," Beya added. "He's not really playing a lot at Real Madrid.

"But I just don't think Jose (Mourinho) is going to want him to go to a rival that could be winning the Champions League."

4 Arsenal were heavily linked with Alvarez during the summer window but he was not interested in a move Credit: Getty

Brazilian starlet Endrick was touted as one for the future and earned a move to Madrid in 2024, but netted only eight times in 48 appearances.



The 20-year-old has only played 160 minutes this season, despite his strong loan with Lyon earlier this year where he hit 16 goals and assists.

Beya continued: "(Antonio) Nusa as well, from (RB) Leipzig. He's one that we've been speaking about and do you know what?

"For him, even this season, five goals, seven assists (in the Bundesliga), doing his business there."

Nusa recently addressed speculation over a move to Arsenal, insisting that he is staying away from the rumours.



However, European football broadcaster Andy Brassell has backed the idea of the Norwegian winger being a success at the Emirates Stadium.

4 Haaland could be an option for Arsenal if City are to be hit with heavy sanctions such as relegation from the Premier League Credit: Getty

"Kevin Schade as well, from Brentford, it could happen," Beya also said, amid the German's three goals in 13 appearances this season.

Breakfast host Alan Brazil then asked if Arsenal should look into a move for Erling Haaland amid the uncertainty over Manchester City.



The Gunners have been told to attempt a January signing given that City could be relegated due to their guilty verdict on financial rule breaks.

At first, Beya couldn't see it happening, but then said: "If they go down next season, then maybe, yeah, that's a possibility."

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham rejected huge Man United contract for one reason
Sports.content:
Manchester United came agonisingly close to signing a 17-year-old Jude Bellingham before he joined Borussia Dortmund.

However, the England international turned down a move to Old Trafford for one key reason despite being offered a lucrative contract.

5 Bellingham snubbed United to join Dortmund aged 17 in July 2020 Credit: Getty

Bellingham had been the most in-demand teenager in Europe having enjoyed a breakout season for Birmingham City.

After making his first-team debut aged 16, the midfielder scored four goals in 41 Championship appearances for Blues.

With clubs across the continent circling to land Bellingham, United were amongst those in the mix for his signature, with a tour of the club's training ground even taking place.

However, the youngster already has his heart set on a move to Dortmund, who completed a £25million deal to sign him in July 2020.

Bellingham went on to join Real Madrid three years later in a deal worth up to £115m.

He has since won the Champions League and LaLiga as well as scoring 52 goals and providing 38 assists in 158 appearances.

United offered 'bigger' contract

Bellingham could have instead spent the last six years starring in the Red Devils' midfield.

According to former Birmingham CEO Dong Ren, United had offered a larger salary as part of their contract proposal to the Blues starlet.

The club's then CEO Ed Woodward even visited Bellingham with several United legends in a bid to convince him to join.

However, Ren revealed they were never factors in his decision to choose a move to Dortmund.

5 United could have landed Bellingham for almost a quarter of his current market value

Speaking in 2022, Ren told Mundo Deportivo: "Jude didn’t make any decision based on money. They offered a much bigger salary compared to the rest. Maybe double.

"He was going to be guaranteed millions in the bank and he didn’t take it.

"He sat down with [Ole Gunnar] Solskjaer, then [Ed] Woodward brought [Alex] Ferguson in one day, then another day [Eric] Cantona in order to try to convince him."

Key reason put Bellingham off

United legend Rio Ferdinand even once recalled being told the key sticking point which prevented Bellingham from joining United.

The former defender said on his Vibe with Five podcast in 2023: "Do you know what? I heard [Bellingham] wanted some assurances about being a first-team player.

"And United weren’t willing to give him those assurances. That’s what I heard from a very good source.

5 United gave Bellingham a tour of their training ground in their bid to sign him from Birmingham Credit: Getty

"He wasn’t given assurances of being around the first team and he’s said, ‘do you know what? I know my worth, I know my value and if you don’t value me the way I see myself I’m going to have to jog on and go to another club’.

"He’s gone and done that and he’s turned round and gone, ’I told you guys, you didn’t believe me, did you?’

"And he’s gone to Real Madrid and he’s tearing down Real Madrid, he’s tearing down the Bernabeu, they’ve just rebuilt it and he’s tearing it down. Unbelievable."

Despite joining Dortmund less than a month after turning 17, Bellingham made 46 senior appearances during his debut season.

Of those, 33 came as part of the starting line-up as he featured in the Bundesliga and Champions League along with winning the DFB Pokal.

Now 23, Bellingham continues to star in Europe for Real Madrid, with his stunning volley against PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday his latest strike for the club.

5 Bellingham once wore a United kit during an academy fixture for Birmingham

Bellingham in a United shirt

Although they missed out on signing Bellingham as a 17-year-old, United could have landed him several years earlier.

That is according to ex-midfielder Nicky Butt, who watched him in action for Birmingham in an academy fixture.

Due to a kit mix-up, Bellingham had even played the match wearing a Red Devils shirt.

Butt told Football Uncensored: "I was there, he actually played in a Man United kit at the Cliff training ground because Birmingham forgot their kit.

"There are pictures of him in a red Man United kit playing against a blue Man United kit and he was by far the best trialist I have ever seen at 14/15.

"Told the club, ‘sign him, do not let this boy go,’ and then he goes.

"Certain times in the past at that football club that wouldn’t happen, in the last ten years since Sir Alex (Ferguson) has left that has happened and that’s the sad part about it."

Bellingham had joined Birmingham's academy at under-8 level in 2010 before spending nine years in the club's youth system.

Bellingham says Dortmund the best move

As for the player's reasons for choosing Dortmund over United, he made them clear after completing his move.

"Man United have a great squad but my decision had nothing to do with Man United.

"I was so focused and so happy with the interest from Dortmund that this became my first choice. For me, it was Borussia Dortmund and that’s it.

"When you find somewhere that’s the best place to be, you kind of ignore everything else."

5 Bellingham continues to show what could have been for United Credit: Getty

Bellingham made his senior England debut four months after joining Dortmund.

Since his maiden cap in November 2020, he has scored 14 goals in 62 appearances for the Three Lions.

Still aged 20, Bellingham won the Kopa Trophy in 2023 as the best under-21 player in the world.

He subsequently finished third in the Ballon d'Or the following year after his debut season with Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo 1000 goals: Date and game predicted for career milestone
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo will achieve one of his most incredible individual feats when he finally reaches 1000 career goals in 2027.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is still hunting Golden Boot awards at his Saudi Arabian side, Al Nassr, months before his 42nd birthday.



3 Goal machine Ronaldo will reach a milestone by scoring his 1000th career goal in 2027 Credit: Getty

Ronaldo has made no secret of his desire to reach 1000 goals, something that has never been done in competitive football.

His fans have long since suspected that the former Portugal international wouldn't hang up his boots until he hit the milestone.

However, his decision to follow rival Lionel Messi in stepping back from playing for his country, having played 234 times for Portugal, has narrowed his opportunities.



It means that Ronaldo can only edge closer to his career dream at club level, but the clock is ticking with Father Time against him.

The forward's contract with Al Nassr expires next summer, and the man himself has admitted he expects it to be his last.



How many goals has Ronaldo scored?

Ronaldo scored his 987th career goal in a 2-1 AFC Champions League Elite win against Qatari side Al Sadd on Tuesday, November 24.

It was his 11th in 14 matches this season for Al Nassr in all competitions, having bagged 30 in 44 across the calendar year.



It means that Ronaldo, who scored three goals at the World Cup, has a scoring pace of roughly 0.75 to 0.79 goals per game in the 2026/27 season.

He is now just 13 goals away from 1000 in total.

3 Ronaldo confirmed that his 23-year international career is over, which leaves Al Nassr as his only route to hit 1,000 goals

When could he score his 1000th goal?

Barring any major injuries, Ronaldo is set to reach four figures for goals between mid-February and mid-March 2027 at his current rate.

Should the Manchester United legend go on a scoring streak and average a goal a game, then it would take him just 13 matches.



That would bring him up to potentially reach 1000 goals against Al-Taawou, on January 29, or a week later against Al-Shamal.

What's more likely is that Ronaldo continues at his current pace, in which he will need 16 to 19 appearances to score 13 more goals.

The earlier end of that scale puts clashes with Shabab Al-Ahli (on February 15) or a home meeting with Al-Ittihad (on March 11).

3 Ronaldo took his season's tally to 11 goals in 14 games across all competitions Credit: Getty



Ronaldo might be slightly delayed in his hunt by being left out of AFC Champions League away matches during the league phase.

He had no involvement in the 6-2 win against Uzbek side Pakhtakor at the start of November.

Ange Postecoglou's men could add further games to Ronaldo's schedule by advancing past the King's Cup Round of 16 or reaching the AFC Champions League Elite knockout rounds.

Yet early exits might push his timeline back to around April, in which case fixtures against Al-Diriyah or Al-Ahli could be his crowning glory.

Sports.title: Furious Premier League refs 'SHOCKED' at Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool being overturned: Row erupts over Man United star's ban being scrapped… despite key panel voting unanimously that decision was RIGHT
Sports.content:
Premier League officials are 'shocked and furious' after the FA overturned Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool - despite the competition's own independent panel unanimously backing the dismissal. Daily Mail Sport understands that the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel has returned a 5-0 verdict in support of referee Sam Barrott's decision to send off Yoro. The panel also backed VAR's decision not to intervene. Their findings will be released next Wednesday. But an extraordinary row has now erupted, with United celebrating a successful appeal while the Premier League and refereeing body Pro Ref stand by the original decision. United appealed against the red card following Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield - Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge - and an independent FA regulatory commission, consisting of three former players, rescinded Yoro's one-match ban on Tuesday. The Frenchman was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he ran clear on goal in the eighth minute. United disputed the referee's view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, having taken a heavy touch. The FA panel appeared to agree, on the basis Yoro did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity, meaning the Frenchman is free to play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday. Referee Sam Barrott showed Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card vs Liverpool Yoro was sent off for this foul on Alexander Isak - but his red card was overturned on Tuesday Barrott and his on-field officiating team from Sunday are believed to be angry at the overturn However, top-flight officials are now understood to be demanding answers as to how this has happened, with Pro Ref chief Howard Webb backing his referees. 'That (the red card) was the referee's call, made on the field,' said Webb. 'Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect - and formed the opinion it wasn't. 'I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.' United sources have branded this interpretation as 'totally wrong' and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott's decision. United dispute that it was a subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed. The Premier League and Pro Ref did not comment. Sports.title: Raheem Sterling avoids jail for £270,000 Lamborghini crash: England star handed suspended prison sentence after telling court he underwent 12-day rehab stint for laughing gas 'problem'
Sports.content:
Former England football star Raheem Sterling avoided prison for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after it was revealed he spent 12 days in rehab.

The 31-year-old was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court today and has been banned from driving for two years.

He was also ordered to complete 100 hours of community service and must pay a victim surcharge of £187 as well as prosecution costs of £85.

Sterling – who is currently without a club but has played for Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea – pleaded guilty after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus SUV on May 28 while under the influence of laughing gas.

Four police forces received reports about the footballer's dangerous driving before he eventually crashed his car into a metal gate on the A327 in Hampshire during rush hour on the morning of May 28.

Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with laughing gas after subjecting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90 minutes of dangerous driving, in which he zig-zagged on the M3 and M25 motorways before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate. Police found six canisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

Raheem Sterling is pictured leaving Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on Wednesday, shaking hands with his solicitor Leo Martin - he avoided prison time

Sterling is seen after being pulled over by police earlier this year while under the influence of laughing gas in his Lamborghini - he later spent 12 days in rehab

In the police station, Sterling was asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but was so impaired that he recorded 52.

The footballer – who wore trainers, a black quarter-zip jumper with a white t-shirt and black trousers – froze as he waited for the judge to enter the court room.

He sat with his back against the wall in the glass dock and kept eye contact with her while she read her sentencing remarks.

District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed that Sterling sought addiction treatment on June 15 and went into rehab for 12 days.

She explained that nitrous oxide had 'become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career', adding that he was a 'role model'.

While his sentence does not mandate therapeutic intervention, the lead therapist at Banbury Lodge – where Sterling checked in – feels further treatment would be 'beneficial'.

His MBE, charitable work and time spent in rehabilitation were cited as mitigating factors, helping him avoid a prison sentence.

Allman added: 'You are 31 years old and a man of previous good character. I accept your character has been positively exemplary.

Sterling leaves the court with his solicitor having been given a suspended sentence

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling

'(But) these offences are so serious that neither a fine nor a community order can be justified. The custodial threshold is clearly crossed, and custody is unavoidable.'

However, custody was avoided because the law was changed in March 2026, with custodial sentences of one year or less presumed to be suspended – unless there are specific aggravating features – because of the overcrowded prison population.

Temporary chief inspector Chris Sharland of Hampshire Police said: 'Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or NOS, is a Class C drug, and driving whilst under its influence is an emerging threat to the safety of motorists on our roads.

'Driving whilst impaired with nitrous oxide can cause unconsciousness, and in the worst-case scenarios neurological damage or death, so there is a very real risk of causing serious harm to yourself or other motorists.

'We urge drivers to be aware of not only the law, but the risk this type of behaviour carries – one decision can have devastating consequences.'

In his pre-sentencing remarks, Sterling's lawyer, Jason Bartfeld KC, said Sterling is 'more concerned not by damage to his reputation' but the 'consequences' it has had for his family, particularly his children.

He added: 'Mr Sterling recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms that brought him to this position and has sought to address these in the most positive and effective way and with some success.

'All of it makes it extremely sad and a matter of his own personal regret, tarnishing his own personal reputation.

'The end point of this is that he is absolutely determined that he will never appear before a criminal court again.'

Police bodycam footage showed the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap.

An officer could be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He could then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Sterling gets back in the car after his sentencing and is banned from driving for two years

Sterling, who won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 2018-19, was then read his rights while being arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

There was a 40mph speed restriction on the M25 as he veered from lane to lane during peak travel time, with one witness fearing a ‘fatal collision’.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange, where the A327 meets the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his career at Dutch club Feyenoord.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28.

During that hearing, Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting.

'Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

The 31-year-old was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after swerving his car on the M25 and M3

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said.

Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone'.

Evidence previously presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon'.

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents.

For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave between the inside and outside lanes and come close to smashing into the central reservation.



'He went into oblivion mode': Inside Raheem Sterling's terrifying fall from grace as he admits dangerous driving - the controversy he never recovered from, his 'huge mistake' in joining Chelsea and why friends fear he is 'completely lost'

Sports.title: Travis Kelce reveals Prince William humiliation and the brutal reason he was left out of photo with now-wife Taylor Swift and the future King
Sports.content:
NFL star Travis Kelce has shared the reason why he was left out of his wife Taylor Swift's photo with royalty.

The Kansas City Chiefs player, 37, and his then-girlfriend Swift, 36, met Prince William and two of his children, Prince George and Princess Charlotte, after they attended the popstar's 2024 Eras Tour concert at Wembley Stadium, London.

The royals posed for selfies with the singer and football player backstage but Travis was recently left red-faced when Prince William admitted during an appearance on the Graham Norton Show that he 'tried to move' the athlete out of the photo.

The tight end reflected on William's awkward confession during the latest episode of his New Heights podcast when a fan called in with a similar issue.

A woman named Debbie sought advice from Travis and his brother Jason about family photos for the Thanksgiving holidays.

She revealed that she was a single mother of two who was dating a man who was 17 years younger than her - earning a few cheeky remarks from the two NFL brothers.

Travis was the PERFECT person to give advice about family photos for this Heights Hotline caller



NEW EPISODE OUT NOW@NissanUSA pic.twitter.com/TcllBjlKYb — New Heights (@newheightshow) November 25, 2026

NFL star Travis Kelce opened up on Prince William wanting to keep him out of a selfie

The football player posed with now-wife Taylor Swift, the royal, Prince George and Princess Charlotte after on of the popstar's Eras Tour concerts in London in 2024

However, she was left facing a predicament ahead of the holiday, revealing that her younger boyfriend had presumed that he would be included in the family photoshoot.

Travis was quick to assist, drawing on his own awkward encounter. Having learned his lesson from the situation with Prince William, the three-time Super Bowl winner instructed Debbie to take two sets of photos.

'I just kind of ran into this - I didn't even know I was running into this - with the Prince of Wales,' Travis began.

'I was the boyfriend of my now-wife, and he didn't necessarily want me in the photos with his daughter, or at least at the time he was like, maybe we just get photos with Taylor, just us. I completely understood that because then you didn't know if there was a forever there yet.

'You don't know, and you don't want the picture to be ruined for eternity if it doesn't work out. So I get it, I get it.

'What you got to do is you've got to take two sets of photos. Let him come on in, feel all jolly and a part of the family, and let him feel all the good feelings with the pup in there and all the kids and everything. But definitely get photos just for you, without him.

'He should understand this. He should understand this as a good man being 17 years younger than you. He should understand this.'

Both Jason and Travis also stressed that Debbie was within her right to tell her boyfriend how she felt about the situation and that he should understand not being included in the photos.

Prince William 'tried to move' Kelce out of the viral selfie the singer took with his two children

The royals also took a solo selfie with the hitmaker without Travis in the frame

During his appearance on the Graham Norton Show, Prince William admitted that he didn't understand the significance of Travis being included in the selfie.

He said that he wasn't aware that at the time Swift was yet to make her relationship with the NFL star Instagram official and admitted he was bemused at the time why Kelce was so keen to be in the photo.

As Norton recalled the Eras Tour photo, he asked whether Prince William was aware of the significance of Taylor's post.

'I wasn't until recently,' William said. 'I hadn't appreciated the significance, and actually – I was trying to move him out of the photo!'

'Travis kept coming back in, and I couldn't work out why he kept coming back in.'

The Kelce brothers hosted Prince William on New Heights back in the summer after striking up a friendship with him at the Eras Tour show.

Travis has previously insisted that he understood His Royal Highness's reluctance over the selfie, saying: 'I get it, man. I was just a boyfriend at that point. I wasn't her husband yet.'

Sports.title: Inside Raheem Sterling's rise from childhood tragedy and poverty to England superstar at the peak of his powers - but Lamborghini crash and laughing gas addiction leave him staring into the abyss
Sports.content:
In September, shortly after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession, Raheem Sterling shared a statement on social media. The goal, he implied with a picture of graffiti on a wall, was to 'be better than yesterday' and the intention was to seek 'progress over perfection', as he captioned the image. But for the former England and Manchester City star to move forward, he has had to fall a long way. The 31-year-old avoided prison, but was handed a 12-month suspended sentence and 100 hours of community service at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court after he was involved in a dangerous crash in May. Sterling had been driving his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus SUV while under the influence of laughing gas, with multiple motorists spotting him using balloons at the wheel while careening down the M25 and M3 motorways. During his sentencing hearing, Sterling revealed that he has undergone a 12-day stint in rehab soon after the arrest, after contacting UK addiction services. The number of footballers in history who have found themselves entangled with the British justice system is not a small one. But against the backdrop of Sterling's personal story, his fall is a particularly poignant one. The former international built a remarkable career out of a difficult upbringing. Raheem Sterling has been handed a suspended sentence and 100 hours of community service after being convicted of dangerous driving The former Manchester City star has experienced some of the highest heights in professional football - but now languishes without a club Sterling lost his father at the age of just two to gun violence, prompting his mother's move from his birthplace of Kingston, Jamaica to the London suburb of Neasden. Speaking to the Players' Tribune in 2018, Sterling admitted that the tragedy had 'shaped his entire life'. 'For a few years, we lived with our grandmother in Kingston, and I remember watching the other kids with their mums and just feeling really jealous,' he revealed. 'I didn't fully understand what my mum was doing for us. I just knew that she was gone. My grandma was amazing, but everybody wants their mum at that age.' His father's shocking death also inspired a gun tattoo inked on his leg above his right 'shooting' foot, there as part of a promise he had made that he 'would never touch a gun in his lifetime'. Although the tattoo prompted criticism from anti-gun campaigners in 2018, Sterling was adamant that his message was aligned with theirs, with the player backed by the FA. After moving to England, his mother Nadine found work as a cleaner. Sterling and his siblings would sometimes help her during her early morning shifts cleaning hotels at 5am before their school day started. With rent a continual challenge for the family as money was tight, they moved house often. But Sterling's prodigious talent on the football pitch was breaking through, with the winger asked to join Queens Park Rangers' youth set-up at just 10 years old. Sacrifices were made to allow for this: in 2021, Sterling released a custom football boot with New Balance paying tribute to the three buses - the 18, the 182 and 140 - he had to catch to make the return journey from home near Wembley to the west London training ground, accompanied by his older sister Lakima. 'The red double-deckers with the blue wool '80s vibe on the seats,' he reminisced. 'Spent ages on those. We'd leave at 3.15 and get home at 11 pm. Every. Single. Day. 'She'd sit upstairs in the little cafe and chill until I was done with training. Imagine being 17 years old and doing that for your little brother. And I never once heard her say, 'Nah, I don't wanna take him.' As a youngster, Sterling's footballing talent was prodigious and helped him sign with QPR at the age of 10 Five years later and Sterling had parlayed this into a move to Liverpool's academy, with the star breaking through to the first team in 2012 'At the time, I didn't understand how much she was sacrificing. Her and my mum got me here. My whole family played a massive part in my life. Without them, you wouldn't even know me.' Football was a necessary focus as well as passion, with Sterling once removed from mainstream education as a youngster and sent to Vernon House, an adapted school to help with behavioral problems. His teacher there, Chris Beschi, told the Guardian in 2018 that he had said to a young Sterling: 'If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or you'll be in prison.' But Beschi was able to see a different side to Sterling too, describing the boy as having 'a kind and innocent passion about him', and as football took over, Premier League rivals clamoured to sign him up to their youth ranks. Nadine was adamant that he should be developed outside of London to avoid any possibility of getting caught up in gang violence, and Chelsea and Arsenal's loss was Liverpool's gain, with Sterling joining the academy at the age of 15 for a then punchy fee of £500,000. After that, Sterling's career quickly gathered momentum. With the arrival of Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish in the dugout in early 2011, Sterling was moved into the Europa League squad, fast-tracking integration with established first-team stars. Playing and travel time was limited, however. Just over a year later, and the player was readied for his first senior start against Wigan Athletic, at the tender age of 17 years and 107 days. The following season saw him named as the club's Young Player of the Year and shortlisted for the PFA Young Player of the Year. By 2014, he was winning the Golden Boy award, and becoming the most expensive English footballer to date with his £49million move to Man City. But against the backdrop of success on the football pitch, there were challenging moments away from it. In 2013, Sterling was accused of two separate counts of assault, one against a former girlfriend and another against a different woman. He was found not guilty of the former, with the latter incident dropped after a witness failed to attend court. Two years later, in March 2015, Sterling was snapped by tabloids reportedly smoking from a shisha pipe. And, in a moment that spoke of what was to come, it was alleged that he might have also been using nitrous oxide for recreational purposes. Manager Brendan Rodgers was keen to protect Sterling and urged people to remember: 'Young players make mistakes.' Sterling had an uneven stint at Liverpool but put on display enough of his talent to earn him the 2014 Golden Boy award His spell on Merseyside also secured him entrance into the England squad, where he became one of the standouts of the 2010s Shortly before his move to Man City Sterling started dating Paige Milian, now his long-term partner and mother of his children (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling) The clean slate offered by Man City might have itself been appealing. Things had become somewhat tricky at Anfield, after Sterling had refused a new deal, with the player booed while on duty for England under then-manager Roy Hodgson. Rodgers and Sterling rowed publicly in the media over suggestions that he had turned down a new contract for financial reasons, and his move to the Etihad came after club legends including Steven Gerrard, Jamie Carragher and Graeme Souness had all criticised his conduct. The first season at the Etihad might have been a false start, with Sterling notably injured in March leading to the premature curtailing of his campaign, but under incoming manager Pep Guardiola, Sterling began flying. At the same time, he was underscoring his importance for England under Hodgson, and then Gareth Southgate. 'In terms of, "Can he fulfil it?", he'll give himself every chance,' Southgate said when asked if he thought Sterling might win the Ballon d'Or after victory against Kosovo in 2019. 'There are some outstanding players around - (Eden) Hazard, (Kevin) De Bruyne, Messi, Ronaldo. 'But he (Sterling) has got the drive, he's got the professionalism, he's got the ability. He's physically and mentally strong for such a small-statured lad.' And against the backdrop of his growth on the pitch, Sterling was becoming an important voice away from it too, frequently speaking out against the racism young black players were targeted with, and from personal experience. In 2017, Sterling was attacked outside Man City's training ground by a convicted football hooligan hurling racist language at him. In 2018, he suffered racist abuse on the pitch while featuring for Man City against Chelsea. Raheem Sterling: BY NUMBERS 396 Premier League appearances, 123 goals 82 England caps, 20 goals 1 Golden Ball 1 PFA Young Player Of The Season 4 Premier League titles 5 League Cups 1 FA Cup GQ magazine described Sterling as football's 'most influential player' in 2019 in recognition of his climb to the very top of the game, and for his increasingly high profile as a campaigner off the pitch. Sterling branded negative tabloid coverage as racist, and made an address to the United Nations. 'Discrimination is discrimination. It doesn't matter if it's your sexuality, or your color, you shouldn't (discriminate) at all', Sterling said, speaking to the UN Human Rights Office for the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination. 'We need – as a collective – to take responsibility. This is a new age where color can't define who you are'. Sterling also established the Raheem Sterling Foundation in 2021, which the footballer funds and which helps to support youth education projects, including fighting knife crime and helping children out of poverty. That year, he was awarded an MBE for services to racial equality in sport. As his public profile hit new heights, Sterling kept scoring, becoming Man City's seventh-highest goalscorer of all time. But limited game time under Guardiola led to a move to Chelsea for £47.5m, and on a salary worth an eye-watering £325,000 per week. Sterling was a focal point of the Man City team which achieved a staggering trophy haul in the late 2010s His move to Chelsea in 2022 set him up to be one of the stars of the club's new era under BlueCo but he failed to hit the right notes across two personally underwhelming seasons After an abortive loan move to Arsenal, Sterling signed for Feyenoord at the start of the year but did not see his deal extended past the end of the season In what might be seen as the beginning of the end, his first season in Chelsea blue failed to hit the heights required. There was chaos in west London as the club cycled through Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter, Bruno Saltor and Frank Lampard in the dugout but Sterling still bagged nine goals and a further four assists in his 38 appearances, as well as securing a place in Southgate's World Cup squad that year. Sterling made an impact in the group stages in Qatar, but was forced home after his family home was burgled. While his long-term partner Paige Milian and three children were not at the property, Sterling was shaken and flew back to Oxshott from the camp before returning in time for the quarter-final against France. While his first season with Chelsea had room for improvement at Stamford Bridge, his second was even limper. The latest manager on the club's merry-go-round, Enzo Maresca, said in August 2024 that he was going to 'struggle' for minutes, effectively frozen out. From there, his on-pitch decline was swift. An abortive loan across the city to Arsenal had the promise of a step up, but Sterling struggled just as hard for game time. A difficult time was compounded by a second break-in at his home, with the family forced to escape but luckily unharmed. On his return to Chelsea, Maresca placed him in the now-infamous bomb squad, forced to train away from the first-team players, share separate, smaller locker rooms, and all but ostracised within Cobham. Offers swirled around Sterling as they have done for all his decorated career, but the possibility of a move to Bayer Leverkusen or Juventus did not go much further than exploratory talks. A switch to nearby Fulham fell through. With money far from a motivating factor, the winger opted not to accept a lucrative contract and move to Saudi Arabia. Instead, Sterling stayed out of the game until his contract was mutually terminated in January of this year. Hopes of finding that at his next club Feyenoord evaporated on his debut. Signed until the end of the 2025-26 season, Sterling stepped onto the pitch in February after nine months out and looked rusty. The critics were brutal, but head coach Robin van Persie did his best to defend his new player. It was too harsh to judge him over just six or eight weeks, he stressed. Within weeks, he was back in the UK, with his arrest coming in May. Any offers that might have come his way over the summer have subsequently dried up. Sterling crashed his £270,000 Lambourghini Urus while driving under the influence The arrest took place shortly after his time in Rotterdam came to an end, with the star pleading guilty in September Since the arrest, Sterling has been keeping a low profile and focusing on his family (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling) With offers from football clubs quieter, the winger has focused on other ventures including his Playmaker Films (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling) Sterling has since worked on his Playmaker Films, a content agency, and launched 'The Cage', a grassroots football competition where teams of four face off for eight minutes with £5,000 on the line. 'Football's about expressing yourself,' he said when interviewed about why he created the contest, which showcases individuality on caged pitches similar to ones he would have learned to play on. 'The game is a beautiful thing'. Sterling's story is of a remarkable rise from adversity to the highest levels in professional sport. His private life has clearly been complicated - District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed his drug problem had 'become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career'. Any way back seems a long way off.
