Sports.title: Featured Comment: Herta deserves credit for trying to make the switch from IndyCar | Brief
Sports.content:
Colton Herta’s bold attempt to make the leap from IndyCar to Formula 1 – via Formula 2 – appears to be over with yesterday’s news he won’t return to the feeder series this year.

It was always a risk, one I’m glad he took and sorry it didn’t work out. I’ve loved the cross overs when they’ve happened.

I loved it when Jacques Villeneuve turned up with his day-glo helmet, gangsta rap overalls and bleached hair. Juan Pablo Montoya ‘effing and jeffing’ and going out of his way to not show Michael Schumacher any respect. Nigel Mansell just being in Milwaukee, let alone winning. Alex Zanardi leaving and winning in that beautiful Target-liveried Reynard then coming back and doing nothing with Williams. Sebastian Bourdais being a winner and also very much not a winner…

It’s a risk, and one that seldom pays off on both sides of the Atlantic. Though Hill, Clark, Fittipaldi, Andretti prove it’s possible, and I guess Villeneuve also if we ignore Sauber, Renault and most of what he says.

It didn’t work for Colton, but he wanted to make the jump and I hope this doesn’t dissuade others from giving it a go in the future. You never know unless you try and most drivers end up not succeeding somewhere in their career, it may as well be because of a leap into the unknown.

@Bernasaurus

Sports.title: WBA Sets 75-25 Split for Teofimo Lopez Against Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
It’s not looking good for Teofimo Lopez to dodge his mandatory obligations at welterweight. Today, the WBA called a purse bid for December 4 in Cypress, Texas, for a fight between WBA welterweight Super Champion Teofimo and Jack Catterall with a slanted 75/25 purse split.

Financially, that should make Teofimo happy. Even with three-quarters of the money guaranteed, he’s shown no eagerness to sign to fight the mandatory he inherited after his win over WBA champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero by majority decision on August 22. Lopez needs a special permit from the WBA to avoid Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs), but he may not get his wish. It’s understandable why Teofimo doesn’t want to fight Catterall. It’s a style that he’s struggled with, and it’s unlikely he would win.

Teofimo (23-2, 13 KOs) wants to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in what would be a lucrative unification, where even if he loses, he’d still do well financially. He needs the WBA title for purse negotiations more so than it being a valuable chip to create more interest in a fight with Ryan.

Teofimo’s title isn’t why fans are interested in seeing the fight. For him, it’s just a negotiation tool to get a better deal, because he lacks Ryan’s popularity to get an even split. Even with a title, you can argue that Teofimo doesn’t rate a 50/50 purse split.

Catterall Risk Explains Lopez Delay

If this were an easy mark, Lopez would be overjoyed at receiving a 75/25 gift split from the WBA. Catterall’s style is similar to Shakur Stevenson’s, which left Teofimo baffled and helpless in a unanimous decision loss over 12 rounds earlier this year at Madison Square Garden on January 31. Teofimo looked embarrassingly bad in that fight. The judges scored it 119 to 109 on all three cards, and he was outlanded 165 to 72.

Defensively, Catterall isn’t as sharp as Shakur, but he’s close enough to be the same kind of nightmare for Teofimo. On offense, Catterall is superior to Shakur, and coupled with his defensive ability, he would be a difficult problem for Teofimo to try and figure out. Besides all that, the pressure that Teofimo would be under would be severe if he needs to defeat Catterall to get to the lucrative payday fight against Ryan Garcia.

If he gets beaten by Catterall, he can forget about fighting Ryan for the time being. Unlike his loss to Shakur, Teofimo wouldn’t be given a straight title shot immediately after. He’d have to rebuild and get in line, which is what he should have had to do after losing to Stevenson instead of being given a crack at Rolly’s WBA title.

Catterall captured his WBA regular welterweight title by beating former mandatory Shakhram Giyasov by a wide 12-round unanimous decision last May. Giyasov was the mandatory challenger that Rolly was avoiding. Now, we’re seeing the new WBA champion Teofimo trying to give Catterall similar treatment. The WBA can stop this cycle by rejecting Teofimo’s request for a special permit.

It’s easy to predict what Lopez’s next move will be if the WBA rejects his appeal. Vacating the WBA belt will be the easiest way of getting Catterall out of his path to a fight with Ryan. Teofimo will still get a nice payday against Ryan, but probably not as nice as it would be if he still had his WBA title.

Sports.title: Brian Mendoza Replaces Keith Thurman in Weak Vergil Ortiz Jr. Co-Feature
Sports.content:
PBC and Golden Boy Promotions made it official today with Brian Mendoza replacing Keith Thurman as Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s opponent for his 10-round co-feature middleweight bout on December 5 at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona.

Ortiz Jr. and Mendoza will be fighting on the undercard of WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion David Benavidez’s unification bout against WBC champion Michal Cieslak on DAZN PPV and Prime Video.

The addition of Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) has received mixed views from fans. Many of them view the 32-year-old as a poor replacement, given his 1-3 record in his last four fights. That’s not exactly top shelf unless losing is the benchmark requirement used to get enlisted as a fill-in opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.

Back in Mediocrity Since Fundora

What Mendoza has got going for him is that he knocked out Sebastian Fundora in the seventh round in April 2023 in a huge upset at the time. Fundora was beating the living daylights out of Mendoza for the first six rounds until he got careless in the seventh and got clipped. Since then, Mendoza’s career has slipped back to what it was before that win. That was his textbook Cinderella night, where he got lucky in a fight that he was getting beaten up in.

What’s interesting is that fans online see this as an upgrade over 38-year-old Thurman, just because of his win over Fundora. If you look at Mendoza’s results since that upset, he’s a major downgrade, and that’s saying a lot because Thurman was not a great opponent. He’s not a middleweight, and definitely not young.

Tim Tszyu beat Mendoza by a wide 12-round unanimous decision in October 2023. That fight was an example of Mendoza being brought back down to earth. It wasn’t even slightly a close fight. It looked like Mendoza wandered into the ring from the crowd, and Tszyu took advantage by beating the stuffing out of him. Serhii Bohachuk did the same thing to Mendoza in a clash for the interim WBC junior middleweight title in March 2024.

The only win for Mendoza in the last three years came against journeyman Jesus Antonio Rojas (12-11-2, 10 KOs). It took that level of opponent for Mendoza to snap his two-fight losing streak. In Mendoza’s last fight, he returned to his losing ways, getting trounced by Yoenis Tellez by a one-sided 10-round unanimous decision in March 2026.

Basically, what we’re seeing here is not a dangerous threat being used as a replacement opponent for Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs), who recently looked like pure gold in wins over Israil Madrimov, Bohachuk, and Erickson Lubin.

A Cheap Showcase for Ortiz Jr.

Yanking Mendoza out of his fight with Eric Priest enabled Sampson Boxing, TGB Promotions, and Golden Boy Promotions to save money on finding a quality opponent. It’s a showcase fight for Ortiz Jr. Ideally, they should have spent some money to enlist a quality middleweight contender like Yoenli Hernandez to put Ortiz Jr. in a sink-or-swim fight.

What Mendoza does have going for him is a strong chin, as he’s never been knocked out in his career. So if the idea is for Ortiz Jr. to get some rounds in to sharpen up after a year on the shelf, Mendoza is the guy for the job. However, the referee may step in and halt this fight anyway because of the likely one-sided nature of it.

Entertainment-wise, Mendoza eating hard shots from Ortiz Jr. is not fun to watch in a PPV co-feature slot. Fans want competitive fights, not slaughters.

Ortiz Jr. is 28 years old, making the move up to middleweight, and has still accomplished little in his career. It’s got to bug him that he sees fighters like Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis taking the express route to superstardom, leaving him behind. The difference is, Ennis has been a risk-taker from day one, hasn’t feasted on weak opposition, and has stayed active. In contrast, Ortiz Jr. hasn’t fought the best, and he’s missed a lot of time in his career due to health and promotional issues.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Gets Worst Possible Replacement In Martin Bakole
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder is facing the worst possible replacement opponent for him in his December 11th fight in Cardiff against the heavy-handed Martin Bakole. It’s not the type of opponent that the 41-year-old Wilder’s legs can deal with at this stage of his career.

Boxing analyst Sergio Mora pointed out this week that Wilder no longer has the mobility at his age to avoid being walked down by a big puncher like Bakole. He feels that Wilder will have problems keeping Bakole off of him and will be forced to slug it out right off the bat from round 1 on December 11th.

“If you don’t fight him off the right way, he’s going to mow you down. And you got to have legs to do that,” said Mora on Chris Mannix’s podcast.

Wilder never really had great leg movement. If you look at his earliest fights against Harold Sconiers and Bermane Stiverne, he wasn’t a mover. He was winning by unleashing his right hand on them. Back then, before the two later shoulder surgeries on that side, Wilder’s right hand was lethal. It made up for his lack of mobility and boxing skills.

After his originally scheduled opponent, Jai Opetaia, dropped out due to a hand injury, the former WBC heavyweight champion Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) wanted a rematch with Derek Chisora or a fight with Jarrell Miller. Neither was selected, which is good news for fans. Both are long in the tooth and don’t have the kind of power that could erase Wilder the way Bakole can.

For what Wilder is aiming for, a world title shot in his next fight, he should have to fight and beat the likes of Bakole to get his wish. It would look pathetic if Wilder is given a title shot after beating an old war horse like Chisora a second time or getting past Miller.

Why Bakole Is A Dangerous Gamble

Despite Bakole being held to a draw against Efe Ajagba in his last outing, and knocked out in the second round by Joseph Parker in a short-notice fight in 2025, Bakole still has power in both hands. He’s dangerous up close when he lands cleanly.

In those two fights, Bakole wasn’t in the best shape in terms of his weight. For this one, he’d been training to fight Solomon Adebayo on the December 11th undercard. Being in shape for this fight means Bakole will be a constant threat to Wilder in the early rounds.

If Wilder’s right hand is back to full strength, he could stop Bakole. However, Wilder hasn’t shown his once-devastating power since 2022, when he knocked out Robert Helenius in the 1st round. Mora and Mannix agreed that Jarrell Miller would have been the better choice to sell the matchup without carrying the same threat as Bakole. The organizers made the right choice because the card needed a high-drama matchup. We don’t see that in the main event or any of the undercard fights.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Picks Safe Money Fights Over Young Sharks
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) is already looking past his December 11 clash against Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) at a 1:30 AM UK start in Cardiff to map out his final two retirement fights. The early morning start time for the Joshua fight is to satisfy American viewers on Netflix, and it’s obviously not ideal for the aging 38-year-old Fury.

Staying up late will be hard on his body and could lead to another off performance, as we saw in his two defeats against Oleksandr Usyk. The last thing Fury needs is to look slow and lose to Joshua, setting a bad start to his three-fight retirement plan.

Today, the Cardiff Council’s licensing sub-committee granted a special variation, extending the stadium’s operating hours until 3:00 AM. This move made it possible for the Fury vs. Joshua fight to begin at 1:30 AM local time in Cardiff.

Also today, Fury revealed his schedule on OOOSCH TV, saying he will fight only two more times after Joshua. He wants a rematch with Joshua if the first fight is competitive, followed by a trilogy bout against Oleksandr Usyk.

“I’m interested in fighting Anthony Joshua, maybe rematch him if it’s a good fight, and then maybe [have] a trilogy with Oleksandr Usyk if it makes sense and if I get a fair shake,” Fury told OOOSCH TV. “There’s nobody else, really, that I’m interested in fighting.”

It’s not a coincidence that the two fighters Fury plans on facing to end his career, Joshua and Usyk, are the biggest money heavyweights in the division. Even if Fury loses to both, he’ll be paid far better than if he were to face another top contender, like Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois, or Agit Kabayel.

Ideally, it would be better for the sport if Fury faced one of those heavyweights or Moses Itauma to serve as a springboard to make a star out of one of the younger contenders or champions. Fighters in the past were willing to do that, yet we see it less and less in an era where fighters are more protective, selfish, careful, and money-focused. As such, you see Fury aiming for 37-year-old Joshua and 39-year-old Usyk for his final two fights instead of the young guns, Dubois and Itauma.

Fury Overlooks His Recent Form

What we saw of Joshua and Fury in recent fights was lackluster performances, showing that both fighters are long in the tooth ahead of their December 11 fight. Those outings may be one reason why there is so little interest in their clash next month. They both looked so feeble that fans can’t get excited about a fight between two faded heavyweights.

To make it interesting for fans, it would have been more appealing to see Fury and Joshua walk the plank against one of the big four: Itauma, Dubois, Kabayel, or Hrgovic. Fans would tune in just to see how the older heavyweights hold up. Putting them in together is not appealing in the least, because there’s no real gain for the winner in a battle of shot fighters. It only gets interesting if you throw Joshua and Fury in the ring with one of those ravenous sharks to see how they fare.

Fury looked terrible stopping 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in seven rounds in Thailand on July 24. One day later in Jeddah, the 37-year-old Joshua was surprisingly dropped by what was supposed to be a soft opponent, Kristian Prenga, before coming back to stop him in the second round.

That fight was very strange, as Prenga didn’t throw any punches in the second round after having Joshua on the verge of being halted as the first round ended. Why not go for the kill? I’ve never seen anything like it, and Joshua got lucky. If Prenga had thrown anything, he likely would have finished Joshua at the beginning of the second round.

Interestingly, the December 11 fight contract doesn’t include a rematch clause for their vacant WBA heavyweight title. That leaves it up to Turki Alalshikh and Netflix to decide whether they wish to finance a second fight between Joshua and Fury. It would be perfectly understandable if they pass. If both look poor or if the card bombs in bringing in subscribers to Netflix, I don’t see why they would want to pay for a second fight.

That goes for putting the winner or the loser in with Usyk. A fight between Fury or Joshua and Usyk would be expensive and wouldn’t produce the numbers or entertainment needed to make it worthwhile. Putting them in with Itauma and watching the timer to see how long they last would be far more fun to watch.

Usyk already beat Fury twice in 2024, and he’s talking about moving down to cruiserweight to fight champion David Benavidez instead of waiting for Fury. You can respect that.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Claims Martin Bakole Win Earns Title Shot
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder believes a victory over his replacement opponent, Martin Bakole, on December 11 in Cardiff will pave the way to a world heavyweight title shot. As wacky as this sounds, it wouldn’t be a shock if it actually happens. The division is starved for recognizable names, and if nothing else, the 41-year-old Wilder is well known.

Turki Alalshikh confirmed that Bakole (21-2-1, 16 KOs) would replace the injured Jai Opetaia as Wilder’s opponent for their co-feature fight on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium.

Bakole is a decent opponent for Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs), but hardly the type of contender that would erase six years of repeated losses. Definitely not good enough to vault Wilder into a world title fight.

“We’re going to be fighting Martin Bakole. He is next, and then after that it’s going to be crazy,” said Wilder in a social media video. “Once I beat him, I’m not going to move forward with the information I’ve received, but once I beat him, you’re looking at the new heavyweight champion of the world. And the new two-time heavyweight champion. Martin, here we come. I appreciate you for accepting the opportunity. Let’s give the fans and the people something to talk about for the rest of their lives.”

Instead of Wilder hoping for a shot at one of the other heavyweight champions, he should be campaigning for the winner of the Fury vs. Joshua WBA title fight. That’s the bigger payday by far.

If Joshua and Wilder both come out victorious, promoters can finally make their long-awaited fight, as long as Fury doesn’t push for an immediate rematch.

How The Title Path Works

Deontay has been beltless since Fury knocked him out in February 2020. Beating 42-year-old Derek Chisora by a 12-round split decision in April and stopping little-known Tyrrell Anthony Herndon in June 2025 in his last two fights aren’t enough to overcome being stopped in five rounds by Zhilei Zhang and beaten by Joseph Parker by a 12-round decision.

Still, Wilder’s commercial leverage gives him an edge over more deserving contenders in the division who have been grinding hard and winning fights. His long 18-year pro career has given him plenty of opportunities to be seen by fans, and that should help when it comes to being picked by one of the current champions.

It’s still asking a lot of Wilder to defeat Bakole. If Bakole comes in near 300 lbs, his punching power could still take out Wilder if he lasts long enough to land something. Wilder’s advantage is that Bakole hasn’t looked good since beating Jared Anderson in 2024. If the ‘Bronze Bomber’ doesn’t take Bakole out early, he can forget about his dream of fighting for a world title.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Threatens to Smack Rayo Valenzuela in Leaked DMs After Walking Away From Zuffa
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela posted a screenshot of an Instagram message exchange between him and Shakur Stevenson on Tuesday, showing the bitterness on Rayo’s part after Shakur left Zuffa without accepting an offer to fight him.

Rayo (16-3, 10 KOs) had hoped to fight Shakur (25-0, 11 KOs) while they were briefly teammates, but Shakur rejected Zuffa’s offer.

Posting the exchange on X, Valenzuela captioned the image, “Saying everything but ‘let’s fight!'”

Valenzuela’s post comes after he was interviewed by Ring Magazine and called Shakur “weak” for leaving Zuffa Boxing instead of being a team player and agreeing to fight him in an in-house contest. Stevenson signed with Zuffa on July 9th of this year, but the two mutually parted ways three months later in October, with Stevenson failing to fight once while signed.

The comments from Valenzuela clearly bothered Shakur, causing him to slide into Valenzuela’s DMs.

“Say bh ass n* watch how loose you is with yo words, All that calling me a p*y st watch that.. Ion play them type of games,” said Shakur.

“Shut yo ass up and fight!” said Valenzuela.

“U a b*h, That’s why u clout chasing. I thought u was more solid then that, But look u using them disrespectful ass words stand on that st when u run into me!!” said Stevenson.

“You a b***h and ain’t nobody scared of you. We can fight next and settle it!” said Valenzuela.

“Just know I will smack the holy st out of u if u keep disrespecting me,” said Stevenson.

“I used to look at you and be like I’d beat tf outta dude!” said Valenzuela.

The interaction shows the bad blood between Rayo and Shakur from the brief period when they were both with Zuffa Boxing. It was a logical fight to make, but Shakur was aiming higher, wanting a bigger money fight. Being dismissed as inadequate has likely gotten on Valenzuela’s nerves because this is a fight that could have easily happened. Stevenson turned it down.

Stevenson would have been better off if he had taken it because he’s just been sitting inactive. At least he would have gotten the opportunity to be seen by fans while showing he’s a team player by fighting one of Zuffa’s fighters. Turki Alalshikh owns 60% of Zuffa, and it would have worked well for Stevenson’s career to fight one of his fighters instead of wasting time trying to get a fight with Devin Haney (31-0, 15 KOs) while insisting on a weight handicap.

In Valenzuela’s interview with Ring Magazine, he was critical of Shakur for trying to get a catchweight against Haney and Raymond Muratalla (24-0, 17 KOs), viewing that behavior as showing weakness.

Shakur is now a free agent and has a purse bid scheduled for November 30th for his mandatory defense against Muratalla. No one has signed Stevenson, and it may not be worth it if he’s going to price himself out and waste time trying to get weight advantages for fights.

Valenzuela is still with Zuffa Boxing and is in negotiations for a fight against WBA lightweight champion Floyd Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs). The two have a December 11th deadline before a purse bid is called.

If Stevenson wanted to smack Valenzuela, he had the perfect chance to do that when he was signed with Zuffa. They wanted the fight, but he turned it down and left the company.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Has Earned His Shot at Usyk
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk is still the best heavyweight in the world, and Agit Kabayel is the man I’d most like to see him fight next. Usyk has already beaten Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua, and Daniel Dubois twice apiece. Kabayel brings a different test. He does his best work to the body, and he’s stopped heavyweights who were supposed to make him pay for coming forward.

Kabayel makes his first defense of the WBC title against Nelson Hysa on Saturday in Düsseldorf. He was elevated after Usyk vacated the belt in June, but the wins that make his case came before the promotion. Kabayel stopped Frank Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang, then took out Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. Sanchez has since knocked out unbeaten Richard Torrez Jr. in two rounds, a result that makes Kabayel’s win over him look even better.

What Kabayel would ask of Usyk

Kabayel went downstairs against Frank Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang and stopped them both. Against Usyk, I’d watch what he does after the first body shot. Can he stay close enough to land a second, or does Usyk turn him and make him walk in all over again? I’d pick Usyk, but that’s the exchange I’d want to see in the eighth or ninth round, when Kabayel has had time to slow him down.

Dubois has had the best year of the other champions. He got up twice in May to stop Fabio Wardley in the 11th and take the WBO belt, then finished the rematch in two rounds in October. There’s a better fight for him in a rematch with IBF champion Filip Hrgovic, whom he stopped on cuts in 2024. Hrgovic has since stopped Moses Itauma in nine rounds to win his title. He entered the ring after Dubois beat Wardley and asked him about fighting in March. That rematch would put two belts on the line and give Hrgovic a chance to answer for his only defeat.

Fury and Joshua will get more attention in Cardiff on December 11 than any of those fights. British fans have waited years to see them settle it, and the winner will have a big win to sell. Usyk has already fought both men over 24 rounds each. Kabayel has spent the past two years earning the opportunity to show what he can do with twelve.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Offers to Fight Liam Paro Over Haney VADA Dispute
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia (26-2, 20 KOs, 1 NC) has stepped forward, offering Liam Paro a fight on four weeks’ notice if he pulls out of his December 19th welterweight unification clash against Devin Haney at the Chase Center.

Garcia posted on X today in response to IBF champion Paro (28-1, 16 KOs) talking about pulling out of his fight against Haney in San Francisco because of his stubborn and strange refusal to enroll in VADA testing.

“Liam Paro I will fight you with 4 weeks notice If you decide to pull out This man is up to no good,” Garcia said on X.

Ryan’s noble gesture gives Paro a fallback position if he decides he doesn’t want to take the risk of fighting Haney, whom he’d have no way of knowing is clean or dirty. In terms of money, Paro fighting Ryan would give him a shot at making more cash. The Australian PPV buys would likely be huge for a fight between Paro and Garcia.

If Haney loses his fight with Paro, he should be plenty concerned because it strengthens Ryan’s hand if he captures the IBF belt from the Australian fighter. Winning a second belt would place Ryan in a position where he could pick anyone he pleases and get the lion’s share of the loot. He wouldn’t need Haney.

Thus far, Haney (33-0, 15 KOs, 1 NC) and his dad, Bill, have given no signs of changing their minds about enrolling in VADA. I don’t know what led to this resistance to being tested. You can argue that when some fighters get popular, it changes them.

Bill made it clear that California State Athletic Commission urine testing is plenty and feels that it is too late for VADA testing despite there being almost a month to go before the fight. Ryan posted this in reaction today: “Devin scrambling for the Victor Conte formula as we speak. He needs to be watched asap as he calls all the people he can to figure it out. You are 4 weeks before the fight; there should be no reason you aren’t testing.”

The Testing Reversal Looks Suspicious

A couple of years ago, Garcia tested positive for Ostarine during a VADA test in April 2024 for his fight with Haney in Brooklyn. For years, the Haneys favored strict VADA enrollment from every opponent, including Devin’s last fight a year ago against Brian Norman Jr. in November 2025 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. For Haney to suddenly decide against VADA testing ahead of his bout against the dangerous southpaw, Paro, raises questions. Why now? That’s what Ryan is wondering about.

Paro Won’t Cave on Paperwork

On June 24, Paro won the IBF title with a 12-round unanimous decision over Lewis Crocker (22-1). Now holding the IBF belt, Paro has no reason to want to go into Haney’s hometown of San Francisco for drug testing that doesn’t include blood testing.

One positive for Haney is that if Paro does walk away over the drug testing issue, it enables Haney to hold onto his WBO belt without risk of losing it. So in theory, he can face Ryan while still holding that title and his unbeaten record. The downside is that his negotiating leverage would take a hit, placing him in a position where he would be facing the far more popular Ryan Garcia while holding just one title, and coming off of a 13-month layoff. Whatever status gain he got from his win over Norman Jr., he’ll have lost it due to sitting for ages and whiffing on fights against Paro and Shakur Stevenson.

If Haney stays on the December 19th card without Paro, he’d still need to find a quality opponent because that’s a DAZN PPV event. That network isn’t going to be happy if Haney finds a scrub as his opponent to keep him safe from losing his WBO belt. Bringing in a quality opponent on less than one month’s notice will put the ring-rusty Haney at risk of losing his strap, which is his golden ticket for a second fight against Ryan.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s legal framework for energy transition: Is the Renewable Energy Act, 2011 (ACT 832), fit for the country’s net-zero ambitions?
Ghana News.content:
By:

Ananpansah Bartholomew Abraham (AB)

(DBE,LLB, BSC, MSC)

0241129910/0200704844

Abstract:

Ghana’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2060 presents significant opportunities and challenges for the country’s energy sector. However, the principal legislation governing renewable energy development, the Renewable Energy Act, 2011 (Act 832), was enacted more than a decade before the country adopted its current long-term energy transition ambitions. This raises an important question as to whether the existing statutory framework is sufficiently equipped to facilitate the transition towards a low-carbon economy.

This article critically examines the adequacy of Act 832, as amended by the Renewable Energy (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act 1045), in advancing Ghana’s renewable energy and net-zero commitments. Through doctrinal legal analysis, it examines the relevant constitutional provisions, statutory framework, judicial decisions, international climate commitments and national energy policies. It argues that although Act 832 provides an important foundation for renewable energy development, its regulatory and promotional orientation falls short of establishing an enforceable decarbonisation framework. In particular, the absence of binding statutory renewable energy targets, the weakening of investment certainty following the amendment of the feed-in tariff regime, and the inadequate integration of climate obligations into renewable energy regulation undermine its effectiveness. The article consequently advocates statutory reform through enforceable renewable energy targets, improved electricity purchase guarantees, adequate financing mechanisms and stronger institutional coordination with Ghana’s climate governance framework.

Keywords: Renewable Energy; Energy Transition; Net-Zero Emissions; Act 832; Climate Change; Ghana; Energy Law.

Introduction

The transition towards sustainable and low-carbon energy systems has become an important component of contemporary energy governance. Globally, governments are increasingly adopting legislative, regulatory and policy measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while ensuring energy security and sustainable economic development. Ghana is no exception. With considerable potential in solar, wind, biomass and other renewable energy resources, the country has an opportunity to diversify its energy mix and gradually reduce its dependence on fossil-fuel-based electricity generation.

The constitutional foundation for environmental protection in Ghana is reflected in article 36(9) of the 1992 Constitution, which requires the State to take appropriate measures to protect and safeguard the national environment for posterity. This constitutional responsibility is reinforced by Ghana’s participation in international climate governance, particularly its ratification of the Paris Agreement in 2016 and the submission of its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in 2021. Under the updated NDC, Ghana committed to achieving an unconditional greenhouse gas emission reduction of 24.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO₂e) by 2030, with an additional 39.4 MtCO₂e reduction conditional on international support, bringing the overall target to 64 MtCO₂e.[1]

Furthermore, Ghana’s Energy Transition and Investment Plan establishes a pathway towards achieving net-zero emissions by 2060. This ambition requires substantial changes in the production, distribution and consumption of energy, alongside the mobilisation of significant public and private investment.

Notwithstanding these commitments, Ghana's energy sector continues to face considerable dependence on thermal generation. The challenge, therefore, is not merely the availability of renewable energy resources or the existence of national policy commitments, but whether the country's legal and regulatory institutions possess the necessary authority and mechanisms to translate those commitments into measurable outcomes.

At the centre of this discussion is the Renewable Energy Act, 2011 (Act 832), as amended by the Renewable Energy (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act 1045). Although the legislation provides a framework for promoting renewable energy development, its original design predates Ghana's current net-zero ambition.

This article examines whether the existing statutory framework is adequate to support Ghana's energy transition. It contends that Act 832 remains largely a promotional and regulatory instrument rather than a comprehensive legislative framework for decarbonisation. It further argues that without targeted statutory reforms, Ghana's net-zero commitments risk remaining policy aspirations rather than enforceable obligations.

Methodology and Scope of the Study:

This article adopts a doctrinal legal research methodology. It examines the relevant constitutional provisions, legislation, judicial decisions, international instruments and national energy policy documents to assess the legal and institutional foundations of Ghana's renewable energy transition.

Particular attention is given to Act 832 and its 2020 amendment, the constitutional provisions governing environmental protection and international business transactions, and the implications of relevant Supreme Court decisions for renewable energy investment.

The analysis also draws on Ghana's updated NDC, the Energy Transition and Investment Plan, the Renewable Energy Master Plan and relevant academic commentary. The objective is to determine whether the existing legal framework creates sufficiently clear, enforceable and financially sustainable obligations to facilitate the country's transition towards net-zero emissions. Ghana's Legal and Institutional Framework for Renewable Energy Development:

3.1 The Renewable Energy Act, 2011 (Act 832)

Act 832 constitutes the principal legislative framework for the development, management and utilisation of renewable energy resources in Ghana. Section 1 identifies its central objective as facilitating the development and utilisation of renewable energy sources for the production of heat and power in an efficient and environmentally sustainable manner.

The Act also seeks to create an enabling environment for investment, diversify energy supply, improve electricity access, promote indigenous technological capacity and encourage public education on renewable energy.

Institutionally, the legislation provides for regulatory oversight by the Energy Commission, while the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) performs important functions relating to electricity pricing and tariffs.

The significance of Act 832 cannot be understated. It provides the legal foundation upon which renewable energy generation, licensing, procurement and grid integration are regulated. Nevertheless, its principal orientation is the promotion and orderly regulation of renewable energy development rather than the imposition of legally enforceable emissions reduction obligations.

This distinction becomes particularly important when the legislation is assessed against Ghana's 2060 net-zero ambition.

3.2 The Renewable Energy (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act 1045)

The 2020 amendment substantially restructured the renewable energy procurement framework.

Under the amended section 25, a competitive procurement scheme was introduced, comprising tendering and auction arrangements. The amendment requires renewable electricity procurement by public utilities to follow an open, competitive and transparent process. It also empowers the Energy Commission, in consultation with the PURC, to determine procurement targets as part of annual energy supply and demand plans.

Section 26 was similarly revised. It provides for the procurement of electricity from consumer generators under a net-metering arrangement and requires certain fossil-fuel-based electricity suppliers and other companies contributing to greenhouse gas emissions to invest in non-utility-scale renewable energy projects to offset emissions and mitigate climate change.

Additionally, section 30A establishes a net-metering scheme intended to encourage self-generation of renewable electricity for electricity cost reduction or climate change mitigation, rather than income generation.

One of the most significant consequences of the amendment, however, was the repeal of sections 27 to 29, together with the removal of the original feed-in tariff framework.

Although competitive procurement can promote efficiency and reduce procurement costs, the removal of guaranteed tariff arrangements raises concerns about investment certainty. This is particularly relevant in renewable energy projects, which often require substantial initial capital investment and long-term revenue predictability.

Consequently, the amendment presents a regulatory tension between achieving competitive electricity procurement and maintaining sufficient financial incentives to attract renewable energy investors. Critical Assessment of Act 832 Against Ghana's Net-Zero Commitments:

The adequacy of Act 832 must be assessed not merely by reference to its original objectives but also by considering the demands of Ghana's present energy transition commitments. Three principal weaknesses emerge from this assessment.

4.1 Absence of Binding Statutory Renewable Energy Targets

A fundamental weakness of Act 832 is the absence of a clear, legally binding national renewable electricity target directly linked to Ghana's net-zero commitments.

Although section 25(3) of the amended Act empowers the Energy Commission, in consultation with the PURC, to determine procurement targets as part of annual energy supply and demand plans, the legislation does not establish a comprehensive statutory renewable electricity trajectory with specific long-term milestones.

The Renewable Energy Master Plan, for instance, identifies a renewable energy penetration target of 10 per cent and an installed capacity ambition of approximately 1,363.63 MW by 2030. However, these targets are contained in policy instruments rather than being expressly entrenched as binding obligations under Act 832.

The distinction between statutory obligations and policy aspirations is important. While policy documents provide strategic direction, their implementation may depend substantially on administrative discretion, political priorities and available resources.

Consequently, the absence of a clearly enforceable statutory target weakens accountability and makes it difficult to measure the extent to which relevant public institutions are legally required to deliver the country's renewable energy ambitions.

A legislative framework designed to support a net-zero transition should go beyond encouraging renewable energy investment. It should establish measurable obligations against which institutional performance can be assessed.

4.2 Weakening of Investment Certainty Following the Removal of the Feed-in Tariff Framework

A second concern relates to the removal of the original feed-in tariff framework through Act 1045.

The feed-in tariff arrangement under the original Act was intended to guarantee the purchase of electricity generated from renewable energy sources through a structured purchase obligation and regulated tariff mechanism.

The repeal of the relevant provisions in 2020 fundamentally changed the investment environment. Although the competitive procurement framework introduced by the amendment may encourage cost efficiency, it does not necessarily provide the same degree of revenue certainty associated with a guaranteed tariff arrangement.

Renewable energy projects are generally capital-intensive and require predictable revenue streams to attract long-term financing. Where investors are uncertain about procurement arrangements, pricing mechanisms and the availability of enforceable purchase commitments, the cost of capital may increase and project development may become less attractive.

Furthermore, although section 26(3) imposes an investment obligation on certain fossil-fuel-related companies to support non-utility-scale renewable energy projects, the effectiveness of this provision depends on the determination and implementation of the relevant investment requirements.

The absence of sufficiently clear implementation timelines and effective enforcement mechanisms raises questions about the practical impact of the obligation.

Similarly, the net-metering framework under section 30A is primarily intended to support electricity cost reduction and climate mitigation rather than commercial electricity generation. While this is a useful mechanism for encouraging decentralised renewable energy adoption, it cannot independently provide the scale of investment required for Ghana's broader energy transition.

The financing challenge is further compounded by concerns surrounding the operational effectiveness and capitalisation of the Renewable Energy Fund. A fund without predictable and adequate financial resources cannot effectively reduce investment barriers or support the development of commercially viable renewable energy projects.

4.3 Constitutional and Contractual Uncertainty in Renewable Energy Investment

A further issue concerns the constitutional requirements governing international business transactions involving the Government of Ghana.

Article 181(5) of the 1992 Constitution provides that the provisions of article 181 relating to loans shall, with the necessary modifications, apply to international business or economic transactions to which the Government is a party.

The Supreme Court's decision in Attorney-General v Faroe Atlantic Co Ltd demonstrates the importance of parliamentary approval in the enforcement of qualifying international business transactions. The decision established that transactions falling within article 181(5) require the constitutionally prescribed parliamentary approval.

The Supreme Court subsequently considered the application of this constitutional requirement in Republic v High Court (Commercial Division), Accra; Ex parte Attorney-General (Balkan Energy Ghana Ltd and Others Interested Parties). The proceedings concerned a power purchase agreement between the Government of Ghana and Balkan Energy Ghana Limited and the constitutional implications of the absence of parliamentary approval.

These decisions have important implications for renewable energy investment, particularly where projects involve foreign investors, government-backed power purchase agreements or other international commercial arrangements.

Although parliamentary approval serves an important constitutional accountability function, uncertainty regarding the application and timing of the approval process may create additional risks for investors and financiers.

Act 832 does not adequately address this constitutional dimension of renewable energy project development. A comprehensive energy transition framework should therefore incorporate clear procedures and institutional safeguards to ensure that relevant power purchase agreements and international investment arrangements satisfy constitutional requirements from the outset. The Relationship Between Ghana's Renewable Energy Legislation and Climate Governance:

The assessment of Act 832 would be incomplete without considering the broader climate governance framework.

Ghana's obligations under the Paris Agreement and its updated NDC establish an important international and national policy foundation for emissions reduction. However, international climate commitments must be supported by domestic legislative and institutional arrangements capable of facilitating implementation.

The Environmental Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1124), represents an important development in this regard. Among other things, the legislation establishes the Ghana Carbon Registry under section 150 and provides for the establishment of a Carbon Market Committee under section 151.

These provisions create an institutional foundation for the registration, tracking and coordination of carbon market activities and internationally transferred mitigation outcomes.

The existence of this framework presents an opportunity to strengthen the relationship between renewable energy regulation and climate governance.

For instance, renewable energy projects may contribute to national emissions reduction objectives while also participating in appropriately regulated carbon market arrangements. However, such opportunities require coordination between the institutions responsible for energy regulation, environmental protection and carbon market administration.

The absence of an express and comprehensive statutory relationship between Act 832 and Ghana's wider climate governance framework creates the possibility of regulatory fragmentation.

It is therefore necessary to ensure that renewable energy legislation is aligned with the Environmental Protection Act, 2025, and Ghana's evolving climate policy architecture. Independent Assessment and Proposed Legal Reforms:

In my assessment, the central difficulty with Act 832 is not necessarily the absence of political commitment to renewable energy development, but rather the limitations of its legislative design.

The Act was enacted primarily to promote and regulate renewable energy development. However, the demands of a net-zero transition require a more comprehensive framework that establishes clear legal responsibilities, measurable targets, predictable investment conditions and effective accountability mechanisms.

Four principal reforms are therefore recommended.

6.1 Introduction of Binding Renewable Energy Targets.

Parliament should consider amending Act 832 to introduce clearly defined and legally binding renewable electricity targets, supported by measurable interim milestones towards 2030, 2040, 2050 and 2060.

Such targets should be aligned with Ghana's NDC and long-term net-zero commitments. The Minister responsible for Energy should also be required to submit annual reports to Parliament detailing progress, implementation challenges and corrective measures.

This would strengthen institutional accountability and transform renewable energy targets from largely policy-driven aspirations into statutory obligations.

6.2 Restoration of a Bankable Renewable Energy Purchase Mechanism

Ghana should consider introducing a more reliable renewable energy purchase obligation capable of providing investors with reasonable revenue certainty.

This need not necessarily involve a wholesale return to the previous feed-in tariff regime. Rather, Parliament could adopt a balanced mechanism combining competitive procurement with regulated minimum purchase guarantees or other enforceable long-term offtake arrangements.

The obligation should extend beyond limited consumer-generator arrangements and provide a sufficiently broad demand-side framework for commercially viable renewable energy projects.

Such an approach would preserve the benefits of competitive procurement while addressing the investment uncertainty associated with the removal of the original feed-in tariff framework.

6.3 Adequate Capitalisation of the Renewable Energy Fund

The Renewable Energy Fund must be supported by a predictable and sustainable financing mechanism.

Government should consider allocating a defined proportion of appropriate existing energy-related levies or other designated public revenue sources to the Fund. Clear eligibility criteria, transparent disbursement procedures and regular financial reporting should also be established.

The Fund should prioritise projects that address financing barriers, support indigenous renewable energy enterprises, promote decentralised electricity generation and improve access to clean energy in underserved communities.

A properly capitalised Renewable Energy Fund would help reduce the financial risks associated with renewable energy development and strengthen private-sector participation.

6.4 Integration of Renewable Energy Regulation with Climate Legislation

Act 832 should be expressly aligned with the Environmental Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1124), particularly its provisions establishing the Ghana Carbon Registry and Carbon Market Committee.

This alignment should provide a coordinated framework for renewable energy project registration, emissions accounting, carbon market participation and the verification of climate benefits.

It should also clarify the respective responsibilities of the Energy Commission, PURC, Environmental Protection Authority and other relevant institutions.

In addition, the constitutional requirements governing international business transactions should be addressed through clearer administrative procedures to minimise uncertainty in the negotiation and approval of renewable energy investment agreements.

Finally, where statutory environmental and climate-related obligations are ignored or inadequately implemented, affected persons may explore appropriate constitutional and judicial remedies. In this regard, the Supreme Court's decision in Ghana Lotto Operators Association v National Lottery Authority is relevant for its recognition of a presumption of justiciability in relation to certain Directive Principles of State Policy. Nevertheless, the application of that principle to specific energy transition obligations would require careful judicial consideration. Conclusion:

Ghana has made significant commitments towards renewable energy development and the achievement of a low-carbon economy. The 2060 net-zero ambition, together with the country's international climate commitments, demonstrates the importance of transitioning towards a more sustainable energy system.

However, the existence of ambitious policy commitments does not automatically translate into effective legal implementation.

The Renewable Energy Act, 2011 (Act 832), remains an important foundation for renewable energy regulation in Ghana. Nevertheless, its promotional and regulatory orientation, coupled with the limitations introduced by the 2020 amendment, raises legitimate concerns about its adequacy in supporting the country's current net-zero ambitions.

The absence of comprehensive binding statutory targets, insufficient investment certainty, financing limitations and inadequate integration with the broader climate governance framework all point to the need for legislative reform.

Ultimately, Ghana's energy transition requires more than policy declarations and institutional encouragement. It requires a coherent legal framework that establishes enforceable obligations, mobilises sustainable financing, protects legitimate investor expectations and strengthens institutional accountability.

The future effectiveness of Ghana's net-zero commitments will therefore depend, to a considerable extent, on whether the country is prepared to move beyond a predominantly promotional renewable energy regime towards a legally enforceable and financially sustainable framework for decarbonisation.

Ghana News.title: Gunshots heighten tension at Nyanyano over chieftaincy dispute
Ghana News.content:
Residents of Gomoa Nyanyano in the Gomoa East District of the Central Region have been thrown into fear following reports of sporadic gunfire amid escalating tensions over a planned homecoming celebration by traditional authorities.

The latest unrest is linked to a protracted chieftaincy dispute that has unsettled the community since the death of its former chief, Nana Obeng Wiabor V.

The planned ceremony has reportedly met resistance from some residents, who fear that holding the event could deepen divisions among rival factions and trigger further violence.

Tensions escalated after a group of residents allegedly gathered at the palace of the deceased chief to protest the planned celebration. An official vehicle belonging to the traditional authorities was subsequently set ablaze.

The incident reportedly led to the arrest of some suspects, sparking anger among sections of the community.

The situation is said to have deteriorated further, with agitated residents allegedly attempting to attack the Nyanyano Police Station as gunshots rang out in parts of the town.

The latest developments have raised concerns about a possible escalation of the conflict, with residents worried about their safety and the security of property.

The violence comes barely a day after reports emerged that an official vehicle belonging to the traditional authorities had been torched at the Gomoa Nyanyano Chief’s Palace in the early hours of Tuesday, November 24.

An eyewitness, Kweku Botwey, narrated that the suspected attackers had earlier threatened to set the palace ablaze over the planned homecoming celebration. He alleged that masked individuals poured petrol on the vehicle before setting it on fire and fleeing.

Nyanyano has a history of violent confrontations over the chieftaincy question. In December 2025, clashes between rival factions left two people injured, prompting the deployment of more than 50 police officers and other security personnel to restore order.

In February 2026, another attack involving more than 100 people reportedly resulted in vandalism at the community palace. Ten suspects were arrested following that incident.

The dispute also disrupted an Easter convention organised by the Church of Pentecost in April 2026, when suspected land guards reportedly invaded the venue and dismantled canopies. The police subsequently suspended public activities in the area as a precautionary measure.

Ghana News.title: GIMPA, Jobberman equip students with skills to navigate the competitive job market
Ghana News.content:
A university degree may open doors, but securing employment requires more than academic qualifications, students at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) have been told.

The message was central to the GIMPA–Jobberman Job Fair 2026, a two-day career development and recruitment initiative organised by the GIMPA Career Services Unit, under the Office of the Dean of Students, in collaboration with Jobberman Ghana.

The event brought together GIMPA students and recruitment professionals for practical career preparation, professional guidance and direct engagement with recruitment opportunities.

The first day of the programme, held at the GIMPA Moot Court, focused on CV and résumé writing, job application strategies and the essential competencies employers look for when recruiting graduates.

In her remarks, the Dean of Students, Professor Augustina Akonnor, reminded students that academic qualifications alone do not guarantee employment or career success. She encouraged them to deliberately develop transferable skills, including effective communication, teamwork, critical thinking and adaptability, which are increasingly valued across different professional sectors.

Speaking on behalf of Jobberman Ghana, Ms. Elikplim Yaa Ayegbe, Marketing and Communication Specialist, highlighted the importance of attitude, professionalism and emotional intelligence in the workplace. She emphasised that professional success is determined not only by what individuals know but also by how they relate to colleagues, respond to challenges and conduct themselves in professional environments.

Mr. Alfred Quaye, Talent Acquisition Specialist, provided practical guidance on preparing effective CVs and navigating the recruitment process. He encouraged students to tailor their CVs to individual job opportunities, incorporate relevant keywords and present their qualifications and achievements honestly and effectively.

He further advised students to research prospective employers, understand the contents of their CVs thoroughly and prepare thoughtful questions ahead of interviews. He stressed that successful job applications require deliberate preparation and an understanding of what employers are looking for.

In her closing remarks for the first day's session, Mrs. Selina Doe Angmor, Career Services Consultant at GIMPA, encouraged students to take full advantage of the career development opportunities available through the Career Services Unit. She highlighted the importance of participating in career coaching, employability training and industry engagement programmes as essential steps towards building successful professional careers.

The second day of the Job Fair moved the engagement from career preparation to practical recruitment and employment opportunities.

Held at Lot 2, GF2 and GF3, the interview sessions ran from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., providing participating students with the opportunity to engage directly with Jobberman's recruitment team and experience aspects of the actual employment selection process.

The interview sessions offered students valuable exposure to recruitment expectations, enabling them to put into practice the lessons from the CV and résumé writing training and gain practical experience in presenting themselves to prospective employers.

By combining employability training with direct interview opportunities, the two-day initiative provided a practical pathway for students to move from understanding the requirements of the labour market to actively engaging with the recruitment process.

Ghana News.title: At least 30 killed in massive fire as fuel truck crashes on Cairo highway
Ghana News.content:
At least 30 people have been killed and 19 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.

Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.

Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.

Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the fuel truck had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.

The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.

It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.

Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished

The tanker crossed the highway's central reservation before overturning and bursting into flames, local media report

The health ministry said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to respond to the fire, while it posted images of Egypt's health minister overseeing the treatment of the injured at one of Cairo's hospitals.

Road collisions are also common in Egypt, often attributed to lax maintenance and the widespread flouting of traffic laws.

Nearly 6,000 people died on Egypt's roads last year, official figures show, a rise of several hundred on the previous year's total.

Emergency responders have since cleared the highway and allowed it to reopen, state broadcaster NMA reports.

A bulldozer could earlier be seen at the scene clearing the burnt-out wrecks of cars.

Ghana News.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
Ghana News.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.

The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.

They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.

Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".

"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.

"Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."

Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.

The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.

In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.

"The chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media reported.

The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case – concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 – met the threshold for criminality.

While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.

However, the judges told the attorney general that, in the public interest, there needed to be a "rethink" in how the trial should move forward, Israeli media report.

Baharav-Miara said she would consider the judges' recommendations.

It has been six years since Netanyahu became Israel's first sitting prime minister to face a criminal trial.

He has always claimed to be the victim of a political witch-hunt and said on Wednesday that the "fabricated cases" against him were now falling apart.

The cases have continued to progress in court while Netanyahu remained in power throughout the war in Gaza, though judges agreed to reduce the number of hearings due to security concerns around the conflict.

The accusations against him have rocked Israeli politics, fuelling already deep divisions. His trial has coincided with controversial, far-reaching judiciary reforms by Netanyahu's government.

For his opponents, Netanyahu's fear of prison has distorted his decision-making as prime minister and made him especially dependent on his far-right coalition partners to remain in power.

This latest development will give a boost to Netanyahu, whose political opponent Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a coalition government after an inconclusive general election last month.

While Netanyahu's parliamentary bloc won more seats than that of his rival, both fell short of an outright majority. Israel's president has offered Eisenkot the first chance to form a new administration.

Netanyahu remains subject to an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, which he also denies.

Ghana News.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
Ghana News.content:
Big technology firms connected to AI continued to see share prices fall on Wednesday, with stock in Nvidia and Anthropic dropping sharply in early trading.

The surge in Nvidia shares after boss Jensen Huang was reinstated was temporary, and the general stock sell-off continued, with all three main US stock market indices down. The tech-dominated Nasdaq has shed over 2%.

The declines come amid concerns over the level and sustainability of AI investment which has rattled investors in recent weeks.

Shares in other major tech firms, including Amazon, Tesla and SpaceX, Micrsoft and Meta were also down.

Nvidia's share price was down 8% in early trading on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's slide as the boost from Huang's return eased.

The resignation and subsequent reinstatement of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang after revelations of his extra marital affairs has seen the market value of the world's premier AI chipmaker fluctuate wildly.

Given Nvidia's position as both supplier and financier of many other firms involved in the AI rollout, its rocky fortnight has had a wider impact.

The US government also announced a raft of new tariffs on countries and trading partners on Wednesday as part of President Donald Trump's flagship trade policy.

The value of big tech companies have sheltered the US economy from global economic shocks, including tariffs, but share prices in recent weeks have been volatile in response to the US midterm elections and other events in the AI industry.

Investors have taken fright at Democrat gains in the US midterm elections, with many having campaigned for tougher regulation of AI firms and even a moratorium on the development of new data centres.

Questions also remain about whether the huge sums being invested in AI will eventually pay off.

"It seems that these companies are trying to one-up each other on the amount of money that they're spending but you have to show that it's worth it, and that's where Wall Street is saying I don't know," said Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management.

Despite concerns, investment in AI is expected to exceed $1 trillion in 2026, according to investment bank Goldman Sachs, which said the technology will remain the "dominant driver of business investment growth" next year.

Shares in Anthropic continued to trade below the $83 they debuted at last week, while Amazon shares fell by more than 5%.

The declines come ahead of the US stock market closing for Thanksgiving on Thursday before opening for a shortened session on Friday.

Ghana News.title: Trump’s accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show
Ghana News.content:
Donald Trump's investment portfolios have bought or sold shares in chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times this year, a review of the US president's financial disclosures shows.

Trump's most recent public declarations of his investment trading show that between January and September the portfolios purchased between $5.2m and $17m (£4m and £13m) in Nvidia stock - and sold between $4.4m and $12m. His portfolios held between $12.5m and $58m of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025.

Financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics report a low and high range of transaction values, so a more precise analysis of how much Nvidia stock was traded is not possible.

The period of recent turmoil at Nvidia and volatility in its share price is not covered by the disclosures. In the last two weeks, co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned and then Trump played a significant part in his reinstatement.

The White House has said that Trump's stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties and neither he nor his family "has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold".

Huang resigned on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs, including with one woman who has alleged ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia's share price dived following news of his resignation.

But on Monday Nvidia's board announced the 63-year-old was being reinstated as CEO.

Trump told US media he had "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring Huang back. The board said it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government" that he posed "no national security risk".

Nvidia's share price surged 31% on Monday following Huang's return. About $1tn (£763bn) was added to Nvidia's market value, but the company's shares are still trading below their value before reports of Huang's alleged affairs began to circulate.

However, concerns remain among both Republican and Democratic politicians about Huang's actions and Nvidia's compliance with US controls over the export of advanced computer chips to China, as well as Trump's involvement in getting him reappointed as CEO.

Nvidia's chip technology and investments have been critical to the growth of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, leading to it becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.

The firm now represents more than 6% of the S&P 500 share index, according to State Street financial services. This makes it the second most valuable company on the index after Apple, whose shares Trump's accounts also frequently trade.

Nvidia also ranks highly in many global indices, meaning that investment accounts held around the world, including pensions, are likely to include its shares.

Our analysis of Trump's Nvidia trades does not include other investment products held by him which may include its shares.

Trump made at least $2.2bn (£1.7bn) from a variety of investments and commercial activities, according to the financial disclosure report for the first year of Trump's second term.

Barbara Perry, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia's Miller Center, told the BBC there is "no precedent for this," adding: "It's beyond anything we've ever seen in the presidency."

Ghana News.title: Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections over 3am finish
Ghana News.content:
Councillors have approved plans allowing December's highly anticipated Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight in Cardiff to finish in the early hours.

Fans in hospitality boxes at the Principality Stadium will be allowed to drink alcohol until 03:00, with the venue closing at 03:30, to align with prime time viewing in the US.

Members of Cardiff Council's Licensing Sub Committee were told 130 police officers would help maintain order at the event on 11 December, with twice the number of stewards present compared to a regular sports event.

A handful of residents had objected to the proposed late finish, raising concerns over noise, antisocial behaviour and public safety, but none came to the meeting.

Councillors were told the event was a "big deal for the city" and would boost the Welsh capital, in terms of "revenue" and "profile."

Huw Thomas, chief inspector with South Wales Police, said the challenge for officers was the length of the programme, compared with other events in the stadium, saying the fight was begin viewed by the force as a "three-day event".

On Wednesday, the council meeting was told 450 out of the 1600 stewards present on the night would be dedicated to fans seated on the pitch area of the stadium.

Mark Williams, Stadium Director at the Principality Stadium, said the ring walk would take place at 01:00 GMT on 12 December, with the fight expected to start at 01:30.

Regarding tickets, he said there were still tickets available, but they were "expecting a capacity of 77,000, if everything sells".

The boxing rivals are expected to contest the WBA 'super' heavyweight title

Councillors heard objectors had raised "legitimate concerns", but measures had been put in place to mitigate them.

Plans for more trains in the early hours of Saturday were outlined, to support spectators getting home after the fight.

In response to concerns over noise, the meeting was told "no external PA system would be used" and noise would be "monitored" on the night.

Councillors heard initial plans to have live music before the fight would not happen but national anthems would be sung.

Regarding alcohol, councillors were told the application was for a "modest two-hour extension on the licence for one night only" and that approximately 10-15 venues were planning to open after hours for fans.

Breathalysers would be used on the gates but only for those, "who look worse for wear", according to Williams.

After a short period of consideration, chair of the committee, Grace Ferguson-Thorne, said the panel had agreed to grant permission, describing the measures taken - including the stewarding levels and the closure of the roof - as "really reassuring".

While early-hour finishes require extensive co-ordination around transport, policing and crowd management in the city centre, the venue already holds a precedent for late-night boxing.

In 2007, Joe Calzaghe's super-middleweight unification victory over Mikkel Kessler did not start until 02:00 to satisfy viewers of the US television network Showtime.

Councillors were told that "not much happened" after the main event.

But other fights in recent years have proved more of a challenge, including Anthony Joshua v Joseph Parker in 2018, which saw the headliners come out for their ring walks at an early time of 22:30.

That fight was attended by more than 78,000 people, which set a record for the largest ever attendance at any Principality Stadium event.

Councillor Sean Driscoll, who declared himself a Joshua fan during the meeting, said he was "sure the Cardiff hospitality businesses" would give Fury "and his fans a warm welcome".

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
