World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
World.content:
About 200,000 tents need replacing, Gaza’s municipalities say, as the European Union urges Israel to reopen all crossings into the territory to aid.

Gaza’s municipalities have warned that winter rains could flood about 1,000 camps and other sites hosting displaced Palestinians in the war-torn enclave, adding that damage to drains and sewers, and a shortage of pumps, have left their crews with little means to clear the water.

After a meeting in Gaza City on Wednesday, the Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities singled out al-Mughraqa and al-Zahra in central Gaza, where water levels in Wadi Gaza could rise suddenly. Across the territory, about 200,000 tents need replacing, and more than 2,000 damaged buildings are at risk of collapse, the union said. Gaza’s Government Media Office had warned on Tuesday that it expected another storm within days.

This is Gaza’s fourth winter since Israel launched its war in October 2023. The union said storms in early November flooded about 70,000 tents and affected more than 350,000 displaced people. During a winter storm this November, families piled sand at tent entrances to keep out the rain. Others carried their children out and salvaged what belongings they could.

One displaced mother said she had cut up the burial shroud she had bought for her son and used it to patch her tent. She wanted to keep the family’s bedding and clothes dry. “I couldn’t get a tarpaulin,” she said.

When the first rains hit, Gaza’s civil defence crews reached only a minority of those who called for help. Most of the other callers received advice by phone, Al Jazeera reported.

Tents waiting at the border

In Brussels on Wednesday, the European Commission called on Israel to reopen all Gaza crossings to humanitarian aid. Commission spokesperson Eva Hrncirova said tents were waiting on trucks outside Gaza because Israel had not allowed them or the equipment needed to put them up to enter.



The UN said earlier this month that more than 150,000 tents were awaiting entry into Gaza.

Al Jazeera’s open-source unit (Ar.) measured a queue of trucks stretching about 1.1km (0.7 miles) along the Egyptian road to the Rafah crossing in a November 17 satellite image, up from about 460 metres (1,510 feet) on October 6. The images do not establish what the trucks carried. Freight from Egypt is routed through the Karem Abu Salem crossing, known as Kerem Shalom in Israel, for inspection rather than entering Gaza through Rafah.

COGAT, the Israeli military body that coordinates aid, said that nearly 100,000 tents had entered Gaza since the start of a winter aid programme. It said Israel would allow reconstruction equipment into Gaza only after Hamas had fully disarmed.

Inside Gaza, aid workers have cleared drains, installed flood barriers and reinforced shelters. The UN’s humanitarian affairs office reported on November 20 that teams had recorded such work at 162 of the 356 flood-prone locations they had identified. Gaza’s municipalities are asking for pumps, backup generators and fuel before the next storm, as well as 10,000 tonnes of cement for emergency repairs and mobile homes that can withstand wind and rain.

World.title: US Education Department probes Virginia schools after sexual abuse scandal
World.content:
The United States Department of Education says it is launching an investigation and withholding funding from a district in the state of Virginia after local officials shut down all of its schools in the wake of a child sexual abuse scandal involving its employees.

“Parents should never have to question whether their child’s school is aiding and abetting child predators,” US Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said in a statement on Tuesday. “The Trump Administration is taking decisive enforcement action to hold those responsible accountable and ensure Virginia schools are safe places for children to learn.”

Officials in Albemarle County, Virginia, announced they were closing all 29 schools in the district last week, after learning that more than 500 staff had not been subjected to a routine background screening for a history of child sexual abuse. The school system has about 2,800 employees, and only a fraction of its $284m budget comes from the federal government.

Local officials emphasised that none of the 524 employees is suspected of abuse.

Approximately 14,000 students attend the schools, and parents have scrambled to find childcare, while many who depend on free school meals for their children have had to look for other sources of food.

Bob Beard, a member of the Albemarle school board, told Al Jazeera that families were struggling to deal with the shutdown, but schools would reopen on Monday.

The child abuse allegations have shaken the county and caught the attention of the Trump administration.



A former elementary school teacher was arrested for possession of child sexual abuse material earlier this year, while a counsellor at another school was put on leave and later indicted on 20 counts of sexual crimes involving seven different children, according to the Albemarle County Police Department.

Two county school officials and a school principal were later charged with failure to report child abuse, and the county’s superintendent of schools resigned.

‘Processes not followed’

Jason Grant, a spokesman for Albemarle County Public Schools, told Al Jazeera that none of the individuals implicated in those cases was among the 524 employees who were hired without the proper screening required to check for a history of child sexual abuse.

“This was not about having the policies in place, this was about processes that were not followed,” Grant said. He said officials were working with the state to “make sure the processes are in place to make sure this doesn’t happen again.”

Grant said all employees in the district undergo several stages of vetting, including a criminal background check and an attestation that they have no history of child abuse or neglect. Then the school system submits their information to the Virginia Department of Social Services to verify that they are not part of the agency’s abuse and neglect database.

For three years, it appears that vetting procedures were not consistently applied. Putting employees hired over that period on leave to carry out background checks meant schools would not be able to run, so officials decided to close them until next week.

“Those were for every range of employee, from teachers to bus drivers to substitutes and across the division, so we couldn’t get coverage for that amount of people,” Grant said.

All but three of the 524 employees have now been properly vetted, and none had background issues, Grant said, adding that the county will reopen schools on Monday.

The Trump administration has long called for the dismantling of the Department of Education. The US president signed an executive order last year that tried to set that in motion.

The department, which distributes federal funding to states for use in schools, also traditionally investigates whether local officials are complying with civil rights laws banning discrimination against minorities and marginalised groups.

Since returning to office in 2025, the Trump administration has cut more than half of the department’s staff and subjected it to wider changes it says are aimed at rooting out “diversity, equity, and inclusion” (DEI) policies.

World.title: Netanyahu says corruption trial ‘must end’ as court suggests dropping case
World.content:
The judges’ recommendations came as Israel’s longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival.

Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for an immediate end to his long-running corruption trial after judges cast doubt on the charges and recommended dropping a case in which he is accused of bribery.

Netanyahu on Wednesday said the “fabricated cases” against him were falling apart, in a televised statement at the Israeli parliament.

The judges’ recommendations came as Israel’s longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival after inconclusive October 27 elections.

Netanyahu’s main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has been tasked with forming a government, and if Netanyahu is no longer prime minister, he would lose his leverage to avoid a potential jail sentence.

“Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family,” Netanyahu said in his speech.

“Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul. Who will give those years back to us?”

“The trial must end immediately,” he added.

During a hearing in Jerusalem on Wednesday regarding three corruption cases against Netanyahu, judges recommended dropping one, reconsidering another and suggested resolving the third through an agreement, Israeli media reported.

In Case 4000, in which Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, judges indicated there was little chance of a conviction.

That case is considered to be the most serious Netanyahu faces and involves him allegedly offering regulatory favours for a telecoms company in exchange for favourable media coverage.

Netanyahu is alleged to have negotiated with Shaul Elovitch, the controlling shareholder of Israeli telecommunications giant Bezeq, to get positive coverage on his Walla news site in exchange for policies benefitting Bezeq.



On Wednesday, Israeli media reported Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman saying that proving the bribery charge in that case faced “considerable difficulties”.

Netanyahu, who has been in power on and off for three decades, has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing and denounced the cases as a politically motivated plot against him.

He is the first sitting Israeli prime minister to stand trial.

Israel’s Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, who was unusually summoned to the hearing on Wednesday, said she would consider the judges’ recommendations and was ready for either a verdict or a plea deal.

Netanyahu allies welcome court proposal

In Case 2000, Netanyahu is accused of fraud and breach of trust over an alleged deal with the owner of Yediot Aharonot for favourable coverage in exchange for curbs on rival newspaper Israel Hayom. Judges on Wednesday questioned whether his actions constituted a crime and recommended reconsidering the case.

In Case 1000, Netanyahu is accused of fraud and breach of trust over allegedly accepting luxury gifts from wealthy individuals in exchange for favours. Judges recommended reaching an agreement to conclude the case.

Netanyahu’s right-wing allies cheered the court’s recommendations and demanded the trial be brought to an end.

“After years of persecution against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the time has come to put an end to a trial that was flawed from the outset,” Israel Katz, who is the defence minister in Netanyahu’s caretaker government, wrote on X.

Netanyahu’s corruption trial opened in May 2020.

During his most recent term, which started in late 2022, Netanyahu proposed far-reaching judicial reforms that critics say sought to weaken the courts.

Eisenkot’s challenge

With coalition negotiations under way, Eisenkot’s camp is already trying to start unravelling some of the Netanyahu-era judicial reforms in parliament.

The presidential contender is expected to meet Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday evening.

His centrist Yashar party said a day earlier that it had agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.

Lieberman has ruled out forming a coalition with Arab-led parties that could hand them a majority in parliament. That has frustrated Democrats chief Yair Golan, who has been pushing Eisenkot to reach a deal with parties representing Israel’s 21 percent Arab minority to make good on his campaign promise to bring down Netanyahu.



Eisenkot also faced a new challenge on Tuesday after the left-wing Democrats suspended coalition talks, further complicating his potential path to power.

The Yashar party leader has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.

World.title: US Army declares Iowa lead azide detonation ‘tremendously successful’
World.content:
Army hails Iowa’s lead azide detonation, claiming no traces of airborne lead have been detected so far.

United States Army officials have hailed Wednesday’s mission to destroy 68 drums of volatile lead azide — a sensitive munitions explosive — at a military base in Iowa as a success, saying it had “wildly exceeded their expectations”.

Speaking at a news conference in Middletown, a southeastern rural city adjacent to the ammunition plant where the operation was carried out, Major General Eric Shirley, the Army official in charge of the disposal effort, said overhead footage showed that “all of the lead azide barrels were definitively removed”.

The controlled detonation at 10:15am (16:15 GMT) destroyed approximately 4,500kg (10,000lb) of deteriorating lead azide — an explosive that has been used in military munitions since World War I.

“There was no secondary explosions. There was no kick-out. There was no infrastructure damage in or around our installation,” Shirley said, adding that the operation was “tremendously successful”.

Officials also said that extensive mitigation measures, including earthworks, foam barriers and gel blocks, had helped to absorb the shockwaves and toxic fallout.

However, Democratic Illinois House Representative Mike Quigley voiced dissatisfaction over how military leaders handled the operation, calling the holiday-eve scheduling and lack of communication “unconscionable”.

In a statement on X, the congressman wrote: “It is unfair that our military leaders are releasing 9,500 pounds of unstable lead azide on our friends in Iowa the day before Thanksgiving.”

‘Zero detection of airborne lead’

Following days of heightened alarm over lead dust contamination and its environmental repercussions, federal officials announced that preliminary data from Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) sensors had detected no airborne lead particles.



Ongoing monitoring efforts continue in the immediately affected blast zone.

A post on the agency’s social media account shortly after the operation said that “ALL EPA real-time air monitors are reporting ZERO detection of airborne lead throughout the region”.

Chemists have noted that lead, as a nonbiodegradable element, cannot be chemically decomposed or destroyed. It persists in the environment, with airborne particles capable of travelling considerable distances before settling on soil and potentially leaching into groundwater.

Detonating large stores of the unstable explosive would decompose the compound into its basic elements – nitrogen gas and metallic lead.

Lead is a potent neurotoxin that poses its sharpest threat to children and pregnant women, with links to learning disabilities, impaired neurological function, mental health challenges, reproductive harm, hearing loss and other impairments.

“The EPA can do millions of tests, but they [must also] test for the breakdown products and the stabilisers and plasticisers [containing] lead azide [which] are endocrine disruptors; some are cancer-causing chemicals,” said Scott Smith, an independent environmental testing expert who was heavily involved in air testing after the 2023 East Palestine, Ohio train derailment and industrial incidents.

The Army Sustainment Command said it would release a final breakdown of the affected area — including lead-dust dispersion and surface-deposition maps — after the operation.

“I believe absolutely that we reduced as close to zero as is absolutely humanely possible the risk to the health and the safety of the people in Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” said Shirley.

World.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
World.content:
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.

The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions.

The move follows the White House's investigation into the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.

China is facing the highest rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35% and then others facing either 20% or 25%.

The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year.

Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of the good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing the products from abroad.

Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.

The proposed tariffs will affect China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, and India.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the latest tariffs issued would "level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy".

He claimed that many of America's trading partners had "for decades" adopted industrial strategies which included "targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression" as well as "other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favor while eroding America's manufacturing base".

But economists have warned tariffs can fuel inflation and push prices up for consumers if businesses pass on higher costs, as well as dampen global trade.

Trump has repeatedly threatened or imposed tariffs during his second term, arguing they will boost US manufacturing and create jobs.

Despite a poor result for the Republican party in the midterm elections, the president has continued to press on with his flagship trade policy.

Trump is also seeking to cut the US trade deficit - the gap between the value of goods it buys from other countries and those it sells to them.

World.title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
World.content:
The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface.

The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course.

Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision.

"The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team.

"It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful."

The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h).

It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 6,200 miles long (10,000km), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space.

Dimorphos is about 150m (500ft) wide and was partly chosen as the target because it is one of an asteroid pair - it orbits around a larger space rock called Didymos, which is about 730m (2,400ft) wide.

The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid.

Before the collision, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes.

World.title: At least 30 killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
World.content:
At least 30 people have been killed and 19 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.

Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.

Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.

Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.

The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.

It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.

Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes.

World.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
World.content:
Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.

The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.

They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.

Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".

"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.

"Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."

Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.

The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.

In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.

"The chances of conviction are low â to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media reported.

The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case â concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 â met the threshold for criminality.

While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.

World.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
World.content:
Big technology firms connected to AI continued to see share prices fall on Wednesday, with stock in Nvidia and Anthropic dropping sharply in early trading.

The surge in Nvidia shares after boss Jensen Huang was reinstated was temporary, and the general stock sell-off continued, with all three main US stock market indices down by closing time. The tech-dominated Nasdaq closed 0.6% lower.

The declines came amid concerns over the level and sustainability of AI investment, which has rattled investors in recent weeks.

Shares in other major tech firms, including Amazon, Tesla and Microsoft closed the day lower, though Meta and SpaceX were in positive territory by the end of the trading day.

Nvidia's share price was down 8% in early trading on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's slide as the boost from Huang's return eased. At close, it ended up 3.4% lower.

The resignation and subsequent reinstatement of Nvidia's CEO after revelations of his extramarital affairs has seen the market value of the world's premier AI chipmaker fluctuate wildly.

Given Nvidia's position as both supplier and financier of many other firms involved in the AI rollout, its rocky fortnight has had a wider impact.

The US government also announced a raft of new tariffs on countries and trading partners on Wednesday as part of President Donald Trump's flagship trade policy.

The value of big tech companies have sheltered the US economy from global economic shocks, including tariffs.

But share prices in recent weeks have been volatile in response to the US midterm elections and other events in the AI industry.

World.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
World.content:
Middletown Mayor Rodney Johnson told the BBC he felt "relieved" and "vindicated" after the detonation.

He watched the blast from his job at a manufacturing plant eight miles (12km) away from the blast - and monitored a camera at his two-bedroom home just one mile from the detonation site.

"We did not feel anything. We did not see anything," Johnson said.

Also eight miles away from Middletown, Sandy Mabeus closed the windows and the garage at her home, brought their outdoor cat inside and hunkered down.

The family watched three separate live streams on iPads and televisions of the explosion as it happened.

"We did not feel or hear a thing here," she told the BBC, adding that she checked the videos to confirm it had actually happened.

"The waiting and wondering has not been a good thing for anybody in the area," she said. "Hopefully they had a very good result and we can just get on with things."

Iowa farmer David Vandenberg lives about 20 miles from the blast site and said he first learned of the detonation around two weeks ago. The Army Corps of Engineers took samples from his yard and pond on Tuesday.

"I was listening this morning, and I did hear a rumble about nine o'clock," he told the BBC on Wednesday, but didn't see or smell anything.

Vandenberg expects officials to return to take more samples but "was happy to see that the blast was relatively contained. "I think the effects will be minimal"

World.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row
World.content:
North Korea has ordered Switzerland's diplomatic representative to leave the country within 48 hours and called for the office to close, in a row over sanctions.

It followed Switzerland's decision to place sanctions on the Songdowon international children's camp in the eastern city of Wonsan, which is attended by Russian and Chinese children among other nationalities.

The camp has been accused of involvement in transferring children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine.

North Korea's state-run news agency KCNA called the sanctions "a blatant hostile act".

Switzerland is one of the few Western nations to maintain dialogue with Pyongyang.

Confirming the expulsion, KCNA said: "The Foreign Ministry of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) declared the head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours."

The diplomatic rebuke comes weeks after Swiss foreign minister Ignazio Cassis made a rare visit to North Korea, where he officially reopened the office and discussed normalising relations.

Swiss authorities said relations between the two countries would be maintained through the North Korean embassy in Bern, and the Swiss embassy in Beijing.

Diplomatic links with North Korea were first established in 1974 and Switzerland opened a co-operation office in Pyongyang in 1997. It was closed during the pandemic and remained shut for six years.

World.title: My family were killed in Ukraine. My mum blamed Zelensky's troops - the truth is complicated
World.content:
If you are outside of the UK, listen to the Who Killed My Family podcast here

Watch our YouTube documentary here, external

As for my grandparents, my investigations suggested the events surrounding their deaths may have been more complicated.

Their house, on the eastern side of Dachne, had been destroyed. Neighbours told me they had escaped to another home on the same street.

I eventually reached a woman I'll call Lina, who lived nearby and was the last person, as far as I know, who saw my grandparents alive.

She could not recall what this date was, but knew it was in the second half of January.

At this time, she said, "the Russians were fully advancing - the edges of the village were being shelled. Then the Ukrainian soldiers moved from the edge of the village into the centre. They hid in people's yards and used side streets to avoid drones."

She said two soldiers entered her property. They had not been wearing any identifying insignia but had been speaking Ukrainian, she said - a language that Lina described as "Bandera", a derogatory term for Ukrainians.

"You're going to have to leave. Why are you still here?" Lina said they had asked her.

She said one had pointed a machine gun at her as she had stood outside her house, while another had gone to see my grandparents. She told me she had feared for her life and then fled her house for the night.

The following day, she told me she had returned to my grandparents' street to check on them.

She had found the door to the house they had been staying in open, she said, despite the freezing conditions.

With drones buzzing overhead, Lina said she had not dared look inside, but had later heard from neighbours that my grandparents had been found dead. She believed it had been the Ukrainian soldiers who visited her house who had shot them.

Another neighbour, who I will call Maria, described discovering their bodies - my grandmother in bed, covered in a blanket, and my grandfather lying on the floor in a pool of now-dried blood.

Maria also believed Ukrainian soldiers had killed them - because, she said, that she too had felt threatened by Ukrainian troops at the time.

"If they had seen me they would have killed me too."

Her theory was that my grandparents had irritated the troops in some way.

"Your grandparents caught them in a bad mood because your grandfather was always asking to be evacuated. And [the soldiers] were, you know, high. They were taking drugs. So your grandparents got in their way," she told me.

Most of the other people in the village I spoke to also believe Ukrainian soldiers killed them, though their testimony is not based on direct evidence.

The new local mayor, appointed by the Russian occupiers when they finally took control of Dachne in February, said she had been present at my grandparents' burial the following month, and said half of my grandmother's skull was missing.

These accounts of how they might have died in January 2025 were deeply disturbing, though no-one had witnessed their deaths and the information I was given could not be independently verified.

The villagers I spoke to - now living in occupied territory - did say there had been some tensions between themselves and Ukrainian troops at the time, because the soldiers had viewed those who remained in Dachne as supporters of Russia.

The clinical causes of my grandparents' deaths are unclear.

Their bodies were not exhumed for nearly 20 months, when the local authorities sent them to a morgue in the occupied region, where a basic autopsy was carried out by a forensics expert.

He told me that my grandmother had died of an explosives injury to the skull - but could not specify its cause.

As for my grandfather, it said his body had shown no obvious signs of injury.

I compared two satellite images of the house in which their bodies were found - from just before and just after when they are believed to have died - and could detect no significant damage to the building in the second image.

I also spoke to a villager who said he had buried my grandparents.

He said he did not know anything about who killed them.

"I wasn't there. But why would you kill old people?" he asked.

World.title: INEC sets up AI unit to combat election misinformation ahead of 2027 polls
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has established an Artificial Intelligence (AI) division within its Information and Communication Technology Department to tackle misinformation and digitally manipulated content ahead of the 2027 general elections.

INEC Chairman, Joash Ojo Amupitan, disclosed this on Wednesday at the Nigeria Election Risks and Readiness Summit 2026 organised by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) in Abuja.

Mr Amupitan, who was represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the commission was strengthening its capacity to detect and respond to emerging forms of digital manipulation, including deepfakes, synthetic voices and fabricated videos.

He warned that such content could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, discourage voter participation and trigger panic or communal violence, particularly when circulated through coordinated online campaigns.

He noted that INEC is strengthening collaboration with media organisations, fact-checkers and civil society groups to ensure that accurate information reaches the public promptly.

The concerns raised by INEC come amid growing attention to the use of digital platforms and artificial intelligence to influence political narratives ahead of the 2027 elections.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, commended CJID and its fact-checking initiative, DUBAWA, for investigating and exposing emerging threats to electoral integrity, including foreign information manipulation, AI-generated disinformation and coordinated online campaigns.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Disu warned that fabricated videos, doctored audio recordings and coordinated false narratives could distort political participation, erode public trust and provoke violence. He added that an election could be attacked through false information even without the use of firearms.

INEC steps up preparations for 2027 elections

Beyond addressing misinformation, Mr Amupitan said the commission was taking steps to improve the efficiency of election-day operations, including procuring about 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and replacing batteries in existing machines.

He added that INEC was also providing climate-controlled storage facilities across states to ensure the proper preservation of election materials.

According to him, the commission reduced the number of voters assigned to each BVAS device from 1,250 to 850, while allocating more devices to polling units with larger voter populations. The adjustment is expected to reduce accreditation time to between one and two minutes.

The commission said it would recruit about 1.41 million ad hoc personnel for the 2027 elections. Approximately 700,000 will be deployed for the presidential and National Assembly elections, while another 700,000 will serve during the governorship and State House of Assembly elections.

The commission also said it had extended the registration period for ad hoc staff from two weeks to two and a half weeks.

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, while the governorship and State House of Assembly elections will hold on 6 February 2027.

Mr Amupitan urged journalists and other stakeholders to complete their accreditation within the stipulated period, explaining that the deadlines were guided by the Electoral Act and could not be arbitrarily extended.

He said INEC is working with security agencies and political parties to identify potential election flashpoints and improve security deployment.

The commission, he added, is using its Election Risk Management tool to identify areas vulnerable to violence and other disruptions. The tool would also guide targeted security deployments during the 2026 Osun governorship election.

Stakeholders discuss election violence, security

The summit also featured a panel session titled “Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security Ahead of 2027”.

The session featured Gloria Korang, programme manager at the West Africa Network for Peacebuilding (WANEP); Bukola Idowu, executive director of Kimpact Development Initiative; Raphael Mgbaegbu, head of social research at NOI Polls; and Safiya Bichi, senior manager at YIAGA Africa, moderated by Tolulope Adeleru-Balogun of News Central Television.

The panel’s focus on electoral violence and security formed part of broader discussions at the summit on election preparedness and the protection of those involved in the electoral process.

Mr Amupitan condemned political violence and attacks on journalists, election officials and party supporters, warning that such incidents could undermine democratic participation and the credibility of elections.

He said INEC is engaging the police, political parties and other security stakeholders through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security to address threats before, during and after the elections.

The commission also called for responsible political communication, urging political parties and their supporters to avoid inflammatory statements and actions capable of escalating tensions.

READ ALSO: INEC selects 520 polling units for mock election in Enugu

Earlier at the event, the European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, said credible elections required more than the conduct of voting and the announcement of results. He said they also depended on a fair pre-election environment, access to reliable information and transparent resolution of electoral disputes.

Mr Mignot noted that the credibility of Nigeria’s elections had implications for democratic stability across West Africa.

Similarly, Norway’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Svein Baera, called for the protection of journalists, fact-checkers, editors, election officials and observers, saying those working to safeguard electoral integrity must be able to perform their duties without intimidation and commended CJID and its partners for supporting media development and efforts to strengthen accountability and democratic processes in Nigeria.

World.title: Delta Killings: Assembly demands justice for slain ex-lawmaker, five others
World.content:
The Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Dennis Guwor, called for a thorough investigation into the killing of a former lawmaker, Moses Anaughe, and five others in Ughelli North Local Government Area.

Mr Guwor made the call during the House’s plenary on Wednesday, condemning the violent incident that occurred at Uduere Community.

The incident, which occurred during a campaign rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress on Monday, claimed six lives.

The speaker described the incident as “shocking” and condemned political violence, thuggery, intimidation and lawlessness ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He urged security agencies to investigate the attack thoroughly and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“As we approach the 2027 general elections, politics should be about ideas, service and democratic engagement, not violence and the destruction of human lives.

“No political ambition is worth the life of any citizen,” Mr Guwor said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also admonished political parties, leaders and supporters to embrace peace, tolerance and respect for the rule of law throughout the electoral process.

On behalf of the lawmakers and management of the Assembly, Mr Guwor extended condolences to the bereaved families, Uduere Community and others affected by the tragedy.

The House observed a one-minute silence in honour of the deceased, particularly Mr Anaughe, a former member.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Mr Anaughe, who represented Ughelli North I State Constituency in 2019, was removed by the court shortly after his inauguration.

World.title: Delta Assembly passes 2027 appropriation bill of N1.272trn
World.content:
The Delta State House of Assembly on Wednesday passed the state’s N1.272 trillion Appropriation Bill for the 2027 fiscal year.

The bill passed through a voice vote at a plenary presided over by the Speaker, Dennis Guwor, in Asaba.

Its passage followed the presentation of a report by the Chairman of the House Committee on Finance and Appropriation, Marilyn Okowa-Daramola (Ika North-East).

On 16 November, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori presented a budget proposal of N1.23 trillion to the Assembly for approval.

Presenting the committee’s report, Ms Okowa-Daramola said N430 billion was retained for recurrent expenditure, as proposed by the governor, while capital expenditure increased from N806.8 billion to N842 billion.

She said the additional N35.2 billion in capital expenditure was to accommodate priority projects aimed at accelerating infrastructure development and improving residents’ living conditions.

Ms Okowa-Daramola said the adjustment would help strengthen infrastructure delivery, stimulate economic activities and promote inclusive development across the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She noted that the fiscal framework aligned with the administration’s development priorities, particularly in education, agriculture, healthcare, industrialisation and youth empowerment.

Ms Okowa-Daramola added that the budget emphasised agricultural production and processing, food security, access to quality healthcare and skills development for young people.

According to her, investment in education, training and capacity building will equip youths with relevant skills to contribute meaningfully to the state’s economic growth.

The Majority Leader of the Assembly, Emeka Nwaobi (Aniocha North), moved the motion to adopt the bill, seconded by Festus Okoh (Ika South).

READ ALSO: Reps urge Tinubu to consider emergency measures in Delta over recurring political violence

Mr Nwaobi also moved the motion for the third reading, which Perkins Umukoro (Sapele) seconded, before the bill passed through a voice vote.

Mr Guwor subsequently directed that the clean copy of the bill be forwarded to the governor for assent.

He commended the governor for his commitment to the state’s continuous development, describing the bill’s passage as a demonstration of the legislature’s commitment to its constitutional responsibilities.

“I wish to thank the governor of Delta for his commitment to the continual development of our state,” he said.

The speaker also praised the Chairman and members of the House Committee on Finance and Appropriation for their diligence, and other lawmakers for their contributions to the bill’s successful passage.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Mbah commissions projects in Oji-River, pledges more development
World.content:
Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, has assured the people of Oji-River Local Government Area of sustained development, promising the completion of critical roads, improved water supply, 24-hour electricity and expanded empowerment programmes.

Mbah gave the assurance on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) tour of Mmam River and Oji-River Central Development Centres and commissioning of several Smart Green Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres built by his administration.

The projects inaugurated were Smart Green Schools at Umuagu and Umuome, Inyi, as well as Primary Healthcare Centres at Umuagu, Enugu-Inyi, Agbadala Achi and Amamkpunato Achi.

Addressing separate gatherings of the people at Central School, Inyi, and Achi Court, after meeting with the electorate, polling unit by polling unit, Mbah appealed to them to bear with him for limiting the inauguration to a few projects, noting that even if he spent the entire remaining part of his administration commissioning projects, it would still not be enough, as they were in their thousands.

He said the important thing was that the projects were serving the needs of the people, promising to redouble his administration’s efforts.

“If we had continued on our commissioning spree today, we probably would not have made it here today. But we only stopped at just two Smart Green Schools and three Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres. We could have gone all the way to commission the rest of the projects, but we saw that we needed to come here to meet with you.

Mbah said his administration’s investments in education, healthcare, infrastructure and human capital development were not by accident, but designed to transform the state’s economy and improve living standards.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

At Inyi, he disclosed that, besides the Smart Green Schools, the government was robustly upgrading the Enugu State College of Health Technology, Oji-River, into a nursing college, with new classroom and hostel blocks and an improved curriculum.

He also announced plans to commence the construction of a 660-megawatt coal-fired power plant, saying the project would guarantee 24-hour electricity supply and support round-the-clock economic activities.

On water supply, the governor said the Oji-River Water Scheme was being upgraded, with the installation of new pumps complete to enable it to produce up to 60 million litres of water daily. He stressed that host communities must enjoy adequate water supply.

Mbah further announced plans to empower 260 women in every ward with business grants, while women operating in cooperative clusters would receive agro-processing equipment and additional financial support. Petty traders and vulnerable households would equally benefit from grants, foodstuffs and cash assistance.

On education, he said the Smart Green Schools were exposing children to modern technology, robotics, artificial intelligence and innovation, while developing their critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

“No longer will our children be limited by lack of modern skills. They will compete with their peers from every part of the world and also guarantee the sustenance of all that we are building today,” he stated.

At Achi, the governor said the critical roads requested by the people, including the Amakpunato-Amoli Road, had already been awarded and funded by his government, expressing optimism that they would be completed before the next rainy season.

“We recognise road infrastructure as essential to connecting communities, farmers and businesses to economic opportunities. So, for us, it is not a favour. It is not also for acclaim. It is a necessary economic enabler,” he added.

Mbah also cited improvements in Enugu’s fiscal performance, saying the state had moved from 30th position nationally in the National Bureau of Statistics’ internally generated revenue (IGR) ranking before his administration to third, behind Lagos and Rivers states.

He said the Smart Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres were designed to expand access to quality education and healthcare, adding that the health facilities would be adequately staffed and provide free services.

The governor urged residents to sustain the development gains recorded in the state, describing the ongoing transformation as irreversible.

He also called for support for President Bola Tinubu and APC candidates in the 2027 general elections, noting that, besides addressing the challenges of strategic infrastructure and appointments in the South East before now, his administration would not have been able to execute the numerous landmark projects in the state without the president’s reforms, which had made more resources available to state governments.

In their remarks, the Senator representing Enugu West, Osita Ngwu; Member representing Awgu/Oji-River/Aninri Federal Constituency, Engr. Anayo Onwuegbu; and Member representing Oji-River State Constituency, Hon. Osita Eze, commended the administration’s projects and engagements in the area.

They assured that political mobilisation and public enlightenment would continue beyond the present tour and project commissioning, saying that the projects executed in Oji-River had provided tangible evidence of the administration’s interventions.

The Director-General of the Enugu APC Campaign Council, Chief Charles Mbah, said the campaign train was in the area to appreciate residents’ support and seek their continued commitment ahead of the elections.

A major stakeholder in Oji-River LGA, Hilary Abaratu of GOWASK Construction Limited, reiterated that Mbah had delivered more than was expected of him in his second term, reminding the people that the governor remained their sure path to more infrastructural development, political relevance and prosperity. He said they must not allow anyone to deceive them.

Earlier, Oji-River Local Government Chairman, Hon Gregory Anyaegbudike, attributed the turnout at the rallies to residents’ confidence in the governor, assuring that the people would support APC candidates across the ballot.

The governor was accompanied by APC Deputy National Chairman, South, Dr Ben Nwoye; the party’s South-East Women Leader, Dr Oby Aji; members of the state party leadership, State Executive Council, government officials and other stakeholders, including the Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Ugochi Madueke, and the Commissioner for Human Development and Poverty Eradication, Prof Benedette Ekwutosi Okoli.

Also on Mbah’s entourage, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism and an indigene of Oji-River also featured prominently during the ward and polling unit consultations by the governor.

World.title: NEC appeals ruling ordering Adebutu‘a inclusion in 2027 Ogun governorship election
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has appealed a judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja directing it to include the Peoples Democratic Party’s Ogun State governorship candidate, Hon Ladi Adebutu, on the list of candidates for the 2027 election.

INEC filed its notice of appeal on Wednesday, asking the Court of Appeal to review the ruling that ordered the commission to recognise Adebutu as the PDP candidate for the forthcoming Ogun governorship election.

The dispute centres on Adebutu’s nomination and recognition as the party’s candidate. Its resolution will determine whether his name appears on INEC’s final list of candidates for the election.

The appeal means that implementation of the Federal High Court’s directive may remain subject to further proceedings and any orders issued by the Court of Appeal. The appellate court is expected to consider INEC’s arguments and determine whether the lower court was right to order Adebutu’s inclusion.

The case has attracted significant political and legal attention in Ogun State, where political parties, aspirants and voters are preparing for the 2027 election. It could also affect the PDP’s internal dynamics as the party consolidates its position ahead of the campaign season.

INEC is responsible for preparing and publishing the final list of candidates, subject to applicable court orders and the provisions of the Electoral Act. Until the appeal is resolved, Adebutu’s candidacy and inclusion on the final list remain unsettled.

The Court of Appeal’s decision will determine whether the Federal High Court’s directive stands or is overturned.
