World.title: Makinde’s campaign group questions Tinubu’s N3.15trn budget cut
World.content:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has questioned President Bola Tinubu’s decision to reduce the proposed expenditure of the 2026 federal budget by N3.15 trillion while retaining the original N31.46 trillion fiscal deficit and N9.22 trillion borrowing plan.

The organisation, which is campaigning for Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s presidential ambition on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), said the decision raised questions about the federal government’s fiscal management and its commitment to transparency.

In a statement issued on Wednesday and signed by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, the organisation demanded that Mr Tinubu explain why the deficit and borrowing projections remained unchanged despite the reduction in overall expenditure.

“The N3.1 trillion expenditure profile reduction is infinitesimal when juxtaposed with the massive budget padding including the appropriation of billions of naira for reportedly duplicated and non-existence projects,” the statement read.

The revised proposal reduces the federal government’s expenditure from N68.32 trillion to approximately N65.18 trillion, representing a cut of about 4.6 per cent.

However, the fiscal deficit remains at N31.46 trillion, equivalent to about 5.64 per cent of Nigeria’s gross domestic product, while planned new borrowing remains at N29.22 trillion.

The borrowing plan comprises N18.43 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The campaign organisation described the adjustment as inadequate, alleging that it failed to address deeper problems in the country’s budget planning and implementation.

“The reduction in expenditure without a corresponding reduction in the fiscal deficit and borrowing plans further exposes the seething corruption in Nigeria’s fiscal coordination under the Tinubu administration while raising apprehension of a decoy by officials to siphon public funds,” the statement said.

The organisation also alleged that the original budget contained billions of naira in duplicated and non-existent projects, describing the expenditure reduction as insignificant when compared with what it called extensive budget padding.

It further criticised the timing of the proposed revision, arguing that the recognition of existing government obligations shortly before the end of the fiscal year reflected weaknesses in budget planning and implementation.

Tinubu’s explanation for budget revision

Mr Tinubu had asked the National Assembly to consider a revised 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from N68.32 trillion to N65.18 trillion while retaining the deficit and borrowing provisions.

In his communication to lawmakers dated 20 November, the president said the adjustments were intended to regularise certain expenditures incurred by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited on behalf of the federal government, address under-provided debt-service obligations and recognise issued capital warrants and supplementary commitments.

READ ALSO: Tinubu pledges rescue of schoolchildren at Maiduguri rally

He also said the revised framework would provide for refunds to ministries, departments and agencies and accommodate priority national interventions.

The president maintained that the revised budget would prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and implementation of the capital budget.

The Makinde-Daura campaign organisation, however, questioned the decision to retain the borrowing plan despite the reduction in planned expenditure.

It also demanded an explanation for the government’s handling of capital budget implementation, alleging that funds had not been released for the 2026 capital budget despite substantial borrowing.

World.title: Tinubu pledges rescue of schoolchildren at Maiduguri rally
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday in Maiduguri, Borno State, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to sustaining peace and security in the North-east and directed security agencies to intensify operations against fleeing insurgents.

The president, who was in Maiduguri for a campaign rally ahead of January 2027, said the peace recorded so far by the armed forces in Borno State and the North-East will be sustained and translated into full economic recovery, the presidential media aide Bayo Onanuga said in a statement.

“Borno State citizens, we all love you. It is good to be here. I feel like I have come home to a family reunion. It’s great to be back in Borno State.

“Let me start by thanking the Governor of the state, Prof. Babagana Zulum. Well done on restoring Borno State and transforming its economy.

“You restored our hope by believing that stability will bring development. I just commissioned some projects on our way here, the National Youth Service Corps Female Lodge and the Borno International Conference Centre,’’ he said.

President Tinubu said the North-East has seen an economic turnaround over the last three years, with growing investments in education, health care, and infrastructure.

The president urged fleeing terrorists to surrender and hand over their weapons.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

President Tinubu also assured the armed forces involved in providing peace in the North East that the government will further prioritise the welfare and well-being of their families.

President Tinubu also said more efforts will be made to gather intelligence to rescue the Askira Uba schoolchildren.

“I think there’s a point to note here: the abducted children of Askira Uba School. They are there, and with our prayers and intelligence, our armed forces will rescue them, Insha Allah, ” he added.

The president said the success recorded so far in the North-east was due to the cooperation of leaders and citizens with the federal government and security forces.

“I can tell you that the love you have shown me, respect and honour will not be forgotten,’’ he said.

The president appreciated his Vice President and running mate, Kashim Shettima, for his steadfastness and loyalty.

“The show of love from Borno State is much. We have been together for some time now. We have seen hope and the restoration of a transformative government. We have seen collaboration and willingness to cooperate. Without the support of the people of Borno State, we wouldn’t have gotten this far. Thank you.

“Thank you, all the leaders in the North East. Particularly, only yesterday we launched the AD-APC book. There I made mention of the role of the then ANPP, our brother, our leader and our partner, former governor, Sen. Ali Modu Sheriff. Thank you very much

“I cannot forget the period we had to work together to bring in the APC. You played a very significant role. A very dependable role. And today, APC is here. I thank Sen. Adams Oshiomhole too, and many of you here.

“I always say this, no matter how short a man is. He can see the sky. Though Sen. Oshiomhole is short, he is seeing the sky all the time. His voice is great, and his mental capacity is very, very rich.

“To all of you, I can see the governor of Imo State, Sen. Hope Uzodinma. Well done. May God bless you. Imo is working because we are all together,’’ the President affirmed.

In his remarks, the vice president thanked President Tinubu for his sustained support for the people of Borno State.

Mr Shettima warned citizens against voting for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the ADC candidate, in the forthcoming election. He said Atiku had lost the support of his political allies because he could not provide sound leadership.

“You don’t expect someone who could not provide leadership at home by reconciling his own people to provide leadership at a national level,’’ the vice president said.

Mr Shettima told party supporters at the rally that President Tinubu’s government had done well for Borno, Bauchi, Taraba, Adamawa, and all the states, and that he should be rewarded with a second term.

The governor of Borno State, Babagana Zulum, thanked the president for his interventions in the state over the years, which he said have translated into recovery and repositioning of the economy.

“If someone has done well for you, like our president, then we should give him a good reward.

“We have witnessed relative peace in Borno State and North-East,’’ he added.

The governor said the president had built universities, roads, and other infrastructure in Borno and Gombe, including the Biu-Maiduguri Road.

He commended the North East Development Commission (NEDC) for providing 10,000 electric buses to the North East, which the Vice President had commissioned for operations.

Governor Zulum also thanked the President for selecting Sen. Shettima as his running mate for a second term.

The APC chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda, handed over flags to the APC’s gubernatorial candidate in the state and others in the forthcoming elections.

World.title: Obasanjo, Jonathan, Osinbajo to attend Plateau Christmas event
World.content:
The Plateau State Government says former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo and Goodluck Jonathan, as well as former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, will attend the third edition of the Plateau Unity Christmas Carols and Praise Festival scheduled for 27 to 29 November.

The government also announced that the festival, organised in collaboration with the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), will be broadcast live for the first time by the international Christian Broadcasting Network (CBN).

In a press statement issued on Wednesday and signed by the Secretary to the State Government, Samuel Jatau, who chairs the festival’s central planning committee, the event is expected to attract worshippers from different denominations, ethnic groups and communities across Nigeria and beyond.

The festival, themed Nations in Worship, will take place at the Ten Commandments Prayer Altar, Du, in Jos South Local Government Area, with activities scheduled to begin at 3:30 p.m. daily.

Mr Jatau said the international broadcast would provide an opportunity to showcase Plateau State’s religious and cultural diversity, as well as its aspiration for peace and unity, to audiences around the world.

Mr Obasanjo, a former military head of state and civilian president, is expected to attend for the third consecutive year, alongside Mr Jonathan and Mr Osinbajo, who is also expected to deliver a sermon at the gathering.

Other prominent personalities expected include the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda; former Minister of Information and National Orientation, Jerry Gana; and the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Alleviation, Bernard Doro.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The organisers also listed David Abioye of Living Word Conquerors Global Assembly and the Plateau State CAN Chairman, Dunka Gomwalk, among the religious leaders expected at the event.

The Gbong Gwom Jos, Jacob Buba, is expected to lead traditional rulers attending the festival. Former governors and ministers from Plateau State, as well as serving and former public office holders across the three arms of government, are also expected.

Cultural diversity, music

A major feature of the festival will be performances by choirs and worship groups from different parts of the country, with participants encouraged to sing in their indigenous languages and wear traditional attire.

Plateau State will be represented by the Irigwe and Tarok choirs, the Ron choir group and the Catholic Women’s Fellowship from Shendam.

Other participating groups include the Hausa Choir from Kano State, combined choirs from Nasarawa and Bauchi states, the Kanuri Combined Choir from Borno State, Fulfulde singers and the Lutheran Church of Christ in Nigeria Women’s Fellowship from Yola, Adamawa State.

The event will also feature a Plateau Unity Choir comprising more than 600 members, a children’s choir and a Bible recitation segment expected to draw participation from families.

Gospel music ministers scheduled to perform include Kaestrings, Judikay, Alpha Dali, Panam Bande, Mizze Adams, Abedebee and 5 Loaves.

The organisers said the festival was designed to promote collective worship, cultural harmony and peaceful coexistence among people from different backgrounds.

Security arrangements

The state government said it had put comprehensive security arrangements in place to protect residents, visitors and other participants throughout the three-day event.

Governor Mutfwang has directed the deployment of security personnel to ensure the safety of those attending, according to the statement.

The government also urged residents across the state’s 17 local government areas to decorate their homes, churches and business premises as part of activities marking the Christmas season.

The annual festival is part of the state government’s efforts to promote Plateau as a destination for religious gatherings, cultural exchange and tourism.

World.title: Troops rescue 5 kidnapped victims, arrest 2 suspected terrorists in Kaduna
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma in furtherance of ongoing counter-terrorism operations, on Wednesday successfully rescued 5 kidnapped victims and arrested of 2 suspected terrorists in separate operations conducted in Kaduna State.

Confirming the rescue operation, Captain Sinivie Tamuno, Spokesman said, “On Wednesday, 25 November 2026, troops of Sector 1 responded to distress calls following attacks by suspected terrorists on Dan Bushiya community in Chikun Local Government Area, during which some residents were abducted.

“Despite encountering an ambush, troops continued their rescue efforts without sustaining any casualties.

“The operation led to the rescue of a woman and her baby, who were abandoned by the fleeing terrorists following sustained pressure from the troops.

“Similarly, on the same day, troops responded to another distress call following the abduction of 5 residents of Kakura village in the same Local Government Area.

“The swift intervention of the troops forced the terrorists to abandon 3 of the kidnapped victims, who were subsequently rescued.

“Efforts are ongoing in conjunction with other security agencies to track and eliminate the terrorists.

“In a related development, on the same day, a joint patrol team conducting search and rescue operations following a kidnapped incident in Danbushiya community, found a national ID card along the terrorists’ withdraw route.

“The discovery subsequently led to the arrest of the bearer identified as Mr Shauibu Musa and another suspect named Aliyu Ahmed.

“The suspected terrorists are in troops custody for further investigation.

The Joint Task Force Operation Fansan Yamma remains resolute in its commitment to combating terrorism and other forms of criminality, securing lives and property, and restoring lasting peace across the North West.

“Members of the public are urged to continue supporting ongoing operations by providing timely and credible information on suspicious activities to the troops and other security agencies.”

World.title: ‘Five bullets’ — NDC supporter recounts attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team in Delta
World.content:
A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has recounted how gunmen allegedly shot him five times during an attack on the campaign team of Ovie Omo-Agege, the party’s candidate for Delta Central, in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The survivor, who sustained gunshot injuries to his chest and mouth, narrated his ordeal in a video shared on the NDC’s X page on Wednesday.

The video showed him speaking from his hospital bed during a visit by Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, its vice-presidential candidate, to survivors of the attack.

Recounting events leading up to the shooting, the man said he had received threats after participating in a 10,000-man march organised by the NDC in Delta State.

According to him, his wife received a telephone call from individuals who threatened to shut down his business.

“To be very precise, on Sunday, when we were in church, in the early hours of the day, they went and sealed the whole business premises. I could not get access to the premises; I could not offload my goods,” he recalled.

“A week later, my truck that brought goods from Lagos, they seized the truck and drove it to the local government secretariat.”

He said the truck was detained for more than four days, adding that no explanation had been provided for its seizure.

The supporter said the attack occurred on Monday while Omo-Agege was addressing supporters at the campaign venue, when gunmen stormed the gathering and opened fire.

He said one of the attackers called out his name before shooting him as he attempted to escape towards his car.

“One of them started shouting, ‘That is Agba, shoot Agba, that is Agba, look at Agba going.’ Before I could say Jack, the gunshot came straight to my chest,” he said.

“There is a bullet here, through the throat. There is a bullet here…five bullets on the chest and the mouth.

“So, the target was just to kill me, but to God be the glory, I’m alive.”

He attributed the attack to his political affiliation and support for the NDC’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates.

“The whole thing is because I’m supporting NDC; I’m supporting Obi and Kwankwaso,” he said.

Another survivor receiving treatment at the hospital also expressed determination to continue supporting the party despite the violence.

“No matter the number of persons they shoot or attempt to kill in their time, Peter Obi will become president, Rabiu Kwankwaso will become vice-president, and Nigeria will be okay,” he said.

Recall in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Nigeria Police Force spokesperson, Ani Iniedu, said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed and several others injured during the attack.

Iniedu said the police would sanction any officers found to have acted improperly, unlawfully or breached professional standards during the incident.

He added that an investigation was ongoing to establish the confirmed casualty figure and determine the circumstances surrounding the violence.

According to him, the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, had ordered increased security deployment, intelligence-led operations and sustained patrols to prevent further violence and restore normalcy in the affected communities.

Meanwhile, the Delta State Government imposed a curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice following the attack.

World.title: Davido, Patoranking, Cubana Chief Priest to attend Odii’s Ebonyi gov’ship campaign flag-off
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

Popular Nigerian music artists, Davido and Patoranking, as well as celebrity businessman and socialite Cubana Chief Priest, will storm, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State capital Thursday for the official flag-off of the governorship campaign of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii.

Other people expected at the event are international businessmen, politicial bigwigs and over 300 friends of Odii across Nigeria and beyond to support their own to actualize his dream of becoming the next governor come 2027.

Odii who stated in a media roundtable pledged that his administration, if elected, will not abandon ongoing or uncompleted projects across the state, promising to prioritise continuity, accountability and proper execution of development projects.

He said his campaign would be issue-based, reaffirmed his determination to pursue sustainable economic development.

He explained that his administration would be guided by a comprehensive manifesto designed to address Ebonyi State’s present realities, past challenges and future development aspirations.

According to him, the manifesto would serve as a roadmap for governance, clearly outlining the promises and programmes his administration intends to implement from the beginning of its tenure.

The PDP governorship candidate maintained that governance should not be about making unrealistic political promises but about identifying existing projects, assessing their relevance and ensuring that viable investments are completed and put to productive use.

“We will never abandon any project. If we must do it, we will have to do it properly,” he declared.

Odii further promised to conduct a comprehensive assessment of ongoing and abandoned projects across the state to determine the resources and interventions required to complete them.

He also stressed the importance of strengthening the state’s economy, noting that a stronger economic base would improve the government’s capacity to deliver infrastructure and other development commitments.

On the issue of political violence, intimidation and thuggery, Odii condemned all forms of electoral violence, assuring supporters that his political ambition was driven by a genuine desire to bring about a change in governance.

He expressed confidence that intimidation and other political attacks would not derail his ambition.

“We mean business. We are not joking. We are fighting for a change in government. We know it, but by the grace of God, nothing can stop us,” he said.

Odii, in turn, expressed his campaign’s readiness to strengthen its media engagement and public communication strategy to reach more residents across the rural and urban areas of the state.

The PDP guber candidate later inaugurated his campaign council led Ambassador Nwanne Ominyi as Director General where he charged them to based their campaign on Issue-based not name calling or character assisination.

He also charged them to shun violence, thuggery or to reply to harrasment by opposition rather report any attack and intimidation to security operatives in the state.

World.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once.

The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history.

The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig.

Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won.

South Africa: three wins

South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown.

Namibia: one win

Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990.

Botswana: one win

Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page.

Angola: one win

Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe.

World.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
World.content:
Barcelona’s English forward #17 Anthony Gordon celebrates with teammates after scoring the team’s second goal during the UEFA Champions League match between Sabah and Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium in Baku on November 25, 2026. (Photo by Giorgi ARJEVANIDZE / AFP)

Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish.

Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium.

The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League.

Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal.

Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence.

Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork.

Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path.

The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player.

Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval.

The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way.

It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him.

Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header.

Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another.

Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him.

Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally.

World.title: Asisat Oshoala graduates with MSc in International Sports Management
World.content:
Super Falcons forward Asisat Oshoala has added another milestone to her illustrious career after graduating with a Master of Science degree in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sports.

A viral video circulating on social media showed the Nigerian football star being called up among the graduands during the institution’s graduation ceremony, drawing attention to her latest academic achievement.

🚨 Super Falcons icon Asisat Oshoala has added another milestone to her career, graduating with an MSc in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sports.



Six-time African Player of the Year, excelling on and off the pitch! 👏🇳🇬 pic.twitter.com/UEklwPSevX — Brila Media (@Brilamedia) November 25, 2026

Oshoala, widely regarded as one of Africa’s most successful female footballers, has enjoyed an impressive career spanning several top clubs in Europe and Asia.

The six-time African Women’s Footballer of the Year has represented clubs including Arsenal, Barcelona and Bay FC, winning several domestic and continental honours.

Oshoala’s graduation also adds to the growing list of Nigerian footballers combining professional football with academic pursuits.

Super Eagles striker Taiwo Awoniyi is among those who have recently earned academic qualifications.

The forward graduated with Merit from the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Business School in September 2026, earning a Postgraduate Diploma in Global Football Sport Directorship.

Awoniyi described the achievement as another proud moment away from the pitch, noting that his football career had not stopped him from pursuing education.

“I have always believed that being a footballer shouldn’t stop you from being a student of the game, and education has become an important part of that journey for me,” he said.

The forward had previously obtained a degree in Business Management from Buckinghamshire New University in 2022.

World.title: 2027 election: Why attack NDC if Obi has no path to victory? Akpata asks
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain Olumide Akpata says the party believes its presidential candidate Peter Obi has a path to victory in 2027 and should be allowed to campaign without intimidation.

Akpata spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday while reacting to political violence in Edo State.

On Wednesday, the Edo State Police Command confirmed that gunmen opened fire on supporters gathered along Airport Road to welcome Obi to Benin City, leaving one person injured.

“Everyone is entitled to their own permutations. You know, everyone is entitled to their own back-of-the-envelope calculations regarding what the outcome will be, right? Which general goes to war without first counting the cost, as the good book says? So, for me personally, indeed, for those of us in the NDC, our permutations would seem to suggest that there is indeed a pathway,” Akpata said.

Questioning the APC’s confidence ahead of the election, the former president of the Nigerian Bar Association asked why the NDC was being prevented from campaigning if it had no prospect of winning.

“If you are that confident, why are your minions and why are those who are acting on your behalf making it difficult for the NDC to campaign? If you are that confident that there’s no pathway, why not leave us to what you consider to be our folly? Leave us alone. Let us continue to delude ourselves. Let us stay where we are. We are fine with that,” he said.

“But why come after us? Why attack my office? Why shoot Senator Omo-Agege? If you are so confident that there’s no pathway for us, let us be.”

Akpata also said the NDC received advance intelligence that armed individuals planned to infiltrate its town hall meeting.

“We got intel this morning that the plan was for some individuals to infiltrate our town hall meeting and come in with attire, with our old NDC caps and T-shirts, and then cause mayhem. Come in armed and cause mayhem,” he said.

He added that the warning was shared with security agencies after friends and family in Benin City also contacted him with concerns.

“I got the intel. Quite a number of other persons got it. A lot of my friends and family in Benin City who had received this information called me out of concern, understandably so. So we had to escalate. We had to send the information to the police. We had to send the information to the State Security Service and all of that,” he said.

According to Akpata, the planned disruption did not occur inside the town hall meeting. “At the town hall meeting, no such thing happened.”

The legal practitioner alleged that the party’s office was attacked after NDC members had left, and said the attack was intended to intimidate them into abandoning the campaign.

“They knew we had left the office. They were probably hoping that one of the staff there would get hit, and then we would be so scared that everybody would shrink into their own corner and be afraid to continue with this contest,” he said

World.title: ‘I receive threats on daily basis’ – INEC Chair Amupitan
World.content:
INEC Chairman, Prof Amupitan

The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, has disclosed that he receives threats on a daily basis over his role in the commission, lamenting the growing pressure and intimidation directed at electoral officials.

Amupitan spoke on Wednesday in Abuja during a strategic consultative meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, ahead of a planned mock election.

He said the commission had recently come under attacks from different groups, adding that some of the RECs were also receiving threatening messages aimed at intimidating them in the discharge of their duties.

“On a daily basis, I receive threat messages, and sometimes, you just feel like whether those distractions are necessary,” he said.

The INEC chairman warned that attacks on the commission amounted to an attack on Nigeria’s democracy, urging electoral officials not to allow intimidation to prevent them from carrying out their responsibilities.

“If you think you are destroying INEC, you are only destroying democracy in Nigeria,” he said.

Amupitan described working for the commission as a thankless responsibility, noting that its officials operate under intense public scrutiny and are sometimes subjected to abuse regardless of their efforts.

“Working for the commission is like a thankless job. No matter what you do, you are under serious scrutiny and sometimes even abused,” he said.

He further observed that the commission had recently become a target of attacks by different groups, while expressing confidence that some RECs had also received similar threats.

“I am also sure that some of you have been receiving same threats from different groups trying to intimidate and harass us,” he added.

Despite the pressure, Amupitan urged the officials to remain committed to their duties, acknowledging the risks associated with their work.

“We cannot just but continue to do our job. The job is hazardous and very risky, and you have put yourself in it,” he said.

World.title: Cross River ALGON Chairmen Defend Otu, Say Governor Inherited ‘Comatose State’
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON), Cross River State Chapter, has cautioned the public against what it described as lies and distortions by opposition politicians, insisting that Governor Bassey Otu inherited a state in deep decay but is gradually rebuilding it.

The 18 local government chairmen, led by ALGON Chairman, Hon. Yibala Inyang, said the governor met the state “in life support and in a state of decay, a comatose state where gratuities, infrastructure, and public morale had collapsed.”

In a statement signed by Inyang, the chairmen were reacting to recent interviews and political statements credited to the New Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate, John Upan-Odey, as well as renewed activities of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the state.

They urged Cross Riverians to “verify facts, and to judge this administration by verifiable development and not by crafted emotions.”

According to the statement, the Otu administration has embarked on a deliberate process of resuscitation, reform and rebuilding since assuming office.

The chairmen listed the payment of retirees’ gratuities, civil service reforms, job creation, decentralisation of infrastructure to local governments, expansion of the state’s airline, Cally Air, and the recovery of Tinapa Resort among the administration’s achievements.

“These are not promises on paper, they are existing and some ongoing programmes that our councils witness daily in the payment of retirees who waited for years, in the repositioning of the civil service for efficiency, in the opening up of rural roads and facilities, and in the renewed drive to return Cross River to its place as a destination for tourism, business, and investment,” the statement said.

ALGON also dismissed Upan-Odey’s candidacy as an alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), describing it as “a true image of desperation.”

The chairmen argued that the opposition was attempting to create a false impression about the state of governance despite what they described as visible progress under Otu’s administration.

“It is normal in democracy that the minority will have their say while the majority will have their way,” they added.

The local government chairmen also called on residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), comply with electoral guidelines and protect their votes.

“We at ALGON are therefore mobilising Cross Riverians to get their voters cards, to keep to all the rules of the electoral process, and to defend their votes,” the statement said.

Addressing the PDP directly, the association declared that the party’s political fortunes in the state had waned, urging its members to align with the APC.

“We also wish to speak directly to our brothers in the PDP on their recent activities in the State, that the time clock has passed and the train of the party in glory has left the station,” it said.

The chairmen maintained that Cross River had moved beyond what they described as a past characterised by “much talk and little result” to a present delivering tangible democratic dividends.

They further cited the renewed push for the Bakassi deep seaport, the revival of Tinapa Resort and the recovery of the state’s oil wells as developments reconnecting Cross River to commerce, tourism and national relevance.

“Cross River does not need a return to yesterday, it needs consolidation of today for a greater tomorrow, and ALGON stands firmly with the people in that forward march,” the statement added.

World.title: Ogun PDP Deputy Guber Candidate, Yemi Kolapo, Installed 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Peoples Democratic Party’s Deputy Governorship Candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has been installed as the first Akinkanju of Egbaland by His Royal Majesty, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, Okukenu IV, the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland.

Sowunmi-Kolapo had earlier been honoured as the Iyalode of Ijemo, a title that paved the way for her historic installation as the Akinkanju of Egbaland under the royal blessings of the Alake.

According to the Palace, the revered title of Akinkanju of Egbaland, the first of its kind, was bestowed on Sowunmi-Kolapo, the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland, in recognition of her positive contributions and commitment to the development of the Egba community, among others.

Oba Gbadebo urged the new title holder to stay committed to greater service, cultural preservation, and unity across Egbaland.

The monarch honoured Sowunmi-Kolapo, who is also the Ameerah of Ogun State, as part of major activities marking the celebration of his 21st coronation anniversary.

The installation ceremony, which held at the Alake Palace on Saturday, was attended by the crème de la crème of the society, including government officials, business moguls, first class traditional rulers and politicians.

The Ogun State PDP Governorship Candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other leaders of the party to celebrate with his running mate.

Addressing dignitaries at the reception ceremony held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo said she was excited by the honour bestowed on her.

She specifically thanked the Alake of Egbaland, saying that the people had spoken loudly ahead of the 2027 governorship election in Ogun.

She reiterated that the forthcoming poll in Ogun was beyond party lines, maintaining that it would be an avenue for the people of the state to reject any underground plot to sell off the state to strangers and political opportunists.

“We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence.

“I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty.

“I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general.

“Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said.

Also at the ceremony, Senator Iyabo Obasanjo was installed as the 1st Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake.

In his remarks, the Ogun PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu congratulated his running mate and other honorees, describing their recognition as well deserved.

According to Adebutu, it’s a recognition of Sowunmi-Kolapo’s years of selfless service, loyalty and commitment to the development of Egbaland. He said her elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflects her courage, motherly leadership and unwavering dedication to unity, culture and the progress of the people.

Adebutu also congratulated Senator Iyabo Obasanjo on her installation as the 1st Iyaniwura of Egbaland, describing it as a fitting tribute to her distinguished public service and contributions to Egbaland and Nigeria.

He said the twin honours by the Alake, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, on the occasion of his 21st coronation anniversary, had further enriched the cultural heritage of Egbaland and brought pride to the PDP family in Ogun State.

World.title: Akano Diamonds Unveils Onodugo High Jewellery Collection Celebrating Heritage, Identity, Legacy
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

.Rooted in personal history and African cultural heritage

Bennett Oghifo

Akano Diamonds, the Nigerian high jewellery house founded by Akunna Nwala-Akano, has unveiled Onodugo, a new collection that explores the relationship between adornment, identity and the enduring power of inheritance.

Presented at an exclusive gathering at The Magister in Lagos, November 17, 2026, the collection reflects the house’s evolving creative vision- cultural heritage, artistic expression and fine craftsmanship creating jewellery intended to transcend generations.

At the heart of Onodugo is an intimate family story, paying tribute to Nwala-Akano’s grandmother, the late Chief Mrs. Susie Nwakego Okigbo Anakwenze, whose traditional chieftaincy title, Onodugo, gives the collection its name.

A woman remembered for her elegance, generosity, strength and profound sense of identity, she shaped her granddaughter’s earliest understanding of jewellery as something far more meaningful than ornament.

For Nwala-Akano, memories of her grandmother’s magnificent, richly layered adornments remain inseparable from the values she embodied, as her jewellery was an expression of personal style, cultural identity, accomplishment and the traditions she carried with pride.

These memories would ultimately inform the philosophy behind Akano Diamonds: that jewellery can hold meaning beyond its material value, becoming a tangible connection between people, their histories and the generations that follow.

“Onodugo is more than a collection. It is a tribute to the woman who taught me the meaning of strength, elegance and generosity. Through these pieces, I wanted to honour her legacy and celebrate the extraordinary way jewellery can preserve our stories, connect generations and become part of the memories we leave behind”, says Akunna Nwala-Akano, founder and creative Director, Akano Diamonds.

Onodugo marks an evolution in the creative language of Akano Diamonds, introducing animal-inspired designs into the house’s repertoire for the first time.

Drawing upon the expressive possibilities of form, precious materials and intricate detailing, the collection explores the intersection of symbolism and contemporary high jewellery design.

Among Onodugo’s most distinctive creations is Olili, a whimsical interpretation of the goat, inspired by the cherished tradition of fattening goats in anticipation of festive celebrations.

Sculpted in gold and embellished with diamonds and richly coloured rubellites, Olili transforms a familiar cultural ritual into an expression of high jewellery artistry.

Each creation forms part of a broader narrative about individuality, remembrance and the lasting emotional significance of treasured objects.

Rather than treating heritage as something confined to the past, Onodugo presents it as a living influence: a source of inspiration capable of informing contemporary design while retaining its connection to history.

The collection also reflects a wider ambition for Akano Diamonds: to contribute a distinctive African perspective to the international high jewellery conversation, creating pieces that resonate beyond geographical and cultural boundaries without losing the identity from which they originate.

An Intimate Unveiling in Lagos

The collection was introduced to a distinguished gathering of guests, collectors and voices from the worlds of jewellery, fashion, culture and design, featuring fireside conversation between Nwala-Akano and internationally recognised jewellery journalist and gemmologist, Katerina Perez, founder of KaterinaPerez.com.

Moderated by Mazzi Odu, founder of Magnus Oculus and an established commentator on fashion, jewellery and design, the discussion explored the creative origins of Onodugo, the role of storytelling in high jewellery and the significance of developing an authentic design identity.

The conversation also considered the place of African creativity within the international luxury landscape and the opportunities for jewellery houses founded on the continent to contribute new perspectives to the global industry.

Guests were subsequently invited to experience the Onodugo, creations up close, discovering the design details and craftsmanship behind the collection.

The evening also celebrated the cultural influences that inform the house’s identity, with musical performances by Nigerian artist Flavour and other indigenous performers.

The spirit of generosity that inspired Onodugo, extends beyond the collection itself.

During the unveiling, Nwala-Akano highlighted the philanthropic work associated with her family’s legacy, including initiatives supported through the Kuku Cares Foundation.

Among these is a partnership with a family initiative supporting rural women, particularly widows, through opportunities in palm produce cultivation and processing.

The initiative reflects a principle that Nwala-Akano associates closely with her grandmother: that true legacy is measured not only by what one possesses, but also by what one gives and the lives one touches.

An African Perspective on Enduring Luxury

With Onodugo, Akano Diamonds continues to articulate its vision of high jewellery as a meeting point between artistic expression, exceptional materials, cultural identity and personal meaning.

For Nwala-Akano, the collection represents both a deeply personal tribute and a statement of creative intent.

It is an expression of the belief that the most meaningful jewels are not simply worn or admired, but become part of the stories families carry forward.

Onodugo is ultimately, a celebration of what endures.

Akano Diamonds is a Nigerian fine and high jewellery house founded by Akunna Nwala-Akano.

Rooted in African heritage and guided by an international creative outlook, the house explores the relationship between exceptional gemstones, craftsmanship, cultural identity and contemporary design.

Through its fine and high jewellery creations, Akano Diamonds seeks to express individuality, celebrate meaningful personal narratives and create pieces intended to be treasured across generations.

World.title: Coca-Cola, CAF Reunite for TotalEnergies CAF AFCON 2027 in East Africa
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Bennett Oghifo

Coca-Cola and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) are coming together once again, with Coca-Cola named anOfficial Competition Sponsorof the TotalEnergies Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) 2027, set to take place in East Africa.

The renewed partnership marks an exciting new chapter in Coca-Cola’s longstanding connection to African football, bringing together two icons united by a shared passion for the game and its ability to connect people across the continent, according to a statement issued by their publicist yesterday.

For nearly 70 years, AFCON has provided the stage for some of African football’s most memorable moments, bringing nations together and inspiring generations of supporters. Coca-Cola has been part of this history, having supported the tournament for the first time 30 years ago. Its return builds on this legacy while looking ahead to the next chapter of African football.

Football in Africa has always been about more than what happens on the pitch. It lives in homes, neighbourhoods, and communities across the continent, expressed through the songs supporters sing, the traditions they share, the pride of national colours, and the celebrations that bring people together. From local viewing centres and cafés to streets filled with supporters, football creates connections across generations and borders. It is this spirit that underpins the partnership: while the stadium hosts the game, the whole continent brings it to life.

Through its partnership with CAF, Coca-Cola will celebrate the people, cultures and shared experiences that make African football unique, connecting the game with music, creativity, and local expression while creating opportunities for fans to experience the excitement of AFCON 2027.

The tournament will once again provide a platform to celebrate the passion and pride of African football, recognising the supporters and communities who are as much a part of its story as the action on the pitch.

“African football is a powerful source of pride, unity and inspiration across our continent.Coca-Cola is proud to reunite with CAF and return to a tournament that holds such a special place in African football. As we look ahead to the TotalEnergies CAF AFCON 2027, we are excited to celebrate the fans and communities who make the game what it is across the continent,” said Luis Felipe Avellar, President of Coca-Cola’s Africa operating unit.

“CAF is excited to welcome Coca-Cola back to African Football after almost 30 years and we are confident that the partnership between CAF and Coca-Cola will contribute to the development and growth of Football on the African continent and advance Coca-Cola’s commercial and stakeholder interest. The substantial confidence that African and International sponsors, partners and investors are showing in CAF is a recognition of the governance, ethics, transparency and business best practices that we have introduced, as well as the world class quality and global competitiveness of African Football and CAF’s Competitions,” said Dr Patrice Motsepe, President of the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

Fans can follow Coca-Cola and CAF on their official social media platforms for confirmed news and updates on the partnership and AFCON Pamoja 2027.

World.title: NICArb Inducts 1,384 New Members as Omonuwa Assumes Presidency
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Wale Igbintade

The Nigerian Institute of Chartered Arbitrators (NICArb) has inducted 1,384 new members as part of efforts to strengthen arbitration and alternative dispute resolution (ADR) practice in Nigeria and across Africa.

The induction coincided with the formal investiture of Mr Omoruyi Omonuwa, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), as the Institute’s President at its Investiture, Induction and Awards Ceremony held on November 20, 2026, at the Oriental Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Although Omonuwa assumed office in July 2026, the ceremony formally marked his assumption of leadership and the transition from his predecessor, Professor Fabian Ajogwu, SAN, who led the Institute before handing over to him.

The 1,384 newly inducted professionals comprise 989 Associates, 344 Members, 38 IMI/NICArb Qualified Mediators and 13 Fellows.

The development reflects the Institute’s expanding professional membership and its efforts to promote arbitration and other forms of alternative dispute resolution as mechanisms for resolving commercial and other disputes.

In his address, Omonuwa expressed appreciation for the confidence reposed in him, pledging to build on the foundation laid by his predecessor and strengthen the Institute’s institutional standing.

He identified the deepening of professional standards, expansion of institutional partnerships and positioning of NICArb as Africa’s foremost hub for arbitration and alternative dispute resolution as key priorities of his administration.

“I am deeply honoured by the trust reposed in me to lead this great Institute,” he said.

He also acknowledged Ajogwu’s contributions to the growth of NICArb, while commending the Governing Council and members for their support.

Addressing the newly inducted members, Omonuwa urged them to uphold the Institute’s values of integrity and professional excellence.

The oath of office was administered by a Justice of the Court of Appeal, Lagos Division, Justice P.T. Kwahar, while the ceremony attracted more than 500 guests physically and approximately 1,000 participants virtually.

The Minister of Information and National Orientation, who was represented at the event, served as the Special Guest of Honour.

Members of the Institute’s Governing Council, senior members of the Bar and Bench, as well as family members and other dignitaries, were also in attendance.

Omonuwa brings more than four decades of legal experience to the presidency, having been called to the Nigerian Bar in 1984 and elevated to the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria in 2004.

He served as Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Edo State between 2007 and 2008 and received the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR) in 2012.

His involvement with NICArb predates his emergence as president.

He became a Fellow of the Institute in 2012, served as pioneer Chairman of its Edo State Chapter and has been a member of its Governing Council since 2018.

His professional experience spans arbitration, constitutional and administrative law, corporate and commercial litigation, revenue and taxation, and election petitions.

He has also handled complex arbitration matters involving sectors such as banking, insurance, telecommunications, power and energy.

Beyond private legal practice, Omonuwa has served in various capacities within the Nigerian Bar Association and other institutions responsible for shaping and regulating the legal profession.

These include the Body of Benchers and committees established to review aspects of the legal profession.

Meanwhile, NICArb honoured Ajogwu with an award for Excellence in Leadership and Services in recognition of his contributions to the development of the Institute over the past 20 years.

The recognition provided an opportunity for the Institute to acknowledge his leadership and service as he formally handed over to his successor.

With the change in leadership and the induction of 1,384 new members, NICArb said it remained committed to advancing arbitration practice, maintaining professional standards and strengthening commercial dispute resolution in Nigeria and across Africa.

The Institute is Nigeria’s premier professional body dedicated to promoting and advancing arbitration and alternative dispute resolution through training, accreditation and institutional leadership.

World.title: Professional Certificates: Court Orders Definite Hearing of Fraud Investigators’ Suit against ICAN
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Bennett Oghifo

A Federal High Court in Abuja has fixed December 9 for definite hearing in the suit by the Chartered Institute of Forensics and Certified Fraud Investigators of Nigeria (CIFCFIN) challenging the power of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) to train and issue qualifying certificates to forensic professionals.

Justice Joyce Abdulmalik gave the ruling on Tuesday, directing ICAN to regularise and serve their processes on CIFCFIN as the matter was only billed for mention.

Counsel to ICAN, Ogochukwu C. Eze Esq, informed the court about his counter affidavit and preliminary objection, adding that he would need time to respond to the substantive suit.

Responding, counsel to CIFCFIN, Shaibu Aruwa (SAN), said he will not respond to the counter affidavit but the preliminary objection.

In the suit brought on their behalf by their counsel, Aruwa (SAN), CIFCFIN argues that by the combined interpretation of Sections 2(a) – (i),3(1)(a) and 4(a) – (c), 6(2), 12(2), 13, (1) () and (g), 17(1l) (a) and (b) and 22 of the Chartered Institute of Forensics and Certified Fraud Investigators of Nigeria (Establishment) Act No. 45, 2022, ICAN cannot offer ‘Certification Programme culminating in the award of Certified Forensic Accountant of Nigeria (CFAN)’.

In the affidavit deposed to by Head of Legal and Corporate Services of the CIFCFIN, Mohammed Arafat, submits that the conduct of ICAN in inviting applicants in the fields of knowledge of chartered accountants, compliance managers, bankers, investment analysts, auditors, and anti-corruption agencies staff and other institutions to register for a seven-day professional certification programme culminating in the award of Certified Forensic Accountant of Nigeria, is outside its mandate and could cause confusion to the general public.

Consequently, CIFCFIN is asking the court to make an order setting aside and nullifying the award of the qualification or the CFAN certificate, or any other qualification or certificate in the field and practice of forensics in Nigeria; and to withdraw, retract, or cease any publication, gazette notice, or public representation asserting that it has power to certify or license.

Further, CIFCFIN wants an order of perpetual Injunction restraining ICAN, its Council, officers, servants or agents from issuing, purporting to issue, advertising, or recognizing “Certified Forensic Accountant of Nigeria (CFAN)” qualification, designation, licence, or certification, or any title or award identical or similar to those created under Sections 3(1)(a), 4(a) – (c) and 22 of the of the Chartered Institute of Forensics and Certified Fraud Investigators of Nigeria (Establishment) Act No. 45, 2022 or any other qualification or certificate in the field and practice of Forensics in Nigeria.

CIFCFIN wants, among others, a declaration that “by the combined provisions of Sections 2(a) -(i), 3(1)(a) and 4(a)- (c), 6(2), 12(2), 13, (1)(0) and (g), 17(1)(a) and (b) and 22 of the Chartered Institute of Forensics and Certified Fraud Investigators of Nigeria (Establishment) Act No. 45. 2022 the Defendant cannot offer “Certification Programme culminating in the award of Certified Forensic Accountant of Nigeria (CFAN).”

World.title: Abiodun’s Economic Drive: Connecting Experience To Securing Stronger represensation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Femi Ogbonnikan

The quest to transform Ogun State into a major industrial and economic powerhouse in Nigeria and beyond has reached another significant milestone.

Governor Dapo Abiodun’s industrialisation drive recently received renewed impetus with the commencement of the $1.8 billion Lee Group First Industrial Park along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, Sagamu.

Beyond the scale of investment involved, the project represents another important step in the administration’s determination to consolidate Ogun’s position as one of Nigeria’s leading destinations for manufacturing, industrial production and private-sector investment.

Little wonder why influential voices, including the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, have continued to applaud the Abiodun administration for its sustained commitment to industrialisation and economic development. Their endorsement is not a blanket assessment. the state’s economy had witnessed remarkable transformation under the governor.

The monarch’s recent commendation is particularly significant because it reflects an appreciation of the broader economic direction of the administration, beyond individual projects and infrastructure interventions.

Speaking at the concluding session of the Town Hall Meeting on the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) and 2027 Budget for Egba Division, held at the MKO Abiola Cultural Centre, Kuto, Abeokuta, on Monday, November 23, 2026, Oba Gbadebo acknowledged the government’s interventions across critical sectors, including road infrastructure, healthcare, housing, education, food security, transportation, youth development and women empowerment.

According to the traditional ruler, the comprehensive development strategy pursued by the administration has strengthened Ogun’s industrial base, expanded economic opportunities, generated employment and improved the socio-economic well-being of residents. His assessment provides an important perspective on the relationship between infrastructure development, industrial expansion and the overall economic fortunes of the state.

For an administration whose economic development strategy places considerable emphasis on industrialisation, infrastructure and private-sector participation, the Lee Group project offers a compelling illustration of the direction of Ogun’s economic transformation and its implications for the future, particularly Ogun East Senatorial District, where Abiodun is seeking a seat in the National Assembly.

The 450-hectare industrial park, located around Makun Bridge near the Sagamu Interchange, is expected to accommodate 29 manufacturing companies and generate approximately 15,000 direct and indirect jobs when fully operational. Its proposed industrial activities cut across food and beverages, footwear, leather processing, personal care products, automotive components, plastics, recycling and other manufacturing sectors.

The significance of the project extends beyond the factories that will eventually occupy the facility. Its development is expected to stimulate a network of supporting businesses, including transportation, warehousing, packaging, equipment maintenance, catering, security and other services. This creates opportunities for small and medium-scale enterprises to participate in the industrial value chain.

For Ogun State, the implication is an opportunity to deepen its manufacturing base, expand employment opportunities and strengthen the contribution of productive economic activities to internally generated revenue.

The investment also raises an important question about the direction of the state’s industrial development: how can Ogun move from being a preferred location for individual manufacturing companies to becoming an integrated industrial ecosystem capable of competing for larger investments in the global economy?

This is where the broader economic vision of the Abiodun administration becomes relevant.

Since assuming office in May 2019, Abiodun has pursued an economic development strategy that places infrastructure and investment attraction at the centre of the state’s development agenda. Ogun’s geographical advantage, particularly its proximity to Lagos, has historically made it attractive to manufacturers.

However, proximity alone cannot guarantee industrial competitiveness.

Investors require accessible roads, reliable energy, efficient logistics, adequate security, available land and a predictable regulatory environment.

Recognising these requirements, the administration has pursued infrastructure development intended to connect industrial communities, commercial centres and emerging economic corridors.

The government’s reported delivery of more than 1,700 kilometres of roads since 2019 is part of this effort. Road improvements around Ota, Agbara, Igbesa, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode and other locations have implications for the movement of raw materials, finished products, workers and agricultural produce.

The underlying economic logic is that infrastructure should not merely connect communities; it should connect production centres to markets and investment opportunities.

For Ogun East, this approach is particularly relevant. The district occupies an important position in the state’s emerging economic architecture, with Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode, Remo and surrounding communities offering opportunities for manufacturing, commerce, agriculture, logistics and tourism.

The Lee Group industrial park, situated around the Sagamu axis, provides a practical illustration of how investment in industrial facilities can complement the state’s broader infrastructure programme.

Perhaps the most ambitious component of Abiodun’s economic vision is the proposed Gateway Deep Sea Port and the accompanying Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone.

On September 24, 2026, the Ogun State Government and global ports and logistics operator, DP World, signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoU) in Paris for the development of the projects, with President Bola Tinubu witnessing the ceremony.

The proposed investment framework envisages more than $7 billion in initial investment, while the projects are projected to generate over 50,000 direct jobs when fully developed.

The Blue Marine Special Economic Zone is proposed to cover approximately 10,000 hectares.

The deep seaport is expected to provide an alternative maritime gateway, ease pressure on the Lagos port corridor and improve the movement of goods into and out of the country.

For Ogun’s industrial sector, the potential implications are considerable. Manufacturers could benefit from reduced logistics bottlenecks, improved access to export markets and opportunities to integrate into regional and international supply chains.

The economic significance becomes clearer when the port is considered alongside the Gateway International Airport, dry ports, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and other planned infrastructure.

Rather than treating these projects as isolated developments, the administration’s strategy is to connect them into a multimodal transportation and industrial network.

This is an ambitious vision that, if successfully implemented, could reposition Ogun as a major commercial and industrial gateway in the country.

Another important component of this vision is energy. No industrialisation programme can be sustainable without addressing the question of dependable and affordable electricity. Manufacturing companies require reliable power to remain competitive. Unpredictable electricity supply increases production costs, weakens productivity and discourages new investments.

The Abiodun administration has therefore identified energy infrastructure as an important component of its broader economic transformation programme.

The proposed OgunLNG project, estimated at $10 billion, represents another component of the state’s investment pipeline.

Together with the planned maritime infrastructure and industrial development initiatives, it reflects an ambition to establish a more comprehensive industrial ecosystem.

The challenge, as with the other major projects, is to translate investment proposals into functioning infrastructure capable of delivering affordable energy, employment and additional productive capacity.

For Ogun East, where industrial expansion and commercial activities are important to economic development, the availability of dependable energy could make a significant difference to the prospects of businesses and investors.

Beyond industrialisation, however, the Alake’s commendation draws attention to the administration’s broader development philosophy. His acknowledgement of interventions in healthcare, education, housing, transportation, food security and human capital development underscores the fact that economic transformation cannot be sustained by physical infrastructure alone.

A thriving industrial economy requires a healthy, educated and productive population. It also requires an enabling environment in which citizens can access opportunities, acquire relevant skills and participate meaningfully in economic activities.

This explains the administration’s continued emphasis on its ISEYA Agenda, which provides the policy framework for investments in infrastructure, social welfare, education, youth empowerment and agriculture.

Speaking through the Commissioner for Finance and Chief Economic Adviser, Mr. Dapo Okubadejo, at the Egba Division budget consultation, Abiodun reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to inclusive and participatory governance.

Okubadejo explained that the Town Hall Meeting provided an opportunity for residents and stakeholders to contribute to the state’s budgetary priorities, stressing that public expectations and citizens’ input remained important considerations in development planning.

He further described the proposed 2027 Budget as a transition budget, structured to consolidate the administration’s achievements, strengthen the state’s fiscal position and establish a framework for the continuation and completion of ongoing projects.

This commitment to continuity is important, particularly given the scale of investments and infrastructure initiatives currently being pursued across the state.

As Oba Gbadebo rightly observed, the government must sustain the momentum by ensuring the timely completion of ongoing projects and consolidating the gains already recorded.

The governor’s senatorial ambition introduces another dimension to the discussion about Ogun’s economic future.

His experience in managing the state’s investment programme, engaging international investors and coordinating infrastructure development provides a basis for examining the kind of economic representation Ogun East could expect from its next senator.

The Senate is not an executive arm of government. A senator cannot independently construct a seaport, establish an industrial park or implement a state-wide industrial policy. However, the National Assembly plays an important role in legislation, budgetary oversight, federal infrastructure approvals and the creation of a favourable policy environment for investment.

A representative with experience in state economic planning could bring useful perspectives to discussions on industrial development, energy, transportation, maritime infrastructure, trade and fiscal policy.

There are also important opportunities for Ogun East to benefit from stronger engagement between the federal government, the state government and private-sector investors.

The district’s economic interests extend beyond the immediate attraction of factories.

They include access to employment, support for local entrepreneurs, improved roads, agricultural processing facilities, educational opportunities and the development of communities surrounding emerging industrial corridors.

Consequently, the debate surrounding Abiodun’s senatorial ambition should include an examination of how his experience as governor could be translated into effective legislative representation and tangible benefits for the district.

There is also a compelling argument for continuity in the state’s economic development agenda.

Ogun has spent considerable time building its reputation as an attractive destination for investment. The emerging industrial parks, proposed deep seaport, special economic zone, airport and energy projects represent investments in a future that requires sustained policy direction, effective institutional coordination and strategic engagement with the federal government.

A change in political responsibility does not necessarily have to mean a break in development priorities.

Indeed, Abiodun’s potential transition to the Senate could provide an opportunity to leverage his executive experience in advancing Ogun’s interests at the federal level, particularly in areas where state development initiatives intersect with federal legislation, funding and infrastructure policy.

However, the industrial drive of the administration must ultimately be measured by outcomes rather than the number of investment agreements or groundbreaking ceremonies.

The Lee Group industrial park must become operational. Its projected 15,000 jobs must translate into actual employment. The proposed deep seaport must move through the necessary stages of development, while the associated industrial and economic zone must attract businesses and generate productive activities.

There must also be deliberate attention to local content, skills development, environmental protection and the participation of host communities.

Ogun residents, particularly young people, should be equipped to secure employment and business opportunities arising from the state’s industrial expansion.

These are the standards against which the administration’s industrial agenda should ultimately be assessed.

Nevertheless, the direction of the economic strategy is clear: Ogun is seeking to build on its established manufacturing advantage by integrating industrial production with maritime transportation, energy, logistics and agricultural processing.

For Ogun East, the implications are especially important because several of these emerging economic corridors intersect with the district’s development prospects.

As the 2027 political season approaches, Abiodun’s aspiration to represent Ogun East in the Senate provides an opportunity for voters to examine his record, his understanding of the district’s economic priorities and his proposed contribution to its future.

The central issue is not simply the movement of a sitting governor from the state executive to the National Assembly. It is whether the experience accumulated in managing Ogun’s development programme can be translated into effective representation, or stronger federal-state collaboration and policies that expand economic opportunities.

The endorsement by the Alake, coming against the backdrop of the administration’s expanding industrial investment drive, reinforces the significance of the economic transformation narrative. It also highlights the expectation that the government must sustain its momentum and ensure that the benefits of development reach ordinary residents.

Ultimately, the Lee Group industrial park is one important chapter in Ogun’s industrialisation story. The proposed deep seaport, the Blue Marine Special Economic Zone, energy investments and expanding infrastructure represent other components of the same ambition.

For Ogun East, Abiodun’s senatorial aspiration therefore presents an opportunity to connect the experience of managing an expanding state economy with the task of securing stronger representation and economic opportunities at the federal level. If the industrial vision is sustained, effectively implemented and translated into measurable prosperity, the district could be among the major beneficiaries of Ogun’s emerging economic frontier.

*Ogbonnikan is a Senior Special Assistant (SSA) to the Ogun State Governor on Media
