World.title: Cabinet gives green light for Mkhwanazi to head Hawks
World.content:
Cabinet has backed KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi for the position of national Hawks head. Image: X

KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi is one step closer to becoming South Africa’s next Hawks boss after Cabinet approved his proposed appointment.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia confirmed the decision in Parliament on Wednesday, 25 November.

The move comes nearly 17 months after Mkhwanazi made explosive allegations of criminal infiltration, corruption and political interference within South Africa’s criminal justice system.



CABINET BACKS MKHWANAZI AS HAWKS HEAD

Cachalia told Parliament that Cabinet had endorsed his recommendation to appoint Mkhwanazi as national head of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), commonly known as the Hawks.

“Today, I can confirm that Cabinet concurred with my proposal that he be appointed to head the Hawks,” Cachalia reportedly said.

The acting minister said the appointment would strengthen South Africa’s fight against organised crime.

Cachalia submitted a memorandum to Cabinet in October seeking approval for Mkhwanazi’s appointment.

Section 17CA of the South African Police Service (SAPS) Act requires the police minister to obtain Cabinet’s concurrence before appointing a national Hawks head.

Lieutenant-General Siphesihle Nkosi has led the specialised crime-fighting unit in an acting capacity since Lieutenant-General Godfrey Lebeya retired in May 2025.



MKHWANAZI PREVIOUSLY RULED OUT HAWKS TOP JOB

Despite Cachalia’s recommendation, Mkhwanazi previously indicated that he had no interest in pursuing the position.

According to Inside Politics, the KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner said in October that he preferred operational policing to detective work.

Mkhwanazi previously served as acting national police commissioner and held leadership positions within the SAPS Special Task Force.

Cabinet’s decision also raises questions about who will succeed him as KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner should he take up the position.

FROM EXPLOSIVE ALLEGATIONS TO HAWKS TOP JOB

Mkhwanazi thrust South Africa’s criminal justice system into the spotlight on 6 July 2025 when he alleged that criminal syndicates had infiltrated law enforcement and intelligence structures.

His allegations implicated senior police and political figures, including then Police Minister Senzo Mchunu.

President Cyril Ramaphosa subsequently established the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry, while Parliament launched its own investigation.

The proposed appointment forms part of Cachalia’s Police Reset Agenda, which prioritises tackling organised crime and corruption.

Authorities have yet to publicly confirm when Mkhwanazi will assume the position.

World.title: Twickenham pitch set to take a Nations Championship pounding
World.content:
Twickenham's famous turf is set for a pounding during the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend. Image: Ian Kington / AFP

Twickenham’s famous turf is set for a pounding during the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend, but chief groundsman Jim Buttar is confident it can take the strain.

The stadium will host six matches over three days from Friday to Sunday as teams from the southern hemisphere group battle northern hemisphere sides to determine their finishing positions.

READ | Another Springbok coach in hot water with World Rugby?



The schedule at Twickenham starts with Italy vs Fiji on Friday and culminates in Sunday’s final between France and world champions South Africa.

‘Leaving nothing to chance’

Jim Buttar, the RFU’s head of grounds and technical operations, said he was leaving nothing to chance.

“The weekend presents a unique challenge with six international matches taking place over three consecutive days, so preparation has focused on maximising surface resilience and recovery capacity,” Buttar told AFP.



“In the lead-up, we have been carefully managing grass growth, root strength, and surface firmness through targeted agronomic practices, including nutrition, irrigation, and light management.

“We have also planned enhanced post-match maintenance between fixtures, with dedicated staff working throughout the event to repair divots, restore surface levels and prepare the pitch for the next game.

“The objective is to ensure players experience a safe, consistent, and high-performing surface for every match across the weekend.”



READ | Nations Championship referees for EVERY match on Finals Weekend

Reinforced by plastic fibres

Twickenham’s pitch, relaid earlier this year, is reinforced by plastic fibres, which strengthens the playing surface.

“Modern hybrid pitch technology, combined with detailed planning and intensive maintenance operations, allows us to manage a demanding schedule like this,” said Buttar, 46.



“The benefit of a reinforced hybrid playing surface is that it is specifically designed to withstand high levels of usage while maintaining player safety and performance characteristics.”

Buttar said his team of around 15 staff would be working around the clock as the Nations Championship reaches its climax.

“The team will be working from early morning through to the completion of the final match each day to ensure the highest possible playing standards are maintained,” he added.



By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Daniël Stevens’ death: Jeffreys Bay nightclub breaks silence
World.content:
Je’Vista Social Café has condemned violence and pledged to assist police in their investigation into the death of 25-year-old Daniël Stevens. Images: Facebook and X

Je’Vista Social Café in Jeffreys Bay has broken its silence following the death of 25-year-old Daniël Stevens, who sustained fatal injuries during an alleged assault outside the establishment.

In a statement, management extended its condolences to Stevens’ family and friends, condemned violence and confirmed that it was cooperating with police.

The statement comes as four murder suspects, aged between 16 and 21, prepare to appear in court.



JEFFREYS BAY NIGHTCLUB RESPONDS TO FATAL ASSAULT

Je’Vista Social Café management expressed sympathy to Stevens’ loved ones following the incident on Saturday, 21 November.

“Our thoughts are with his loved ones during this difficult time,” management said.

The establishment also addressed the safety of its patrons.



“We do not condone violence of any kind. The safety of every patron inside our establishment is of the utmost importance to us.

“Our entire team is committed to upholding the law and will continue to do so to protect everyone who comes through our doors.”

Management pledged to continue assisting investigators.



“We are cooperating fully with the police and will continue to assist them with their investigation in every way we can.”

FOUR SUSPECTS TO APPEAR IN COURT

Stevens allegedly came under attack after stepping in to help a friend.

He sustained serious head injuries and died on Monday, 23 November.



Eastern Cape police arrested four suspects in Jeffreys Bay, Kariega and Humansdorp on Wednesday morning.

The suspects are due to appear in the Humansdorp Magistrate’s Court on Thursday on a murder charge.

Meanwhile, tributes continue to pour in for Stevens as friends rally behind his family to help cover legal expenses.

World.title: Ncikazi chooses his words carefully on Ouaddou
World.content:
The former Orlando Pirates assistant coach and Abdeslam Ouaddou two coaches came faced off in the Betway Premiership in Soweto on Tuesday night.

His former club grabbed a late 2-0 victory. Boitumelo Radiopane broke the dealock in the 89th minute before Bheki Mabuza buried the game in stoppage time.

Following the final whistle, Ncikazi and Ouaddou avoided a handshake.



MANDLA NCIKAZI AVOIDS ABDESLAM OUADDO HANDSHAKE QUESTION

As reported across local media in recent weeks, Ncikazi left Orlando Pirates under a dark cloud. He reportedly endured a strained relationship with the Bucs head coach.

Ncikazi spent five years at the Soweto club before leaving in October 2026 to return to Golden Arrows as head coach.

When asked about the handshake after the match, Ncikazi responded with humour but made it clear that he was not prepared to discuss the matter publicly.



“I avoided that question, guys. If I shoot a Shabalala who’s sitting in this chair, this chair belongs to someone else,” Ncikazi told journalists. “I’ll shoot him but I’ll also be shooting to the chair. So, just be careful. For I am that person.”

Rather than elaborate on his relationship with Ouaddou, Ncikazi spoke about his five-year association with Pirates and the role the club played in his coaching career.

“Pirates have done everything for me. I’ve grown as a human being,” Ncikazi explained.



“I respect the supporters. I respect the institution. I respect the management. I respect a lot of other people in the club. They’ve given me the love. They’ve given me the growth that I have.”

ORLANDO PIRATES PLAYERS STILL SHARE A BOND WITH NCIKAZI

The 57-year-old also reflected on his relationship with the players he worked with during his time at the Buccaneers.

“You saw the players. When they see me, it’s like they see their father. And that’s what I’ve been to them,” he said. Ncikazi was also reluctant to disclose private details about his experiences inside the Pirates dressing room.



“I can’t tell you stories of all, and everything that I’ve gone through with the players. That is not for public consumption. It’s the family issue that you go through. Good or bad. So let’s keep it at that level.”

He concluded by reaffirming his respect for the club. “Hence I’m not going to say more, it ends there. There’s nothing more. And I will always respect them.”

Ouaddou’s side moved two points clear at the top of the Betway Premiership standings following the victory, while Arrows remained 11th after extending their winless league run to six matches.

World.title: Airline in crisis: Norse Atlantic seeks funding to stay airborne
World.content:
Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic is exploring options to stay afloat as it faces a "critical" financial situation. Image: Wikimedia Commons

Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic, hit by surging jet fuel prices due to the Iran war, said on Wednesday it was exploring options to stay afloat as it faces a “critical” financial situation.

The company’s share price plummeted on the Oslo stock exchange on Wednesday, closing down by 85 percent.

“The company’s financial situation is critical. It is dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations,” Norse Atlantic said in a stock exchange filing.



The company “has explored various strategic alternatives and entertains discussions for a potential takeover”, it added.

In talks for short-term financing

The company also said it was in talks with several parties to obtain short-term financing, noting however that “there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution”.

Founded in 2021, Norse has specialised in low-cost long-distance flights, currently operating a fleet of 12 Boeing 787 Dreamliners.

Its problems are not new but they have worsened with the sharp increase in jet fuel prices resulting from the war in the Middle East.

“No one has so far managed to make low-cost work on long-haul routes. Norse had very good cards to play because it was able to lease large aircraft at a very affordable price,” said Hans Jorgen Elnaes, an analyst at the consulting firm WinAir.

“But they have encountered headwinds, including lately with, obviously, the price of aviation fuel, which has more than doubled since the war began in the Middle East,” he told the broadcaster TV2.



Ceasing operations

The entire aviation sector has been hit by the rising prices.

Spanish airline Plus Ultra announced on Tuesday that it was ceasing operations, while Latvian carrier Air Baltic filed for US Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September.

World.title: Tamlin Blake murder: Two accused remain behind bars
World.content:
Two men accused of murdering acclaimed South African artist Tamlin Blake will return to court on 1 December. Image: X

Two men accused of murdering acclaimed South African artist Tamlin Blake will remain behind bars until their next court appearance on Tuesday, 1 December.

Ronnie Van Willigh (32) and Pedro Fryster (31) appeared in the Riebeek West Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, 25 November, on charges of murder and possession of stolen property.

STATE REVEALS DETAILS OF TAMLIN BLAKE’S MURDER

Western Cape National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) spokesperson Eric Ntabazalila outlined the allegations against the pair.



“The State alleges that on 22 November 2026 the two men killed Tamlin Blake by hitting her on her head with a sharp object several times causing her untimely death,” he said.

He added: “They were found in possession of her cellphone and its cover.”

Both men have requested Legal Aid representation.

MURDER ACCUSED RELEASED FROM PRISON DAYS BEFORE ATTACK

Van Willigh reportedly walked out of prison just four days before Blake’s murder.



The 32-year-old had served a sentence for housebreaking and theft.

RIEBEEK WEST RESIDENTS DEMAND JUSTICE

The killing has sparked outrage across the Swartland community.

Rural and Farmworkers Development Organisation chief executive Billy Claassen has called on communities to unite against violent crime.



Community members reportedly plan to launch an online petition opposing bail for the accused.

Blake, the chief curator of the Spier Arts Trust, died in the attack at her Riebeek West home on Sunday, 22 November.

World.content:
COSMO CITY - Johannesburg is on the brink of a new political chapter, with a mayor and executive expected to be elected on Friday.

But for residents of Cosmo City, Ward 100, the political uncertainty is secondary to the daily struggle for basic services.

READ | Election of Joburg mayor postponed

Crumbling roads, sewage spilling into the streets and water shortages are fuelling frustration.

Residents are hoping the incoming administration delivers the services their community desperately needs.

World.title: WATCH | Heavy rains trigger flooding in Joburg
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Severe weather has hit Johannesburg.

Reports include flooding, hailstorms, overflowing bridges, and damage to homes.

Several bridges and major roads are submerged, including on Witkoppen Road, Belgrave Street, and Bryanston Drive.

READ | Man's body recovered after Soweto flood tragedy

Johannesburg Metro Police Department has warned motorists not to drive through flooded crossings.

The organisation warns that water can conceal damaged roads, open manholes, and strong currents that can sweep vehicles away.

Heavy rain and diversions are also causing traffic congestion in the inner city, Braamfontein, Parktown, Vrededorp and surrounding routes.

World.title: Msunduzi Local Municipality incoming council faces pressure to tackle service delivery
World.content:
PIETERMARITZBURG - The incoming administration will grapple with service delivery backlog and ageing municipal infrastructure in KwaZulu-Natal’s capital city.

Residents in Msunduzi Local Municipality in Pietermaritzburg have been complaining about the slow pace of basic service delivery provision for years and hope the incoming administration will deliver.

One local governance expert believes uMsunduzi needs a solid and stable council to prioritise service delivery.

READ | Faku re-elected Buffalo City mayor

The Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Portfolio Committee is urging all parties in the hung Msunduzi Council to work together to achieve political and administrative stability.

The hung Msunduzi Local Municipality in Pietermaritzburg only swore in councillors before adjourning its first council sitting.

The mayor, deputy mayor, speaker and chief whip are expected to be elected in the next sitting.

World.title: WATCH | Parties confident about who will govern Ekurhuleni
World.content:
EKURHULENI -The spotlight is firmly on the new Ekurhuleni leadership as the metro holds its first council sitting following local government elections.

After the 224 councillors in Ekurhuleni were sworn in, it was agreed that the election of mayor and speaker would be deferred to Friday.

As the horse trading among political parties continues, ActionSA, who are viewed as kingmakers, are confident that their mayoral candidate, Xolani Khumalo, will be elected Deputy Mayor, alongside an ANC mayor in Ekurhuleni.

READ | eNCA coalition builder | The numbers game in Ekurhuleni

ActionSA says it will also hold the mayoral chains in both Johannesburg and Tshwane.

One person who won't be inside council chambers is outgoing mayor, Nkosindiphile Xhakaza.

This comes after the ANC failed to receive enough votes on the proportional representation ballot to secure seats for candidates on the PR list.

While political parties here seem certain who they'll be working with, the ANC will outline its coalition partners in a media briefing on Thursday

World.title: Cabinet backs recommendation to appoint Mkhwanazi as new Hawks boss
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Cabinet has approved Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia's recommendation to have KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi appointed as the new Hawks head.

Cachalia confirmed this to Parliament on Wednesday.

"We appointed General Mkhwanazi to head the priorities and organised crime committee in the NATJOINTs about six months. Today, I can confirm that cabinet concurred with my proposal that he be appointed to head the DPCI, which I think is an important step in fighting organised crime."

The post has been vacant since Godfrey Lebeya’s retirement in May 2025.

The South African Police Service Act governs the appointment process.

It requires Cabinet concurrence and formal reporting to Parliament.

Mkhwanazi's appointment would place him in charge of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, which investigates serious organised crime and corruption.

World.title: MKP ordered to reinstate Zuma-Sambudla and Ndhlela
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The High Court in Johannesburg has ordered the uMkhonto weSizwe Party to reinstate Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla and Nhlamulo Ndhlela as members.

The pair’s respective expulsions have been declared unlawful and unconstitutional.

The party had booted the duo out in June for misconduct, sowing division, and violating its constitution.

READ | Duduzile Zuma, Nhlamulo Ndhlela challenge MK Party expulsion in court

But the High Court found that the party failed to prove that a valid presidential decree could expel the two.

It also found that the organisation had bypassed its own disciplinary procedures.

The National Assembly Speaker and the IEC also have 48 hours to follow the administrative steps to reinstate Ndhlela as an MP.

World.title: 7am sharp! Pick n Pay gears up for extended Black Friday deals
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - As South Africans gear up for Black Friday, it is always a good idea to check available deals before swiping that card.

This year, Pick n Pay's biggest concentration of deals will be rolled out in an extended Black Friday special.

Speaking to eNCA, Pick n Pay chief Marketing Officer Katherine Madley said doors open at 7am from 26 November to 29 November for major in-store Black Friday promotions.

Shoppers, according to Madley, can expect deals at Pick n Pay Hypermarkets on household appliances.

Selected household essentials will also go on sale, with Madley presenting the promotion as one that caters to every customer's needs.

Customers looking to stock up on luxuries for Christmas can also find deals, while those preparing for some other social gathering will be sorted on deals on ‘all things braai’.

“We've got a set of commodities that are on special, especially for the South African who stocks up before the festive season.”

Outside of in-store deals, this year Pick n Pay’s online shopping platform launched three days of online exclusives, which began on November 2-26.

These platform offers allowed customers access to both grocery and clothing deals.

World.title: Voices of Change | Can Courthouse Dogs Help Survivors Find Justice? | 25 November 2026
World.content:
Justice Should Not Depend On How Well Someone Carries Their Trauma

The pursuit of justice for survivors of sexual violence requires more than rigorous investigation and prosecution. It also requires institutions capable of recognising the human consequences of the experiences they are tasked with examining.

There is a difficult contradiction at the heart of seeking justice after sexual violence. A survivor may enter the criminal justice system carrying the psychological consequences of an experience that the system subsequently asks them to describe, remember and defend in considerable detail. Their ability to participate in this process can influence how their evidence is received, yet the conditions under which they are expected to participate may compound the very difficulties they are experiencing. The question is not whether courts should scrutinise testimony, but whether they sufficiently understand the circumstances in which that testimony is given.

Access to justice is often discussed in terms of legislation, policing, prosecution and the availability of legal representation. These are indispensable components of a functioning criminal justice system, but accessibility also has a human dimension. Being afforded the opportunity to give evidence is not necessarily the same as being placed in conditions that allow someone to communicate that evidence effectively. When survivors encounter repeated questioning, unfamiliar environments and prolonged uncertainty, the emotional demands of pursuing justice can become another burden to navigate. Recognising these challenges requires institutions to examine not only whether their procedures are legally sound, but also how those procedures are experienced.

The difference between testing evidence and testing endurance

The credibility of a witness remains a legitimate consideration in criminal proceedings. However, the relationship between memory, emotional presentation and truthfulness is not straightforward. Speaking on eNCA's Voices of Change podcast, advocate and prosecutor Megan Hopewell explains that fragmented memory is “not necessarily a sign of lack of credibility”. Her observation exposes an important distinction: a witness's difficulty communicating an experience should not automatically determine how the substance of their evidence is understood.

This distinction matters because institutional assumptions can shape decisions long before a matter reaches final judgment. If the ability to recount events confidently becomes an informal measure of credibility, people who struggle to communicate under pressure may face an additional disadvantage. None of this removes the responsibility to test evidence or protect the rights of an accused person. Instead, it challenges criminal justice institutions to ensure that their assessment of evidence is informed by an appropriate understanding of trauma, rather than an expectation that distress should manifest in predictable ways.

Rethinking what meaningful support looks like

The possibility of introducing courthouse facility dogs into South African criminal proceedings provides an interesting lens through which to examine these institutional responsibilities. Hopewell's research investigates whether specially trained dogs could offer comfort to vulnerable witnesses during testimony. The significance of the proposal lies less in the presence of an animal than in the underlying recognition that the environment in which evidence is given deserves greater consideration. It invites institutions to investigate whether reducing unnecessary distress could improve a witness's ability to participate without changing the standards against which their evidence is assessed.

However, meaningful support cannot be defined exclusively by those providing it. South Africa's history, including the use of dogs as instruments of intimidation during apartheid, illustrates why an intervention associated with comfort for one person may have an entirely different meaning for another. Cultural sensitivity and individual consent must therefore be fundamental to the design of any animal-assisted support programme. The principle extends beyond courthouse dogs: institutions cannot claim to empower vulnerable people while denying them a meaningful choice in how they receive assistance.

Measuring justice beyond the courtroom outcome

A more trauma-informed criminal justice system requires safeguards, appropriate training, locally relevant research and sustained institutional accountability. Innovation may contribute to that transformation, but it cannot replace investment in existing support structures or resolve the wider barriers that survivors encounter. The effectiveness of any new intervention must be assessed against evidence rather than enthusiasm, with procedural fairness remaining central to its implementation.

Ultimately, the strength of a justice system should be measured not only by its ability to reach legally sound outcomes, but also by whether people can participate in its processes with dignity. Supporting survivors need not mean protecting their testimony from scrutiny. It means ensuring that scrutiny does not become unnecessarily entangled with their capacity to withstand distress. Justice becomes more accessible when institutions recognise that giving evidence is a legal responsibility undertaken by a human being, not a test of emotional endurance.

References

eNCA Voices of Change: Can Courthouse Dogs Help Survivors Find Justice? Jenna-Leigh Bilong in conversation with Megan Hopewell, 26 November 2026.

World.title: Sabina Chege demands answers over stolen phone as MPs face scrutiny
World.content:
Nominated MP Sabina Chege claimed that a fellow legislator stole her week-old iPhone during a chaotic House sitting. [File, Standard]

High drama gripped the National Assembly on Wednesday afternoon after Nominated MP Sabina Chege publicly claimed that a fellow legislator stole her week-old iPhone during a chaotic House sitting, demanding that Speaker Moses Wetang’ula unmask the culprit captured on parliamentary CCTV.

Standing on the floor of the House, Chege recounted how the device vanished amid a heated confrontation on the Minority side in June 2023 and was later tracked to Nairobi’s Donholm estate, sparking murmurs, uneasy glances and a heated debate over integrity inside the august House.

World.title: Wetang'ula orders CCTV review as Sabina Chege renews missing phone
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula has ordered a fresh review of CCTV footage capturing a member of Parliament allegedly picking up a mobile phone during a confrontation in the House in June 2023, following renewed demands by nominated MP Sabina Chege to have her device returned.

Wetang’ula, who chairs the Powers and Privileges Committee, said he would recuse himself from the proceedings and appoint another MP to review the recordings and present findings to the House, in a move aimed at ensuring the matter is handled appropriately.

“As your Speaker, I will take the following action. Although I am the Chairperson of the Powers and Privileges Committee, I will recuse myself from chairing this matter. I will forward the CCTV footage to the Committee and appoint another Member to act on my behalf, review the footage and present a report to this House,” he said.

The decision follows fresh revelations by Chege, who told Parliament that she had never recovered her phone, which allegedly disappeared during the confrontation involving several female legislators on June 8, 2023.

Chege narrated how she realised the device was missing after her colleague, Rosa Buyu, picked up her handbag while coming to her rescue during the altercation.

She said the phone was a newly purchased iPhone 16, barely a week old, and that she immediately raised the alarm but was assured by officers from the Sergeant-at-Arms that it could not disappear within the parliamentary chamber.

“That phone was an iPhone 16, Mr Speaker. I had just bought it. It was actually one week old. I had colleagues who were around me, whom I even asked to give me back my phone,” she said.

Chege explained that she was advised to seek medical attention following the confrontation and subsequently tracked the phone from Nairobi Hospital, where its location initially showed that it was still within Parliament.

She said the device's location later shifted to an area around Protection House, near Bunge Towers, before it was eventually traced to Donholm.

“When I got to Nairobi Hospital, we tracked my phone and established that it was still within Parliament. An hour later, its location had changed to an area near Protection House and Bunge Towers. The next day it was tracked somewhere in Donholm and from that time I did not get my phone,” she said.

The nominated MP said she reported the incident to parliamentary police, the Clerk of the National Assembly and the House Powers and Privileges Committee but had yet to recover the device.

“I want to say, till today, I have never recovered my phone,” she told the House.

Chege appealed to Wetang’ula to identify the person captured in the CCTV footage or ask them to return the phone before the current parliamentary term ends.

“To save the image of this House, please name the person. At least my phone should be returned,” she said, adding that a colleague had previously claimed to know who took the device but declined to disclose the identity.

However, her remarks triggered sharp exchanges, with some legislators questioning the manner in which the matter was being presented and warning against damaging Parliament's reputation.

Homa Bay Town MP Millie Odhiambo dismissed the incident as an issue that should not be elevated into a question of institutional integrity, arguing that members could contribute towards replacing the device.

“You can make a WhatsApp group and donate a phone for her. Don't tarnish the name of Parliament because you are a crying baby. You make people think Parliament steals people's properties,” Odhiambo said.

Ruaraka MP TJ Kajwang expressed concern that the allegations risked further damaging the reputation of legislators, saying the House needed to address issues that had become associated with its members.

“I have been in this House for 15 years. I do not want to end my term and request a renewal of my term with a tag of a thief,” he said.

Kajwang added that allegations circulating about MPs, including claims of selling recruitment opportunities, were damaging public confidence and needed to be addressed.

Lamu East MP Ruweida Obo also weighed in, declaring that most legislators did not engage in stealing other people's property.

“Sisi wengi si wezi, sisi hatuibi cha mtu na chetu hatutaki kiibiwe,” she said.

Wetang’ula, in his defence of the decision to review the footage, maintained that the recordings would help establish what happened and clear members who may have been wrongly implicated.

He clarified that he had not declared any legislator a thief, but had only indicated that CCTV footage showed a male member picking up a phone from a seat after the altercation.

“The Speaker never said there was a thief. The Speaker said a member took the phone. It is not right and morally comprehensible for anyone to take another person's property without their consent,” he said.

He cautioned MPs against relying on social media speculation and artificial intelligence-generated images to accuse colleagues, saying the CCTV review would provide an opportunity to establish the facts.

“It is easy and juicy to go on social media and use AI and amplify things and call people names. The CCTV will absolve everybody,” he said.

World.title: Ledama Ole Kina court battle over Sh1.2m dispute takes new turn
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina has been granted a stay of execution in a Sh1.2 million compensation dispute with former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken.

The court has given the senator an opportunity to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The Employment and Labour Relations Court, sitting in Nairobi, issued the orders on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and scheduled the matter for mention on February 18, 2027.

The development follows a protracted legal dispute arising from Rotiken's dismissal, in which the court awarded him Sh1,220,737.61 in compensation.

During Tuesday's proceedings, Ole Kina sought between 30 and 45 days to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The court subsequently granted a stay of execution pending further proceedings in the matter.

In a statement, Rotiken's lawyer, Tonge Yoya, said the stay of execution did not invalidate, overturn or extinguish the original judgment, insisting that the senator remained legally obligated to settle the award.

The claimant's legal team also told the court that it intended to challenge pending applications by Ole Kina, arguing that some of the issues had already been determined in previous proceedings.

The lawyers said an application dated November 19, 2026, seeking to amend a preliminary objection filed on September 25, 2026, was directed to be served upon them.

Ole Kina was further directed to file and serve written submissions on the preliminary objection within 14 days.

The objection is anchored on the doctrine of res judicata, which bars parties from reopening matters that have already been conclusively determined by a competent court.

Rotiken's lawyers contend that a previous application by the senator seeking a stay of judgment was dismissed on April 24, 2026, and argue that subsequent applications touching on the same issues should not be entertained.

However, the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) is considering a request to release funds to settle a court-awarded compensation to Zakayo Rotiken, a former employee of Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina, in a labour dispute that has resurfaced following a dramatic confrontation between the senator and auctioneers.

In a letter addressed to the parties in Employment and Labour Relations Court Cause E165 of 2021, Rotiken versus Ledama Ole Kina, the Commission confirmed that it had received a request seeking the release of funds to settle the decretal sum and costs awarded by the court.

The letter signed by the Commission's Director of Litigation and Compliance, Anthony Njoroge, states that the request has been placed before the Commission for consideration, with a decision expected once deliberations are concluded.

"The Commission's decision shall be communicated to you as soon as the Commission has concluded its deliberations on the matter," reads part of the letter.

The development comes against the backdrop of a viral video showing Senator Ole Kina threatening to shoot a female auctioneer who had gone to repossess a milk delivery lorry belonging to his Enkanasa Cow Milk Company over an outstanding financial obligation.

The confrontation sparked public outrage, with questions emerging over the circumstances surrounding the attempted repossession and the senator's conduct towards the auctioneers.

The dispute is linked to a labour case filed by Rotiken, who had been employed by Ole Kina before his dismissal. The former employee moved to court seeking redress over his termination, resulting in a monetary award against the senator.

The dispute stems from a court case filed by former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken against Senator Ledama Ole Kina at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Nairobi. The court awarded Rotiken KSh 1,220,737.61 in compensation following his dismissal.

The latest communication from the Parliamentary Service Commission signals that the institution is considering facilitating settlement of the court award, although it has not yet made a final commitment to release the funds.

World.title: Ruto backs Didmus Barasa for Bungoma governor in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa with President Ruto at a political rally in Mt Elgon during the President’s development tour in the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has thrown his weight behind Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa in the race to succeed Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka in 2027, setting the stage for a contest over the county's political leadership.

During his ongoing tour of Western Kenya, the President rallied support for Barasa, signalling his preference for the legislator in the battle for control of Bungoma County after the next General Election.

Barasa has expressed confidence in securing the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party nomination, citing his development record and grassroots mobilisation in Kimilili as the foundation of his gubernatorial bid.

The MP has urged Bungoma leaders aligned with Kenya Kwanza to unite behind his candidature, arguing that a common political front would strengthen the region's bargaining power within the national government.

He said he intends to replicate his development model in Kimilili across the county's 45 wards, prioritising healthcare, education and youth empowerment.

“I want to take the development model we have implemented in Kimilili and extend it to all the 45 wards in Bungoma. Our people deserve better healthcare, improved education infrastructure, functional vocational training centres and quality early childhood education facilities,” he said.

The legislator pledged to strengthen county hospitals, improve the availability of medicines and expand access to healthcare services at the grassroots.

He also promised to invest in vocational training centres to equip young people with practical skills for employment and entrepreneurship, while improving Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE).

Barasa identified agriculture, trade, infrastructure and youth entrepreneurship as key sectors requiring investment to unlock Bungoma's economic potential. He said his proposed administration would prioritise accountability, efficient use of public resources and improved service delivery.

His bid has received backing from a section of county leaders, including Senator Wafula Wakoli of Ford Kenya and Webuye East MP Martin Pepela.

However, Ruto's apparent preference for Barasa has attracted opposition from Sirisia MP John Waluke, who has questioned the endorsement and instead declared support for Westlands MP Tim Wanyonyi, who is associated with the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM).

Waluke argued that Bungoma residents should determine their next governor without external political influence.

“Bungoma belongs to its people, and the people must decide who will lead them in 2027. We cannot allow the gubernatorial contest to be determined through political endorsements from outside. Residents must be given the freedom to choose a leader who represents their interests,” he said.

The contest is also unfolding amid political differences between Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, adding to the competing interests shaping Bungoma's succession politics.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: These three countries offer long-term stays to Egyptians without visa
World.content:
Several countries are easing entry procedures for tourists by exempting certain nationalities from the requirement to obtain a visa in advance, or by allowing them to stay for extended periods.

These measures aim to attract visitors and boost travel and tourism.

Georgia, Serbia, and Thailand are among the destinations that offer flexible entry and residency options—though the specified duration and conditions vary depending on the traveler’s nationality and the type of travel documents they hold.

Georgia

Georgia allows citizens of certain countries, including Egypt, to enter its territory without a visa, with the option to reside, work, and study for up to 365 days.

This makes it a destination that offers a long-term stay without the need for a prior entry permit.

Georgian authorities require tourists to hold health and accident insurance for the entire duration of their stay, with a minimum coverage value of 30,000 Georgian Lari—equivalent to approximately US$11,000.

Arrival procedures in Georgia are straightforward, consisting primarily of presenting travel documents for inspection by border authorities.

Serbia

Serbia offers a range of facilities for travelers, particularly regarding entry procedures and the recognition of certain visas and residence permits issued by other countries.

Furthermore, Serbia is not subject to the ETIAS system, which applies to travelers visiting various other European destinations.

One requirement is that individuals staying in private accommodation—rather than hotels—must register their residence details with the local police within 24 hours of arrival.

Additionally, Serbian authorities permit holders of certain valid visas or residence permits issued by specific countries and regions to enter the country, subject to certain conditions.

These provisions apply to holders of documents issued by countries within the Schengen Area, as well as by Ireland, the UK, and the US.

Thailand

Thailand continues to enhance its facilities offered to visitors through policies designed to allow longer stays for nationals of many countries.

This supports the tourism sector and makes the country an attractive option for those planning extended holidays.

A key benefit of these arrangements is the option to apply for an extension of one’s stay from within Thailand—by contacting the relevant immigration office so long as the applicable regulations permit such an extension.

This measure allows visitors to remain in the country for an additional period without the need to depart and go through the entry process all over again.

Any approval for an extension remains subject to the terms and conditions stipulated by the immigration authorities.

World.title: MP says progress is being made to ban GTAVI in Egypt
World.content:
The Chairman of the Communications Committee in the House of Representatives, MP Ahmed Badawy, warned that the game Grand Theft Auto VI poses an extreme danger to the younger generations in Egypt.

“We have issued significant recommendations to block this game, as it violates the Information Technology Law and presents a risk to young people,” Badawy said during a phone interview interview with Ahmed Moussa’s TV show “Ala Massoulity” (On My Responsibility).

The Chairman of the Communications Committee noted that there are nearly 40 million GTA VI players worldwide.

He added, “We are not against electronic games in general, but this specific game poses a danger to the youth.”

Badawy further explained that discussions have been held with the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, and coordination is underway with the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority, alongside meetings aimed at putting an end to the game’s presence in Egypt.

“Blocking the game is not the only solution; there must also be parental supervision to monitor children,” he stressed.

Badawy added: “It is an extremely dangerous, addictive game—some people spend 14 hours a day playing it. It has a direct impact on the younger generation. In line with directives issued by President Sisi in January, a ‘Digital Safety Law’ will be enacted within a few weeks to protect our youth.”

He further noted: “Those who play GTA become addicted to it, and the game contains content that runs counter to moral standards. Measures will be introduced in the coming days, and the role of the family is crucial. The head of the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority has emphasized that the spread of this game poses a risk to the younger generation and must be addressed.”

Badawy noted that the game is not yet widespread in Egypt with far less than one million players so far.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egypt and Sudan call on Ethiopia to change its unilateral policy
World.content:
The Egyptian Cabinet issued a joint statement on Tuesday on the conclusion of the state visit of the Sudanese Prime Minister Professor Kamel al-Tayeb Idris.

Both sides stressed the inseparable nature of the Sudanese and Egyptian water security and agreed on the necessity of defending both countries’ full water rights and uses under the 1959 Agreement and not permitting any encroachment upon those rights.

They confirmed that their position is based on a call for cooperation and dialogue to protect the right to life and support the right to development, and on joint action to achieve mutual benefit in accordance with international law.

Egypt and Sudan both welcomed African positions that recognize the entitlement of the both Nile Basin downstream states to defend their water rights alongside the interests of their peoples, and to pursue development on an equal footing with the rest of the continent.

The two parties agreed to follow up on the implementation of the outcomes of the coordination meetings within the framework of the Permanent Joint Technical Body for Nile Waters under the 1959 Agreement, to study and formulate the unified position to be adopted by the two countries on all matters related to Nile waters, in addition to meetings of the 2+2 mechanism between the foreign and irrigation ministers of the two countries.

Both sides reiterated their complete rejection of any unilateral measures in the Eastern Nile Basin and agreed that the unlateral actions of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), which violates international law, has grave consequences and constitutes a continuing threat to the downstream Nile states.

They called on Ethiopia to change its unilateral policy and restore cooperation in accordance with rules applicable under international law, particularly the principles of no significant harm, prior notification, consultation and consensus.

Restoring stability

The two sides affirmed their determination to enhance joint coordination to restore stability in Sudan.

Egypt reiterated its rejection of any threat to Sudan’s unity and territorial integrity, and stressed its continued support for the Sudanese people and their national institutions.

Both sides reaffirmed the principles set out in a statement from the Egyptian Presidency, dated December 18, 2025, regarding the direct link between Egyptian and Sudanese national security: foremost among them preserving Sudan’s sovereignty, territorial unity and integrity, safeguarding its resources and the rights of the Sudanese people, categorical rejection of the establishment of or recognition of parallel entities, and the protection of Sudanese state institutions from interference.

Egypt reiterated its full readiness to take all measures and actions permitted under international law and the mutual defense agreement between both countries to support Sudan and ensure these red lines are never crossed.

Both sides condemned the targeting of civilians and infrastructure in Sudan by rebel militias, in particular power stations and water installations, including through the launch of drones from a neighboring country.

They renewed their call for respect for Sudan’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, and for supporting its national institutions, foremost the Sudanese Armed Forces, in fulfilling their constitutional duty to preserve Sudanese national security, protect its borders, defend its resources, prevent the dissipation of its assets and safeguard its water rights.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: The Trump team is getting more and more evasive about Jensen Huang
World.content:
When Jensen Huang was shockingly reinstalled as CEO of Nvidia on Monday, both Nvidia’s board of directors and President Donald Trump cast it as the result of the administration’s assurances that he wasn’t a national security risk and faced no legal jeopardy.

But pretty much ever since then, those assurances have appeared less than ironclad.

All of which reinforces what a massive risk both Trump and Nvidia just took, which should be ratcheting up concerns among some very skeptical GOP lawmakers.

What Nvidia and Trump initially said

The board said in its initial statement Monday morning that its talks with senior government officials left it “confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk” — despite the fact that he had an affair with a woman who US officials feared could be working with Chinese intelligence.

Trump said shortly thereafter on social media that the US government “has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”

Trump also said that, despite questions about prohibited Nvidia chips making their way to China, Attorney General Todd Blanche “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that [Huang] has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

But other officials have yet to publicly double down on those assurances. And Blanche was rather evasive in an interview Monday night. Even Trump has repeatedly emphasized very real caveats.

In addition to the assurances he offered on Truth Social on Monday morning, Trump in a later CNBC interview claimed the Justice Department had “exonerated” Huang.

“They did a study. They did a pretty good investigation,” Trump said. “And they felt that he himself was exonerated. I don’t know what word you want to use.”

The US Commerce and Justice Departments previously said investigators had conducted an in-person interview with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as part of an investigation into whether the Singaporean-based company had been diverting US semiconductors.

But now Blanche is talking around all that, with increasingly evasive comments about what sort of investigations have occurred or been opened — even accusing reporters of “mocking” him by asking the questions.

“What I said last week is that we were looking into it,” Blanche said at the Justice Department on Tuesday. “The FBI, law enforcement, looks into things all the time. That doesn’t necessarily become a criminal investigation. Doesn’t necessarily become an indictment. It just literally is that it’s looking into things.”

Pressed on whether Jensen Huang had been investigated, Blanche threw the question back at reporters. “What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what?”

He went on to say, “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.”

And the night before, when Fox News host Laura Ingraham asked whether Huang had been cleared of being a national security risk and of illegal activity, Blanche never offered a direct answer.

He instead referred to a Wall Street Journal story Ingraham had mentioned in her lead-up, and declined to comment on it. Then he mentioned extensive discussions within the administration — but without ever saying that those discussions had confirmed Huang was in the clear.

Blanche eventually landed on saying: “A lot of thoughtful process by administration officials went into this decision, and the right decision was reached, I believe.”

And perhaps most strikingly, despite Trump’s claim that the DOJ had “exonerated” Huang, Blanche wouldn’t even confirm the DOJ had opened an investigation.

Ingraham asked twice whether the investigation was now closed, and Blanche balked.

“That assumes there’s an investigation that’s open. And I — that’s never been discussed publicly,” Blanche said.

That’s a long way from Trump’s claim about Huang having been “exonerated.”

While Blanche was evasive, others in the administration were non-existent when it came to vouching for Trump’s assurances.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio was a case in point.

It was Rubio who disseminated a memo to senior US officials warning about potential counterintelligence risks posed by Huang’s affair with Alice Huang (no relation).

But on Monday, Rubio said nothing publicly about Jensen Huang’s reinstatement.

He ignored a CNN reporter’s shouted question about it during a public event with a foreign dignitary.

Maybe that wasn’t the forum for an in-depth answer on the subject. But Rubio would seem to be a hugely significantly witness for Trump’s assurances. And the fact that the administration didn’t put him forward was conspicuous.

Trump watered down his assurances, too

And even Trump, later Monday morning in his CNBC interview, qualified his assurances.

When talking about whether Huang might have known about prohibited chips making their way to China, Trump said that “he certainly did not know about it.”

But then he quickly added a less-than-certain caveat, appending “or at least that’s been our very powerful impression.”

Later in the interview, Trump twice qualified his assurances about Huang’s lack of legal liability by saying that “we believe” Huang is in the clear.

“I gave them enough assurance,” Trump added.

He later said: “You can only give the assurance as to what you know. But we feel very strongly that he’s in good shape — very good shape.”

What it means

None of these comments preclude something else coming out about Huang.

Perhaps Trump and those around him are indeed very confident that nothing is going to come out to undercut their assurances. But they just won’t completely own those assurances yet.

And Blanche’s evasive interview and Rubio’s lack of comment both suggest this could be a familiar dynamic: Trump coming to a conclusion based upon what he wants to believe, and those around him scrambling to justify and bolster his preferred narrative.

But there seem to be plenty of people bent on learning more. And time will tell how well the administration’s qualified assurances hold up.

World.title: Like ‘family businesses’: Inside the Nvidia board that ousted and rehired Jensen Huang
World.content:
New York — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gushed last year that support from longtime board members Tench Coxe, Mark Stevens and Harvey Jones was crucial to helping him navigate three decades of running the company.

“They not one time gave up on the company and us,” Huang told the Acquired podcast of the board members and other early employees.

Those same supporters have now helped see Huang through his biggest challenge yet — restoring his role as CEO following an unprecedented corporate scandal. But their close relationships have also raised questions about the board’s independence and whether it was equipped to hold Huang accountable and protect shareholders’ interests.

Including Huang, nearly half of Nvidia’s 11-person board has been with the company since its early days. Its three longest-serving members — Coxe, Stevens and Jones — saw the value of their combined holdings in the company jump by nearly $2.5 billion from Friday to Monday, after Huang was brought back.

His reinstatement marks a sharp turnaround from a week ago, when Jones said the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation, and had no intention of bringing him back. And it comes despite Huang’s relationship with a woman that US officials feared could be a Chinese intelligence asset, as well as multiple reports about an extramarital affair with a subordinate. President Donald Trump has also been open about his role in pushing the board to give Huang his job back.

“The appearance of the relationship between the board and Jensen is most akin to family businesses that go public — that’s a domain in which it’s not uncommon for directors to be there for a long time,” said Jo-Ellen Pozner, management professor at Santa Clara University’s Leavey School of Business. “But those kinds of companies are not major players in the global economy.”

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, the Yale professor known as the “CEO Whisperer,” on Monday called the Nvidia board’s decision to reinstate Huang a “complete failure of corporate governance” and urged them to resign.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on this story.

The Board

Aside from Huang, whose board seat was restored along with his CEO title, four members of Nvidia’s board have been with the company for around three decades.

That includes Jones, who was named last week as Nvidia’s first-ever board chair after joining the company at its inception in 1993. At the time, he’d been serving as CEO of software firm Synopsys, where Nvidia’s original founders had been customers before they approached Jones to bring his operational expertise to the board of their new company.

Coxe and Stevens, early Nvidia investors, have also served on the board since 1993, although Stevens took a two-year hiatus from 2006 to 2008. Brooke Seawell, who previously worked alongside Jones at Synopsys, joined Nvidia’s board in 1997.

Having long tenured board members means having a “longstanding mission and espirit de corps that a lot of people pointed to as a source of strength for the company,” said Eric Talley, professor at Columbia Law School and co-host of the Beyond Unprecedented podcast. But “it does set up situations where a board might be very, very reluctant to exercise real oversight over someone who’s now become their old friend and someone who has given them loyalty over the years.”

That may be why, for example, the board had been reluctant to challenge Huang’s opposition to succession planning that left them flat-footed, causing investors to panic when news of his affairs and concerns about national security risk came to light.

Even many of the board members who have joined, by Nvidia’s standards, more recently, have, by current, typical corporate governance standards, been there a relatively long time.

Research on corporate boards suggests that the “maximum efficacy” of a board member peaks around eight to 10 years and then “trails off dramatically,” Pozner said.

“Boards that have longer tenures are referred to as zombie boards,” she said, “because the implication is that people then are asleep at the wheel in terms of their ability to engage in active oversight because they become like insiders.”

Reinstating Huang

Still, Talley noted that when it came to reinstating Huang, the board was in a difficult position: stick with their original decision to move on without Huang and risk angering some of their biggest customers and the president “who can wield a fairly heavy governmental and regulatory hammer.” Or it could reverse course, which “makes the board look weaker,” and puts them at risk if additional issues arise from the ongoing internal, state and federal investigations.

Going forward, the board may be mindful of keeping a tight leash on Huang to ensure it doesn’t look ineffective, Talley said. It appointed its newest member, Suzanne Nora Johnson, the retired vice chair of Goldman Sachs who joined Nvidia in May, to lead the National Security and Export Controls Oversight Committee it created last week amid the scandal.

Jensen Huang reacts as employees applaud his return to office after Nvidia reinstated him as the company’s CEO, in Santa Clara, California, on November 23, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a social media video. Zhengzhong Tu/UGC/Reuters

Nvidia’s longtime board members also stood to gain financially from Huang’s return. Jones, Coxe and Stevens together own more than 62 million shares in the company, according to data compiled by FactSet based on the most recent filings to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The combined value of their holdings declined by nearly $5 billion from the end of October, before the Huang debacle began, through Friday, before making up around half of those losses Monday when Haung’s return boosted the stock by more than 30%.

It is typical for corporate board members to own stock in the company; it aligns their interests with those of the shareholders they represent. Nvidia’s board may have decided that, like for them, Huang’s return was in the best interest of all shareholders given the dramatic decline in the stock price following his exit.

However, experts say significant holdings could lead to short-term decision making. Nvidia’s longtime board members have all seen their personal wealth rise dramatically in recent years as the company’s valuation skyrocketed.

“Now you’re an insider to that company, your portfolio starts to take on the look of an employee’s portfolio,” Pozner said. “It’s impossible then to separate yourself from the company in a way that allows you to maintain the kind of distance that board independence is supposed to ensure.”

World.title: Iran’s leaders want a baby boom. A struggling economy stands in the way
World.content:
Iran must address its declining population by encouraging young people to marry and have children, according to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

The country of 93 million faces a demographic crisis, with an aging population and falling birthrate as young couples struggle to afford homes and start families amid a deepening economic slump.

In a statement attributed to him on Tuesday, Khamenei said Iran must address shortcomings in past population policies, describing population growth as a “strategic priority.”

His message was read at a ceremony for the National Population Rejuvenation Award, which honors efforts to help families and increase Iran’s birth rate.

Khamenei, who has not made a public appearance since becoming Supreme Leader in March, urged officials to make it easier for young people to marry, support childbearing, improve individual health and promote “a family-centered culture” to help Iran overcome what he called “a critical period.”

His message follows several warnings from Iranian officials about the consequences of a spiraling rate of marriages and births.

“The country’s demographic situation is extremely critical,” Marzieh Vahid Dastjerdi, secretary of the National Population Headquarters, said last month.

The fertility rate has fallen from 6.7 children per woman in the 1980s to 1.34, Dastjerdi said, with several provinces now seeing their populations decline as a result.

“If we do not act today to reverse the decline in marriage and childbearing, our demographic opportunities will be lost one after another,” she said, predicting that the country’s population could shrink by two-thirds to just 31 million over the next 75 years.

An Iranian family sits at the water edge of Chitgar Lake, an artificial recreational lake and park officially known as the Lake of the Martyrs of the Persian Gulf, in northwestern Tehran on April 26. Atta Kenare/AFP/Getty Images

The speed at which Iran’s population is aging makes it a demographic outlier in the Middle East, where many countries are grappling with challenges of growing youth populations. In less than two decades, Iran has transitioned from a youthful and fast-growing society into below-replacement fertility.

Unlike advanced economies facing similar demographic challenges, Iran risks growing old before it becomes prosperous, with decades of crippling US sanctions and economic mismanagement leaving it ill-equipped to absorb the financial burden of an aging population.

One Iranian official called the country’s demographic trend a “mega-crisis.”

The number of births registered in 2012 was 1.3 million. In 2025, it was 892,000. Over the same period, the percentage of the population aged 14 and younger declined from 25.3 percent to 15.8 percent. At the other end of the scale, the population aged 60 and over rose from 8.2 percent to 12.6 percent.

Decline in marriage

Unless the trend is reversed, the over-sixties will account for nearly a third of the population by 2050. And caring for that aging segment of society will become more arduous.

“The growing trend of one-child families in recent years has created numerous educational, psychological and social problems,” according to Fatemeh Mohammadbeigi, who serves on the parliament’s health commission.
