World.title: Madinah’s mountains blend natural beauty with rich Islamic heritage
World.content:
MADINAH: The mountains of Madinah region stand among Saudi Arabia’s most significant natural and historical landmarks, combining striking geological formations with sites linked to the life of the Prophet and key events in Islamic history.

Their rugged terrain, diverse landscapes and cultural significance make them destinations that offer both scenic beauty and a connection to the region’s rich heritage.

Among the best known is Mount Uhud, located about four kilometers north of the Prophet’s Mosque. Closely associated with the Prophet’s life, the mountain was the site of the Battle of Uhud in the third year after Hijrah, when 70 of the Prophet’s companions were martyred. It is also known for its distinctive igneous and volcanic rock formations and natural cavities.

Nearby is Mount Al-Rumah, which played a pivotal role in the battle. Situated around three kilometers from Mount Uhud, the hill was the position assigned by the Prophet to archers and witnessed events that shaped the outcome of the confrontation.

To the southwest of Madinah lies Mount Ayr, a prominent geographical landmark about seven kilometers from the Prophet’s Mosque. The mountain marks the southern boundary of Madinah’s sacred precinct. Along its western foothills stands the Dhul Hulayfah Miqat Mosque, while the historic Wadi Al-Aqiq runs nearby, enhancing the area’s cultural and natural importance.

Mount Sela, northwest of Madinah and about 700 meters from the Prophet’s Mosque, is linked to the Battle of the Trench. The Prophet used the mountain as part of a defensive position against confederate forces, and together with the trench it helped form a protective barrier around the city.

The area surrounding Mount Sela is home to several notable historical and architectural landmarks, including Al-Fath Mosque, Bani Haram Cave and Thaniyat Al-Wada, as well as other heritage sites.

In Yanbu governorate, the Radwa Mountains are renowned for their dramatic geological formations, abundant water resources and picturesque landscapes. Among the region’s most prominent mountain ranges, they also benefit from their proximity to the Red Sea coast.

The mountains are linked to a notable chapter in Saudi history, having been the site of the 1945 meeting between King Abdulaziz bin Abdulrahman Al Saud and King Farouk of Egypt in the Radwa Bay area.

Together, these mountains reflect the geographical diversity and cultural depth of Madinah Region. They also highlight the importance of preserving the area’s natural and historical landmarks and promoting awareness of their role in shaping the region’s identity.

World.title: Brazil says proposed new US tariffs ‘unacceptable’
World.content:
BRASILIA: Brazil’s government on Wednesday voiced “outrage” over “unacceptable” US proposals to impose tariffs on Brazilian aircraft and sugar, as part of a battery of new levies on major trading partners.

“The unilateral decision by the USTR [Office of the United States Trade Representative] is an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process. Brazil will not yield to this type of threat,” President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s office said in a statement.

World.title: Jordanian crown prince discusses bilateral ties with Irish president in Dublin
World.content:
LONDON: Jordan’s Crown Prince Al-Hussein bin Abdullah II discussed regional developments and bilateral ties with Irish President Catherine Connolly in Dublin on Wednesday.

Al-Hussein affirmed Jordan’s readiness to enhance cooperation and investment opportunities with Ireland, and said that he looked forward to Connolly’s participation in next month’s high-level conference on “Humanity in War” at the Dead Sea, according to the Jordan News Agency.

He noted the convergence of views between Amman and Dublin on many regional issues, particularly the Palestinian cause.

He also visited Greenway Hub at Technological University Dublin and met its president, Deirdre Lillis, to discuss collaboration in advanced technologies, research, and intellectual property.

Al-Hussein and Princess Rajwa launched the Jordan-Ireland ICT Forum in Dublin on Wednesday. He outlined Jordan’s plans to expand its digital economy and support companies to scale beyond national borders.

The forum connects representatives from Jordanian tech companies and leaders of top Irish firms across various technology sectors.

Sami Smeirat, the Jordanian Minister of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, emphasized the forum’s importance in strengthening tech and innovation partnerships, noting that the digital economy was a key aspect of Jordan’s growth strategy, the JNA added.

On the sidelines, Al-Hussein met Jordanian nationals in Ireland working in cloud computing, digital infrastructure, social media, and AI in medicine and fintech to discuss opportunities for cooperation with Jordanian institutions.

World.title: Bangladesh raises minimum wage for garment workers after weeks of protests
World.content:
DHAKA: Bangladesh raised the minimum monthly wage for entry-level garment workers Wednesday by 36 percent to 17,000 takas ($136) from 12,500 takas after weeks of violent protests that closed factories and disrupted production as workers demanded the minimum wage be doubled.

The workers took to the streets, fought with police and attacked factories for weeks as they demanded better wages and said higher inflation had made their lives difficult.

The garment industry is Bangladesh’s main sector to earn foreign currency through exports, mostly to the United States and Europe. It represents about 80 percent of the country’s total exports and directly employs about 4 million workers, mostly women from rural areas.

A government-appointed wage board approved the new wage structure early Wednesday after nearly 12 hours of meetings between workers’ and employers’ representatives.

The six-member board, including two representatives each for workers and employers, approved the new wage structure in a 4-2 vote supporting 17,000 takas as the minimum wage. The other two board members sided with workers’ revised demand for 18,000 takas per month.

The wage board also revised monthly wages for other workers.

It was not immediately clear if the workers would accept the new wage structure.

World.title: Iran claims LNG tanker ablaze in Hormuz after hitting mine
World.content:
A ​ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) hit ‌a ‌naval ​mine ‌and ⁠caught ​fire in ⁠the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's ‌Revolutionary Guards claimed on Wednesday evening.

Reuters ⁠could ⁠not independently verify the report carried by ‌state media on Wednesday.



Earlier on Wednesday, an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a “restricted zone” in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, the semi-official Fars news agency reported, citing a statement from the Iranian army.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy also said two oil tankers had struck naval mines, exploded and caught fire in the strait, according to a statement carried by state media. It said the vessels had been attempting to use an unauthorized route through the waterway.

In another statement on Wednesday, Iranian army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said the military had deployed new systems and upgraded existing ones to strengthen surveillance and control of the strait.

He warned that vessels passing through without coordinating with Iranian forces had faced greater risks and struck mines in recent weeks.

Tehran has told Washington it will not restore normal shipping through the strait until its demands are met, including the lifting of a US naval blockade of Iranian ports and an end to the war on all fronts.

Under a proposal conveyed through Qatari mediators, Tehran has offered to reopen the waterway within 48 hours of Washington meeting its conditions.

World.title: Daesh attack kills two Syrian security personnel in Hasaka, state media says
World.content:
DAMASCUS: An Daesh attack killed two Syrian internal security personnel and wounded five others in the northeastern city of Hasaka, Syrian state television reported on Wednesday.

The attack targeted a military headquarters in the city’s Mushairfa neighborhood, Hasaka’s internal security chief Marwan Al-Ali told state broadcaster Ekhbariya.

The internal security forces said in a statement that four Daesh militants carried out the attack. All four died, two in clashes with security forces and two in suicide explosions, the statement said.

Daesh declared a new phase of operations against President Ahmed Al-Sharaa’s government in February and has since mounted a series of attacks against military and security forces, particularly in northern and eastern Syria.

In September, Syrian authorities said they had dismantled a Daesh cell operating across four provinces and arrested several of its leaders and members.

Sharaa, who fought Daesh during Syria’s civil war when he led the Al-Qaeda-linked Nusra Front, severed ties with Al-Qaeda in 2016. His government joined the US-led coalition against Daesh in November 2025.

The militant group lost its last territorial foothold in Syria in 2019 but continues to operate through clandestine cells.

World.title: Colombia police reveal 76 hostages were caught in supermarket siege
World.content:
BOGOTA: Colombian police said Wednesday that 76 people were held hostage during a 17-hour supermarket siege in Cartagena, more than double the number initially reported.

Security forces stormed the supermarket before dawn, freeing all the captives unharmed and killing one of three assailants.

The gunmen allegedly took refuge in the store following a failed attempt to rob an armored vehicle.

A police source told AFP the number of hostages was far higher than the roughly 30 initially reported by President Abelardo de la Espriella.

Armed forces’ footage from the raid showed troops in camouflage moving through the shopping center past shuttered storefronts, with rifles raised and officers working to separate hostages from the hostage-takers.

Authorities feared the hostage-takers would try to leave the store among the captives.

Dozens of people lay face-down on the floor as they were identified and several men in shorts and T-shirts were led away in handcuffs under police guard.

De la Espriella traveled to Cartagena during the crisis, arriving with a police escort while dressed in military fatigues and carrying a sidearm and radio transmitter.

Cartagena’s airport was closed and a massive operation was launched involving hundreds of security personnel from the police, army and special forces.

Now police believe there were only three assailants and there is growing evidence the plot may not have been expertly planned.

“There was a lot of fear at that moment because the kidnappers were quite drunk,” supermarket employee Dayro Rafael Velazquez told Caracol Radio.

Since taking office in August, the right-wing president has often embraced military imagery and a hard-line security message as Colombia faces its worst wave of violence in a decade.

In a video shared on social media he delivered a public warning to the hostage-takers.

“This is the first and final warning” he said “handover the hostages, leave with your hands up.”

The president had earlier ruled out the involvement of guerrilla or paramilitary groups.

The siege coincided with the 10th anniversary of Colombia’s peace accord with the FARC guerrillas, a milestone overshadowed by a surge in violence across the country.

Late Monday, authorities blamed a dissident FARC faction for a car bomb attack in the central city of Villavicencio that wounded 25 people and caused extensive damage.

Separately, the presidency said attacks on electrical infrastructure cut power supplies in several southwestern regions, describing them as retaliation by armed groups against an intensified security offensive.

World.title: How the Houthi siege of Taiz is leaving Yemen’s children vulnerable to preventable diseases
World.content:
TAIZ/LONDON: World Children’s Day, which fell on Nov. 20, passed unmarked in the Yemeni city of Taiz, where an ongoing Houthi siege is depriving children of lifesaving medical care.

Ten days earlier, a distraught mother from a mountain village south of the city had appeared in a harrowing video on social media, cradling the lifeless body of her baby girl, Gaza.

According to the Yemeni Human Rights Network, the child had fallen ill and was being driven to a hospital in Taiz when the vehicle came under fire from Houthi gunmen and was forced to turn back.

Unable to reach medical care because of the siege, Gaza died.

She was not the first child to die as a consequence of the civil war triggered by the Houthi revolt 12 years ago, and she is unlikely to be the last.

This week, the UN revealed that about 350,000 children in Taiz governorate had missed scheduled measles and rubella vaccinations because of insecurity and restrictions on humanitarian access.

For some, the consequences could be fatal.

On Wednesday, the Disease Surveillance Department at the Ministry of Health’s office in Taiz told Arab News that 2,804 suspected cases of measles, including 280 laboratory-confirmed infections, and 26 deaths had been recorded across the governorate so far in 2026.

Health authorities have also recorded 1,605 cases of cholera, 71,303 cases of acute diarrhea, 1,646 cases of febrile illness and 50,040 suspected cases of malaria, of which 4,354 have been confirmed.

According to figures released in July by the Taiz Office of Public Health and Population, more than 14,400 cases of measles had been recorded across governorates under the authority of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the first six months of the year, resulting in the deaths of 87 children.

Taiz recorded the highest death toll (18), followed by Aden (14), Hadramaut (12), and Abyan and Lahj (11 each).

These figures cover only government-controlled or contested areas of Yemen, where health services, although severely compromised by the war, are in better shape than in territory held by the Houthis.

Comparable statistics for areas entirely under Houthi control are unavailable, but the World Health Organization estimates that these account for 70 percent of Yemen’s measles cases.

Dr. Fahed Al-Namer, manager of the immunization program in Taiz governorate, told Arab News that the blockade and security concerns had severely hampered the delivery of vaccines and other medical supplies to areas recently seized by the Houthis.

Delays during vehicle inspections risked compromising temperature-sensitive vaccines, medical supplies could be confiscated, and the safety of vaccination teams could not be guaranteed.

The Houthis, he added, had been obstructing vaccination campaigns in areas under their control for more than a year.

“We have 70 health facilities in the areas recently seized by the Houthis that are now completely devoid of vaccines,” he said.

Mohammed Al-Masani, director of the Taiz provincial office of Yemen’s Ministry of Information, told Arab News: “The supply of medicines and medical equipment between Aden and Taiz has completely ceased, and the city is now suffering from a complete lack of access to medicines through official channels due to the blockade and tightened sanctions.

“Medicines that enter through smuggling are at risk of spoilage and loss of efficacy due to improper transport and storage, thus exacerbating the risks.”

The disruption of vaccination programs poses a serious threat not only to individual children but also to entire communities.

Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. The virus can also be transmitted through contact with contaminated surfaces.

Although symptoms typically begin with a fever and runny nose, followed by a distinctive rash, the disease can cause life-threatening complications, particularly among young children and those with weakened immune systems.

Nearly 350,000 children in Taiz governorate have missed lifesaving measles and rubella vaccinations amid the ongoing conflict. (Reuters)

Even in countries with advanced health systems, measles can result in hospitalization among unvaccinated patients.

Where hospital care is inaccessible, complications such as pneumonia and encephalitis — inflammation of the brain — can prove fatal.

Two doses of the measles vaccine provide highly effective protection against the disease. However, preventing transmission across entire communities requires vaccination coverage of about 95 percent to achieve what is known as herd immunity.

In Taiz, Al-Namer fears this threshold is increasingly beyond reach.

“In those Houthi-controlled areas of Taiz province, a total of 347,000 children, aged between six months and five years, have been denied the measles booster dose, which is essential for strengthening both individual and herd immunity,” he said.

Even in Taiz city, existing vaccine stocks could run out within weeks.

“For the city of Taiz, we have a stock of vaccines that will last until the end of December or mid-January — supplies we obtained before the siege. Beyond that point, however, there will be a shortage.”

On Nov. 4, the WHO released an emergency response plan for Yemen, “as escalating conflict drives mass displacement, overwhelms health facilities and threatens access to lifesaving care.”

Three days later, Yemen’s Ministry of Health launched an emergency national measles and rubella vaccination campaign.

Supported by the WHO, UNICEF and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, the six-day campaign aimed to immunize more than 950,000 children ages 6 months to 5 years across 100 districts in 11 governorates.

However, Yemen’s territorial fragmentation has left hundreds of thousands of children beyond the reach of vaccination teams.

According to a Nov. 15 assessment by the Anaween Center, only six of Yemen’s governorates are entirely under the control of the internationally recognized government. Five, including Taiz, remain contested, while 11 are controlled by the Houthis.

The resurgence of measles is symptomatic of a much broader public health emergency, the scale of which is laid bare in the WHO’s response plan.

As of Oct. 25, 1,677 deaths and 7,395 injuries had been reported since the escalation in violence by the Houthis in early August.

However, the WHO warned that the toll was “likely to be higher given figures from the Ministry of Public Health and Population exclude casualties in areas inaccessible to WHO and its partners.”

More than 270,000 people have been internally displaced, placing additional pressure on already overstretched health services.

The WHO reported that “hospitals face critical shortages of medicines, fuel, oxygen and other medical supplies,” and that “health facilities and ambulances have also come under fire.”

Compounding the crisis is a deterioration in child nutrition.

Data published in September showed that more than a quarter of the nearly 2,900 children screened by mobile nutrition teams working with WHO partners in accessible areas were suffering from acute malnutrition, including more than 200 with severe acute malnutrition.

The findings offer a troubling indication of how rapidly conditions could deteriorate if the fighting continues.

Even before the latest escalation in violence, the WHO said, “projections published in Feb. 2026 estimated that more than 2.2 million children under five would experience acute malnutrition, including over half a million with severe acute malnutrition.”

With their immune systems already weakened by hunger, malnourished children are particularly vulnerable to infectious diseases such as measles.

Although the lack of reliable data from Houthi-controlled territory makes it difficult to establish the full extent of Yemen’s health crisis, available figures point to a substantial burden of measles infections.

In its Nov. 7 assessment, the WHO reported that a total of “22,800 measles cases, including 128 measles-related deaths, had been reported in Yemen as of Oct. 4, 2026.”

And vaccines are far from the only essential supplies failing to reach Taiz.

According to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, or OCHA, the city has been effectively cut off since the beginning of October.

“We are seeing increasingly that the fighting makes it impossible for us to get in and impossible for people to get out,” Jens Laerke, an OCHA spokesperson, said on Oct. 23, warning of a rapidly deteriorating humanitarian situation.

“Access roads have been cut off and that means that very little fuel, food or other supplies have reached the city since.”

Human Rights Watch has called on the Houthis to “immediately open vital roads for essential goods and aid to civilians” in Taiz.

The Houthi siege of Taiz has restricted humanitarian access and disrupted the delivery of essential medical supplies. (Reuters)

“Throughout the 11-year-long siege of Taiz, the Houthis have bombed, starved, and denied humanitarian aid to a million residents of the city with scant adherence to international law,” Niku Jafarnia, Yemen researcher at Human Rights Watch, said in a statement.

“Efforts by the Houthis to cut off food, water, and medicine to Taiz show their utter disregard for civilian lives.”

The Taiz-based Human Rights Information and Training Center documented a series of incidents between Sept. 3 and Nov. 9 “in which the health sector in Taiz Governorate was subjected to a series of simultaneous and systematic violations and attacks by the Houthi militia.”

These included attacks on five hospitals and health centers, as well as ambulances, resulting in deaths and injuries among patients and paramedics.

Medical equipment had been looted, while restrictions on the movement of supplies had caused “a severe shortage of fuel, oxygen, medicines, and supplies, which has curtailed medical services and threatened the operation of incubators, intensive care units, and dialysis.”

For the children of Taiz, the combined effects of violence, malnutrition, preventable disease and dwindling medical supplies mean that surviving the war increasingly depends on access to even the most basic health care.

As the death of baby Gaza illustrates, that access can mean the difference between life and death.

World.title: Iraq in discussions with Apple to activate Apple Pay
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi authorities are holding official talks with Apple to introduce Apple Pay in Iraq as part of a broader push to expand digital payment services.

Head of the Communications and Media Commission (CMC) Baligh Abu-Kallal said in early November that Iraq is negotiating with Apple over launching Apple Pay, privacy policies, and gaming sector cooperation.

In August, Iraq accredited Apple as a verified digital platform, covering services such as the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads under local regulations.

Abu-Kallal stated that launching Apple Pay depends on completing technical, legal, and financial procedures, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Iraqi banks have also signaled interest in digital wallet expansion amid wider banking modernization and digital payment reforms.

Earlier in July, an Iraqi government source mentioned that the committee in charge of activating Apple Pay services met with Apple’s regional managers to make the service accessible in Iraq.

The initiative is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to enhance the electronic payment infrastructure and boost the adoption of modern technology, thereby fostering financial inclusion and advancing digital transformation.

Iraq aims to make Apple Pay available to users, in accordance with the government’s strategy to expand the online payment sector and support the transition to a digital economy.

World.title: Iraq expands digital services for Iraqi Airways
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has expanded digital services for Iraqi Airways to facilitate passenger travel and reduce airport congestion.

Travelers can complete check-in procedures and issue their electronic boarding passes online before arriving at the airport.

Passengers can also choose their preferred seats in advance during booking or check-in.

Users can now electronically change their flight schedules and destinations without visiting a sales office.

The airline enhanced its electronic reservation and online payment systems for both domestic and international flights.

A new pricing structure lets passengers select different fare classes with varying baggage allowances and modification terms.

Passengers can use these services through the Iraqi Airways official website or via the mobile app.

The step is part of the company’s strategy to grow its digital capabilities, improve passenger experience, and stay up with the latest standards in the aviation industry.

The service generally opens for check-in between 48 and 24 hours before the scheduled flight departure and closes up to two hours prior to takeoff.

World.title: Iraq’s judiciary rules that Baghdad can deploy forces along all borders
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that the federal government in Baghdad can deploy troops to secure all international borders, including those in Iraqi Kurdistan.

The decision backs Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s push to assert central control over border crossings and oil fields across the country.

The court affirmed federal jurisdiction over international borders, customs oversight, and the auditing of oil and gas fields, while allowing shared management with regional authorities and provinces.

Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal takeovers of Kurdish-run border crossings and disputed oil fields following an oil smuggling investigation. The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) described the moves as constitutional violations and military threats, calling instead for dialogue.

The crackdown, which also targets militias with ties to Iran, is seen by analysts as part of Zaidi’s larger effort to consolidate power. As a result, the Supreme Judicial Council has called on all parties to uphold the 2005 constitution.

A day earlier, al-Zaidi ordered federal authorities to take control of all border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan and directed the Oil Ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salah al-Din, and Nineveh provinces.

The KRG was instructed to approve crude oil and petroleum product exports only through the federal Oil Ministry.

The directives followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company and a wider campaign against illicit oil networks—including alleged smuggling in Jurf al-Sakhar linked to the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group, which denied the accusation.

World.title: Iraq presses OPEC+ to raise oil output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is pushing OPEC+ to raise its estimated crude oil production capacity ahead of the group’s scheduled meeting on November 29 to set 2027 output quotas.

Baghdad rejected preliminary findings from OPEC+’s independent capacity review—conducted by consultant DeGolyer and MacNaughton—which put Iraq’s capacity at 4.9 million barrels per day, according to Reuters.

OPEC+’s review estimated Iraq’s sustainable production capacity at approximately 4.9 million barrels per day. However, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair contends that Iraq can achieve a capacity of 5.2 million barrels per day.

Additionally, there are broader efforts within Iraq aimed at increasing this figure even further to support a larger production allowance.

Iraq’s current OPEC+ production limit stands at 4.43 million barrels per day. In OPEC’s November report, Iraq reported October output at 4.88 million barrels per day, while OPEC’s external secondary sources estimated it lower at 4.49 million barrels per day.

Capacity figures serve as a key benchmark for calibrating member quotas in 2027. Higher capacity estimates strengthen a member’s case to pump more oil or claim a larger share of group output.

To restore its economy and meet its financial obligations, Baghdad is looking for more oil earnings. Iraq threatened to leave OPEC earlier in 2026 due to the capacity assessment, but it subsequently dropped the threat when the UAE left OPEC and OPEC+ in May 2026 to increase output.

World.title: Iraq foils oil smuggling operations in Dhi Qar, Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi National Security Service (INSS) announced on Wednesday that it foiled oil smuggling operations across Dhi Qar and Kirkuk provinces.

The actions are part of a wider government crackdown led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi against illicit oil trade and pipeline tampering.

Security forces uncovered an illegal tap on an oil pipeline in the al-Luhays area, which is administratively part of Basra province. Three hoses connected to illicitly installed valves were siphoning crude oil into tanker trucks.

With judicial authorization, INSS units intercepted and seized a vehicle illegally modified with side openings to offload fuel. Kerosene was found inside its tank, and a suspect was arrested.

Earlier in the week, Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council reported an organized crude oil smuggling ring using tankers near the Dhi Qar–Basra border, leading to detentions of a suspect and several Energy Police officers.

A committee completed fieldwork investigating alleged smuggling of Kirkuk oil through Iraqi Kurdistan toward Iran and Afghanistan.

The operations follow recent security deployments in Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, in Babil province and arrests related to pipeline breaches in Najaf.

World.title: Kata’ib Hezbollah retains core Jurf Al Sakhar stronghold and absorbs 2,000 fighters into state payroll
World.content:
Bahjdad (IraqiNews.com) – Five days after federal security forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr), informed sources revealed to Al-Mada newspaper—in a report on Wednesday, November 25, 2026—that the military operation has produced no substantive change to the balance of power on the ground.

According to the report, Kata’ib Hezbollah retains full control over the town center and its vital surrounding perimeter, including the areas of Abd Ways, Al-Farsiya, Al-Hujayr, and Al-Fadhiliya.

No federal security forces have entered this core perimeter—referred to by insiders as the “Kata’ib Hezbollah Square”—and the newly inaugurated joint control headquarters remains situated outside Jurf al-Sakhar’s administrative boundaries.

Rather than retreating, the faction utilized the official deployment announcement to absorb more than 2,000 of its previously off-roster fighters into the official payroll of the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) under the 72nd and 79th Brigades, shifting their financial burden onto the state budget while securing institutional cover and legal immunity.

Field accounts indicate that the federal deployment touted by Baghdad was largely confined to peripheral sectors and routine troop rotations:

Iraqi Army: Deployment was restricted to the 38th Brigade of the 10th Division along the northwestern edge of Jurf al-Sakhar toward Anbar’s Amiriyat al-Fallujah axis and the canal linking Lake Habbaniyah to Lake Razzaza west of Karbala.

Federal Police: The only state force maintaining direct contact with Kata’ib Hezbollah zones simply rotated existing positions, replacing the 16th Brigade with the 17th and 11th Brigades without advancing into faction-held territory.

Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS): No CTS units deployed inside Jurf al-Sakhar, aside from a Karbala provincial regiment stationed at the garrison camp in Musayyib district outside the subdistrict’s borders.

Meanwhile, informed sources noted that Kata’ib Hezbollah leveraged the publicized “withdrawal” to execute a wide-scale military redeployment, transferring substantial weaponry and equipment to establish new positions in western Anbar and western Karbala in anticipation of a potential renewed military confrontation between the United States and Iran, while Iranian and Houthi advisors remain active inside Jurf al-Sakhar.

Political observers cited by Al-Mada suggest Tehran and allied factions orchestrated a nominal concession in northern Babylon—long targeted by Washington as a financial artery for Iran—in order to open a new security and political front against the Kurdistan Region.

According to these assessments, Tehran is pressing Baghdad to obtain a list of Iranian Kurdish opposition members residing in Kurdistan and relocate them to Samawah in southern Iraq to neutralize their potential involvement in any U.S.-Iran conflict.

This geopolitical maneuvering coincides with Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s announcement on Tuesday of heightened anti-smuggling measures around the Kurdistan Region’s perimeter, alongside Erbil’s denial of rumors regarding federal troop deployments inside the region or a return to the 1991 “Blue Line.”

Simultaneously, allies of Al-Zaidi view the nationwide crackdown on oil pipeline tapping as leverage to prosecute and imprison leaders of defiant armed factions by choking off illicit revenue streams. The anti-smuggling drive took a sharp political turn after Najaf MP Abdul-Hadi Al-Hasnawi stated that a farm implicated in oil pipeline tampering in Najaf belongs to the Harakat al-Nujaba militia rather than a private family, following arrest warrants issued for two of his brothers.

In Erbil, former Kurdistan Parliament member Abdul-Salam Barwari warned that actors implicated in Jurf al-Sakhar’s illicit economy are attempting to deflect scrutiny by manufacturing crises around the Kurdistan Region—effectively signaling that oil theft is not confined to northern Babylon.

While characterizing Al-Zaidi’s official rhetoric on state monopoly over weapons as generally measured, Barwari cautioned that commentary from aligned media and activists revives a 2017 Kirkuk-style mentality hostile to Iraq’s constitutional federalism, seeking to exploit internal Kurdish political tensions following the recent reactivation of the Kurdistan Parliament.

World.title: Turkey highlight urgent European demand for Development Road at Baghdad Transport Expo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Transport Wahab Salman Al-Hasani announced on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, that Iraq is reclaiming its economic role as a vital transit bridge between East and West through an integrated infrastructure vision linking seaports, airports, railways, and highways, while Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloğlu revealed that European officials inquire daily with mounting urgency about the completion timeline for the Iraq-Turkey Development Road project.

Speaking during the opening of the Iraq International Exhibition and Conference for Transport, Airports, and Logistics at the Baghdad International Fairground.

Al-Hasani stated that the Ministry of Transport is modernizing its operational systems to convert Iraq’s strategic geography into an engine of economic strength.

He highlighted major milestones in southern Iraq, noting that core components of the Grand Faw Port are nearing completion as Iraq’s maritime gateway to global markets, reinforced by the recent inauguration of the Khor al-Zubair immersed tunnel to shorten transport distances and connect ports to inland road networks.

Al-Hasani confirmed that the strategic Development Road project has reached advanced stages in its engineering designs, establishing an overland economic corridor linking the Arabian Gulf to Europe via Iraq and Turkey to diversify national revenue, attract investment partnerships, and generate employment.

Alongside maritime and rail infrastructure, he noted that the ministry is upgrading air navigation systems, modernizing domestic airports, and expanding Iraqi Airways’ international route network to elevate aviation safety and global connectivity.

Addressing the conference alongside international partner firms and diplomatic envoys, Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu underscored that disruptions in global supply chains have made diversifying transport routes and enhancing corridor efficiency critical.

Positioning the Middle East at the crossroads of Asia, Europe, and Africa, Uraloğlu stated that complementing Turkey’s existing East–West transit lines with a North–South axis through Iraq’s Grand Faw Port creates an unprecedented commercial and logistics artery between Asia and Europe.

Uraloğlu emphasized that the success of the Development Road depends not only on physical rail and highway construction, but also on streamlining border crossings, accelerating customs procedures, and implementing digital transformation across transit networks so borders function as gateways rather than barriers.

Offering the international expertise of Turkey’s engineering and contracting sectors to support Iraq’s infrastructure rollout, he concluded by noting that European officials contact Ankara every day persistently asking when the Development Road will be completed—a testament, he said, to how recent developments in Europe have validated the corridor’s strategic necessity.

World.title: US dollar edges higher across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged slightly higher across major domestic parallel markets on Wednesday morning, November 25, 2026, with purchasing bids hovering near the 169,000-dinar threshold in key commercial centers after briefly testing the 168,000-dinar range earlier in the week.

According to morning market figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra with notable regional spreads.

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,250 IQD against buying offers of 168,750 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks recorded the sharpest uptick, quoting retail selling rates at 169,950 IQD—just 50 dinars shy of the 170,000-dinar mark—alongside purchasing bids of 169,700 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices posted retail selling rates at 169,750 IQD and buying offers at 169,250 IQD per $100.

Wednesday’s modest rebound keeps parallel market rates trading roughly 17,250 to 17,950 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official cash rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar)—a spread of approximately 11.3% above the official rate, down slightly from the wider gap recorded at the start of the trading week.

World.title: Election Commission: Rectify wrong roll entries during SSR via Form
World.content:
Sources told TOI that incorrect entries in the electoral roll published after SIR may be flagged by electors, booth-level agents or any other person. BLOs should not make changes solely on the basis of automated identification, an official said.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Through Form 8, meant for changes in particulars, the ongoing special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls across 24 states and UTs will offer an opportunity for rectification of any incorrect or erroneous entries in the existing electoral roll based on the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise undertaken earlier.EC Wednesday directed booth-level officers concerned to undertake a field verification where the particulars of an elector in the existing roll do not match the information collected during SIR. These particulars may include the electorâs name, date of birth, mobile number, photograph, among others.âWherever any mismatch is noticed, the same shall be flagged for verification and for taking necessary corrective action,â EC said in a letter to chief electoral officers of the 24 states/UTs where SSR is being conducted.Sources told TOI that incorrect entries in the electoral roll published after SIR may be flagged by electors, booth-level agents or any other person. BLOs should not make changes solely on the basis of automated identification, an official said.âIn respect of such flagged entries, the BLOs shall visit the electors concerned during the ongoing SSR to verify their particulars and obtain duly filled-in and signed Form 8, wherever required. The electoral registration officer (ERO) or assistant ERO shall examine and dispose of such applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure,â EC said.The poll body further instructed that the update of demographic particulars be effected only through Form 8, duly signed by the aggrieved elector and subject to verification and approval by the competent authority.

World.title: Cabinet ministers advised to avoid foreign travel; Parliament session likely by December 15
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid continuing suspense over the governmentâs plan to push the delimitation bill, Cabinet ministers have been asked to avoid planning overseas travel and engagements and remain prepared for Parliament to be convened at short notice, possibly anytime before mid-December.

PM Narendra Modi is learnt to have hinted at the likelihood of a parliamentary session by December 15 at the Cabinet meeting chaired by him Wednesday. Government sources have maintained that the Constitution amendment bill to implement the womenâs reservation law from the 2029 general elections and increase the strength of Lok Sabha by around 50 per cent is likely to be introduced in the next sitting of Parliament.



The governmentâs decision not to prorogue the monsoon session, which was adjourned sine die on Aug 13, has also fuelled speculation that itâs meant to facilitate early resumption of Parliamentary proceedings. Keeping the session alive allows the parliamentary affairs ministry to reconvene both Houses at three daysâ notice without going through the process of summoning a fresh session.

Although NDA has maintained a tight lid on its legislative strategy, senior functionaries have expressed confidence that the government will secure the two-thirds majority required to pass the Constitution amendment bill.





This is a significant challenge, given that the oppositionâs united stand had thwarted the governmentâs attempt to get the legislation through when it was first introduced in April.

The political landscape, however, has changed since then, with the INDIA bloc showing signs of fragmentation. The government is understood to be factoring in these developments while assessing its numbers and prospects of securing the required support.

The proposed legislation seeks to link the implementation of womenâs reservation with a delimitation exercise that would redraw parliamentary constituencies and substantially expand Lok Sabhaâs strength. The proposed expansion and the methodology for delimitation have been among the principal points of contention, with opposition parties raising concerns over their potential implications for the political representation of states.

However, the government has tried to assuage concerns by saying that each stateâs share of seats in the Lok Sabha will increase by 50 per cent.

World.title: After 30 years in jail, former Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassin seeks parity with Rajiv Gandhi's killer in SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Invoking the ground of parity with former PM

AG Perarivalan, who was a death convict but was allowed to be released and is now a practising lawyer, Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been in jail for over 30 years and is facing a death sentence for the assassination of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, requested the SC on Wednesday that the same reformative approach should be taken for him also and his sentence be commuted to life imprisonment.

SC reserved its order.

Appearing before a bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Singh, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for Rajoana, said that he was a misguided youth at the time of the offence and he is now a reformed man. Rohatgi contended that Rajiv Gandhi killer Perarivalan is now a practising lawyer after his death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment and the sentence was later remitted by the apex court on the ground that he spent 30 years in jail.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines



The senior advocate said his client also spent more than 30 years in jail and he should also be allowed the same relief.

Opposing his plea, ASG KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, said that no relief should be extended to him as the convict had himself declared he did not have faith in the Constitution and judicial system. But Rohatgi said the statement was made 30 years ago during trial and that should not be a ground to deny him liberty after three decades.

World.title: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move high court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Surprised by an order of a special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue here cancelling the non-bailable warrant (NBW) against a wanted businessman who had been evading arrest for the last four years, the

is likely to move the Delhi high court challenging the grounds on which relief was granted to him in absentia.

The case pertains to Dinesh Pandey of Saanag group in India and Somap group in Singapore, who was granted relief on Nov 14 by the special court, which cancelled the NBW against him.

Sources said he is wanted in connection with the investigation into transfer of Rs 10.4 crore allegedly through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd (AJL), a company which has since been taken over by Young Indian, controlled by Congress leaders Rahul and Sonia Gandhi.

A senior ED official tracking the case said it was settled practice that warrants against an absconding accused were not cancelled so long as he stayed away and did not appear before the investigators.

âThe order also faults the investigating officer for placing part of the case diary before the court in a sealed cover, although sealing sensitive material for the courtâs perusal is routine in serious economic offences,â the official said. The court, he added, ignored the accusedâs undertaking that he would return by Jan 2026 and appear before the court. He did not keep that promise.

World.title: Allahabad high court to hear Rahul Gandhi’s plea against PIL, says Supreme Court
World.content: The bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that HC, during the fresh hearing on Vigneshâs PIL, would hear Rahul Gandhiâs submissions against the petition

World.title: Vande Mataram at J&K waqf event sparks row
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Several Muslim clerics who attended a J&K Waqf Board function where

was played in full expressed regret and said they had prayed for repentance, as the national song triggered a religious controversy in Kashmir.

The clerics, who attended Mondayâs Waqf Day event in Srinagar, said they had neither endorsed the song in their hearts nor through their words. âSince we attended the gathering, if our participation has hurt anyoneâs religious sentiments, we sincerely repent before Allah and pray that He accepts our repentance,â they said in a statement on Wednesday.

The function was attended by Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, waqf board chairperson and senior BJP politician Dr Darakhshan Andrabi, Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf Ahmad and other dignitaries.



All six stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyayâs 1875 poem Vande Mataram were played at the event in accordance with a Union home ministry protocol directive issued earlier this year that mandated the full version at state functions, official events and legislature sessions.

In August, the President cleared the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, putting Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem.





The amendment did not alter the stanzas, but made disrespect or disruption punishable.

Adopted as a slogan during the freedom movement, the poem was abridged in 1937 when the Congress Working Committee approved only its first two stanzas to respect religious diversity.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Mirwaiz Umar Farooq-led Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU), an amalgam of religious organisations and institutions, said there was no legal obligation to play the song at an official function, and criticised the waqf board for playing it at an event organised by an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments.

It said playing Vande Mataram at the event conflicted with Islamâs principle of Tawheed, or absolute oneness of Allah. âWhile Islam encourages love for oneâs homeland, it draws a clear distinction between love for oneâs homeland and its worship. Any expression or practice that attributes divinity to the motherland is contrary to the fundamental Islamic belief of Tawheed and is, therefore, un-Islamic and impermissible for Muslims,â MMU said.

It said it was considering legal advice and urged Muslims entrusted with religious responsibilities to uphold their beliefs without compromise. Andrabi was not available for comment.

World.title: Omar government breaks silence on Sheshnag row, says lake safe
World.content: Forest minister Altaf Kaloo said the earthmover seen in the viral video was operating 200 to 300 feet away from the lake and at a higher elevation. He said not even a grain of soil had entered the lake.

World.title: PM Modi wants ITI courses aligned with industry needs, jobs closer to home
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Wednesday called for public sector undertakings (PSUs) to strengthen their links with Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for training and recruitment of youth, pitching a âClassroomâCompanyâCareerâ approach to bridge the gap between skilling and employment and create job opportunities closer to home, which will help address migration to some extent as well.

Chairing the monthly PRAGATI meeting, PM suggested that PSUs should assess their future manpower requirements and partner with ITIs to train and recruit candidates in relevant trades. He also encouraged them to support practical training and apprenticeships and give greater priority to hiring trained ITI graduates.

While reviewing the ITI ecosystem and the implementation of PM-SETU, PM Modi called upon chief ministers and chief secretaries to provide leadership in strengthening ITIs and deepening industry participation under PM-SETU.



Officials said the PM threw a challenge to chief secretaries to set up five clusters across big states, three in small states and one in UTs in the next three months.

Under PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), a âclusterâ refers to a group of govt ITIs linked through a hub-and-spoke model, with one major ITI serving as the hub and several smaller ITIs functioning as spokes.

Reviewing a power project, PM Modi suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind power projects. He said that such projects should be developed closer to centres of consumption wherever feasible, taking into account local resource availability and demand. World.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites massive fire on highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 30 people
World.content:
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor's office said in a statement.

The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.

At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading amongst the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.

Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.

Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.

Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.

In January, 21 people were killed and 16 injured in a massive multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

World.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
World.content:
The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6. The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided.

Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government. The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders.

“And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally.

The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions. The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30.

The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute.

The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144.

A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise.

Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents.

After the Single Judge Bench had refused his pleas for an interim stay of the elections, Mr. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.

World.title: Governor seeks CM’s report on compliance with SC’s directions
World.content:
Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam.

The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”.

Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions.

It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday, that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon, but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team.

World.title: Infrastructure works for Knowledge City under way, says T.N. Minister for Industries
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Minister for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce S. Keerthana on Tuesday said infrastructure works for Knowledge City is under way in the phase one construction of the project.

She was speaking at the curtain raiser event of the India Global Education Summit 2027 (IGES) held in Chennai. The 872-acre Knowledge City is coming up in Tiruvallur district on the northern outskirts of Chennai where innovation, knowledge and research would be enhanced by bringing together universities, research labs, and research-oriented industries in a collaborative ecosystem.

In the first phase, 413 acres are being developed. The Minister noted that plot allocation under this would begin by April 2027. Further, one-lakh-square-foot Knowledge Tower is also being built where plug-and-play facilities would be provided to enable foreign universities to function. Sources in Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation Limited (TIDCO) noted that the tower would be ready by the later part of 2028.

Speaking about the project, Ms. Keerthana said, “Institutions such as University of Melbourne and IIT Madras are already engaged with us. Further, five institutions have already signed memorandums of understanding to take up space there.”

The second edition of the IGES will take place from February 3, 2027 to February 5, 2027 in Mamallapuram. The summit aims to discuss knowledge economy which includes artificial intelligence, skilling, among others. The summit will be hosted in partnership with National Indian Students and Alumni Union (NISAU), a UK body representing universities.

Minister for Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology and Digital Services R. Kumar invited people, companies and institutions to invest in the AI city and Knowledge City that has been planned in the State.

Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu Managing Director B. Vishnu Chandran, TIDCO Chairman and Managing Director D. Karthikeyan, IIT Madras Director V. Kamakoti, Data and AI director, Microsoft Cecil Sunder, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology and Digital Services department Additional Chief Secretary Atul Anand and NISAU founder Sanam Arora also spoke at the event.

World.title: Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign.

During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security.

He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution.

“We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar.

At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it.

He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district.

World.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
World.content:
In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”.

In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”.

He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”.

The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties.

Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

World.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case
World.content:
The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer.

Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house.

The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages.

The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation.

The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry.

In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. The protesters raised slogans alleging lack of safety for women.

The DMK’s women wing also staged a demonstration at the Four Roads junction in Kallakurichi demanding the arrest of the MLA. They burnt the effigy of the MLA and raised slogans against him.

Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

World.title: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent
World.content:
No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, scheduled for November 26, senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration.

United stand: Editorial on protests against SIR

The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands.

An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu, was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. It stated: “This is to inform you that we, the Delhi People Against SIR, are going to observe Constitution Day as per the details given.”

The email further stated that participants would assemble outside Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 and march towards Jantar Mantar via Kali Bari Marg. “This is for your information and any follow-up/arrangements,” it added.

“We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, told The Hindu.

Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration.

Public notice 🔶Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on 26.11.2026. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march. 🔶Section 163 BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi District. Unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas are prohibited. 🔶All are requested to comply with the order u/s 163 BNSS and cooperate with Police. Violations will invite legal action. — DCP New Delhi (@DCPNewDelhi) November 25, 2026

However, New Delhi police officers denied receiving the intimation and stressed that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remain in force in the area and warned that action would be taken against gatherings in violation of the restrictions.

The police said “preventive” security measures would be put in place to prevent any unauthorised gathering in the area. These would include multi-layer barricading, deployment of additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, to disperse crowds and prevent protesters from assembling in violation of the prohibitory orders.

People Against SIR was formed on October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.

The platform has claimed that more than 50% of the voters who were on Delhi’s electoral rolls in January 2025 and voted in the February 2025 Assembly election have either been deleted or categorised as doubtful following the revision exercise.

The organisers have described SIR as an attack on the Constitution and the right to vote, alleging that the exercise disproportionately affects marginalised communities, including minorities, Dalits, transgender persons, women, migrant workers and the homeless.

The November 26 march will also demand the restoration of pre-SIR electoral rolls and that no elections be conducted on the basis of the revised rolls. Other demands include the impeachment of and legal action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and the repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of election commissioners.

November 26 marks the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949.

World.title: Bangladesh ties of 'great importance' to Pakistan, President and PM tell visiting parliament speaker
World.content:
Bangladesh Parliament Speaker Hafizuddin Ahmad on Wednesday met with President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where the Pakistani leaders reaffirmed that Islamabad attached “great importance” to its ties with Dhaka.

The parliament speaker, accompanied by a parliamentary delegation, arrived in the country on Monday on a six-day official visit at the special invitation of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq. This is the first official visit to Pakistan by a speaker of the Bangladesh parliament, according to the PM Office (PMO).

On Wednesday, Ahmad and his delegation called on President Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr, where the president noted that “Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Bangladesh, which are rooted in shared history, common faith and deep cultural and familial affinities”, his office said.

The Bangladeshi delegation included MP Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, chairman of the standing committee on foreign affairs; MPs Humam Quader Chowdhury, Muhammad Nazibur Rahman, Nilufar Chowdhury Moni, and Nasser Rahman; as well as Bangladesh High Commissioner to Pakistan Iqbal Hussain Khan.

On Pakistan’s side, the meeting was attended by Sadiq, Senators Sherry Rehman and Saleem Mandviwalla, MNAs Naveed Qamar and Dr Shazia Sobia Aslam Soomro, along with the convener of the Pakistan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship Group in NA.

Later, PM Shehbaz hosted a dinner at the PM House in honour of the visiting speaker and members of the parliamentary delegation.

“Welcoming the speaker and his delegation, the prime minister said that Pakistan attaches great importance to its fraternal ties with Bangladesh,” PMO said.

Recalling the shared history and cultural affinities between the two countries, the premier underscored the importance of closer institutional cooperation and stronger people-to-people contacts.

The prime minister noted that the “extensive engagements of the visiting parliamentary delegation in Pakistan indicate a huge scope of collaboration in parliamentary domain”, PMO said.

He emphasised that regular parliamentary exchanges would provide a robust foundation for closer bilateral cooperation across various avenues of mutual interest.

PMO also shared pictures of PM Shehbaz individually meeting the members of the visiting delegation.

‘Pakistan ready to extend defence cooperation with Bangladesh’

During his meeting with the visiting delegation, President Zardari emphasised the need to strengthen Pakistan-Bangladesh relations through expanded parliamentary exchanges, trade and economic cooperation, educational links and people-to-people contacts, calling for a “forward-looking approach based on sovereign equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit”.

He noted the “renewed momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in high-level exchanges, education, trade, culture and people-to-people contacts”, the Presidency said.

The president expressed hope for the early finalisation of around 26 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) “under consideration, which would provide an institutional framework for expanding bilateral cooperation”.

He “reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to extend defence cooperation with Bangladesh”, also highlighting the “considerable potential” for cooperation in agriculture, industry, food security, disaster management, digital governance and space research.

On connectivity, President Zardari welcomed the commencement in January of direct flights by Biman Bangladesh Airlines and emphasised the need to increase flight frequency and destinations in view of growing demand. He also called for exploring direct maritime links to facilitate trade and economic cooperation.

Discussing trade and economic relations, the president noted that bilateral trade remained below its potential.

Therefore, he called for effectively utilising existing mechanisms, including the Joint Economic Commission (JEC) and the Joint Working Group on Trade, to explore preferential trade arrangements and advance the priority areas identified during the JEC session held in October last year.

President Zardari noted that ongoing exports of Pakistani rice under the government-to-government agreement could serve as a basis for broader cooperation on food security and the supply of essential commodities.

“Pakistan, in line with Bangladesh’s request, is also ready to provide technical expertise for the refurbishment of sugar plants in Bangladesh,” the Presidency statement read.

President Zardari encouraged greater private-sector engagement across a range of sectors, including textiles, pharmaceuticals, leather, automobiles, construction materials, minerals, chemicals, ceramics and jute.

He offered Pakistan’s assistance in facilitating training for Bangladeshi parliamentary officials at the Pakistan Institute for Parliamentary Services (PIPS) and sharing its institutional expertise in operating a bicameral legislature.

The president expressed Islamabad’s desire to further strengthen parliamentary cooperation with Dhaka, as well as highlighted bilateral cooperation in the education and media sectors.

President Zardari welcomed progress under the China-Bangladesh-Pakistan Trilateral Mechanism, particularly the identification of 12 priority areas of cooperation during the Kunming meeting on June 19, 2025, the statement said.

He appreciated Bangladesh’s humanitarian gesture of hosting over one million Rohingya refugees, reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for their safe, voluntary and dignified return to Myanmar in accordance with international law, and called upon the international community to ensure sustained humanitarian assistance.

The president expressed confidence that Ahmad’s visit would help advance bilateral relations and pave the way for more high-level exchanges between the two countries.

Meanwhile, Ahmad thanked the president for the warm welcome and hospitality extended to him and his delegation, according to the President House.

The speaker conveyed the greetings of Bangladesh President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

The statement said: “Recalling his personal memories of Pakistan, he underscored the importance of parliamentary diplomacy and expressed his desire to promote closer engagement between the two Parliaments through exchanges and regular institutional interaction.

“He also noted the popularity of Pakistani television dramas in Bangladesh, reflecting the cultural affinity between the peoples of the two countries.”

Relations between Islamabad and Dhaka have improved since the ouster of former Bangladeshi premier Sheikh Hasina, during whose tenure ties between the two countries remained shaky.

In February, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal attended the oath-taking ceremony of PM Rahman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

World.title: Diesel price dips below Rs350 after 4 months; petrol rate down by Rs4
World.content:
The government reduced the price of diesel by Rs5 per litre and that of petrol by Rs4 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs314 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs348 per litre on Nov 26 (Thursday).

The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.
